Toutes les gardes existantes (merge clean, résolution de conflit par agent + une retry, blocage sur findings ouverts, revue fraîche) s'appliquent désormais contre `arjj` : mêmes règles, autre cible.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Une branche épic fork d'`arjj` (pas du défaut) quand le mode est actif.
- Le merge (manuel + Full Auto) atterrit sur `arjj`.
- La résolution de conflit Full Auto (un agent, une retry) cible `arjj`.
- Les gardes de workflow (provenance, revue, findings, ownership de session) restent identiques en forme.

user_stories.title: Garder `arjj` en sync avec l'amont (reste mergeable)
user_stories.description: Opération guardée « sync `arjj` avec l'amont » : merge/pull de la branche par défaut dans `arjj`, avec reporting de conflits et résolution par agent optionnelle. Dispo à la demande et/ou avant de proposer la PR. Journalisée dans `git_sync_log`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- `arjj` peut être amenée à jour de l'amont sans perte.
- Les conflits sont surfacés (jamais de drop silencieux), résolvables par agent si opt-in.
- Chaque op de sync est journalisée dans `git_sync_log`.

user_stories.title: GitHub sync : proposer une PR `arjj` → défaut
user_stories.description: Nouvelle action dans l'écran GitHub sync : détecter la divergence (ahead/behind `arjj` vs défaut), créer ou mettre à jour une PR (head=`arjj`, base=défaut) via Octokit, draft par défaut, trackée dans `pull_requests`, journalisée dans `git_sync_log`, avec lien projet et statut live (SSE).
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Un clic crée / met à jour la PR (une seule ouverte à la fois pour le même head/base).
- La divergence est affichée avant création.
- Draft par défaut ; bascule vers PR régulière possible.
- Le statut PR (open/merged/closed) est persisté et mis à jour en live via SSE ; entrées dans `git_sync_log`.

user_stories.title: Flux de release dérivé de `arjj`
user_stories.description: `release/v<version>` et le tag `v<version>` partent de `arjj` (une release contient tout le travail Arij intégré). On garde CHANGELOG, push du tag, draft GitHub release optionnel, et Done→Released.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- La branche release et le tag dérivent de `arjj`, pas du défaut.
- Les epics inclus passent Done→Released comme aujourd'hui.
- Le contenu d'une release = l'état de `arjj` au moment du cut.

user_stories.title: Sécurité & provenance de `arjj` (artifact Arij)
user_stories.description: `arjj` vit dans le dépôt de l'utilisateur mais est un artifact Arij : jamais de force-push sur `arjj`, jamais de suppression de la branche par défaut, toute op destructive exige une preuve de provenance explicite (discipline du marqueur de clone §3.3). État (nom + toggle + PR/divergence) persisté de façon restart-safe.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- `git push --force` sur `arjj` et suppression de la branche par défaut sont refusés.
- Toute op destructive sans preuve de provenance est refusée.
- Le state (settings + `pull_requests` + `git_sync_log`) survit à un restart.

user_stories.title: Compatibilité rétro & transition des projets existants
user_stories.description: Projets déjà sur le modèle défaut : détecter si `arjj` existe ; proposer un bootstrap depuis le défaut ; toggle projet pour repasser au comportement actuel (fallback = zéro régression). Export/import `arji.json` inchangé.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Un vieux projet démarre sans casser (fallback actif par défaut).
- Toggle off = comportement actuel bit-à-bit.
- Toggle on = bootstrap propre de `arjj` depuis le défaut, sans perte de données.
- L'export/import `arji.json` reste stable.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Passe de refinement — ticket maintenu en Backlog

Seul ticket des deux colonnes de planification qui ne peut pas être démarré tel quel. Sa section « Décisions à trancher (à confirmer avant implé) » liste 5 questions qui changent le contenu des stories, pas seulement leur implémentation. Elles sont regroupées ici pour pouvoir être répondues en une fois.

**Question de fond, en amont des cinq : adopte-t-on ce modèle ?** Le ticket se décrit lui-même comme un « changement radical proposé » et amende §3.3 et §5.7 de la spec. Tant que ce oui/non n'est pas donné, les 7 stories sont spéculatives — c'est la raison principale du maintien en Backlog.

Puis, si oui :

1. **Nom de la branche.** `arjj` est-il le nom voulu, ou une coquille pour `arij` ? Le dépôt utilise déjà `arji.json`, donc la question n'est pas rhétorique — le nom apparaît 8 fois de façon cohérente, ce qui peut être délibéré comme répété. Et est-il figé ou configurable par projet ? (la story 1 prévoit `git_integration_branch`, ce qui répond « configurable » — à confirmer.)
2. **Bascule dure ou opt-in.** Quel défaut pour `git_use_integration_branch` sur un projet **nouvellement créé** ? La story « Compatibilité rétro » ne tranche que le cas des projets existants (fallback = off).
3. **PR `arjj` → défaut : draft par défaut ou PR régulière ?** Les critères de la story 4 disent draft ; confirmer que c'est la décision et pas une hypothèse d'écriture.
4. **Les releases découlent-elles de `arjj`** (état intégré au moment du cut) ou de la branche par défaut une fois la PR mergée ? Ça change §5.6 et toute la story 5.
5. **Sync amont → `arjj` : à la demande seulement, ou automatique avant chaque PR ?**

### Dépendances ajoutées dans cette passe

`B-arij-130` et `B-arij-131`. Les deux corrigent le chemin de merge que ce ticket retarge (cascade des stories côté merge ; conflit → 409 + pré-vol sans écriture dans l'arbre vivant). Les traiter avant évite de porter les mêmes bugs sur la nouvelle cible et de réécrire deux fois les mêmes fichiers.

La priorité High est laissée inchangée : le ticket n'est pas dispatchable tant qu'il est en Backlog, donc la baisser n'aurait rien changé au fonctionnement et aurait effacé un signal d'intention.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Planning pass — kept in Backlog, and why.**

This is the one ticket in the two planning columns whose blocker is a decision rather than work. Its own description frames the `arjj` trunk as a *changement radical proposé*, and it rewrites the base of §3.3 (worktrees, merge, releases) and §5.7 (GitHub sync). That is not something to hand to an agent on the strength of a proposal. It also still waits on B-arij-130 and B-arij-131, both of which are correctly retained as dependencies — they are merge-path defects, and this epic retargets the merge path.

Questions blocking promotion:

1. **Go / no-go on the model itself.** Is `arjj`-as-trunk approved, or is it still an option being weighed against staying on the default branch? Everything else here is downstream of that answer.
2. **The branch name.** `arjj` is one keystroke from the project name `arij`. Deliberate, or a typo that would be permanent once branches, tags and settings are written against it?
3. **Settings scope.** The first story requires "les 2 clés se round-trip via l'API de settings" — global keys, or project-scoped? Arij supports both, and the seventh story's retro-compat promise ("un vieux projet démarre sans casser") reads as per-project.
4. **Release cut before the PR merges.** The fifth story derives the release branch and tag from `arjj`. Is a tagged release allowed to exist that the upstream default branch does not yet contain, or must the `arjj` → default PR merge first?
5. **What keeps `arjj` in sync.** The third story requires it to stay mergeable with upstream but does not say what triggers the sync — a manual action on the GitHub sync screen, or a scheduled routine alongside `ci_watch` and `github_issue_sync`?

Answering 1 and 2 is enough to unblock; 3–5 could be settled during the build if the direction is confirmed.

epics.title: buildSecondOpinionPrompt injects the full branch diff with no size budget
epics.description:
Adjacent to 8LsTw3ETWFFr (fencing of the second-opinion diff), deliberately left out of that diff: same call site, different failure mode — size rather than injection.

`lib/auto-mode/second-opinion.ts:393` computes the final diff with no bound:

```ts
const finalDiff = await simpleGit(worktreePath).diff([`${baseBranch}...HEAD`, "-U3"]);
```

and `buildSecondOpinionPrompt` (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts`, `## Independent Second Opinion`) embeds all of it. Nothing between the two truncates, samples or measures. A wide epic — a lockfile refresh, a generated-file churn, a large refactor — produces a multi-megabyte diff that becomes the bulk of the prompt for the gate that decides whether Full Auto merges into the base branch.

Every neighbouring evidence channel already carries a budget: `buildCiFixPrompt` bounds the spec with `CI_FIX_MAX_SPEC_BYTES` precisely because its CI evidence is byte-budgeted, the telescope payload has `payloadChars`/`truncated`, and Dreaming caps at 30 sessions. This one has nothing.

**Why it is not just a cost issue.** The gate's verdict is mandatory: a negative verdict or any open finding parks the epic and the merge never happens. A prompt that overruns the provider's context does not fail loudly as "diff too large" — it fails as a session that ran, saw a fraction of the change, and submitted a verdict on it. A silently partial merge gate is worse than a gate that refuses.

**Reproduction (not executed — read off the code paths).** Enable the second-opinion gate on an epic whose branch diff against the base is larger than the reviewing provider's context, and observe that no code path caps, samples or reports the diff size.

**Why it was not fixed in 8LsTw3ETWFFr.** That ticket names exactly two problems (no neutralisation, fixed-length fence) and a one-line suggested fix. A cap is a behaviour change on the gate — truncating what the last pre-merge check reads is a trade-off that deserves its own decision, in particular whether an over-budget diff should be truncated with an explicit marker or should hold the merge outright. My read is that holding the merge is the safer default, since the gate's whole purpose is to refuse rather than to guess, but that is the call this ticket should make.

What is *not* settled is what the gate should do when the diff exceeds a budget — and because the second opinion is a **mandatory merge gate**, that is a product decision rather than a drive-by fix. The two options fail differently:

- **Truncate with an explicit marker** (consistent with the sibling evidence channels that already carry byte budgets). The gate keeps voting, but on a fraction of the change. A wide epic — a lockfile refresh, generated-file churn, a large refactor — gets approved by a reviewer that never saw most of it. That failure is silent, and it is on the *merge* path.
- **Hold instead of deciding.** Over budget → park the epic with a deep-link notification, mirroring the existing "no MCP-capable eligible provider" case, which already holds rather than emitting a false rejection.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Planning pass — held in Backlog on one product decision, not on missing detail.**

The defect is well established: `lib/auto-mode/second-opinion.ts:393` computes `diff([\`${baseBranch}...HEAD\`, "-U3"])` with no bound, and `buildSecondOpinionPrompt` embeds all of it. Nothing between the two truncates, samples or measures.

What makes it unstartable as written is that the two candidate fixes have opposite failure modes, and this gate is the last thing standing between Full Auto and the base branch:

- **Cap it** with an explicit truncation marker. The gate then always votes, sometimes on a fraction of the change — a mandatory reviewer that reads 20 % of a lockfile-churn epic and approves is worse than no gate, because it manufactures evidence.
- **Hold instead of deciding blind.** Over the budget, the merge is parked with an explicit trace and a deep-link notification, the way the "no MCP-capable provider" case is already handled. Safe, but a wide-but-boring epic (a lockfile refresh, generated-file churn) now needs a human every time.

Project convention is explicit that this is not a drive-by call: *"changing what a gate reads is a product decision"*.

**Questions blocking it:**

1. Cap-and-vote, hold-and-park, or a hybrid (cap the diff, but *hold* when truncation actually fired)?
2. If capped — what budget, and is it shared with the other prompt sections or its own? The sibling channels already carry byte budgets; this one should derive from the same named constant family rather than inventing a number.
3. Should a truncated-and-approved second opinion be recorded distinctly on the session, so a later audit can tell a full read from a partial one?

My recommendation, for what it is worth: hybrid. Cap with the marker so the common case still runs, and park when the marker fired — that keeps the gate honest without demanding a human for every wide epic. Say the word and it can be promoted with that written into the criteria.

epics.title: Server listens on all interfaces while proxy.ts trusts a spoofable Host header: LAN peers can run commands
epics.description:
**Observed (2026-09-06, main @ 0484bdf)**

- `package.json` scripts run `next dev` / `next start` with no `-H`, and Next defaults to `0.0.0.0`. Live check: `ss -ltnp` shows `LISTEN *:3000 … next-server`.
- `proxy.ts:28-44` decides "local" purely from the `Host` header. Any non-browser client sets it freely (`curl -H 'Host: localhost' http://<lan-ip>:3000/api/...`). Browsers are correctly blocked (Origin check), so this is a LAN / VPN / port-forward exposure, not a web one.
- Every `/api/*` route is unauthenticated. Reachable consequences for a LAN peer:
  - `POST /api/settings/mcp-servers` with `command: "/bin/sh", args: ["-c", "<payload>"]`, then `POST /api/settings/mcp-servers/<id>/test` → `lib/mcp/probe.ts:209` spawns it via `StdioClientTransport` as the Arij user.
  - `PATCH /api/settings` accepts **any** key (`app/api/settings/route.ts:81-85` only type-checks a few known keys), so `verify_commands` (run with `shell: true`) or `global_prompt` (prepended to every agent prompt) can be set.
  - `POST .../build` dispatches agents with `bypassPermissions` into the user's repo; every ticket/spec/log is readable.

**Expected**
- Bind loopback by default (`next dev -H 127.0.0.1`, `next start -H 127.0.0.1` in `package.json` and `bin/arij.mjs`); make `-H 0.0.0.0` + `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` an explicit, documented opt-in.
- For the opt-in remote mode, add a real per-boot credential on `/api/*` (the proxy cannot see the peer address).
- Allowlist writable keys in `PATCH /api/settings`.

Found by the 2026-09-06 tech check (security section). Related: agent child processes inherit the full `process.env` (`lib/claude/spawn.ts:288`), so a prompt-injected agent can read every exported credential; `lib/mcp/probe.ts:212-215` already shows the stricter allowlist pattern.

`npm audit --audit-level=high` currently exits **1** (measured locally against the lockfile-consistent install): one high advisory, `browserslist <=4.28.6` (GHSA-c83g-rgw3-j3cx, GHSA-73wf-gq98-2v4g), pulled only through **dev** dependencies:

```
@vitejs/plugin-react → @babel/core → @babel/helper-compilation-targets → browserslist
shadcn → browserslist
```

So `npm test` is never reached on any push or PR; `verify` (tsc/lint/build) and `e2e` are separate jobs and still run, so the PR shows partial green. `__tests__/ci-workflow-gates.test.ts` does not pin the audit step, so nothing in the suite catches the ordering.

Note also that local `main` is 230 commits ahead of `origin/main` (last push 2026-08-31), and the last pushed commit's run shows `verify` failing at Lint and `e2e` failing at the Playwright step (logs expired). CI has effectively not gated the last six days of merges.

**Expected**
- Run `npm audit` after `npm test`, or in its own non-blocking job, or gate with `--audit-level=high --omit=dev` (what ships) plus a non-blocking full audit for visibility.
- Refresh the lockfile so `browserslist` resolves to the fixed 4.29.x (already within `^4.28.1`, no code change).
- Extend `ci-workflow-gates.test.ts` to pin that `npm test` is not preceded by a step that can fail on a dev-only advisory.

epics.title: claude-code cancel cannot escalate to SIGKILL (dead `!child.killed` guard) and never signals the process group
PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF inside rebuild migrations is a no-op under drizzle's transaction (latent cascade data loss)
epics.description:
**Observed (2026-09-06, main @ 0484bdf)**

Migrations `0003`, `0012`, `0029`, `0051` rebuild tables with the pattern `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF; CREATE __new…; INSERT … SELECT; DROP TABLE …; ALTER TABLE … RENAME`. Drizzle's sqlite migrator (`node_modules/drizzle-orm/sqlite-core/dialect.js:657-671`) runs `BEGIN` before executing the batch and `COMMIT` after. SQLite ignores `PRAGMA foreign_keys` while a transaction is open, and `lib/db/index.ts:60` sets `foreign_keys = ON` on the connection.

Reproduced with better-sqlite3 on a scratch DB (parent + child with `ON DELETE CASCADE`):

```
BEGIN; PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF; CREATE p2; INSERT p2 SELECT p; DROP TABLE p; RENAME; COMMIT
→ child rows after rebuild: 0   (cascade fired)
PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF set BEFORE BEGIN, same rebuild
→ child rows after rebuild: 1   (safe)
```

Nothing has been lost so far only because 0003/0012 are baseline-stamped on existing databases and 0029/0051 rebuilt tables nobody references. The next rebuild of a referenced parent — e.g. `agent_sessions`, the natural fix for the row-layout problem where `prompt` sits before 27 hot columns — would silently cascade-delete every `agent_session_chunks`, `agent_session_sequences` and `session_artifacts` row and NULL the `qa_reports` / `notifications` / `grading_reports` / `verify_reports` links (or abort on `ticket_comments.agent_session_id`, NO ACTION).

**Expected**
- In `lib/db/init.ts` `initDb()`: `connection.pragma("foreign_keys = OFF")` before `migrate()`, `ON` after, then `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` and throw on violations.
- Add a test that rebuilds a referenced parent through `initDb` and asserts child row counts survive.
- Correct the "following 0003, 0012 and 0029" guidance in migration comments.

Found by the 2026-09-06 tech check (database section).

- Install propre (`npm ci` — ce worktree n'avait aucun `node_modules`) ; `__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` vert.

`sourceFiles()` (`__tests__/helpers/class-list-scan.ts:622`) ne lit que `app`, `components`, `hooks` — jamais `__tests__`, donc les trois fichiers de test ajoutés sont hors du périmètre du scan. Les deux sites partagent la même constante : les corriger ensemble, sinon le scan reste rouge sur l'autre.

epics.title: Nothing reconciles qa_reports at boot, so stranded `running` rows stay stranded
epics.description:
Split out of the "stranded `running` QA report" epic, which fixed only the READER half. The write path is untouched and is filed here on purpose.

## The gap

`qa_reports.status` is moved off `running` in exactly one place: the tail of the scheduler closure in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/qa/check/route.ts:265`. Three ordinary paths skip that tail:

- a server restart mid-check — `failOrphanedRunningSessions()` fixes the `agent_sessions` row and never looks at `qa_reports`;
- a launch closure that rejects — `handleLaunchFailure` marks the session terminal, and the update after the `await` never runs;
- cancelling a still-queued check — `agentScheduler.remove()` splices the closure out, so nothing throws and nothing updates the report.

There is no `qa_reports` equivalent of `failOrphanedRunningSessions()`. `agent_sessions` is reconciled at boot; `qa_reports` is not.

## What the reader fix does and does not cover

The readers now derive liveness from the session (`isCheckLive` / `checkStatusLabel`, `lib/qa/aggregate.ts`), so a stranded row prints `interrupted` on both `/qa` and `/projects/:id/qa` and no longer drives a forever-poll. But the COLUMN still says `running`, so:

- every future consumer that reads `qa_reports.status` directly starts out wrong, and has to learn the two-column rule;
- rows already stranded in a user's database stay stranded on disk;
- `SUM(liveCheckSql())` and every derivation pay a LEFT JOIN on `agent_sessions` to answer a question the column should have answered.

This is the standing two-halves rule (write path vs existing backlog): the readers cover neither half of the DATA, only the display.

## What a fix looks like

A boot-time reconciliation beside `failOrphanedRunningSessions()`: move every `qa_reports` row that says `running` while its `agent_session_id` is NULL or points at a terminal session to a terminal status of its own. `interrupted` is currently a derived word with no stored value — either add it to the column's vocabulary (free-form TEXT, no migration needed for the value itself) or reuse `cancelled`/`failed`, but the choice must be made once and the readers' derivation kept as the fallback for rows written between reconciliations.

Two halves to state explicitly in the fix:

1. NEW writes — the boot hook, plus whatever the cancel path should do synchronously;
2. the EXISTING backlog — rows already stranded need the same sweep, and its row count should be measured on a real dev database rather than estimated.

Note that a report whose session died mid-run has no `report_content` — the same statement writes both — so a reconciliation must not claim `completed`.

## Evidence

Observed live on a scratch stack during the reader work: seeding a `running` session and restarting the dev server printed `[boot-cleanup] Failed 1 running session(s) orphaned by restart` and left the matching `qa_reports` row on `running`. That is the whole bug in one log line.

epics.title: The prompt-sweep VACUUM claim is spent on the first budgeted run too — the deferral was never merged
epics.description:
Found while implementing the chunk half (`ly6iuvd1bMSD`). **The chunk ticket's premise is stale**: it states that "the prompt half now defers its claim to the run that drains the backlog, carrying `retentionPromptsReclaimPendingAt` (`RETENTION_PROMPTS_RECLAIM_PENDING_AT_CONFIG_KEY`)". That constant does not exist anywhere in the repository. I grepped every local and remote ref:

```
for b in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads refs/remotes); do
  git grep -l "RECLAIM_PENDING" "$b" -- lib/routines/constants.ts; done
# -> no output
```

`c239284` (K_oThcxpS6sb, the prompt sweep) is on `main`, but review finding 1's fix for it is not — not on `main`, not on any branch. So the prompt half carries the identical defect today.

## What

`lib/routines/retention.ts`, in the claim block:

```ts
if (vacuumAllowed && !promptsAlreadyVacuumed && prompts.cappedPrompts > 0) {
  vacuumClaims.push(RETENTION_PROMPTS_VACUUMED_AT_CONFIG_KEY);
}
```

`prompts.reachedRowBudget` — the backfiller's own "over-cap rows left for the next run" signal (`lib/agent-sessions/prompt-backfill.ts:68`) — is read for the status message and nowhere else. Run 1 caps `maxCappedPrompts` rows (default 500), VACUUMs, and permanently records `retentionPromptsVacuumedAt`; runs 2..n cap the remainder and their freed pages sit on SQLite's free list for the life of the database.

## Severity is genuinely lower than the chunk half

The measured live-database prompt backlog is 38 rows / 27.0 MB against a 500-row budget, so it drains in a single run and strands nothing *on that database*. The defect only bites a project whose pre-cap backlog exceeds 500 rows. That is why it is low, not medium.

## The fix is now mechanical

`ly6iuvd1bMSD` landed the mechanism the prompt half needs:

- `writeConfigMarks(routineId, patch)` (was `claimVacuum`) already takes `Record<string, string | null>`, so a mark can be set by one run and cleared by another;
- `RETENTION_CHUNKS_RECLAIM_PENDING_AT_CONFIG_KEY` is the naming template, and `crud.ts`'s `INTERNAL_CONFIG_KEYS` is where the sibling key must be registered;
- `isoMark()` reads a durable ISO mark, treating an unparseable one as absent.

**And the prompt half needs no bound.** The chunk half is bounded at `RETENTION_RECLAIM_MAX_DEFERRAL_DAYS` = 7 only because sessions age past the retention window daily, so `reachedDeleteBudget` never means "done forever". Prompts are capped on the write path: that backlog drains once and never refills, so a plain "defer until `!reachedRowBudget`" is correct and terminates. Different trade, which is why this is a separate ticket rather than something I folded into the chunk diff.

## Reproduction shape

Mirror `__tests__/session-chunk-retention.test.ts` → "reclaims every batch's pages, not only the first run's": seed more over-cap prompt rows than `maxCappedPrompts`, run the routine to exhaustion through the real deps, read `PRAGMA freelist_count`. The chunk probe measured **398 pages stranded** before the fix and 0 after.

Deliberately not folded into `ly6iuvd1bMSD` — its diff carries a red→green proof (8 red at `0484bdf`, 31 green) that an unrelated second fix would have muddied.

epics.title: e2e : le composeur global de `/` vise projects[0] de tout l'espace de travail — course en fullyParallel
epics.description:
Observé pendant B-arij-OZUKyqpxmKaT, sur une exécution parallèle (`--workers=2`) de `desk-mobile-layout.spec.ts` + `chat-mobile-layout.spec.ts` + `desk-toasts.spec.ts` :

```
✘ e2e/desk-toasts.spec.ts:5 › global composer confirms a real creation and opens its ticket
  Locator: getByRole('status').filter({ hasText: 'Notification global -Qo0DtgpNspR' })
  Expected: visible — element(s) not found
```

**Ce n'est pas une régression du correctif** : le fichier passe seul (3/3), et la même combinaison parallèle est verte 3 fois de suite sur la branche corrigée et 1 fois sur l'arbre ramené à `2ab4558`. C'est une course.

Mécanisme : sur `/`, `NowDesk` passe `targetProjectId={composerProjectId ?? activeProjectId}` — les deux valent `null` hors d'un projet — et `DeskComposer` retombe alors sur `projects[0]`, c'est-à-dire le **premier projet de tout l'espace de travail**, pas celui que le spec a créé. La base e2e est partagée et `fullyParallel: true`, donc ce projet appartient couramment à un autre worker, dont le teardown le supprime en vol : le POST échoue, le toast rendu est un `role="alert"` et le `getByRole("status")` attendu n'apparaît jamais.

C'est la forme exacte du piège « une assertion e2e indexée sur un état global est une course par construction ». Le spec ne peut pas vérifier que le ticket a atterri dans **son** projet non plus : la ligne suivante interroge `epics WHERE project_id = ?` avec l'id du fixture, ce qui est vrai par chance tant que le projet du fixture est premier.

Piste : soit le spec sélectionne explicitement son projet dans la pilule projet du composeur avant de taper (le contrôle réel existe), soit le cas « global » n'assère que sur des propriétés qui ne dépendent pas du projet visé. À décider en lisant `e2e/desk-toasts.spec.ts:5-27`.

epics.title: Le popover @doc de l'éditeur de spec est rogné par l'overflow de sa carte, pas par le viewport
epics.description:
Constaté pendant B-arij-181, **antérieur à ce correctif** : mesuré identique sur la merge-base `f4c5ab5` et sur la branche corrigée.

## Symptôme

Sur `/projects/:id/spec`, la liste de suggestions `@` de `MentionTextarea` est bien dans le viewport, mais un ancêtre en `overflow` la coupe : seuls ~57 px des ~190 px de la liste sont peints. C'est un défaut différent de celui de B-arij-181 (débordement *du viewport*), dans un autre composant.

## Mesures (Chrome via Playwright, `next dev`, projet de test avec 18 documents, 8 suggestions affichées)

Hauteur peinte = intersection du rect du popover avec chaque ancêtre clippant.

| Build | Viewport | rect | hauteur | bas du clip | **visible** | caché par l'ancêtre |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| merge-base f4c5ab5 | 1440 × 1000 | 809.8 → 1003.8 | 194 | 866.8 | **57** | 137 |
| merge-base f4c5ab5 | 1280 × 420 | 229.8 → 423.8 | 194 | 866.8 → 286.8 | **57** | 137 |
| branche B-arij-181 | 1440 × 1000 | 809.8 → 1000 | 190.3 | 866.8 | **57** | 133.3 |
| branche B-arij-181 | 1280 × 420 | 229.8 → 420 | 190.3 | 286.8 | **57** | 133.3 |

Le correctif de B-arij-181 a supprimé le débordement du viewport (le bas passe de 1003.8 à 1000), mais **la hauteur visible ne bouge pas** : le rognage vient de la carte SPEC, pas de la fenêtre.

## Cause

`components/spec/SpecEditor.tsx` monte `MentionTextarea` dans une colonne flex scrollante (`flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col [&>div]:min-h-0`), à l'intérieur d'une carte qui clippe en `overflow-y`. Le popover est `position: absolute` dans le wrapper `relative` de `MentionTextarea` : il est donc rogné par le premier ancêtre scrollant, quelle que soit la place dans la fenêtre.

## Reproduction

1. Un projet avec au moins 4 documents texte (pour dépasser la hauteur visible).
2. Ouvrir `/projects/:id/spec`, onglet **Écrire**.
3. Taper `@` en début de document.
4. La liste est coupée net au bas de la carte SPEC ; la carte ne défile pas pour la rattraper.

## Piste

Le placement fenêtré ne suffit pas ici : il faut sortir le popover du flux clippé — portail (`createPortal` vers `document.body`) avec positionnement fixe calculé sur le rect de l'ancre, ou `position: fixed` sur le popover. `lib/documents/mention-placement.ts` (livré par B-arij-181) donne déjà la décision de côté et le plafond de hauteur ; seul le conteneur de rendu change.

Vérifier au passage les autres montages dans un ancêtre scrollant : `components/story/CommentThread.tsx` et `components/shared/SendToDevDialog.tsx` (non mesurés — l'overlay de ticket n'a pas exposé son champ commentaire pendant la sonde).

Aucune modification de source faite pour ce constat ; serveur de test arrêté, arbre Git propre.

epics.title: Cancelling a QA check finalises the session but not its qa_reports row, so the readers settle on `interrupted` for a check that ends `cancelled`
epics.description:
Adjacent to c0qg9nFMKc_M (the stranded-`running` readers fix) and to B-arij-253 (boot reconciliation of `qa_reports`). Same class — a path that ends the session without touching the report row — but a different path, and one that also bites a check that is NOT stranded.

## Mechanism

`DELETE /api/projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts:452-458`) does `agentScheduler.remove()`, `processManager.cancel()`, then `markSessionCancelled()` — the SESSION row goes terminal immediately. `lib/projects/cancel-sessions.ts` does the same three writes on project deletion. Neither touches `qa_reports`.

The only writer of `qa_reports.status` is the tail of the scheduler closure in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/qa/check/route.ts`, which only runs once `waitForProcessCompletion(sessionId, POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000)` returns. Two consequences:

1. **Cancel while running — a ≤2 s window.** For up to one 2 s poll tick the session reads `cancelled` while the report still reads `running`. Both readers on `/projects/:id/qa` (`hooks/useQaReports.ts`, `components/qa/ReportDetail.tsx`) derive liveness from the session via `isCheckLive`, so a history poll landing in that window stops BOTH polls and draws the report `interrupted` with no content. The closure then finalises the row as `cancelled` with whatever partial output `resolveSessionOutput` returns — and nothing reads it again until the page is reloaded. The word is not false (`interrupted` is the honest reading of two disagreeing columns), but it is not the row's word either, and the partial body never appears.

2. **Cancel while queued — stranded for good.** `agentScheduler.remove()` splices the closure out, so the tail never runs and the row stays `running` forever (this is one of the three strand paths the parent ticket names). The readers print `interrupted`; the row never says `cancelled`.

## Fix sketch (write path, not readers)

Move the matching `qa_reports` row to `cancelled` in the same place the session is cancelled — the DELETE route and `cancelProjectSessions` — keyed on `qa_reports.agent_session_id = sessionId AND status = 'running'`, with `completed_at` set. That closes both consequences with one write and makes the closure's later update a no-op (it already guards nothing; it should then only write when the row is still `running`, or it will overwrite `cancelled` with `cancelled` plus the partial output — decide which body wins).

A reader-side alternative (a bounded settle loop after the live → terminal edge in both pollers) was considered and rejected inside c0qg9nFMKc_M: it re-introduces a poll after every transition for a ≤2 s server-side ordering that the write path can simply remove.

## Repro

Seed a `running` `qa_reports` row behind a `running` session, open `/projects/:id/qa`, cancel the session through the DELETE route, and watch the history and the pane: with a poll landing inside the window they read `interrupted` and stay there; the row reads `cancelled` in SQLite. Cancelling a still-queued check leaves the row `running` in SQLite indefinitely.

epics.title: useConversations reports a failed conversations fetch as an empty project, so the chat strip creates a duplicate Brainstorm after a network error
epics.description:
Adjacent to g1QITi0PPFOq (fast open duplicates the Brainstorm), found while fixing it. **Deduced from code, not measured.**

## What happens

`hooks/useConversations.ts` swallows fetch errors: both the mount fetch (`.catch(() => {})` then `.finally(() => setLoading(false))`) and `refresh()` leave `loading = false` and `conversations = []` after a failed `GET /api/projects/{id}/conversations`. That state is byte-identical to a settled, genuinely empty project.

`openChatConversation()` in `components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx` now gates on `loading` (the g1QITi0PPFOq fix), but once loading is false it still takes the create branch on an empty list. So: transient network failure on the mount GET → user clicks `collapsed-chat-strip` → `POST /conversations` → a second "Brainstorm" next to the one the server auto-creates on every GET (a healthy project never has zero). The 3 s poll then brings both back. Same durable-duplicate class as g1QITi0PPFOq, different trigger (failure window instead of in-flight window).

## Reproduction (expected)

1. Fresh project; let one GET run so the server holds its one Brainstorm.
2. Block `GET /api/projects/{id}/conversations` (devtools offline, or `route.abort()`), load `/projects/{id}`, wait for the failed GET to settle.
3. Unblock the network, click the chat strip.
4. `GET /api/projects/{id}/conversations` → 2 rows labelled "Brainstorm".

## Suggested shape

Expose a `failed`/`settled` flag from the hook (or an `error`), and have the panel create only after a *successful* empty fetch — on the current server that branch is effectively dead, so it could equally just refuse and offer a retry. A deferred create after loading was deliberately not added in g1QITi0PPFOq because this failure path is the only case it would fire on.

epics.title: Regression gate copies `__tests__/helpers/*` onto the merge-base, so a fix to a test helper can never show red
epics.description:
Found while closing pJ7Gf8eAh7QO (the focus-ring colour sweep), whose fix lives in `__tests__/helpers/tailwind-outline.ts`.

## What happens

`lib/verify/regression-check.ts` selects "test files" from the branch diff with `DEFAULT_TEST_FILE_PATTERNS` (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/__tests__/**`) and copies every match onto a detached merge-base worktree for the red run. `**/__tests__/**` matches every file under `__tests__/`, helpers and fixtures included (`__tests__/helpers/tailwind-outline.ts`, `class-list-scan.ts`, `db-mock.ts`, `mock-fetch.ts`, …).

So when the defect being fixed is *in* a test helper — a scanner that loses sites (B-arij-206), a resolver that cannot see a colour (pJ7Gf8eAh7QO) — the fix is copied onto the merge-base together with the tests, the red run is green, and the gate reports `test_passes_on_base` for a correct red→green diff. Fixes to test infrastructure are exactly the class of bug the focus-ring epic produced three times.

## Reproduction

Deduced from the code path, not observed under the gate: in this project `bug_regression_check` is unset (default off) and only `bug_regression_command` (`npm test -- {files}`) is configured.

1. A branch changes `__tests__/helpers/<x>.ts` and a test under `__tests__/` that fails without that change.
2. `runRegressionCheck` → `testFiles` includes the helper (it matches `**/__tests__/**`).
3. The red worktree receives the helper at the branch's blob → the tests pass → `test_passes_on_base`.

Proven by hand for pJ7Gf8eAh7QO instead: with the merge-base helper on disk the five test files fail 105/125; with the branch helper they pass 125/125.

## Expected

Either treat only files matching a test-file *name* pattern (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) as the tests to carry over, keeping everything else in the diff — helpers included — at the merge-base; or let the pattern list distinguish "select" (which files prove a test exists) from "copy" (which files the red worktree receives). Either way, the settings UI and the bug-fix prompt should say which files the red run copies, so a session working on test infrastructure knows the mechanical gate cannot judge it and proves red by hand.

epics.title: NamedAgentSelect reports an empty change when a preselected agent's list loads inside a <form>
Ticket overlay still walks the whole session list when the ticket has no session yet
epics.description:
## What remains after iV8mOCjlrxAM

`hooks/useTicketOverlayData.ts` answers one question from `GET /api/projects/:projectId/sessions`: "what is the newest agent session of this ticket?" Since iV8mOCjlrxAM it reads the list through `findUnifiedSession` (`lib/agent-sessions/session-list.ts`), which stops at the page holding the first match, and aborts the walk when the overlay closes or the ticket changes.

What the client cannot shorten is **"no match"**: a ticket that has never had a session can only be known to have none once the last page has been read. So opening a fresh ticket on a project with a long session history still costs one round trip per page.

## Measured

Chrome via Playwright against `next start` (production build — `next dev` double-invokes the effect under Strict Mode and would double every count), `/tickets` registry (mounts the overlay without the desk's own session poll), scratch project with 733 sessions = 4 pages at the default page size of 200. Requests to the list route per overlay open:

| newest session of the opened ticket is… | before iV8mOCjlrxAM | after |
|---|---|---|
| on page 1 | 4 | 1 |
| on page 2 | 4 | 2 |
| nowhere (no session yet) | 4 | **4** |

## Proposal (route contract change — the reason it was not folded into iV8mOCjlrxAM)

Add an optional `?epicId=` filter to the sessions list route, applied to both streams it merges (`agent_sessions.epic_id` and `chat_conversations.epic_id`), keeping the keyset cursor and the newest-first order unchanged. With `?epicId=<id>&limit=1` the overlay's lookup becomes one request in every case, including "no session yet".

Points to pin when doing it:
- the filter narrows the row set without changing the sort key, so `nextCursor` semantics hold — needs a route test with the epic's rows spread over several pages;
- the response without the parameter must stay byte-identical (existing `__tests__/sessions-list-*.test.ts` unchanged and green);
- an epicId with no rows returns `{ data: [], nextCursor: null }` (200) so a client reads "no session yet" in one request;
- `useTicketOverlayData` then passes `epicId` and `limit: 1`, still skipping `chat_session` rows; `__tests__/ticket-overlay-session-paging.test.tsx` gets a "no session yet costs one request" case while its early-exit and abort assertions stay green.

Out of scope: `useAgentPolling`'s failure badges and the Sessions page genuinely need the whole list and keep `fetchUnifiedSessions`.

epics.title: React Compiler still declines 34 functions recorded in KNOWN_BAILED — opening each surfaces 44 real violations
epics.description:
Follow-up to 9niAS9OwiaOJ (React Compiler bails with no diagnostic). That sweep opened 30 of the 48 components the ticket listed and turned the guard into an app-wide coverage test, `__tests__/react-compiler-coverage.test.ts`. It also left a ledger: `KNOWN_BAILED` in that test holds **34 functions** (26 components/pages, 8 hooks) the compiler's lint rules still never read, each with the construct it stops on in the compiler's own words.

## Why they were recorded rather than rewritten

Every one of them stops on a `finally` clause, a `throw` inside `try/catch`, a `try` without `catch`, or an `eslint-disable` of `exhaustive-deps`. Rewriting the construct is mechanical — but it was measured (by linting an in-memory copy with the construct neutralised) that the moment each function is read again, the compiler reports what the silence was hiding: **44 real violations** — 37 `set-state-in-effect`, 6 `refs`, 1 `immutability`. Rewriting the construct without fixing what it uncovers turns a silent function into a red `npm run lint`, so the two are one change per function, and that is real per-component work with behaviour risk (mostly load-in-effect hooks that set `loading` synchronously inside the effect), not a mechanical sweep.

## The ledger (as of tip b84df51)

`app/`: `projects/[projectId]/documents/page#DocumentsPage`, `frictions/page#ProjectFrictionsPage`, `git-sync/page#GitSyncPage`, `github-issues/page#GitHubIssuesPage`, `layout#ProjectLayout`, `spec/page#SpecPage`.

`components/`: `auto-mode/AutoModeDialog`, `chat-page/ChatPageView#ChatWorkspace`, `documents/ScanProjectDialog`, `github/GitHubConnectBanner`, `kanban/EpicCreateDialog`, `night/NightRunDialog`, `qa/ReportDetail`, `qa/StartQaCheckDialog`, `routines/RoutinesSettings#RoutineEditor`, `routines/RoutinesSettings#RoutinesSettings`, `session-live/useSessionFiles`, `session-live/useSessionStreamPager`, `sessions/SessionOutputStream`, `settings/McpServersSection`, `shared/AgentActionsBar`, `spec/MemoryPanel`.

`hooks/`: `useChat`, `useDiff`, `useEpicDependencies`, `useEpicPr`, `useGitHubConfig`, `useGitStatus`, `useKanban`, `useProjects`, `useQaReports`, `useReviewComments`, `useUsage`, `useWorktrees`.

The exact construct and the violations behind each entry are the reason strings in `KNOWN_BAILED`.

## How to work one

1. Rewrite the construct with one of the shapes used in 9niAS9OwiaOJ: a trailing reset after the `try/catch` when no `return` remains inside it (check with an AST walk, not by eye); otherwise `await inner().finally(...)` with `inner` an `async` function; hoist a `throw` out of the component into a module function.
2. Run `npx eslint <file>` — the hidden violations now report. Fix them (a `loading` set synchronously in an effect usually becomes a render-time adjust keyed on the id, or initial state).
3. Delete the entry from `KNOWN_BAILED`; the coverage test fails until you do, on purpose.

## Mechanism, for whoever picks this up

The plugin compiles each function through `lower()` (BuildHIR) → validations (`refs`, `set-state-in-render`, derived-state, `set-state-in-effect`) → `buildReactiveFunction`. A `todo` raised while lowering, or a rule suppression, comes before the validations and silences them all; a `todo` raised in `buildReactiveFunction` (a `??`/`?.`/ternary inside `try/catch`) comes after, so the rules still report and only the optimisation is lost. `npm run lint` now shows both kinds as `react-hooks/todo` warnings (114 on the tip: 49 `finally`, 12 `throw`, 2 `try` without `catch`, 51 value blocks); only the first three kinds are bails.

`next.config.ts` does not enable `reactCompiler` today, so the cost is lint coverage. The day it is switched on, every entry here is also a component the compiler will not optimise.

epics.title: Verify reports are fetched by useEpicDetail but never rendered: the ticket overlay's data hook drops them
epics.description:
Found while re-measuring the stored specification for E-arij-246 (story etGOeA6iOvJL), on `main` 77b0039.

**What is on main**
- `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts` serves the newest `verify_reports` row and re-runs the commands on POST.
- `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts` fetches that route (`fetchVerification`, guarded by a request sequence) and returns the parsed report in its result.
- `hooks/useTicketOverlayData.ts` destructures `epic, userStories, loading, updateEpic, refresh, setPolling, gradingReport` from `useEpicDetail` and does not take the verification state.
- `git grep -i verification -- components/ticket components/story hooks/useTicketOverlayData.ts` finds nothing. The only UI mention of verification is `components/settings-piscine/VerificationBand.tsx` (the settings form).
- `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` still says the report is read by "the EpicDetail panel"; that panel was removed by the Piscine redesign, and `components/ticket/TicketOverlay.tsx` never picked the report up.

**Effect**
A user who configures `verify_commands` gets a persisted pass/fail report per code stage, a `ticket:updated` event carrying `verifyReportId`/`verifyStatus`, and a merge gate that acts on it, but no surface shows the report, the failing command, or its output tail. The old ticket text of E-arij-246 called the "ticket-detail verification reports" part of the merged feature; the spec now says plainly that no component renders one (1.2 and 8).

**Expected**
The ticket overlay shows the newest verify report for the epic (status, per-command name / exit code / duration / tail), refreshes on the `verifyStatus` ticket event, and offers the manual re-run the route already supports. The fetch in `useEpicDetail` is already there; the gap is between the overlay hook and a component.

epics.title: Stored spec still describes a Kanban board with drag-and-drop columns (5.2), and the 4 stack table has garbled rows
epics.description:
Left over after the spec correction done for E-arij-246 (story etGOeA6iOvJL), which was scoped to 1.2, 8 and the verify-stage mentions. The `to_merge` status is not mentioned in 5.2 at all.

epics.title: Agents composites : listes ordonnées de repli à la place de l'escalade
epics.description:
## Contexte

Aujourd'hui trois mécanismes distincts choisissent ou re-choisissent un agent, et ils ne se parlent pas :

1. `named_agents.escalates_to` (`lib/db/schema.ts:517`, migration `0039_named_agent_escalation`) est une chaîne de repli d'agent nommé, mais elle refuse tout changement de provider (`readEffortEscalationTarget()`, `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:530-562`) et ne se déclenche qu'à la tentative 3 — or `DEFAULT_PIPELINE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:60`). Sans relever `pipeline_max_attempts`, cette escalade n'est jamais atteinte : le mécanisme est de fait mort par défaut.
2. `pickAlternativeReviewProvider()` (`lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts:129-149`) parcourt la liste ordonnée en dur `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (`lib/agent-config/constants.ts:232-241`) pour l'escalade des tentatives 3/4+ (`stages.ts:781-796`) — mais au grain *provider*, et elle jette l'agent nommé (`namedAgentId: null`, modèle par défaut du CLI).
3. Le smart dispatch (`lib/agent-config/smart-dispatch.ts`) choisit par fiabilité mesurée, mais uniquement en Full Auto et opt-in.

Décision produit : modèle binaire. Soit on choisit un agent spécifique et on s'y tient, soit on utilise un agent composite — une liste ordonnée d'agents nommés, dont on peut créer autant qu'on veut. L'existant (1) et (2, en tant qu'escaladeur) est retiré.

## Plan d'implémentation

### Schéma

Un composite est une ligne de `named_agents` portant `kind = 'composite'`, pas une table séparée. C'est la décision structurante : `agent_provider_defaults.named_agent_id` (les 21 `AGENT_TYPES`, scope global et projet), `chat_conversations.named_agent_id`, `qa_reports.named_agent_id`, `agent_sessions.named_agent_id` et les deux sélecteurs (`AgentSelectPill`, `NamedAgentSelect`) pointent déjà vers `named_agents.id` — un composite devient donc assignable partout sans toucher une seule FK. Une table `composite_agents` séparée obligerait à unir deux types dans chaque FK et chaque picker.

- `named_agents.kind` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT `'simple'` (`'simple' | 'composite'`).
- Nouvelle table `composite_agent_members` : `composite_id` (FK → `named_agents.id` ON DELETE CASCADE), `member_id` (FK → `named_agents.id` ON DELETE CASCADE), `position` INTEGER, index unique `(composite_id, position)` et `(composite_id, member_id)`.
- Pas d'imbrication : un membre doit être `kind = 'simple'`. Refusé à l'écriture, ce qui évite de réintroduire une détection de cycle.
- Un composite n'a ni `provider` ni `model` propres : les colonnes existantes sont neutralisées pour lui (valeur sentinelle documentée), la validation d'écriture les ignore.
- `agent_sessions.composite_agent_id` (nullable) : le composite qui a dispatché. `agent_sessions.named_agent_id` continue d'enregistrer le membre qui a réellement tourné, sinon `getNamedAgentDispatchReliability()` (`lib/agent-config/stats.ts:208`) regroupe tout sur le composite et les statistiques de fiabilité perdent leur sens.
- Migrations écrites à la main : fichier numéroté sous `lib/db/migrations/` + entrée dans `meta/_journal.json` avec un `when` strictement supérieur au dernier appliqué. `npx drizzle-kit generate` est interdit (snapshots figés à 0013). Vérifier le numéro le plus haut contre le tip de `main` juste avant le merge — plusieurs branches ajoutent « le prochain » numéro en parallèle.

### Démolition

- Retrait de la colonne `named_agents.escalates_to` (migration de suppression), de `validateEscalationTarget()` (`lib/agent-config/named-agents.ts:105-140`), du contrôle `escalatesTo` dans `components/agents-workshop/AgentIdentityCard.tsx`, de `readEffortEscalationTarget()` et du compteur d'escalades dans `getNamedAgentStats()` (`lib/agent-config/agent-stats.ts`).
- Retrait des deux branches de bascule d'agent de `resolveStageAgent()` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:760-796`) et de la trace `PIPELINE_REASONS.effortEscalation` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:203-206`).
- Piège à ne pas rater : la branche « autre provider » appelle `pickAlternativeReviewProvider()`, mais cette fonction sert *aussi* à la ségrégation de review (reviewer ≠ builder, `lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts:129-149`), qui reste voulue. On retire l'appel comme escaladeur, pas la fonction.

### Résolution et échelle

- `resolveAgentByNamedId()` / `resolveAgentForDispatch()` (`lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:397-515`) déplient un composite en un membre pour un rang donné.
- Échelle du runner : agent simple → on retente le *même* agent (reprise de session en tentative 2 via `previousAttemptSessionId`, puis à neuf), jamais de bascule. Composite → chaque tentative descend d'un rang ; la longueur de la liste devient le budget de tentatives, ce qui retire `pipeline_max_attempts` comme verrou d'escalade. `PIPELINE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN = 12` reste le garde-fou global.
- Ce qui fait descendre d'un rang : `status: failed`, `transition_refused`, et `silent`. Ce qui ne fait pas descendre : un verdict de review négatif et un échec de la porte de régression ou de la vérification déterministe — ce sont des cycles de fix, avec leur propre budget (`maxFixCycles`) ; les confondre consommerait la liste d'agents pour un désaccord de review. `asked_question` et `cancelled` restent terminaux : si l'agent pose une question, on attend l'utilisateur.

### Hors périmètre (tickets de suivi à filer)

- Le sort du smart dispatch : c'est un troisième chemin de choix automatique qui contredit le modèle binaire ; le convertir en « stratégie d'ordre » d'un composite (ordre manuel vs par fiabilité) est une idée à part entière.
- Le plafond de concurrence par agent nommé : la limite est globale (une colonne sur `named_agents`, valable partout, y compris hors composite), donc elle n'a plus rien à voir avec les composites. C'est un changement d'ordonnanceur (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts`, qui ne compte aujourd'hui qu'un `Set` de sessions par projet sans savoir quel agent tient chaque slot), avec sa propre question de blocage de tête de file (position retenue : admission dans le désordre) et un paramètre à propager sur la vingtaine d'appelants de `agentScheduler.submit()`. Epic distincte.

epics.title: formatRelative tops out at days, so old stamps read "400d ago" instead of "1y ago"
epics.description:
Found while landing E-arij-155 (English-only interface on a localization substrate). Not a regression introduced by that epic in the strict sense — it is a consequence of its own consolidation — but it changes rendered text on every screen that stamps an age, so it should be a deliberate decision rather than a side effect.

## What happens

`lib/i18n/format.ts:formatRelative` has four bands: seconds → minutes → hours → days. There is no month or year band, so the day count simply keeps growing.

Measured (probe run against the real module, then deleted):

```
45 days  → "45d ago"    (fr: "il y a 45 j")
400 days → "400d ago"
```

## Why it changed

Story 2 of E-arij-155 collapsed six duplicated relative-time helpers into this one family. One of them, `relativeFromNow` in `components/agents-workshop/EditorFooterBar.tsx`, had month and year bands and rendered `1mo ago` / `2y ago`. Deleting it was correct — the whole point of the epic is that a second language must not clone formatting logic — but the shared family it was folded into does not have those bands, so those surfaces now print a raw day count.

The four-band spelling is deliberate: the Piscine frames are drawn with `5m ago` / `3h ago` / `2d ago`, and `Format.relativeStyle` is catalogue data precisely so English `narrow` produces exactly that. Nobody chose "400d ago" though — it is what falls out at the end of the last band.

## Why it was not fixed in the epic

Adding month/year bands changes rendered text on 20+ screens that read `formatRelative` (the desk strata, the tickets registry, session lists, the spec footer, the chat roster). Story 4's acceptance criterion is that rendered English is byte-identical, so widening the bands inside that story would have broken the very property the story is verified against. It is a frame-level typography decision, not a sweep.

## Suggested fix

Add `month` and `year` bands to `formatRelative`, keeping the mono-grid rewrite (`onMonoGrid`) and reading the style from `Format.relativeStyle` as today, so both locales follow. Then check the affected stamps in a browser — English `narrow` gives `2mo ago` / `1y ago`, French `short` gives `il y a 2 mois` / `il y a 1 an`, and both need to sit on the same grid the current bands do.

`__tests__/i18n-format.test.ts` is where the band boundaries are pinned; new cases belong there.

epics.title: NamedAgentSelect renders uncontrolled on first paint when the caller passes a null value without allowClear
epics.description:
## What

`components/shared/NamedAgentSelect.tsx:112` resolves the Radix `Select`'s value as:

```tsx
value={value ?? (allowClear ? NO_AGENT_VALUE : undefined)}
```

The prop is typed `value: string | null`. When a caller passes `null` **and does not set `allowClear`**, the expression yields `undefined`, so the `Select` mounts *uncontrolled* and flips to *controlled* the moment the user picks an agent. React warns once per component, and an interaction made in the gap is silently lost.

## Reachability

Of the four call sites, only `components/kanban/RefinementDialog.tsx` sets `allowClear`. The others pass a caller-owned value with no clear affordance:

- `components/shared/AgentDispatchDialog.tsx:99` — `value={agentProps.value}`
- `components/night/NightRunDialog.tsx:388`
- `components/releases/ChangelogAgentPopover.tsx:68`

Any of those that starts its state at `null` mounts uncontrolled.

## Provenance — this is pre-existing, not a composite-agents regression

Verified identical on `main` at 77b0039:

```
$ git show main:components/shared/NamedAgentSelect.tsx | grep -n "value={value"
112:      value={value ?? (allowClear ? NO_AGENT_VALUE : undefined)}
```

Found while auditing the composite-agents epic (E-BwEtdU8xBcbs), whose workshop story asks that the pickers start from a defined value. That story's criterion is about the flip caused by the *fetched agent list* arriving — `AgentSelectPill` is clean there (`checkedValue()` always returns a defined string, defaulting to `DEFAULT_AGENT_VALUE`). This one is a different trigger: caller state, not the fetch. It was deliberately left out of that epic's diff rather than absorbed.

## Suggested fix

Give the control a defined sentinel from the first render regardless of `allowClear` — the `NO_AGENT_VALUE` row can stay hidden when `allowClear` is false while the value stays defined — and sweep the three call sites for a `null` initial state.

## Testing note

The project has established that the real Radix `Select` renders in jsdom and that React's controlled/uncontrolled warning is observable by spying on `console.error`, so this is unit-testable without mocking the primitive. Mount the control **outside** a `<form>`: Radix renders a hidden native input for form participation whose events bubble and can fire the form's handlers.

epics.title: The full en message tree is serialized into every page's flight payload (~98 KB raw, ~67% of /)
epics.description:
Carved out of E-arij-155 review finding `_0CSG2dr1HU9`, whose anchored half (the double-catalogue *static import* in `lib/i18n/format.ts`) was fixed in `bdffec91` and is now pinned by `__tests__/i18n-client-catalogue-graph.test.ts`. This is the second half, which that fix explicitly and honestly left alone ("The provider's resolved message payload remains"). Filing it so it is not lost.

## Measured at `bdffec91` (production build, `next start` on port 3417)

- `lib/i18n/messages/en/*.json` serialised compactly: **97,852 bytes**, 46 namespaces, 2,180 keys.
- `GET /` HTML: **145,752 bytes**. `/tickets` 155,973 · `/chat` 148,040 · `/agents` 136,487.
- The whole tree is in `/`'s payload regardless of what `/` renders. Markers found in `/`'s HTML, one occurrence each:
  - `Bypass permissions` (`ProviderOptions`, an `/agents` string) at byte offset 86,225
  - `Acceptance criteria`, `Failed to create epic`, `No direct transition from`
- The client *chunks* are now correctly small — the only catalogue JSON reaching them is `en+fr/Format.json` and `en/ProviderOptions.json` (the two carrier chunks are 30,655 and 15,429 bytes). The 115,448-byte both-catalogues chunk cycle 1 measured is gone.

## Cause

`NextIntlClientProvider` in `app/layout.tsx:84` is given no `messages` prop, so it resolves to next-intl's server variant, which awaits `getMessages()` and serialises the entire resolved tree into the flight payload of every route.

## Why it is low, not blocking

Arij is a localhost single-user app (spec §3.1), so this is parse/eval cost on loopback, not transfer. It matters because it is a property of the **substrate**, and it grows by one full catalogue per locale the follow-up "French locale + language switcher" epic adds.

## Suggested direction

Pass an explicit `messages` prop scoped to the namespaces a route actually needs (next-intl supports partial message trees with `pick`), or move the provider off the root layout for the routes that need only a handful of namespaces. Either way, add a payload-size assertion so a later widening cannot re-land silently — the existing import-graph test guards the static-import axis only, not the serialised-payload axis.

epics.title: Composite-agents branch owes 110 i18n extractions after main merged E-arij-155
epics.description:
## What

`main` advanced from `77b0039` to `7a5ec7be` while E-BwEtdU8xBcbs (composite agents) was in review, merging E-arij-155 (English-only interface on a localization substrate). That epic enabled `i18n/no-bare-jsx-copy` at **error** severity for `components/**/*.tsx` and `app/**/*.tsx` (`eslint.config.mjs:32-39` on `7a5ec7be`), and extracted every existing string into the catalogue.

The composite-agents branch was written against the pre-i18n `main` and carries bare English copy. Merging it as-is lands a **red lint** on the default branch.

## Measured, not estimated

Ran main's own rule (`eslint-rules/no-bare-jsx-copy.mjs` @ `7a5ec7be`, with main's exact `allowPattern`) against the branch's 13 changed component files:

| count | file |
|---|---|
| 24 | `components/session-live/SessionInfoCard.tsx` |
| 16 | `components/agents-workshop/CompositeMembersBand.tsx` |
| 15 | `components/agents-workshop/AddAgentCard.tsx` |
| 9 | `components/agents-workshop/AgentRosterCard.tsx` |
| 8 | `components/agents-workshop/CompositeIdentityCard.tsx` |
| 8 | `components/agents-workshop/TheNumbersBand.tsx` |
| 8 | `components/shared/AgentSelectPill.tsx` |
| 7 | `components/agents-workshop/AgentIdentityCard.tsx` |
| 6 | `components/agents-workshop/WhereHeWorksBand.tsx` |
| 5 | `components/shared/NamedAgentSelect.tsx` |
| 3 | `components/agents-workshop/AssignmentsView.tsx` |
| 1 | `components/agents-workshop/AgentsWorkshopView.tsx` |
| **110** | **TOTAL** |

**The same rule against `main`'s versions of those 11 files: 0 violations** (exit 0). So the extraction is complete on `main`, and 110 is purely this branch's debt.

Lower bound on what survives a merge: the **24** in the two files `main` has no version of at all (`CompositeIdentityCard.tsx`, `CompositeMembersBand.tsx`) — those are 100% ours. Upper bound 110; for the 11 modified files, `main`'s extracted text wins on lines we did not touch, so the true figure sits between.

## Merge conflicts, separately

`git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD 7a5ec7be` reports **8 conflicting files**, all UI:
`AddAgentCard.tsx`, `AgentIdentityCard.tsx`, `AgentRosterCard.tsx`, `AssignmentsView.tsx`, `TheNumbersBand.tsx`, `WhereHeWorksBand.tsx`, `SessionInfoCard.tsx`, `AgentSelectPill.tsx`.
(`AgentsWorkshopView.tsx`, `agent-initials.ts`, `NamedAgentSelect.tsx`, `hooks/useAgentConfig.ts` auto-merge.)

## Not a defect in either epic

Neither branch is wrong; they are two epics that touched the same 10 files in parallel. Filed as a distinct integration task rather than absorbed into the composite-agents diff, because i18n-ifying the new workshop surface is E-arij-155's contract, and folding it in would change what the composite review actually reviewed.

## Also worth noting

`i18n-key-coverage.test.ts` and the other 11 `i18n-*` guard tests on `main` were **not** run against the merged result — only the rule was. Expect additional catalogue-coverage work beyond the 110 lint errors.

## Reconciliation expiry

Measured against `main` at `7a5ec7be`. Migration numbering is currently clean (main added **zero** migrations; it still tops out at `0052_refinement_actions`, idx 51, so the branch's `0053`/`0054`/`0055` do not collide). **Both** claims expire as `main` advances.

epics.title: 16 placeholder-only text controls remain across app/ and components/
epics.description:
Sized while closing M-6h-z3vvxVm, which fixed the single site it named (`StartQaCheckDialog`'s "Prompt name for reuse" input) and asked for the wider population to be measured. This ticket carries the remainder.

## Defect class

A text control whose only accessible name is its `placeholder`. A placeholder is a **last-resort fallback** in the accessible-name spec, some screen readers do not announce it, and it fails the name-from-author expectation for a form control. It is a distinct class from vhFDZvDCY161's (`<label>` present but with no `htmlFor`) — these sites have no `<label>` at all, so a label-enumerating sweep cannot see them.

## Measurement

Measured on `main` at `2a7808b4` **after** M-6h-z3vvxVm's fix, by walking the TypeScript AST (not grep — template-literal props and the slash of a self-closing tag both defeat a regex scanner here).

- 290 `.tsx` files scanned
- 88 text controls (`input`, `textarea`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `GhostInputPill`)
- 48 carry a `placeholder`
- **16 are placeholder-only** — no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`, no wrapping `<label>`, no `id` with a matching `htmlFor`

Scanner control: run against the pre-fix tree it reported 17 and named `StartQaCheckDialog.tsx`; post-fix it reports 16 and does not. Four sites were additionally hand-checked against source and all four confirmed.

## The 16 sites

| n | File | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | `components/settings/McpServersSection.tsx` | `:686` agent types, `:703` tool allowlist, `:722` secrets |
| 3 | `app/piscine-preview/page.tsx` | `:686`, `:694`, `:706` — demo surface, lowest priority |
| 2 | `components/tickets-registry/NewTicketView.tsx` | `:147` title (GhostInputPill), `:167` description |
| 1 | `components/usage/MonthlyCapTile.tsx` | `:108` monthly cap |
| 1 | `components/spec/MemoryPanel.tsx` | `:544` memory editor |
| 1 | `components/spec/SpecUpdateDialog.tsx` | `:101` instruction |
| 1 | `components/review/InlineCommentForm.tsx` | `:37` comment body |
| 1 | `components/review/ReviewActions.tsx` | `:206` back-to-dev reason |
| 1 | `components/import/FolderSelector.tsx` | `:23` folder path |
| 1 | `app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/page.tsx` | `:552` ticket filter |
| 1 | `app/inbox/page.tsx` | `:199` reply/comment |

## Note on `GhostInputPill`

`components/piscine/GhostInputPill.tsx` renders a bare `<input>` with no authored name, but it **does** spread `{...props}`, so `aria-label` reaches the DOM and the naming is the caller's job. Of its 4 production mounts, 2 already pass `aria-label` (`RegistryFilters`, `VersionPill`) and 2 do not (`NewTicketView`, `MonthlyCapTile`) — those 2 are counted above. The primitive itself is not a defect; per-mount naming is.

## Verification requirement

Assertions must go through `getByLabelText`, **not** `getByRole(..., { name })`: the accessible-name computation falls back to `placeholder`, so a role+name query resolves a placeholder-only control and reports it as named. `getByLabelText` has no such fallback. `getByPlaceholderText` proves nothing at all here.

## No mechanical guard sees this class

Nothing in the repo currently fails when a new placeholder-only control lands. The AST scanner used for this census is a good candidate for a committed convention test, but it can only be added **once the population is at zero** — otherwise it lands red. That guard is part of this ticket's close, not a separate one.

epics.title: Chat : le SheetContent mobile n'a ni SheetTitle ni SheetDescription (deux avertissements Radix)
epics.description:
Trouvé en balayant la famille des primitives Radix pendant 37cBKUyjl1bC (DialogContent sans DialogDescription). **Défaut adjacent, pas causé par ce correctif** — présent avant le diff.

## Observé
`components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:394` rend un `SheetContent` sans `SheetTitle` **ni** `SheetDescription`, et sans `aria-label`/`aria-describedby` :

```tsx
<SheetContent
  side="right"
  showCloseButton={false}
  className="w-full max-w-none p-0 sm:max-w-none"
  data-testid="unified-panel-mobile-sheet"
>
  {chatWorkspace}
</SheetContent>
```

`components/ui/sheet.tsx` est construit sur `@radix-ui/react-dialog` — la même primitive que `DialogContent`. Radix émet donc **deux** avertissements à chaque ouverture, sur deux canaux différents :

- `console.error` — `` `DialogContent` requires a `DialogTitle` for the component to be accessible for screen reader users. `` (`TitleWarning`, dist/index.mjs:296)
- `console.warn` — ``Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.`` (`DescriptionWarning`, dist/index.mjs:309)

## Pourquoi c'est un vrai défaut
Le manque de **titre** est plus grave que le cas Dismiss que 37cBKUyjl1bC vient de fermer : le panneau de chat mobile s'ouvre en plein écran et n'a aucun nom accessible du tout. Un lecteur d'écran annonce « dialog » et rien d'autre — l'utilisateur ne sait pas ce qui vient de s'ouvrir ni ce qu'il vient de recouvrir. `sheet.tsx` exporte déjà `SheetTitle` et `SheetDescription` ; il n'y a rien à écrire dans la primitive.

## Périmètre
C'est le seul `<SheetContent` du dépôt (`AlertDialogContent` et `DrawerContent` n'existent pas ici), donc l'instance et la classe coïncident.

Le correctif attendu : un `SheetTitle` (probablement `sr-only`, le panneau ne peint pas de titre) plus un `SheetDescription`, avec une clé dans le catalogue `en`.

## Note sur la garde mécanique
`__tests__/dialog-description-coverage.test.ts` (ajouté par 37cBKUyjl1bC) balaye l'AST de tous les `DialogContent` de `app/` et `components/`. Il **ne voit pas** ce site : il est keyé sur le nom de balise `DialogContent`, et `SheetContent` est un autre nom pour la même primitive. Élargir cette garde à la famille (`SheetContent`, et tout futur ré-export de `react-dialog`) fait partie de ce ticket — sinon le troisième ré-export repassera au travers.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Pi + Oh My Pi ajoutés aux providers CLI

Commit `46eab87`. Suite complète verte (257 fichiers / 2544 tests), `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Ce que sont réellement ces deux CLI

- **Pi** = `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, binaire `pi` — harness terminal minimal, headless via `--mode json`.
- **Oh My Pi** = paquet npm `oh-my-pi`, **extension de Pi**, pas un agent autonome : son binaire `oh-my-pi` ne fait que `doctor`/`init`/`version`. L'agent, c'est `pi` avec l'extension chargée (prompt système remplacé par un orchestrateur multi-agents).

Il est donc modélisé comme `pi … -e oh-my-pi`. `-e` résout les sources npm à la demande, donc ça marche que l'utilisateur ait fait `pi install oh-my-pi` ou non (réseau requis au premier run). La disponibilité se réduit à « `pi` est dans le PATH », comme pour Pi.

### Comportement des providers

| | Pi / Oh My Pi |
|---|---|
| Commande | `pi --mode json [--tools …] [--session <ID>] [--model <M>] [-e oh-my-pi] -p <prompt>` |
| plan / analyze | `--tools read,grep,find,ls` (pi n'a pas de système de permissions — la capacité passe par l'allowlist d'outils) |
| code | jeu d'outils par défaut (ajoute write, edit, bash) |
| Résultat | dernier `message_end` assistant — exactement ce que le mode texte de pi imprime — avec repli sur les tours précédents puis sur la sortie brute |
| Resume | `--session <ID>`, id pris dans l'en-tête `{"type":"session","id":…}` du flux |

**Point non évident :** en `--mode json`, pi sort avec le code 0 **même quand le run s'est terminé sur une erreur modèle** (seul son mode texte mappe ça sur exit 1). `handleExit()` déclasse donc le succès en se basant sur le `stopReason` du dernier tour, pas sur le code de sortie. Sans ça, un run raté serait enregistré comme réussi.

### Câblage

`ProviderType`, registre, `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` / `PROVIDER_LABELS` / `PROVIDER_TIERS` (Tier 2), `/api/providers/available`, `useProvidersAvailable`, classification resume. Les deux sont ajoutés **en fin** de `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` pour que la ségrégation reviewer/builder continue de choisir les mêmes alternatives qu'avant.

### Deux nettoyages au passage

- `normalizeProvider()` dans `agent-resolution.ts` était une chaîne de 9 `if` à maintenir en phase avec `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` → remplacée par `isAgentProvider()` (idiome déjà utilisé dans `named-agents.ts`).
- `AgentMonitor` étiquetait « CC » **tout** provider autre que Gemini/Codex — donc opencode, qwen, kimi… et maintenant Pi. Il retombe désormais sur `PROVIDER_LABELS` ; « CC » et « Gemini » restent inchangés.

### Vérification

35 tests unitaires dans `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts` (args, parsing du flux, extraction du session id, détection d'échec, cycle de spawn complet avec `child_process` mocké).

En plus des tests, j'ai fait tourner les arguments que le provider émet à travers le **vrai parseur de pi** (`dist/cli/args.js` du paquet publié) : aucun flag inconnu, aucun diagnostic, le prompt arrive bien dans `messages`.

**Limite documentée dans le code :** pi ne traite l'argument après `-p` comme prompt que s'il ne commence pas par `-`, et n'offre pas de séparateur `--`. Un prompt commençant par un tiret simple serait avalé comme option inconnue (run avec prompt vide). Inatteignable aujourd'hui — tous les prompts Arij sont composés par template et commencent par un titre — mais c'est noté dans `lib/providers/pi.ts`.

### Hors périmètre

Le chat streaming (`/chat/stream`, `/sessions/resumable`) restreint déjà les providers à claude-code / gemini-cli / codex par une allowlist en dur, antérieure à ce ticket. Je ne l'ai pas élargie : c'est une décision produit séparée. MCP reste limité à claude-code / codex — pi n'a pas de support MCP natif (uniquement via un adaptateur tiers).

comments.content:
Done — commit `46eab87`, ticket moved to review.

## What I found first

The ticket had no user stories, so I researched what these CLIs actually are before writing code. The important discovery:

**Oh My Pi is not an agent CLI.** It's an npm *extension* for Pi — its own `oh-my-pi` binary only does `doctor`/`init`/`version`. The agent is `pi` with the extension loaded, which swaps Pi's system prompt for a multi-agent orchestrator. So it's modelled as `pi … -e oh-my-pi`, not as a separate binary.

**Pi** is `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (binary `pi`), headless via `--mode json`.

## Implementation

`lib/providers/pi.ts` + `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts` (the latter extends the former, adding `-e oh-my-pi`):

- **Mode mapping** — Pi has no permission system, so capability rides on the tool allowlist: plan/analyze get `--tools read,grep,find,ls`; code keeps the default set.
- **Result** — last assistant `message_end`, which is exactly what Pi's own text mode prints.
- **Resume** — `--session <ID>` from the stream's session header.

One non-obvious thing worth flagging: **in `--mode json`, Pi exits 0 even when the run ended on a model error** — only its text mode maps that to exit 1. `handleExit()` therefore downgrades success based on the final turn's `stopReason`. Without that, failed runs would be recorded as successful.

Wiring covers `ProviderType`, the registry, `PROVIDER_OPTIONS`/`LABELS`/`TIERS`, the availability route, the client hook, and resume classification. Both are appended at the end of `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` so reviewer/builder segregation keeps picking the same alternatives as before.

35 new tests in `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts`; full suite 2544 tests passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Beyond the tests, I ran the args my provider emits through **Pi's real parser** from the published package — no unknown flags, no diagnostics, prompt lands in `messages`.

That exercise turned up a caveat I documented in the code: Pi only treats the argument after `-p` as the prompt if it doesn't start with `-`, and offers no `--` separator. Unreachable today (all Arij prompts are template-composed and start with a heading), but a leading-dash prompt would be silently dropped.

## Two cleanups I made along the way

- `normalizeProvider()` was a 9-branch `if` chain needing manual sync with `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` — now uses `isAgentProvider()`, matching the existing idiom in `named-agents.ts`.
- `AgentMonitor` labelled *every* provider except Gemini/Codex as "CC" — including opencode, qwen, kimi, and now Pi. It falls back to `PROVIDER_LABELS`; "CC" and "Gemini" are unchanged.

## Left out deliberately

Chat streaming and `/sessions/resumable` restrict providers to claude-code/gemini-cli/codex via a pre-existing hardcoded allowlist. I didn't widen it — expanding chat support is a separate product call. MCP stays claude-code/codex only; Pi has no native MCP support.

comments.content:
Both findings fixed in `e3de439`. Full suite: **2563 tests / 259 files passing**, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Major — resume capability drift

The finding was correct. Six dispatch sites hardcoded `claude-code || gemini-cli || codex`, so a Pi resume silently started fresh.

New `lib/agent-sessions/resume-capability.ts` is the single source of truth, and it **splits three questions** the inline checks had conflated:

- `isResumableProvider` — the CLI can continue a session
- `providerAcceptsAssignedSessionId` — dispatch pre-assigns a UUID
- `providerReportsOwnSessionId` — the CLI names its own session

That third one exists because of Pi specifically. Pi prints its own session header, so a minted UUID would be stored, never used by the CLI, then replayed into `--session` on a later resume. `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` was doing exactly that for every resumable provider — fixed.

**No existing provider changes behavior.** Dropping codex from the resume gate is a no-op since `validateResumeSession` already rejected it, and the UUID pre-assignment keeps its own set.

## One call I had to settle on evidence

The codebase contradicted itself on codex, and I nearly got it wrong:

- `fix(codex): enable session resume` (Feb 2026) enabled it in three places but missed `validate-resume.ts` — so it never actually worked.
- `feat: autonomous build → review → fix pipeline` (Aug 2026) states the opposite: *"the build routes' local list ... wrongly includes codex."*

I first unified by making codex resumable, which broke two tests and prompted me to check dates. The August verdict is both newer and technically right — `CodexProvider.parseSessionId()` returns nothing, so the only storable id is one Arij invented, which `codex exec resume` doesn't know. Codex stays non-resumable, with the reasoning and both commits documented in one place.

## A second bug found along the way

`/sessions/resumable` returned `null` from `normalizeProvider` for anything outside its 3-provider list — and `null` **drops the provider filter entirely**, so the endpoint offered other providers' sessions as Pi resume candidates. Dispatch would then hand a Claude session id to `pi --session`. Fixed via `isAgentProvider`.

## Minor — Kanban label

`EpicCard` now resolves through `PROVIDER_LABELS`, matching `AgentMonitor`.

## Tests (+19)

Capability-set unit tests (including the invariant that a self-reporting provider never gets an assigned id), Pi resume and no-minted-id cases in pipeline dispatch, Pi/Oh My Pi/non-resumable cases in `validateResumeSession`, and EpicCard label coverage.

Two notes: the 3 eslint errors in `EpicCard.tsx:157` and `lifecycle.ts` are pre-existing — I confirmed via `git stash` that they're identical before my changes, in code I didn't touch. And I left `/chat/stream`'s local list alone: it's the chat allowlist rather than a resume check, the reviewer didn't flag it, and changing it would alter codex chat behavior.

`validateResumeSession()` vérifiait que le provider de la session précédente sait reprendre, mais pas qu'il **s'agit du même provider** que celui qu'on lance. Un id de session Gemini de même scope pouvait donc partir dans `pi --session`.

L'appel pré-boucle ne pouvait pas connaître le provider de la première review — la validation a donc été déplacée dans la boucle.
