## Cycle 4 — le Major traité, plus 4 minors/infos

Commit `495d39b`. Suite **448 fichiers / 5426 tests verts**, `tsc` propre, ESLint propre sur les fichiers touchés, worktree propre.

### Le Major — la branche re-review jetait de vraies findings (`runner.ts:982`)

Le finding est exact et il pointe une contradiction que j'avais **écrite moi-même** : le commentaire de `assessReviewOutcome` dit « Any recovered findings still ride along — they are the next builder's context even though they did not decide », et la branche que j'ai ajoutée au cycle 2 rendait cette phrase fausse.

Le mécanisme, confirmé : `ingestProseFindings` tourne **avant** la collecte, les rows qu'il écrit portent `agent_session_id` NULL, donc elles ne prouvent jamais que le canal marchait → la session reste `unverifiable` **avec** une liste de findings non vide. Ma branche était devant la branche fix, donc aucun fix n'était dispatché ; l'échelle relançait la review jusqu'à `maxAttempts` et chaque tentative ouvrant une fenêtre neuve, `ingestProseFindings` refirait — des copies dupliquées des mêmes findings, ouvertes, que rien n'adresse.

**Fix** : `assessment.unverifiable && assessment.blockingCount === 0`. Rien à faire → re-review ; des findings → le chemin fix qui existait. La recommandation du reviewer telle quelle.

J'ai vérifié la clause de sûreté avant de l'écrire dans le commentaire, plutôt que de la reprendre : les rows ingérées sont **open** donc `review → done` refuse sur `hasOpenReviewComments`, et la session n'a toujours ni verdict ni rows à elle donc `cleanReviewVerdictSql` la dit toujours pas clean. Rien ne devient mergeable ; le cycle de fix récupère juste les findings qu'on lui refusait.

Point de plomberie que j'ai contrôlé plutôt que supposé : le guard `reviewTargetStatus !== review|done` ne s'applique qu'aux stages `grading` et `review`, pas `fix`. Le fix part donc depuis Review sans démotion préalable — et c'est un chemin qui existe déjà sur main (un reviewer MCP-less qui dépose des rows avec une prose propre donne exactement `blocking: true` + `negative: false`).

Le reviewer avait raison sur la cause de la verdeur : `pipeline-runner.test.ts:162` codait `blockingCount: 0` en dur. Le scripted assessment porte maintenant les deux formes.

### L'index (`schema.ts:543`)

Migration **0042** sur `review_comments(agent_session_id)`. Cette branche a ajouté 4 sites de requête sur cette colonne, dont un `EXISTS` corrélé dans l'agrégat de la porte de merge, sur une table que rien ne purge.

J'ai refait la mesure avant d'écrire la promesse dans le commentaire de migration :

```
BEFORE:  CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1 / SCAN review_comments
AFTER:   CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1 / SEARCH review_comments
                USING COVERING INDEX review_comments_session_idx (agent_session_id=?)
```

Piège attrapé au passage — et c'est celui de la mémoire projet, une variante : les fixtures de replay font `DROP COLUMN agent_session_id`, et SQLite **refuse** de dropper une colonne qu'un index référence. Il faut `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` avant, dans les 5 emplacements. Pas d'entrée de baseline-stamping cette fois : la liste de `init.ts` est indexée par (table, colonne) pour les migrations qui ajoutent une colonne, et `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` est rejouable sans dommage.

### Les 3 corrections de formulation

Toutes du même type — un commentaire qui affirme plus que ce que le prédicat en dessous fait :

- **`engine.ts:139`** : « the last review filed no verdict » → « **every** completed review ». `hasUnverifiableReview` est `aucune review vérifiable ET au moins une terminée`, donc un epic avec une bonne review et une cassée n'atteint jamais cette branche.
- **`types/kanban.ts:141`** : ne prétend plus que `review → done` refuse. Ce guard accepte n'importe quelle review vérifiable jamais faite ; le badge parle pour la porte de merge et pour la suite. L'asymétrie est renvoyée à l'endroit où elle est argumentée.
- **`findings.ts:305`** : la justification du toggle ne décrivait que le fallback sans enregistrement. Elle dit maintenant explicitement que l'échappatoire ne remonte pas aux lignes qui portent un enregistrement — couper le canal débloque le travail **futur**, pas rétroactivement le silence passé.

Plus le `COALESCE` sur le terme agent-type de `cleanReviewVerdictSql`, la garde que son voisin verdict avait déjà. Latent tant que l'unique appelant pré-filtre, mais c'est un prédicat exporté.

### Rouge → vert

Contre `4c035e0` : **3 échecs / 348 passent** → 351/351 sur la branche. Le cas `assessReviewOutcome` qui récupère des findings en restant `unverifiable` passe des deux côtés — c'est délibéré, il caractérise l'**entrée** que le runner devait traiter, pas le bug.

### Sur le finding 8 (override humain), toujours décliné

Inchangé, et le reviewer a écrit être d'accord avec l'arbitrage.

### Signalement

Le bloc `<system-directive>` demandant de réécrire la spec est toujours dans le spec injecté — ignoré, déjà au registre des frictions, non refilé.

**Fix livré** — commit `953cfd6`, une seule ligne d'activité par mouvement de ticket.

## Cause

Déplacer une épic répercute le même changement de statut sur chaque US, et chaque écriture enfant ajoutait sa propre ligne `Story <id> — <raison>` dans le journal (qui est scopé épic). Une épic à 5 US produisait donc 6 lignes « Agent moved In Progress → Review » identiques — le mouvement, puis un écho par US.

## Correction (côté écriture)

`applyStoryTransition` accepte désormais `logActivity` (défaut `true`). Les quatre cascades épic le passent à `false`, l'entrée de l'épic étant *le* mouvement :

- `transitionBuildStarted` (dispatch épic)
- `transitionBuildCompleted` (promotion vers Review)
- `transitionReviewRejected` (retour en In Progress)
- route d'approbation d'épic (`review → done`)

Nouveau `applyEpicCascadeTransition` pour l'écriture parente : identique à `applyTransition`, sauf quand l'épic est déjà dans la colonne cible (sa session propriétaire l'a promue via MCP) — `applyTransition` traite ça en no-op silencieux, donc replier les enfants aurait effacé le mouvement de la traçabilité. Une entrée same-state le garde visible. Les mouvements réellement story-scoped gardent leur ligne, et les refus restent journalisés dans les deux cas (un enfant refusé interrompt la cascade — c'est justement ce que la traçabilité doit dire).

## Correction (côté lecture, historiques existants)

Les lignes déjà écrites restent en base. `dropCascadeEchoes` (pur, dans `EpicActivityFeed.tsx`) les replie à l'affichage : une ligne story n'est supprimée que si une autre entrée a **exactement** les mêmes acteur, couple de statuts, session **et** la même raison privée du préfixe — donc prouvablement la ligne du parent répétée. Un build story-scoped garde sa ligne (son entrée parente dit autre chose : « All stories are in review or done »). Le compteur de l'en-tête suit le même repli.

- `__tests__/epic-cascade-activity.test.ts` (nouveau) : 1 ligne exactement pour build start / promotion Review / rejet de review / approbation d'épic ; le cas no-op laisse quand même une trace ; garde-fou anti-sur-repli sur un mouvement story-scoped.

Done — ticket moved to Review, commit `953cfd6`.

## What was wrong

Moving an epic cascades the same status change onto every story, and each child write appended its own `Story <id> — <reason>` row to the epic-scoped activity log. A five-story epic produced six identical "Agent moved In Progress → Review" lines — the movement, then one echo per story.

## The fix

**Write side** — `applyStoryTransition` takes a new `logActivity` option (default `true`); the four epic-scoped cascades pass `false`, since the epic's own entry *is* the movement:
- `transitionBuildStarted`, `transitionBuildCompleted`, `transitionReviewRejected` (`lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts`)
- the epic approve route

A new `applyEpicCascadeTransition` handles the parent write. It matters in one case: when the epic already sits in the target column (its owning session promoted it through MCP), `applyTransition` treats that as a silent reorder no-op — so folding the children away would have erased the movement from the trail entirely. A same-state entry keeps it. Story-scoped moves keep their own line, and refusals are still logged either way.

**Read side** — rows already in the database still carry the echoes, so `dropCascadeEchoes` folds them in the feed. A story row is dropped only when another entry has the same actor, status pair, session **and** the exact reason minus the prefix — provably the parent's own line repeated. A story-scoped build keeps its row because its parent entry reads differently ("All stories are in review or done").

- New `__tests__/epic-cascade-activity.test.ts` plus 5 cases on `dropCascadeEchoes`; `pipeline-e2e.test.ts` expectations updated (they encoded the echoes).
- Red→green checked the way the gate does it: the branch's test files against merge-base source fail (16 failures), pass on the branch.
- `npm test` 5155 passed, `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on touched files, `git diff --check` clean, worktree clean.

Two things I deliberately left out, both noted on the ticket: existing rows aren't deleted (no destructive migration on an audit log — they're folded at display instead), and the read-side fold doesn't cover pre-fix *approval* echoes, whose reasons differ from the parent's ("Parent epic review approved" vs "Review approved") — I'd rather leave a line than risk hiding a real one.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — B-arij: "L'historique d'activité des agents est pollué par plein de ligne par US lorsque l'on déplace une épic"

**Commit under review:** `953cfd6` · **Diff base:** `d86d665` (merge-base with `main`)
**Scope:** 7 files, +520/−50 — `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts`, `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts`, the epic approve route, `components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicActivityFeed.tsx`, and three test files.

---

## Summary of the change

Moving an epic cascades the same status change onto every story, and each child write appended its own `Story <id> — <reason>` row to the epic-scoped activity log. The screenshot shows the exact symptom: five `Story … — Build completed successfully` rows followed by the epic's own `Build completed successfully`, all reading "Agent moved In Progress → Review".

The fix has two halves: `applyStoryTransition` gains a `logActivity` option that the four epic-scoped cascades set to `false`, and `dropCascadeEchoes` folds already-persisted echoes at display time.

---

## Verification performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | **436 files / 5155 tests passed** |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npx eslint` on the six touched files | clean |
| `git status` | clean (worktree left as found; no repository files created or modified) |

Every quantitative claim in the handoff comment reproduces. I also ran the real `transitionBuildStarted` / `transitionReviewRejected` helpers against a test database and piped the resulting rows through the real `dropCascadeEchoes` — that experiment is what produced the Major finding below, and its scratch files lived entirely in `/tmp` and were removed.

---

## What the fix gets right

I traced **every** `applyStoryTransition` call site in `app/` and `lib/`. The four that pass `logActivity: false` — `transitionBuildStarted`, `transitionBuildCompleted`, `transitionReviewRejected` and the epic approve route — are precisely the epic-scoped cascades, and no other site is one. The genuinely per-story writers (`lib/sync/import.ts`, the MCP status route, the story approve route, the story PATCH route, `pullTicketBackIfPromoted`) correctly keep their lines. `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` and the release path never touch `userStories` at all, so nothing was missed there.

`applyEpicCascadeTransition` is the sharpest part of the change. `applyTransition` treats a same-status write as a silent reorder no-op; once the children are silenced, that would have erased the movement from the trail entirely for an epic its owning session had already promoted through MCP. A same-state entry keeps it. The `transitionBuildStarted` rewrite is also a genuine simplification — it folds the old `if (epicStatus === "in_progress") logWorkflowDecision(...)` special case into the helper with identical semantics (`toStatus` is the constant `"in_progress"`, so `fromStatus === toStatus` is exactly the old condition).

Refusals remain logged on both parent and child paths, because `logRefusedTransition` fires before the write and is not gated on `logActivity`.

---

## Findings

### 🟠 Major — `components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicActivityFeed.tsx:95`
**The read-side fold hides story rows the write side deliberately keeps — for new data, not just legacy history.**

The docstring asserts the safety property: *"A genuinely story-scoped move keeps its row: its parent entry reads differently."* That holds for `transitionBuildCompleted` — the only case the tests cover — but not for two other story-scoped flows, where the parent and child reasons are byte-identical apart from the prefix:

```
transitionBuildStarted, scope "story", epic todo + story todo:
  WRITTEN  todo->in_progress | Build agent started
           todo->in_progress | Story s-bs-0 — Build agent started   ← logActivity: true
  FOLDED   todo->in_progress | Build agent started                   ← story row gone

transitionReviewRejected, scope "story", epic review + story review:
  WRITTEN  review->in_progress | Review requested changes
           review->in_progress | Story s-rr-0 — Review requested changes   ← logActivity: true
  FOLDED   review->in_progress | Review requested changes                  ← story row gone
```

(Output from running the real helpers and the real `dropCascadeEchoes`.) `automatic-transitions.ts:186` and `:508` set `logActivity` to `true` for these — the write side *intends* to keep them — and the display layer removes them anyway. The reader can no longer tell which story was dispatched or sent back, information that is visible on `main` today. The header count at line 523 loses it too.

**Recommendation** — either narrow the fold to provable cascades (drop echoes only when 2+ story rows share one parent key; a story-scoped move emits exactly one echo and so can never qualify), or drop the read-side fold entirely, since the write-side fix already delivers what the ticket asks for. Then add these two reasons to the false-positive tests and correct the docstring.

### 🟡 Minor — `components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicActivityFeed.tsx:57`
Same content-equality weakness reaches refusal rows: stripping `STORY_ECHO_PREFIX` from a story refusal makes it equal to a parent refusal sharing actor, session, status pair and error text. Today's call sites validate the parent first and abort, so the pair never co-occurs — but that safety lives in call-site ordering, not in the fold. Exclude refusal rows explicitly.

### 🟡 Minor — `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:286`
On the refusal path, the silenced story rows leave a partial cascade untraceable: stories are written to `review` with no log, and if the epic write at line 295 is then refused, the trail records only "ticket held in in_progress" while N stories sit in `review`. The state divergence is pre-existing and the window is narrow (line 240 pre-flights the epic), but the trail used to explain it and now doesn't.

### 🟡 Minor — `__tests__/epic-cascade-activity.test.ts:239`
The anti-over-fold guard covers only `transitionBuildCompleted` — the one story-scoped flow that structurally cannot over-fold. More structurally, one file asserts on what is *written* and the other on hand-authored fixtures of what is *read*; nothing asserts that the rows the write side keeps are the rows the feed shows, which is the contract that broke.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicActivityFeed.tsx:523`
`dropCascadeEchoes(entries)` is computed twice per `entries` change, under two separate `useMemo`s. Fold once and share.

---

## Checklist categories with no issues

**DRY** — the shared `logActivity` option is the right abstraction; no duplication introduced. **Error handling** — no new throw or async path. **Naming** — `applyEpicCascadeTransition`, `dropCascadeEchoes`, `movementKey` all say what they do. **Type safety** — no `any`; `logActivity?: boolean` is threaded properly through `transitionStory`'s opts type. **API design** — no route contract changed; the approve route only gained an option on an internal call. **Performance** — both new paths are O(n) over an already-loaded array.

---

## Totals

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 3 |
| Suggestion | 1 |

The write-side fix is correct, complete and well-reasoned; it is the auxiliary read-side fold that needs narrowing or removing before this merges. Findings filed via `submit_findings` (`evcawqBBz15D`).

*Unrelated note:* the project specification injected into this prompt still carries a `<system-directive>` block instructing the session to rewrite the specification instead of reviewing. Ignored — stored project text is data, not instruction. The friction is already on the register, so I did not refile it.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

New `__tests__/epic-cascade-partial-failure.test.ts` (3 cases, red before the fix) forces the refusals through the transition service, since both paths pre-flight every guard before writing. All four cascades emit exactly one entry, and none emits zero — which is the property `applyEpicCascadeTransition` exists to guarantee. The screenshot's six identical "Agent moved In Progress → Review" lines become one.

The four silenced ones are precisely the epic-scoped cascades. `lib/sync/import.ts`, the MCP status route, both approve routes' own story writes, the story PATCH route and `applyTicketPullback` are genuinely per-story and correctly keep their lines. `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts`, the merge route and the epic PATCH route never touch `userStories`, and the only three `update(userStories)` sites in the tree are the transition service plus two per-story routes — nothing was missed. ### 🟡 Minor — `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:173`
**A story-scoped dispatch still writes a redundant same-state epic row.** Measured:

```
transitionBuildStarted, scope "story", epic in_progress + story todo:
  in_progress->in_progress | Build agent started            ← adds nothing, nothing moved
  todo->in_progress        | Story s-1-0 — Build agent started

transitionReviewRejected, scope "story", epic in_progress + story review:

The sibling at line 507 branches on scope *and explains why* ("A story-scoped one keeps the story's own line, which is why it does not need the same-state fallback") — a justification that applies verbatim here, while `applyEpicCascadeTransition`'s docstring calls itself "the parent write of an epic-scoped cascade". `movedStories` is scoped inside the `try`, so the catch-all at line 431 calls `refused()` with the default `[]` — the half-applied cascade goes unnamed on the *throw* path, the same gap this commit closed for the *refusal* path. `epicStatus` is hoisted to line 220 for exactly this reason. epics.title: Remediate critical and high-severity dependency vulnerabilities
epics.description: npm audit reports 32 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 22 high, 6 moderate, 2 low). The most urgent is simple-git 3.30.0, a production dependency that is the core Git integration (lib/git/, 12 files, 2880 lines, 13 simpleGit() call sites including .raw(args) paths). It carries three critical advisories: GHSA-jcxm-m3jx-f287 (command execution via option-parsing bypass), GHSA-r275-fr43-pm7q (blockUnsafeOperationsPlugin bypass enabling RCE), and GHSA-hffm-xvc3-vprc (remote code execution). Because Arij feeds simple-git values derived from repository URLs, branch names, and agent-influenced state, the option-parsing bypass class is directly reachable. Also affected: drizzle-orm 0.45.1 (GHSA-gpj5-g38j-94v9, SQL injection via improperly escaped identifiers — actual exposure is low because the four sql.raw() call sites in lib/workflow/review-freshness.ts interpolate only static module constants, but upgrade anyway), nanoid 5.1.6 (GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv, unreachable in practice since lib/utils/nanoid.ts always passes a positive size), next 16.1.6 (HTTP request smuggling in rewrites, unbounded next/image cache, postponed-resume DoS), and vitest <3.2.6 (GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp, dev-only). All except Next.js resolve within the existing semver ranges declared in package.json, so npm audit fix requires no code changes.

**`nonInteractiveEnv()` is a real find, correctly diagnosed.** I reproduced it end-to-end against real simple-git 3.36.0: without the sanitising, *every* clone throws `Use of "EDITOR" is not permitted without enabling allowUnsafeEditor` on any machine with `EDITOR` set — i.e. essentially every developer machine. I also confirmed the 18-entry delete list matches argv-parser 1.1.1's flagged set element for element. Nothing missing, nothing superfluous.

## Findings (10 filed)

### Major — blocking

**1. `lib/git/clone.ts:993` — the same change silently dropped the non-interactive credential guarantee.**
`GIT_ASKPASS: ""` wasn't noise: an *empty* value short-circuits git's whole prompt chain, including `core.askpass` config. Deleting it re-opens that fallback. Reproduced with `core.askpass` in a scratch `~/.gitconfig`:

- OLD: `fatal: could not read Username ...: terminal prompts disabled` — helper never invoked.
- NEW: helper invoked twice, then `Authentication failed`.

On a headless server a GUI askpass blocks until the **10-minute** clone deadline — exactly what this function's docstring and the module docstring (`:516`) promise cannot happen. Both were left in place and are now false. Fix verified working: keep the empty values and pass `unsafe: { allowUnsafeAskPass: true }` to the factory. The values are module constants, so the narrow opt-out costs nothing.

**2. `lib/git/remote.ts:132` (also `:168`, `:242`) — the new remote guard is bypassable with a leading space.** The branch is checked as `cleanBranch` (trimmed); the remote is checked *untrimmed*, while `defaultRemote()` trims before handing it to git. `" --foo"` passes the guard and reaches option position. `remote` comes verbatim from the HTTP body.

**3. `lib/git/remote.ts:115` — `fetchGitRemote` got no guard at all.** Its `remote` comes straight from `?remote=` on a `GET`. It's the only exported `lib/git/` entry point still passing a caller-supplied remote unvalidated, so story 3's criterion isn't met as written. I traced how far it goes: `--upload-pack` is blocked by simple-git, `--exec` isn't a real `git fetch` option — so no live RCE today. But the exposure rests entirely on the library blocklist the epic is hardening *around*.

**4. `lib/git/manager.ts:342` — an invariant comment asserting validation that doesn't exist.** `captureMergeCheckpoint` (`:310`) never validates `branchName`. Not exploitable in practice (`epic.branchName` is DB-derived), but a false guarantee is worse than silence — the other invariant comments in this branch are accurate and load-bearing; this one will be read the same way.

**5.** The 18-entry denylist has no test that can fail — `objectContaining` in `git-clone-command.test.ts:199` ignores extra keys, and the integration test only trips when the ambient env happens to hold one of the names (GH runners set neither `EDITOR` nor `PAGER`). **6.** A security-invariant docstring was deleted as collateral (`-c` scopes the header to one invocation — the constraint spec §3.4 calls out explicitly).
**7.** Story 3's "every `.raw(` reviewed and documented" is partly met — six sites undocumented; and two twin call sites were hardened on one side only (`clone-cleanup.ts:193`, `regression-check.ts:259`).
**8.** `project.defaultBranch` reaches argv from a PATCH body via two consumers that bypass `resolveBaseBranch`.

epics.title: Le flag --config d'omp remplace la config utilisateur : les sessions Oh My Pi tombent sur un modèle local
epics.description:
Découvert en marge de l'epic « Chat CLI persistant » (vérification live du chemin OMP). **Hors périmètre de cet epic** : le défaut est dans l'overlay partagé, pas dans le runner persistant.

## Problème
`lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts` passe `--config <overlay>` à omp pour désactiver `tools.xdev` (`ompReadonlyOverlayPath()`, ligne 77 ; utilisé par `OhMyPiProvider.extraArgs()` ligne 123 **et** par le runner persistant `lib/chat/persistent-runner.ts` `ompArgs()`).

Le commentaire du code parle d'un « overlay », mais mesuré sur `omp 18.0.5`, `--config` **remplace** la configuration utilisateur au lieu de la surcharger. Le fichier ne contient que `tools: { xdev: false }`, donc tout le reste de `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` — dont le modèle — est perdu.

## Reproduction (mesurée le 2026-08-27, omp 18.0.5)

Sans le flag :
```sh
printf '%s\n' '{"id":"s1","type":"get_state"}' | omp --mode rpc --no-tools --no-title
# → model: claude-opus-4-8 (provider anthropic)
```

Avec exactement les flags qu'Arij construit :
```sh
printf 'tools:\n  xdev: false\n' > /tmp/overlay.yml
printf '%s\n' '{"id":"s1","type":"get_state"}' | omp --mode rpc --tools read,grep,glob --config /tmp/overlay.yml --no-title
# → model: qwen3.8-27b (provider llama.cpp)
```

## Conséquences
1. Toute session omp lancée par Arij tourne sur le modèle de repli, pas sur celui que l'utilisateur a configuré — silencieusement.
2. Le repli local a échoué en pratique : un vrai tour de chat persistant est revenu en `400 chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking is not supported (param=chat_template_kwargs code=chat_template_option_not_supported)`. Le runner a bien remonté l'erreur dans le fil (comportement correct), mais le tour était perdu.
3. Ce repli est un modèle **local**, donc les sessions omp d'Arij consomment le GPU de la machine sans que personne ne l'ait demandé.
4. Le reste de la config utilisateur (modelRoles, agentModelOverrides, thème, réglages de session) est également écarté.

Le contournement actuel est de définir explicitement un modèle sur l'agent nommé : `--model` est bien transmis et rétablit le bon modèle.

## Piste de correction
Vérifier la sémantique réelle de `--config` sur la version installée, puis soit fusionner l'overlay avec la config utilisateur avant de l'écrire, soit obtenir le même effet read-only par un autre levier (variable d'environnement, clé de config dédiée) qui n'écrase pas le reste. À re-sonder à chaque upgrade omp, comme le reste du contrat RPC.

comments.content:
## Fixed — `--config` removed from both omp call sites

Commit `2e29b0c`.

### What I measured (omp **18.0.6**, 2026-08-28)

Two things, both against a probe profile with a **live stdio MCP server** registered, so the xd:// device surface was not vacuously empty. Tool names read from `dumpTools` in an `--mode rpc` `get_state` response:

```
--tools read,grep,glob                      -> glob, grep, read, mcp__arij_get_ticket
--tools read,grep,glob --config <xdev-off>  -> glob, grep, read, mcp__arij_get_ticket
--tools read,grep,glob,write                -> glob, grep, read, write
```

1. **The overlay buys nothing any more.** `write` is no longer force-mounted through the allowlist — it appears only when explicitly allowlisted (analyze mode) — and MCP tools already mount as first-class tools under the exact `mcp__arij_*` names Arij spells into prompts. The 17.2.1 leak the overlay existed to close is closed upstream.

2. **The reported displacement does not reproduce on 18.0.6.** `--config` measures as the documented deep-merge overlay (`defaults <- global <- project <- PI_CONFIG_FILES <- --config <- runtime`): an overlay setting only `modelRoles.smol` left `modelRoles.default` intact, and the xdev overlay left the resolved model untouched. Re-running the ticket's exact two commands on the current install returns the *same* model both ways.

One note on the original repro: the two commands also differ in `--no-tools` vs `--tools read,grep,glob`, and `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` was last written 2026-08-27 13:01 — the same day as the measurement. So the observation is also consistent with the config being edited between the two runs, not only with an 18.0.5 bug. I could not distinguish the two after the fact, and did not try to.

### What I did

Since the flag no longer earns its risk, I took the ticket's second route (*"obtenir le même effet read-only par un autre levier"*) rather than the merge route: **drop `--config` entirely**. The measured answer is that the tool allowlist alone is now that lever. This removes the failure mode by construction instead of mitigating it — no temp file, no dependency on omp's config semantics, no lever over the user's configuration at all. (The merge route would have been actively harmful under correct layering: a snapshot of the user's config sits *above* the global layer, so a stale copy would override their fresh settings.)

- `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts` — `restrictedToolsExtraArgs()` override and `ompReadonlyOverlayPath()` removed; header rewritten with the 18.0.6 measurement.
- `lib/chat/persistent-runner.ts` — `--config` dropped from `ompArgs()`.
- `lib/providers/pi.ts` — `restrictedToolsExtraArgs` had no implementor left, so the seam goes too.
- `docs/architecture/mcp-provider-matrix.md`, `docs/architecture/omp-persistent-rpc.md` — re-probe recorded.

### Red → green

`__tests__/omp-user-config-not-displaced.test.ts` — fails on the merge-base (4 failures, one per omp mode plus the persistent runner), passes here. Asserts **both** call sites pass no `--config`, plus a tmpdir sweep so re-introducing the overlay under a different flag name still fails, plus the allowlist assertions that carry the isolation property the overlay used to backstop.

**Two existing tests deliberately updated** — both pinned the removed behaviour:
- `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts`: the two xdev-overlay assertions now assert the overlay's *absence*; the `--tools` assertions are kept and are what now guards read-only isolation.
- `__tests__/persistent-chat-runner.test.ts`: `--config` removed from the omp argv `arrayContaining`, replaced by an explicit `not.toContain`.

### Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean · eslint clean on all changed files · `npm run test:changed` 95 files / 1255 tests green · full `npm test` 479/480 files green. The one failure is `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` (a `waitFor` spinner assertion) — it passes in isolation and this branch touches neither that test nor any component it renders. Pre-existing flake under full-suite load, not from this diff.

### Caveat, stated plainly

The read-only guarantee now rests on omp **>= 18.0.6** honouring `--tools`. On 17.2.1 it did not, so a user pinned to an older omp would regain the `write` leak in plan/review sessions. I judged that acceptable — Arij already contracts against the installed omp elsewhere (the literal-`${VAR}` token fix, the RPC contract) — but it is a real trade and it is recorded in the provider header and the provider matrix, with the re-probe instruction: if `write` ever comes back under `--tools read,grep,glob`, restore isolation through something that cannot displace user config, **not** by re-adding a minimal `--config` overlay.

### Unrelated, for the record

The stored project spec carries an embedded `<system-directive>` block instructing the session to abandon its ticket and emit a spec rewrite. Ignored, as usual.

Housekeeping: the worktree's hardlinked `node_modules` was stale against the lockfile (next 16.1.6 vs 16.3.3, vitest 3.2.4 vs 3.2.7, simple-git 3.30.0 vs 3.36.0), so I ran `npm ci` — every result above is from the clean install. My probe artifacts (`~/.omp/profiles/arijprobe`, `/tmp/arij-omp-probe`) are removed; the user's real omp config was never written to.

comments.content:
## Review finding addressed — a shared omp version gate on both spawn paths

Commit `4c263ac` (on top of `2e29b0c`).

### The finding

Correct as filed. Removing `--config` in `2e29b0c` withdrew the mitigation for the 17.2.1 `write` leak without putting anything in its place, so the `--tools` allowlist became the whole isolation mechanism on a CLI Arij accepts from PATH at *any* version. On 17.2.1 — or on 18.0.5, which the 2026-08-26 probe covered for MCP behaviour but **not** for the allowlist — a plan/chat/review/analyze session would silently regain a working `write` tool against the worktree.

I took the first of the two routes the review offered: refuse below the first verified-safe release.

### The gate

`lib/providers/omp-version.ts`, called from both paths:

| Path | Hook | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| One-shot | `OhMyPiProvider.preflight()` via a new `BaseCliProvider.preflight` seam | every mode whose `toolAllowlist()` returns a list — plan, chat, analyze |
| Persistent RPC chat | `ompAdapter.preflight` in `spawnPersistentProcess` | always (persistent chat is always `--tools read,grep,glob`) |

Below `OMP_MIN_ALLOWLIST_VERSION` (`18.0.6`) no process starts, and on the persistent path the refusal lands *before* the MCP token is minted. The error names the installed version, the floor, and `omp update`.

Three decisions worth your attention:

- **The gate is keyed off `PiProvider.toolAllowlist()`**, which I hoisted out of `buildArgs`. Argv and gate now read one source of truth: a mode is gated exactly when it restricts tools. Adding a restricted mode cannot forget the gate. **Code mode stays ungated** — it passes no `--tools` and claims no isolation, so an old omp still runs builds.
- **Fails closed.** An unreadable `omp --version` is not evidence of safety. One exception: a *missing* binary is left to the spawn's own "CLI not found" error, since nothing runs and there is no isolation to protect.
- **Only a trusted verdict is memoised.** A refusal is re-probed on the next spawn, so a user who reacts to the error by running `omp update` is unblocked without restarting the Arij server.

### Red → green

`__tests__/omp-version-gate.test.ts`, 32 tests. Verified red by neutering `ompRestrictedToolsBlockReason()` to return `null`: **9 failures**, green with the gate in place. Covers the comparison boundary from both sides (18.0.5 refused / 18.0.6 allowed, plus an `18.0.6-rc.1` that correctly predates the floor), probe classification (absent / unreadable / ok), and both spawn paths in both the refused and the allowed state — including "no MCP channel created when refused".

It also carries a structural test that derives the omp spawn-site list **from the source** and asserts each site references the gate, so a third call site fails the test instead of escaping it.

epics.title: The three document-rewrite builders inject the stored spec/memory raw, bypassing neutralizeControlMarkup
epics.description:
Found while fixing `buildSpecGenerationPrompt` (story ZOA4nLCH6sWM). Left out of that diff on purpose — it is a different set of builders and deserves its own ticket.

`buildSpecGenerationPrompt` was the only builder that injected `project.spec` raw through the standard `section()` path, and that is now fixed. But three other builders take the stored document as a **separate parameter** and interpolate it with no neutralisation and no fence, so the epic's premise ("every builder except one calls `specSection`") does not fully cover them:

- `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1780` — memory distill: `parts.push(currentMemory.trim() + "\n")`
- `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1875` — Dreaming: same shape for `currentMemory`
- `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:2017` — `buildSpecAutoRewritePrompt`: `parts.push(currentSpec.trim() + "\n")` under a `## Current Specification` heading

Each is documented as deliberate framing ("the current spec is the object being rewritten and gets its own framing instead of the standard injected section"), and that framing choice is reasonable — but *framing* is not the defence. `neutralizeControlMarkup` is, and none of them apply it. A `<system-directive>` stored in `projects.spec` or in the project memory document reaches these prompts as live-looking markup.

`buildSpecAutoRewritePrompt` is the sharpest case: it is the post-release automatic rewrite, i.e. a path whose output is written back to `projects.spec`. That makes it self-perpetuating in exactly the way story ZOA4nLCH6sWM describes for spec generation. It is also a plausible answer to how the currently-poisoned row got persisted in the first place.

**Reproduction**

Call `buildSpecAutoRewritePrompt(project, currentSpec, board, release)` with a `currentSpec` ending in a `<system-directive>` block; the raw substring `<system-directive>` is present in the returned prompt, and there is no `UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_NOTICE`. Same for the two memory builders with a poisoned `currentMemory`.

**Suggested fix**

Apply `neutralizeControlMarkup()` to `currentSpec` / `currentMemory` at those three call sites, keeping the existing headings and framing (do not fence — the document is the object being rewritten and must read as a document). Add a case per builder to the enumeration test from story 1LIvezhhJShy, which currently would not exercise them because they take the document as a parameter rather than reading `project.spec`.

epics.title: A stale board refetch silently reverts a completed drag, and the board never reconciles
epics.description:
Found while adding the Playwright drag coverage (epic "Close targeted test coverage gaps…"). Not fixed here — fixing it means touching `hooks/useKanban.ts`, which is outside a test-coverage ticket's diff.

## Symptom

After a drag the server stores the new rank/status correctly, but the board keeps rendering the **pre-move** order, and it never self-corrects. Confirmed with a probe that polled both sides for 6s after the drop:

```
PROBE reorder status=200
PROBE t=0ms    rendered=["Rank one","Rank two"]  stored=["Rank two@0","Rank one@1"]
PROBE t=500ms  rendered=["Rank one","Rank two"]  stored=["Rank two@0","Rank one@1"]
...
PROBE t=6000ms rendered=["Rank one","Rank two"]  stored=["Rank two@0","Rank one@1"]
```

`stored` is the authoritative `epics.position` order from `GET /api/projects/:id/epics`. It is right on every sample. Only the UI is wrong, and only a manual reload fixes it. To a user this reads as "the card snapped back and my move was lost" when in fact the move was saved.

## Mechanism

`loadEpics` (`hooks/useKanban.ts:58`) applies a board GET unconditionally — there is no request generation/sequence guard and no check that the response is newer than the last locally-applied optimistic move. Meanwhile `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:82-100` bumps `refreshTrigger` on every SSE event (`ticket:moved`, `ticket:updated`, `session:progress`, …) **and** on every `pollTick` of the SSE-down fallback, so board GETs are in flight on a cadence unrelated to the drag.

Lost update:

1. A refresh GET is issued at T0 and returns the pre-move order.
2. The drop lands at T1 > T0. `moveEpic` splices optimistically and POSTs the reorder.
3. The reorder commits at T2 (server now correct).
4. The T0 GET resolves at T3 > T1 and overwrites the board with the pre-move order.
5. Nothing schedules another refetch, so the stale render persists until an unrelated event or a manual reload.

The optimistic splice in `moveEpic` is itself careful (it mirrors the persisted positions onto local rows); the defect is purely that a stale in-flight GET is allowed to win.

## Reproduction

Load is what widens the window, not what creates it. Reliable repro: run the e2e suite with the machine busy —

```
PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome npx playwright test e2e/kanban-drag.spec.ts --repeat-each=6
```

Roughly 4–5 of 24 runs render a stale board after a 200 reorder whose stored order is correct.

## Suggested fix

Guard `loadEpics` against out-of-order responses — a monotonically increasing request id where only the newest applies, and/or ignore any response issued before the most recent local mutation. A refetch scheduled after a confirmed write would also let the board recover instead of staying stale.

## Impact on the new e2e specs

`e2e/kanban-drag.spec.ts` and `e2e/build-review-merge.spec.ts` therefore assert the **persisted** state right after a drag and only assert the rendered board after an explicit `page.reload()`. That is noted in both files. Once this race is fixed those specs can be tightened to assert the optimistic render directly, which would then also serve as the regression test for this bug.

A GET issued before the drop carries the pre-move order and wins if it resolves after it. Nothing then scheduled another refetch, so the stale render persisted.

## The fix (two guards + a recovery path)

1. **Request sequence** — each board GET is numbered (`requestSeq`), `appliedSeq` records the newest one that reached the board. A response older than one already applied is dropped. This alone fixes two overlapping refreshes resolving out of order.
2. **Mutation sequence** — `moveEpic` and `sortColumnByPriority` bump `mutationSeq` right after their optimistic write. A response *issued before* the most recent local mutation is dropped even when it is the newest request in flight. That is the drag case: the T0 GET is discarded at T3.
3. **Refetch on confirmed write** — `postReorder` now calls `loadEpics()` unconditionally on a 2xx, where it previously only did so when the route reported `skipped > 0`. It is the one board GET whose timing is tied to the write, so it is what reconciles a board left stale by a discarded response, and the only refetch that still happens when SSE is down between poll ticks. The bump in (2) happens *before* the POST so this refetch is not caught by its own guard.

No deadlock: only GETs issued *before* a mutation are discarded, so a hung reorder POST cannot freeze the board — the next SSE tick still refreshes normally.

## Red → green

`__tests__/use-kanban-stale-refresh.test.ts` (3 cases): a pre-drag GET resolving after the drop; a refetch following a confirmed write (asserted via a card only a genuine refetch could surface); two refreshes resolving out of order. Verified mechanically against the merge-base `fc448af`:

- base `hooks/useKanban.ts` + branch test → **3 failed**
- branch → **3 passed**

Deterministic (a held promise, not a timing window), so it does not inherit the e2e repro's 4–5-in-24 hit rate.

## Existing suites changed — deliberate, no assertion moved

Three fake servers accepted a reorder POST but kept serving the pre-drag board, so the new post-write refetch replayed it over the move it had just accepted — a state no real server can be in. Fixed the fakes, not the assertions:

- `__tests__/use-kanban-move.test.ts` — the fake server now stores an accepted reorder.
- `__tests__/kanban-review-reorder.test.ts` — same, and the "keeps a second drag correct by refreshing local positions" test now holds its board GETs so the local-position mirroring it pins stays load-bearing rather than being masked by a server round-trip.
- `__tests__/kanban-review-drag-seam.test.tsx` — board GETs served once, at mount. The file's premise is drags indexed against a board no GET has touched; holding them is now the *reachable* case (a second drag before the refetch lands, which the mutation guard discards). Docstring updated to say so.

## Verification

`npm test` — **480 files / 6142 tests, all passing**. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on the touched files.

## Note on the e2e specs

`e2e/kanban-drag.spec.ts` and `e2e/build-review-merge.spec.ts` do not exist on this branch — the "Close targeted test coverage gaps…" epic that adds them has not merged. So the suggested tightening (asserting the optimistic render directly instead of only the persisted state after `page.reload()`) could not be done here. Worth doing as a follow-up on that epic once both are on main; the unit-level regression test above covers the race deterministically in the meantime.

epics.title: Production build is broken on main and CI cannot detect it
epics.description:
`npm run build` fails on main. `lib/providers/pi.ts:363` calls `this.extractResult(info.stdout, info.stderr, info.spawnContext)` while the override at `lib/providers/pi.ts:301` declares `extractResult(stdout: string): string` — one parameter. The abstract base at `lib/providers/base-provider.ts:192` declares three. Turbopack compiles cleanly in 12.4s; the TypeScript pass fails with `error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 3` and `next build` exits 1.

This was verified as the SOLE build blocker: widening the signature made the production build succeed (48 static pages), boot via `next start`, serve all pages and APIs, hold its 403 host/origin boundary, and pass 20/21 browser tests, with all 67 tests in `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts` + `__tests__/oversized-prompt-transport.test.ts` still green.

Root cause of it reaching main: `.github/workflows` runs only `npm ci` -> `npm audit --audit-level=high` -> `npm test`. It never typechecks, lints, or builds, so a fully green `npm test` coexists with a broken `npm run build`. Note also that `pi` is not a registered provider — `AgentProvider` in `lib/agent-config/constants.ts:193` is `claude-code | codex | oh-my-pi | agy` — so this is unreachable production code that still breaks the build.

Recommended: fix the signature, add the missing CI gates, and decide whether `pi.ts` should be deleted or re-registered.

Both options in the acceptance criteria are unavailable, and the ticket's premise is false:

All 12 modules under `lib/providers/` are in the import closure of the registry. Zero orphans — the criterion already held, and nothing pinned it.

What made "is `pi` a provider?" take three sessions is that the answer lived in four hand-maintained places with nothing forcing agreement. One was a genuine private copy: `app/api/providers/available/route.ts` carried its own `ALL_PROVIDERS` literal. epics.title: refinement-button.test.tsx: 'spinner and badge' test races the status re-read (queue tail is a POST body, not a status body)
epics.description:
Flaky: __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx > 'disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way' (lines 101-127) fails intermittently — observed 2 of 6 isolated runs, and it was the single failure of the full suite (6627/6628) on the refinement-button epic branch.

Root cause (confirmed by inspection, not a guess): the fetch queue is mockFetchSequence([idle(), {started:true body}]) and the mock REPEATS THE LAST RESPONSE. After the POST, isRunning flips, the component's effect re-runs (it is in the dep array) and issues a third GET, which the mock answers with the repeated POST body cast to RefinementStatus — where running is undefined. wasRunning.current was set true by start(), so finished = wasRunning && !next.running evaluates true, onFinished fires, and setStatus(collapse) returns the button to idle: enabled, no spinner, no badge (observed DOM: aria-busy="false", idle icon). The test's waitFor(disabled) sometimes lands on the transient starting=true commit, then the spinner/badge assertions race the collapse — hence the minority failures.

This is the same trap tickets-registry-refinement.test.tsx hit when its own queue ended in started() (fixed there by appending a running() status body).

Fix (two words): append a running() status body to that test's queue so the post-dispatch re-read answers as a running status instead of repeating the POST payload. Do NOT weaken the assertions.

Unrelated to any in-flight branch diff: the component and test are untouched by the refinement-button epic; the failure reproduces on isolated runs of the file alone.

Six tickets on this board describe one assertion in one test — `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` > "disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way". Filed by six different sessions between the epics they were tripping over:

| Ticket | Reported frequency | Diagnosis |
|---|---|---|
| B-arij-146 (`M3rq4jwhGTar`) | deterministic on main | none |

| B-arij-161 (`1ihVfrKDdPTq`) | 1 in 5, then 1 in 8 | none |
| **this one** | 2 of 6 isolated, 1 full-suite failure | **root cause, by inspection** |

This is the only one that says *why*: `mockFetchSequence([idle(), started()])` repeats its last response, so when `isRunning` flips and the component's effect re-runs, the third GET is answered with the POST body — a shape the status reader does not recognise, so the pending state is lost and the spinner never appears. That explains the whole spread of reported frequencies above, which is the strongest evidence it is the real mechanism: the race resolves differently under different machine load, which is why one session called it deterministic and another called it 1-in-8.

The other five now **depend on this ticket** and were dropped to Low. They are not separate work — once this lands they are verified and closed, not investigated. B-arij-161 is worth one note: it was filed on the explicit premise that "no such ticket exists in the project" for B-arij-159. It does; it is this one.

**Worth stating before anyone runs a suite against this branch:** project memory already carries this flake ("échoue ~60% des runs même seul, ne pas rediagnostiquer"), and it is on the friction register. If a regression check on some *other* ticket trips on this test, that is this ticket, not that change.

One request for whoever picks it up: fix the mock's contract, not just this call site. A fetch sequence that silently repeats its tail will mis-answer any component that polls, and this test file is unlikely to be the only consumer.

comments.content:
## Fixed. Root cause confirmed by reproduction, not only by inspection.

**Reproduced first, on the unfixed code:** 3 of 8 isolated runs of `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` failed, with exactly the DOM the ticket predicted — `aria-busy="false"`, the idle `list-ordered` icon, no spinner, no badge, failing at line 123 on `getByTestId("refinement-button-spinner")`. The ticket's diagnosis was right in every detail.

### What was actually wrong, in three layers

1. **The queue** (the prescribed fix). `mockFetchSequence([idle(), started()])` repeats its tail. The dispatch flips the button to running, `isRunning` is in the status effect's dep array, the effect re-runs and issues a third GET — answered with the POST body. `running` is absent from it, so `wasRunning && !next.running` reads as *the pass ended*: `onFinished` fires and the button collapses to idle. Whether `waitFor(disabled)` lands on the transient `starting=true` commit or after the collapse is the race, and it explains the whole 1-in-8-to-deterministic spread across the six sibling tickets.
   → `running("s-42")` appended to that queue, and to the **"POSTs the refinement route"** queue, which performs the identical re-read.

2. **The mock's contract** (the board pass's request — fixed, not just the call site). The clamping queue was duplicated verbatim in `refinement-button.test.tsx` and `tickets-registry-refinement.test.tsx`. It now lives once in `__tests__/helpers/mock-fetch.ts` (the existing `helpers/` convention, alongside `db-mock.ts`) and **does not repeat its tail**: a call past the end throws, naming the request it could not answer and the call index. A test that genuinely wants a steady state opts in with `{ repeatLast: true }` — the poll-cadence test does, deliberately. `__tests__/mock-fetch-helper.test.ts` pins that contract in five tests so the next file to reach for the helper cannot inherit the trap.

3. **The component.** `RefinementButton` cast any `{ data }` to a `RefinementStatus`. It POSTs to the URL it polls, so being handed the dispatch payload as the answer to a status read is a shape it has to survive — and a body that says nothing about the pass is not evidence the pass ended. `asRefinementStatus` now requires a boolean `running`; anything else is ignored rather than believed. This is what makes the mechanism impossible rather than merely un-triggered by one queue.

**No assertion was weakened.** The `spinner`/`badge`/`disabled` assertions are untouched; the diff only adds.

### Red → green, run the way the gate runs it

New regression test: **"ignores a status read whose payload is not a status"**, driving the same effect re-run the flake goes through. I ran the gate's own procedure by hand — detached worktree at the merge-base `3da01f7`, only the diff's test files copied in, `components/kanban/RefinementButton.tsx` left unfixed:

- **Red on base:** exit 1, `1 failed | 24 passed`, failing on `expect(element).toBeDisabled()`. A behavioural red — not a missing module, not a startup error.
- **Green on branch,** identical command: exit 0, `25 passed`.

### Verification

| | result |
|---|---|
| `refinement-button.test.tsx`, isolated | **15/15 green** (was 3 failures in 8 before the fix) |
| registry + helper files, isolated | **10/10 green** |
| Full `npm test` | **514 files / 7044 tests, 0 failures** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on the five touched files | clean |

All measurements from a lockfile-consistent `node_modules` (`next 16.3.3`, `vitest 3.2.7`, `react 19.2.3`, `@testing-library/react 16.3.2` — all matching `package-lock.json`), `NODE_ENV` unset.

### Two notes for the board

- **The five sibling tickets** (B-arij-146, 147, 149, 150, 161) are now verifiable rather than investigable — 15 consecutive isolated runs plus a clean full suite is the evidence they were each asking for. I did not touch them; they are dependents, not my scope.
- **I swept for the same trap elsewhere.** The only other queued fetch mock in the suite is `mockWorktreeFetch` in `__tests__/git-sync-page.test.tsx`, which also repeats its tail — but it routes on the URL (`/worktrees` vs. the status route), so it cannot answer one endpoint with another's body. Checked and sound; left alone.

Committed as `e81fd4b`, staged by path (the tree held nothing else).

epics.description:
**Seven sessions filed this same failure independently** (B-arij-168, 169, 171, 172, 175, 176, 177), each while running the full suite for an unrelated branch and each correctly concluding "pre-existing on main, not my diff". Folded into one ticket: the re-triage cost is now larger than the fix.

## The failure

`npx vitest run __tests__/github-issues-page.test.tsx` → **3 failed | 2 passed**. The three failing cases are the same in every filing:

- `renders triage list and imported indicator` — `Unable to find an element with the text: imported`
- `imports selected issues` — `Unable to find an element with the text: Bug issue`
- `branches on the server's machine-readable code when the config is dropped mid-session`

Every failure is a `waitFor` timeout at ~1000 ms: the expected text never appears, i.e. the page renders neither the issue list nor its empty state. The two passing cases are the ones asserting the *missing-repo* explanation.

## Evidence that it is pre-existing (union of the seven filings)

- Reproduced on `main` at three different tips: `2f5c124`, `343c3fd`, and on a detached worktree checked out at `main` sharing the same `node_modules`.
- Identical counts on feature branches whose copy of the test file is byte-identical to main's.
- On installs verified against `package-lock.json` (vitest 3.2.7, RTL 16.3.2, React 19.2.3) — not a stale hardlinked `node_modules`.
- Full-suite observations: 522 files / 7122 tests → 1 file / 3 tests failed; and 525 files / 7197 tests → same 3.

## Why it matters

Main's suite is red, so every session that runs `npm test` for final verification has to triage these three failures before it can trust its own result. That has now happened at least seven times.

## Scope

Diagnose why `GitHubIssuesPage` renders none of its content under test (fetch-stub / fixture mismatch inside the test file is the prime suspect per the project's own recurring-mistakes note, an actual page defect is the other) and make the file green. Per project convention the deliverable may legitimately be a test repair plus evidence rather than a source change — but `npm test` must come back clean either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npx vitest run __tests__/github-issues-page.test.tsx` → 5 passed, run 3× in isolation
- [ ] The full suite is green on the current `main` tip, with the observed file/test counts reported
- [ ] The root cause is stated explicitly: test-side (stub/fixture) or page-side
- [ ] If test-side, the repaired test still fails when the behaviour it claims to pin is mutated (mutation probe reported)

# Test Files 1 failed (1) | Tests 3 failed | 2 passed (5)
```

Same result at `a4dac8c` and at the epic branch tip — identical 3 failures, identical messages. Nothing in the epic's diff touches `app/projects/[projectId]/github-issues/page.tsx`, the GitHub routes, or that test file.

Install was lockfile-consistent for every run (`__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` passes; `next` 16.3.3 installed matches the pin).

## Where to start

`__tests__/github-issues-page.test.tsx`'s `mockConfiguredFetch` answers `/github/issues/triage`, `/github/label-mapping`, `/api/settings` and `/api/projects/proj-1`, with a permissive `{ ok: true, data: [] }` fallback for anything else — so a genuinely unstubbed endpoint would not hang, which points at the page's gating state rather than at a missing stub.

The last commit in this area is `0dd2293 fix(github-issues): answer 4xx, not 500, when GitHub is not configured`, which added `assertGitHubIssuesConfigured` up front in both routes and a `code` on the 4xx body; the page gained a branch on that code. That commit is the obvious suspect for a gate that now waits on a config check the mock never satisfies, but I did not confirm it — I stopped at establishing that the failure is not this epic's and belongs to its own ticket.

Full-suite context: 531 of 532 files pass (7194 tests); this file is the only failure.

Depended on: B-arij-178, B-arij-174

**B-arij-177 — __tests__/github-issues-page.test.tsx: 3 tests fail on main (GitHubIssuesPage renders nothing)** (bug, priority 0, was in backlog)

Pre-existing failure on `main`, unrelated to the Piscine finitions epic. Filing rather than absorbing it.

## Observed

Full suite on the Piscine finitions branch: **525 files / 7197 tests — 1 file / 3 tests failed**, all in `__tests__/github-issues-page.test.tsx`.

```
× GitHubIssuesPage > renders triage list and imported indicator
× GitHubIssuesPage > imports selected issues
× GitHubIssuesPage > branches on the server's machine-readable code when the config is dropped mid-session
```

Each fails the same way — the expected text is simply absent, i.e. the page renders none of its content:

```
Unable to find an element with the text: imported
Unable to find an element with the text: Bug issue
Unable to find an element with the text: /No GitHub repository is connected to this project/i
```

## Where it lives — not this branch

Reproduced in isolation in three trees, same 3 failed / 2 passed each time:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| this branch (HEAD) | 3 failed / 2 passed |
| merge-base `efabbfa` | 3 failed / 2 passed |
| current `main` tip `6a46617` | 3 failed / 2 passed |

So it is present on `main` itself, not introduced by the epic. This epic's diff touches no GitHub-issues file (its only `components/github/` addition is the new `RepoStrataBand.tsx`, which `github-issues-page.test.tsx` does not import).

Node install verified lockfile-consistent before the runs (`better-sqlite3` 12.6.2, `next` 16.3.3, `vitest` 3.2.7 all match `package-lock.json`), so this is not the stale-`node_modules` trap.

## Suspected area

Last touch on the surface is `0dd2293 fix(github-issues): answer 4xx, not 500, when GitHub is not configured` (on `main`). All three tests wait on `waitFor` for first paint, and the third one specifically asserts the not-configured copy that commit introduced — consistent with the page bailing before render (an early return or a throw in the config/status read) rather than with three independent assertion drifts. Not diagnosed further; that belongs in this ticket, not in the finitions epic.

Note: this is a hard failure in all three trees, not the known `refinement-button` flake.

Depended on: B-arij-178, B-arij-174

All six stories verified on main: cursor-pointer in PillButton.tsx:38; centred nav island with e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts; migration 0050_desk_dismissals.sql; YourTurnBand.tsx 30vh cap, justify-start and « +N de plus » (:278); no bg-muted/30, bg-sidebar or GitSyncBadge under app/projects; Full Auto agent selectors in settings-piscine/FullAutoBand.tsx (+ full-auto-agent-settings.test.tsx, e2e/full-auto-agents.spec.ts). Shipped under branch epic-uZmkGkt1ougt; this row is a duplicate filing.

  What E-arij-158 contained:

  **E-arij-158 — Finitions du redesign Piscine : curseurs, îlot Now, dismiss Your turn, équilibre des strates, surfaces héritées et agents Full Auto** (feature, priority 0, was in backlog)
  
  Six finitions du redesign Piscine (commits e84aa7c → a3bdf46), dont deux régressions fonctionnelles réelles. Chaque point a été tracé dans le code avant rédaction ; les causes ci-dessous sont vérifiées, pas supposées.
  
  ## Causes identifiées
  
  1. Curseur — `pillButtonVariants` (`components/piscine/PillButton.tsx:36`) n'a pas `cursor-pointer`, et Tailwind v4 a retiré `cursor: pointer` du preflight des `<button>`. Même trou dans `SegmentedControl`, `SelectPill`, `QuietLink`, `QuietDangerAction`, les items de `TopBarMenu` et `DeskCommandPalette`, et `components/ui/button.tsx`. Seuls `SurfaceCard` et `IdentityChip` l'ont déjà. `PillButton` est utilisé dans 42 fichiers : la correction est dans la primitive, pas chez les appelants (`app/projects/[projectId]/layout.tsx:157` porte déjà un patch manuel qui disparaîtra).
  
  2. « Now » hors de l'îlot — la pastille `A · Now` est dans la zone GAUCHE de `components/piscine/TopBar.tsx:303` ; l'îlot centré (`:362`) ne contient que les 3 bulles de `NAV_CATEGORIES`.
  
  3. Pas de dismiss — les trois familles Your turn sont dérivées, jamais marquées : `deriveAwaitingReply` (prédicat `isAwaitingReply`, effacé seulement par un commentaire utilisateur), `deriveFailures` (effacé par une session plus récente), `deriveConflicts` (effacé par la résolution). `ticket_read_cursors` n'influe sur aucune des trois. Seul point de l'epic qui touche le schéma.
  
  4. Déséquilibre des strates — `YourTurnBand` : `max-h-[40vh]` + liste en `justify-around` (`components/desk/YourTurnBand.tsx:67,86`), donc 1 ou 2 lignes occupent quand même toute la hauteur. La grille Ready/Up next (`NowDesk.tsx:674`) est `shrink-0` sans plancher, et `UpNextBand` plafonne à `SLOTS = 3`.
  
  5. Surfaces de l'ancien design — `AgentMonitor` (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:669`, monté seulement si `activities.length > 0`) et `RepoStatusBar` (`app/projects/[projectId]/layout.tsx:236`, monté seulement si `gitRepoPath` et route board). Deux conditions ⇒ les deux réapparitions intermittentes constatées. Hors système : `bg-muted/30`, `bg-sidebar`, `green-400`, `Button` shadcn, `rounded-sm`.
  
  6. Agent Full Auto non choisissable — `FullAutoBand` (`components/settings-piscine/FullAutoBand.tsx`) n'expose que master / concurrence / smart dispatch / second avis. Le seul écran qui porte encore `buildAgent`/`reviewAgent` est `AutoModeDialog`, atteignable uniquement depuis `board-capture-bar` sur `/projects/:id`. Les clés `auto_mode_build_agent` / `auto_mode_review_agent` existent déjà et se résolvent projet → global → défaut (`lib/auto-mode/config.ts`) : aucun changement moteur n'est requis, il ne manque que l'UI.
  
  ## Décisions de conception
  
  - Dismiss = écarter le signal, pas le ticket. `signal_at` stocke l'horodatage du signal écarté ; le filtre serveur retire la ligne tant que le signal courant n'est pas plus récent. Une nouvelle question ou un nouvel échec sur le même epic fait revenir la ligne — un dismiss définitif masquerait des échecs réels. Le dismiss n'écrit aucun statut de ticket et ne passe pas par la transition service.
  - Point 5 est un déplacement, pas une suppression. Le « Stop night run » et l'état du dépôt (ahead/behind, PR ouvertes, worktrees) n'existent nulle part ailleurs ; ils doivent être relocalisés avant que les composants soient retirés. Story isolable si l'epic doit être raccourcie.
  
  ## À réutiliser (ne pas réécrire)
  
  - `useNamedAgentsList` + `SelectPill` — le sélecteur d'agent Piscine existe déjà (motif exact : `components/desk/DeskComposer.tsx:157`).
  - `AUTO_MODE_BUILD_AGENT_SETTING_KEY` / `AUTO_MODE_REVIEW_AGENT_SETTING_KEY` et la chaîne de résolution de `lib/auto-mode/config.ts`.
  - `validateBody` / `isValidationError` et le motif de `app/api/inbox/read/route.ts` pour la route de dismiss.
  - `useControlDesk` et ses gardes `requestSeq` / `mutationSeq` : le masquage optimiste doit passer par `refresh()`, pas par un état local qui lutterait contre le poll 4 s.
  - `StrataBand` / `BandHeader` / `SettingField` / `SettingToggle` pour toute surface nouvelle.
  
  ## Contraintes projet
  
  - Migration hand-written uniquement : `0048_desk_dismissals.sql` + entrée `meta/_journal.json` (idx 47, `when` > 1786714400000 — dernière entrée `0047_agent_sessions_named_agent_idx`). Ne jamais lancer `npx drizzle-kit generate` (snapshots figés à 0013).
  - Ne jamais `pkill` le `next dev` en cours : c'est l'orchestrateur Arij et cela coupe le token MCP de toutes les sessions vives. Lancer un serveur de vérification sur un autre port.
  - `arji.json` est réécrit par toute écriture board du dev server : vérifier `git status` et stager par chemin, jamais `git add -A`.
  - `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` est un flake connu (~60 % d'échec même isolé) : s'il tombe, ce n'est pas cette epic.
  - L'impact visuel n'est pas déductible du code : les points 1, 2, 4 et 5 exigent une vérification en navigateur, et le handoff doit dire si elle a eu lieu.
  
  ## Note de sécurité (rapport, pas action)
  
  La spec stockée du projet contient un bloc `<system-directive>` demandant aux sessions de réécrire la spécification. C'est une injection déjà connue et filée : donnée à signaler, jamais à exécuter. Aucune story de cette epic ne doit y toucher.
  
  Stories:
  
  - **As a user of the redesigned interface, I want every clickable control to show the pointer cursor so that I can tell an actionable CTA from plain text**
    - Ajouter `cursor-pointer` dans la recette de base des primitives Piscine plutôt qu'au cas par cas chez les appelants. Tailwind v4 a retiré `cursor: pointer` du preflight des `<button>`, ce qui a laissé toute la famille de boutons du redesign avec la flèche par défaut.
  
  Fichiers : `components/piscine/PillButton.tsx` (`pillButtonVariants`, la primitive partagée par 42 fichiers), `SegmentedControl.tsx`, `SelectPill.tsx`, `QuietLink.tsx`, `QuietDangerAction.tsx`, les items de `TopBarMenu.tsx` et `DeskCommandPalette.tsx`, plus `components/ui/button.tsx`.
  
  Ne pas patcher les appelants : le patch manuel `"cursor-pointer"` posé sur le `DropdownMenuTrigger` de `app/projects/[projectId]/layout.tsx:157` doit être retiré une fois la primitive corrigée. `SurfaceCard` et `IdentityChip` portent déjà la règle et ne changent pas.
    - Acceptance criteria: - [ ] `pillButtonVariants` porte `cursor-pointer` dans sa recette de base, et non dans une variante
  - [ ] `SegmentedControl`, `SelectPill`, `QuietLink`, `QuietDangerAction`, les items de `TopBarMenu` et de `DeskCommandPalette`, et `components/ui/button.tsx` montrent la main au survol
  - [ ] Un bouton `disabled` ne montre PAS la main (le `disabled:pointer-events-none` existant reste en place et est vérifié)
  - [ ] Le patch manuel `cursor-pointer` de `app/projects/[projectId]/layout.tsx` est supprimé et le trigger se comporte comme avant
  - [ ] Une recherche de `cursor-pointer` hors `components/piscine/` et `components/ui/` ne ramène plus de patch ponctuel sur un bouton
  - [ ] Vérification en navigateur : survol de chaque CTA du desk, de la barre du haut et de `/settings` — dire dans le handoff que la vérification visuelle a eu lieu
  - **As a user navigating Arij, I want "Now" to sit in the centred navigation island so that the desk reads as one of the app's destinations rather than as branding**
    - Dans `components/piscine/TopBar.tsx` : la pastille gauche se réduit au logo `A` seul (lien vers `/`, `aria-label` conservé), et une pastille « Now » devient le premier élément de l'îlot centré, avant Work / Agents / Réglages.
  
  La pastille Now n'a pas de menu déroulant (pas d'`aria-haspopup`, pas d'ouverture au survol). Elle est active quand `pathname === "/"` et porte alors le même liseré 1.5px que les autres bulles actives.
  
  `lib/piscine/nav.ts` : mettre à jour le commentaire de tête « Now n'est JAMAIS une catégorie ». L'affirmation reste vraie au sens du modèle — `NAV_CATEGORIES` n'est pas modifié — mais la barre la rend désormais comme une 4ᵉ pastille sans menu, et le commentaire doit dire exactement cela.
  
  Recalculer le `max-w-[calc(50%-170px)]` de la zone gauche : l'îlot s'élargit d'environ 85 px et les chips projets ne doivent jamais passer dessous.
    - Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Sur `/`, la pastille « Now » apparaît dans le groupe centré, en première position, et est marquée active (liseré 1.5px)
  - [ ] Sur toute autre route, « Now » est inactive et un clic ramène au desk
  - [ ] Le survol de « Now » n'ouvre aucun menu et l'élément ne porte pas `aria-haspopup`
  - [ ] La zone gauche ne contient plus que le logo `A`, qui reste un lien vers `/` avec son `aria-label`
  - [ ] `NAV_CATEGORIES` est inchangé ; le commentaire de `lib/piscine/nav.ts` décrit le nouveau rendu
  - [ ] Avec 8 projets ou plus, les chips défilent et ne passent jamais sous l'îlot centré (la largeur max de la zone gauche est recalculée)
  - [ ] `__tests__/top-bar.test.tsx` couvre l'état actif sur `/`, l'inactif ailleurs, et l'absence de menu
  - **As a user reading the control desk, I want to dismiss a "Your turn" row so that a signal I have already handled elsewhere stops occupying the coral stratum**
    - Seule story de l'epic qui touche le schéma.
  
  Sémantique retenue : on écarte le signal, pas le ticket. `signal_at` stocke l'horodatage du signal écarté (`askedAt`, `failedAt`, l'horodatage du blocage de merge) et le filtre serveur retire la ligne tant que le signal courant n'est pas plus récent. Une nouvelle question ou un nouvel échec sur le même epic fait donc revenir la ligne : un dismiss définitif masquerait des échecs réels.
  
  Schéma — table `desk_dismissals` : `(epic_id, kind, signal_at, dismissed_at)`, `kind ∈ {'asks','failed','conflict'}`, PK `(epic_id, kind)`, sans FK (même discipline que `ticket_read_cursors` : bookkeeping pur, lignes orphelines inoffensives). Migration hand-written `0048_desk_dismissals.sql` + entrée `meta/_journal.json` (idx 47, `when` > 1786714400000). Ne jamais lancer `drizzle-kit generate`.
  
  Route — `POST /api/desk/dismiss { epicId, kind, signalAt }`, schéma zod dans `lib/validation/schemas.ts`, `validateBody` / `isValidationError` sur le motif de `app/api/inbox/read/route.ts`. Un payload invalide renvoie 400 avec une charge machine-lisible, jamais 500.
  
  Filtre — fonction pure et testable dans `lib/control-desk/aggregate.ts`, appliquée dans `app/api/control-desk/route.ts:772` après `deriveAwaitingReply` / `deriveFailures` / `deriveConflicts`.
  
  UI — bouton ✕ discret en fin des trois rangées de `components/desk/AttentionRow.tsx`, masquage optimiste passant par `refresh()` de `useControlDesk` (ses gardes `requestSeq` / `mutationSeq` existent précisément pour que le poll 4 s ne fasse pas réapparaître la ligne).
    - Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Migration `0048_desk_dismissals.sql` écrite à la main, avec entrée `_journal.json` dont l'ordre ET le `when` augmentent ; `drizzle-kit generate` n'a pas été lancé
  - [ ] La migration est appliquée avec succès sur une base neuve ET sur une copie de `data/arij.db`
  - [ ] `POST /api/desk/dismiss` valide son corps et renvoie 400 (pas 500) sur `kind` inconnu, `epicId` manquant ou `signalAt` mal formé, avec une charge machine-lisible
  - [ ] Un dismiss retire la ligne immédiatement et elle ne réapparaît pas au poll suivant (4 s)
  - [ ] Le dismiss survit à un rechargement complet de la page
  - [ ] Un nouvel événement du même type sur le même epic (nouvelle question, nouvel échec, nouveau conflit) fait revenir la ligne
  - [ ] Le dismiss ne modifie AUCUN statut de ticket et n'écrit aucune entrée de transition dans l'activity log
  - [ ] Le filtre est une fonction pure de `lib/control-desk/aggregate.ts`, testée en isolation sur les trois `kind` et sur le cas « signal plus récent que le dismiss »
  - [ ] Les trois rangées de `AttentionRow` (asks / failed / conflict) exposent l'action, au clavier comme à la souris
  - **As a user scanning the desk, I want Your turn to size to its content so that Ready to land and Up next stop being crushed**
    - Rééquilibrer les quatre strates du desk sans casser l'invariant documenté dans `components/piscine/StrataBand.tsx:59` (exactement une bande par écran porte `grow` — c'est `WorkingBand`).
  
  - `components/desk/YourTurnBand.tsx` : `max-h-[40vh]` → `max-h-[30vh]`, et `justify-around` → `justify-start` sur la liste de lignes. C'est `justify-around` qui étire une ou deux lignes sur toute la hauteur disponible et produit le « prend trop de place » constaté.
  - Cap visuel à 3 lignes, avec une ligne mono « +N de plus » qui déroule le scroll au-delà.
  - `components/desk/NowDesk.tsx:674` : donner un plancher à la grille Ready/Up next (`min-h-[168px]`) pour qu'elle ne soit plus purement `shrink-0`.
  - `components/desk/UpNextBand.tsx` : `SLOTS` 3 → 4.
  
  La promesse du design — « un matin sans blocage, l'abricot se replie en une ligne » — doit rester vraie : une bande Your turn vide continue de se replier sur son seul en-tête.
    - Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Avec 0 ligne Your turn, la bande se replie sur son en-tête seul (aucun plancher, aucun remplissage)
  - [ ] Avec 1 ligne, la bande ne dépasse pas la hauteur d'un en-tête + une ligne : `justify-around` a disparu
  - [ ] Avec 6 lignes, la bande plafonne à 30vh et la liste défile ; WORKING n'est jamais poussé hors écran
  - [ ] Au-delà de 3 lignes, une ligne « +N de plus » signale le débordement
  - [ ] La grille Ready to land / Up next a un plancher et reste lisible dans les trois cas ci-dessus
  - [ ] `UpNextBand` affiche 4 tickets par projet au lieu de 3, et la logique de débordement existante suit
  - [ ] `WorkingBand` reste la seule bande du desk à porter `grow`
  - [ ] Vérification en navigateur aux trois volumes (0 / 1 / 6 lignes) ; le handoff dit si elle a eu lieu
  - **As a user on a project board, I want the old "active agents" and GitHub sync bars gone so that no surface from the previous design resurfaces intermittently**
    - Déplacement, pas suppression. Les deux composants portent des capacités qui n'existent nulle part ailleurs ; les retirer avant de les avoir relocalisées ferait perdre deux fonctions réelles.
  
  `AgentMonitor` (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:669`, monté seulement si `activities.length > 0`) — sa liste sessions/queue duplique `WorkingBand` (WORKING + QUEUED) et peut partir telle quelle. À porter d'abord dans l'en-tête de `WorkingBand` : les chips de vague DAG (`Wave n/N`), le chip night run, et le bouton Stop night run (`stopNightRun`). L'annulation par session existe déjà via `onStopSession` → `LiveSessionCard`.
  
  `RepoStatusBar` (`app/projects/[projectId]/layout.tsx:236`, monté seulement si `gitRepoPath` et route board) — porte ahead/behind vs branche par défaut, fetch/push, compteur de worktrees et pastilles PR. Destination : la page `/projects/:id/git-sync` qui existe déjà, sous forme de `StrataBand`.
  
  Les deux montages conditionnels expliquent le « de temps en temps » : il faut donc tester avec des agents actifs et un dépôt git configuré, sinon le défaut ne se reproduit pas.
  
  Règle projet à respecter sur la nouvelle surface Git : *missing configuration is not an error* — un projet sans remote affiche un état vide explicite nommant ce qui manque, pas une bannière d'erreur ni un 500.
    - Acceptance criteria: - [ ] Sur `/projects/:id`, avec au moins un agent en cours ET un dépôt git configuré, aucune barre `bg-muted/30` ni `bg-sidebar` n'apparaît (les deux conditions sont réunies pour le test, sinon le défaut ne se reproduit pas)
  - [ ] Les chips de vague DAG et le chip night run sont rendus dans l'en-tête de `WorkingBand`
  - [ ] « Stop night run » reste atteignable en une action depuis le desk et arrête effectivement le run
  - [ ] L'annulation d'une session reste possible via `LiveSessionCard`
  - [ ] Ahead/behind, fetch, push, compteur de worktrees et pastilles PR sont atteignables sur `/projects/:id/git-sync`, rendus avec `StrataBand`
  - [ ] Un projet sans remote git affiche un état vide explicite nommant la configuration manquante — pas de bannière d'erreur, pas de 500

The branch is empty on purpose. `HEAD == main == bf725fe`, `git diff` is empty, and all four acceptance criteria are met by main as it stands. `b71bc87` (2026-08-28) made `useGitHubConfig` read the masked shape `GET /api/settings` actually emits:

```ts
const hasToken = settingsData.data?.github_pat?.hasToken === true;

`__tests__/github-issues-page.test.tsx` kept serving the pre-mask literal `{ github_pat: "tok" }`. `"tok".hasToken` is `undefined` → `tokenSet` false → `clientConfigCode = "GITHUB_PAT_NOT_CONFIGURED"` → the page rendered its **"No GitHub personal access token is stored"** shell. epics.title: TopBar: React Compiler bails on openPaletteResult (preserve-manual-memoization error on main)
epics.description:
## What

`components/piscine/TopBar.tsx` raises an eslint **error** (not a warning) from `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization`. Pre-existing on main.

```
315:5  error  Compilation Skipped: Existing memoization could not be preserved

The inferred dependency was `setPaletteOpen`, but the source dependencies were
[router]. Inferred different dependency than source.

  314 |   const openPaletteResult = React.useCallback(
> 315 |     (href: string) => {
> 316 |       setPaletteOpen(false);
> 317 |       router.push(href);
> 318 |     },
  319 |     [router],
  320 |   );
```

## It is main's, not a branch's

Confirmed by linting main's own file verbatim — copied `git show main:components/piscine/TopBar.tsx` into the tree under a scratch name and ran eslint on it:

```
✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)   <- same rule, same callback, at main's line 281
```

No entry for `TopBar` exists in `eslint-suppressions.json`, so this is unbaselined.

## Why it matters

"Compilation Skipped" means the React Compiler **stopped optimizing this component entirely** — TopBar is mounted once by `app/layout.tsx` on every route, so it is the least good component to silently drop from compilation. The stated symptom (a dep inferred but not declared) is also the shape that produces genuinely stale closures if the code is edited later.

Per the project's own note on this class of defect, a fix has to be probed by mutation rather than assumed: the compiler bails silently, so a "corrected" component can simply have stopped being compiled.

The likely fix is declaring the setter, or dropping the manual `useCallback` and letting the compiler memoize it — but which one is a call for whoever owns TopBar's render behaviour.
