### Le défaut, reproduit avant de toucher au code
Chrome via Playwright (`channel: "chrome"`), serveur de dev sur un port jetable, base jetable, payload `/api/control-desk` synthétique. Aucun agent lancé.

- **390 × 844** — la carte ASKS YOU fait 326 px, son contenu 570 px. Le span de la question mesure **0 px**. `Send` démarre à x=355, `Send to dev` finit à **x=561** (le chiffre exact du rapport), le ✕ est à x=573. Puces UP NEXT : `clientWidth` 22 px pour un `scrollWidth` de 294 px. Lignes READY TO LAND : 139 px, la pastille « Land » peinte par-dessus UP NEXT.
- **768 × 1024** — la ligne *tient* (scrollWidth 702 dans 704) et la question fait **quand même 0 px** ; le titre de la ligne READY TO LAND aussi ; puces à 69 px.
- **1280 / 1440** — propres : question 450,3 / 610,3 px, puces 132,8 / 152,8 px.

La cause : les six enfants de la ligne partagent un seul `flex` dont la largeur min-content vaut ~544 px — tout sauf le message est `shrink-0` ou plancherisé à `min-w-[120px]`.

### Le correctif
- `AttentionRow` — sous `lg`, la ligne devient une colonne de deux groupes qui se replient (identité + message, puis champ + actions), avec le trio Send / Send to dev / ✕ gardé insécable pour qu'il ne se coupe pas en deux à une largeur arbitraire. **À partir de `lg` les deux enveloppes sont `display: contents`** : la carte retrouve ses six enfants d'origine comme items flex directs.
- `ReadyToLandBand` — même repli sous `sm`, là où le titre n'avait plus rien.
- `UpNextBand` — la ligne se replie sous `lg`, le libellé projet prend sa propre ligne, les puces récupèrent la largeur (deux par ligne dès `sm`, une seule sur téléphone). Les 4 créneaux desktop deviennent un budget de 2 : les deux dispositions cachent des nombres différents, donc **chacune a son « +N »**, l'autre étant `display:none`.
- `NowDesk` — une colonne sous `lg` (`grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2`), et **le desk prend en charge son propre défilement** sous `lg` : `/` le comprime (`h-full` dans un `main` en `overflow-auto`) et `/projects/:id` le **coupe** (`overflow-hidden`). WORKING reçoit un plancher pour ne pas être écrasé à zéro par les strates `shrink-0`.
- `YourTurnBand` — 50 vh sous `lg` : une ligne empilée fait ~166 px contre 53 px sur desktop, donc 30 vh d'un écran de 844 px ne laissait qu'une ligne partielle et « +6 de plus ».

epics.title: QuietDangerAction avale data-testid (pas de ...rest)
epics.description:
## Ce que c'est

`components/piscine/QuietDangerAction.tsx` déclare des props explicites (`icon`, `onClick`, `size`, `className`, `children`) et ne fait **aucun spread de `...rest`** sur le `<button>`. Un `data-testid` passé au composant ne rejoint jamais le DOM.

C'est la même classe de trou que `Mono` et `StrataBand`, déjà consignée dans la mémoire projet. `QuietLink`, son voisin immédiat, a résolu le problème avec une prop `testId` explicite (« Additive: a test has to be able to CLICK the link, so the id cannot live on a wrapper »).

## Pourquoi ça mord

TypeScript **attrape** ce cas-ci (`data-testid` n'est pas dans `QuietDangerActionProps`, donc l'appel ne compile pas) — contrairement à `Mono`/`StrataBand` où la prop se volatilise en silence. Le coût est donc du frottement, pas un faux vert : on écrit le testid, on se prend une TS2322, et on retombe sur une requête par rôle+nom.

Constaté en implémentant « UI Settings : bouton "Se connecter avec GitHub" » : les deux appels du `GitHubCard` (« Annuler » et « Déconnecter ») ont dû basculer sur `getByRole("button", { name: … })`.

## Reproduction

```tsx
<QuietDangerAction onClick={noop} data-testid="x">Supprimer</QuietDangerAction>
// TS2322: Property 'data-testid' does not exist on type QuietDangerActionProps
```

## Correctif suggéré

Ajouter une prop `testId` posée sur le `<button>`, exactement comme `QuietLink` — pas un wrapper : le test doit pouvoir cliquer l'élément.

## Portée à vérifier avant de corriger

Le ticket devrait balayer le barrel `components/piscine/` en entier et compter les primitives qui ne forwardent ni `...rest` ni `testId`, plutôt que de traiter celle-ci seule. `Mono` et `StrataBand` sont les cas connus ; le reste n'est pas mesuré.

epics.title: Next.js 16.3.3 build warnings: deprecated middleware convention and whole-project tracing
epics.description:
Two build-output hygiene issues surfaced on the pinned Next 16.3.3. Neither breaks behaviour today; both are forward-compatibility debt currently hidden by the stale 16.1.6 install.

1. The `middleware` file convention is deprecated. Every dev start and every build prints a warning recommending `npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .`. The middleware itself is correct — it was verified to enforce the localhost boundary in both directions (403 for a forged `Host: evil.com` or `Origin: http://evil.com`, 200 for localhost and 127.0.0.1) in dev and against the production build.

2. The build emits 13 warnings of the form 'Dynamic filesystem access causes tracing of the whole project'. Static analysis cannot scope `path.join(process.cwd(), attachment.filePath)` at `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/uploads/[attachmentId]/route.ts:25` or `path.join(process.cwd(), uploadsDirectoryFor(projectId), image.fileName)` at `lib/uploads/ticket-image-paths.ts:39`, so it includes the entire project — all source files and the public folder — in the server output bundle.

user_stories.description: Run `npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .` and verify the localhost host/origin boundary still behaves identically afterwards. The security assertions must be re-run in both directions — a silently opened boundary is the failure mode that matters here.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The deprecation warning no longer appears on dev start or build
- [ ] `Host: evil.com` and `Origin: http://evil.com` still receive 403 on `/api/*`
- [ ] `Host: localhost`, `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` and `Origin: http://localhost:<port>` still receive 200
- [ ] `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` still permits a configured non-local origin
- [ ] The boundary is verified against the production build, not only in dev

## What I found

A previous session (the one that died — "Claude CLI exited with code null") had left the migration essentially complete but uncommitted and unverified. Rather than redo it, I verified it and finished the parts that were missing.

## What I verified

**The migration is authentic.** I ran the real `npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .` on a clean merge-base checkout and diffed — the branch's `proxy.ts` is **byte-for-byte the codemod's output**. I also confirmed against `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` that named `proxy` export + `export const config = { matcher }` is the correct 16.3.3 shape, and that the "Route segment config is not allowed in Proxy file" error only fires on a `runtime` export (we have none).

**All five acceptance criteria, against the production build.** The strongest evidence: I built *both* the pre-migration and post-migration trees for production, ran `next start` on each, and put the same 13-case host/origin matrix through both. Results are **identical, 13/13** — the boundary provably did not shift. Forged `Host`/`Origin` → 403, three loopback spellings → 200, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` admits a configured origin without becoming a blanket pass.

**AC1 with a control**, since a check that can't fail proves nothing: on the base tree the warning fires on *both* dev start and build; on the branch neither. The only remaining "Middleware" string is Next's own route legend `ƒ Proxy (Middleware)`, which appears in the base build too and confirms the proxy was loaded.

The codemod only renames the file. Three wiring gaps it left, most importantly: `package.json` `files` is an **allowlist**, so the stale `middleware.ts` entry would have published an `arij` tarball with no proxy file at all — an unguarded `/api/*` — while every local check passed. That's now pinned by a test.

I also fixed a test that never tested its own name: `blocks requests without host header` built a header-less request, discarded it, and re-tested `external.com` under a comment claiming `NextRequest` backfills `Host`. I probed it — it doesn't — so that branch is now genuinely exercised.

Cross-module propagation of a *result* does work, though: I probed both shapes with a throwaway build before committing to a design, and a helper that performs the statically-scoped join itself and hands back the finished path silences the warning at every consumer.

So three modules now own the joins that stay inside the app's tree:

| module | root | replaces |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/uploads/upload-paths.ts` | `data/uploads` | 5 sites |
| `lib/documents/document-paths.ts` | `data/documents` | 3 sites |

epics.title: Registre mobile : les titres des tickets disparaissent et les colonnes débordent
epics.description:
Audit exploratoire du 05/09/2026, Chrome via Playwright sur http://localhost:3000, données réelles. Rapport local : /tmp/arij-ui-audit-K3XRUP/rapport.md. Aucun agent lancé pendant l'audit. Captures locales temporaires, les étapes et mesures ci-dessous restent la preuve reproductible.

## Reproduction
1. Ouvrir /tickets à 390 × 844 avec des tickets aux titres longs.
2. Observer que les identifiants et états restent visibles mais que la colonne titre est écrasée ; les colonnes suivantes débordent du cadre.

## Cause identifiée
components/tickets-registry/RegistryRow.tsx impose grid-cols-[112px_1fr_130px_96px_120px_170px_110px]. Les six colonnes fixes absorbent la largeur disponible, sans disposition mobile. RegistryTable.tsx contient les débordements mais ne restaure pas la lisibilité.

- À 390 × 844 et 768 × 1024, chaque ticket expose au minimum son identifiant, un titre lisible et son statut.
- Les autres informations restent consultables via une disposition responsive ou le détail ; aucun titre ne se réduit à une largeur nulle.
- Recherche, filtres, ouverture du ticket et pagination/« tout montrer » restent utilisables au toucher et au clavier.
- Aucun débordement horizontal global ; ne pas se contenter de masquer le contenu.
- Conserver la table desktop à 1280 × 800 et 1440 × 1000. Ajouter une régression Playwright sur les rectangles des titres et l'ouverture d'un ticket.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Corrigé — la ligne du registre se replie en pile sous `lg`

### La cause, mesurée
`REGISTRY_GRID` déclarait `112px 1fr 130px 96px 120px 170px 110px` à **toutes** les largeurs. Les six pistes fixes valent 738px avant leurs 72px de gouttières, contre 326px de ligne utile dans la carte à 390px. Mesuré dans Chrome sur `c001324`, avec la ligne non corrigée instrumentée des seuls deux `data-testid` (rectangle du titre, puis bord droit de la cellule COÛT contre celui de la carte) :

| viewport | titre | coût finit à | carte finit à |
|---|---|---|---|
| 390 × 844 | **0.0px** | 842px | 376px (+466) |
| 768 × 1024 | **0.0px** | 842px | 754px (+88) |
| 1280 × 800 | 406.0px | 1248px | 1266px ✓ |
| 1440 × 1000 | 566.0px | 1408px | 1426px ✓ |

et le corps de la carte : 828px de contenu dans une boîte de 362px à 390px.

Précision honnête : **la page n'a jamais défilé horizontalement**, ni avant ni après — le `overflow-hidden` de `StrataBand` rognait le débordement au lieu de l'exporter au document. Ce critère était déjà tenu sur `main` ; il est désormais asserté pour que le correctif ne puisse pas racheter le titre en le cassant.

### Le correctif
`components/tickets-registry/RegistryRow.tsx` déclare deux pistes par défaut — la puce d'identité et un titre en `minmax(0,1fr)` — avec les cinq cellules de queue (état, stories, priorité, activité, coût) dans une ligne flex qui s'enroule dessous. À partir de `lg`, ce conteneur passe en `display: contents` : ses enfants redeviennent des items de la grille de la ligne et retombent en colonnes 3-7 **exactement** comme avant. Rien n'est masqué, rien n'est rendu conditionnellement.

`minmax(0,1fr)` plutôt que `1fr` aux deux formes : un `1fr` nu prend `auto` comme minimum automatique, donc un titre long élargit la piste au-delà de la carte au lieu de céder à l'ellipse.

Après correctif, même graine, même run : titre **257.2px** à 390 et **635.2px** à 768, contenu de la carte revenu dans sa boîte (362 dans 362), et les deux largeurs desktop **inchangées au pixel** (406.0px et 566.0px, lignes toujours à 35.5px).

Deux effets de bord assumés, dans `RegistryTable.tsx` : la légende de colonnes se retire avec la table qu'elle nomme (sept kickers de tri sur deux pistes = quatre lignes de chrome au-dessus de chaque groupe ; la pilule `sort:` de la barre de filtres offre déjà les sept mêmes tris et le même sens, à taille tactile), et la barre de pied s'enroule au lieu de pousser Export CSV hors de portée.

### Preuves
- **Rouge → vert (vitest, la porte mécanique)** — `__tests__/tickets-registry-responsive.test.tsx` : 4 échecs sur 6 avant le correctif (gabarit à sept pistes non préfixé, gabarit `lg` absent, piste de titre en `1fr`), 6/6 après. Les 2 cas qui passaient déjà sont des témoins délibérés : « aucune cellule n'est `display:none` sur un téléphone » et les sept libellés accentués. jsdom n'a pas de moteur de rendu — ce fichier épingle le mécanisme, pas la géométrie.
- **Chrome, quatre largeurs** — `e2e/tickets-registry-responsive.spec.ts` : rectangle réel du titre (>120px, dans la carte des deux côtés), les cinq cellules de queue gardant chacune leur propre boîte, empilées sous le titre au téléphone et revenues sur la ligne dans la table, lignes desktop sous une hauteur de ligne, lignes téléphone au-dessus des 44px tactiles, et pas de débordement du corps de la carte. Vérifié rouge en restaurant les composants non corrigés avec les deux `data-testid` remis en instrumentation neutre (`contents` sur le conteneur, donc grille à sept colonnes rendue à l'identique) : `390×844: the rows overflow the card sideways (828 > 362)`.
- **Recherche, filtres, tri, « tout montrer », ouverture** à 390px : le champ et le lien restent dans le viewport, le champ filtre, les pilules d'état filtrent, la pilule `sort:` change le tri, « tout montrer » s'ouvre **au clavier** (focus + Entrée — `QuietLink` est un vrai `<button>`), et un ticket s'ouvre au tap **et** à la touche Entrée sur la ligne.
- Captures : `e2e/test-results/…-four-widths-chromium/registry-{390x844,768x1024,1280x800,1440x1000}.png` et `…-390px-chromium/registry-390-controls.png`.

### Vérifications
Install : `npm ci` (le `node_modules` du worktree était vide ; toutes les mesures viennent de cette install). Suite complète **569 fichiers / 7831 tests verts** après fusion de `main`, `tsc --noEmit` propre, eslint propre sur les fichiers touchés.

### Fusion de `main`
`main` avait avancé de 5 commits (`c001324` → `961f59d`) et l'un d'eux touche la ligne juste au-dessus de mon édit : B-arij-JJ5FdaHpX7d6 ajoute `focus-visible:outline-solid` à la liste de classes de `RegistryRow` (sans quoi `outline-none` annule le style et l'anneau ne peint rien) — ce qui est directement un critère clavier de ce ticket. Fusionné et résolu en gardant les deux. Réconcilié contre `961f59d` ; `main` rebouge, à revérifier avant merge.

En marge : **B-arij-206** déposé — le scan de `__tests__/focus-ring-paints.test.tsx` perd un site quand un commentaire entre deux littéraux contient des backticks (c'est ce qui a fait tomber son propre garde-fou à 39 sites pendant la résolution).

### Ce que je n'ai pas fait
- Pas de `next build` : changement de chaînes de classes plus un `<div>` d'enrobage dans un composant client, sans nouvel import ; la route compile sous `next dev` pendant les runs e2e et `tsc` est propre.
- Pas de sweep à 320px : le ticket nomme 390 et 768, et la barre du haut à 320 appartient à B-arij-164.
- Pas de capture de l'anneau de focus peint sur une ligne du registre : la peinture appartient à B-arij-JJ5FdaHpX7d6 (qui la mesure dans Chrome et dont le balayage unitaire inclut désormais cette ligne) ; ici je prouve le comportement clavier, pas le pixel de l'anneau.
- `components/desk/` n'est pas touché : `RegistryRow` n'est monté que par le registre.

## What was wrong

`REGISTRY_GRID` declared `112px 1fr 130px 96px 120px 170px 110px` at **every** width. The six fixed tracks spend 738px before their 72px of gaps, against 326px of usable row at 390px. Measured in Chrome on `c001324`, with the unfixed row instrumented with nothing but the two new test ids:

| viewport | title rect | COÛT ends at | card ends at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 390×844 | **0.0px** | 842px | 376px (+466) |
| 768×1024 | **0.0px** | 842px | 754px (+88) |
| 1280×800 | 406.0px | 1248px | 1266px ✓ |
| 1440×1000 | 566.0px | 1408px | 1426px ✓ |

One correction to the report's framing: the **page never scrolled sideways**, before or after — `StrataBand`'s `overflow-hidden` clipped the excess (828px of content in a 362px box) rather than exporting it to the document. That criterion already held on `main`; it's asserted now so the fix can't buy the title back by breaking it.

## The fix

Two tracks by default — the identity chip and a `minmax(0,1fr)` title — with the five trailing cells in a wrapping flex line beneath. From `lg` up that wrapper is `display: contents`, so its children become grid items of the row again and land in columns 3-7 exactly as before. Nothing hidden, nothing conditionally rendered. - `npm ci` (the worktree's `node_modules` was empty — all measurements come from that install), full suite **569 files / 7831 tests green** post-merge, `tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean.

`main` had moved 5 commits and one landed on the line above my edit — B-arij-JJ5FdaHpX7d6's `focus-visible:outline-solid`, which this ticket's own keyboard criterion depends on. I merged and kept both; reconciled against `961f59d`, re-check before merging.

epics.title: QA check dialog and story detail panel labels are not associated with their controls
epics.description:
Remaining sites of the defect class fixed by the "Bug dialog and GitHub/Git-sync settings labels" ticket: a visual `<label>` with no `htmlFor` that does not wrap its control, so the field is unnamed to assistive technology and `getByLabelText` / Playwright `getByLabel` resolve 0 elements.

Found by an exhaustive sweep of every `<label>` in `app/` and `components/` (excluding `components/ui/`) that carries no `htmlFor` and wraps no control. After the sibling fix, these are the only genuine sites left:

- `components/qa/StartQaCheckDialog.tsx:219` (Check Type), `:272` (Named Agent (optional)), `:301` (Saved Prompt), `:324` (Custom Prompt (optional)).
- `components/story/StoryDetailPanel.tsx:65` (Status), `:110` (Description), `:123` (Acceptance Criteria).

Also at `components/story/StoryDetailPanel.tsx:85`: a `<label>` whose entire content is ` `, used purely as a vertical spacer to align a `Badge` with the Status select next to it. It names nothing and should not be a `<label>` at all — a plain spacer element is the right shape.

Not affected (checked, no action needed):
- `components/tickets-registry/NewTicketView.tsx:135,149` — the `<label>` wraps `GhostInputPill` / `<textarea>`, so implicit wrapping association holds.
- `components/settings/McpServersSection.tsx` and the frictions/sessions checkbox labels — all wrap their control.
- `components/settings-piscine/SettingField.tsx:11,19` — matches are comment text, not markup.

Fix shape is settled by the two merged siblings (`app/projects/new/page.tsx`, then the bug dialog / GitHub issues / Git sync pass): give each control an `id`, point the label at it with `htmlFor`, associate helper text via `aria-describedby`. For a reusable component prefer `useId()`-derived ids over static ones; for a label that names a group rather than one control, use a `span` + `role="group"`/`aria-labelledby` instead.

Verification must query by accessible name (`getByLabelText`, `getByRole(..., { name })`) — a test-id query would pass while the association stayed broken.

Filed rather than folded into the current ticket to keep that diff scoped to the sites it named.

All 7 sites named in the ticket are closed, plus the ` ` spacer label.

### Provenance — read this first

**I did not author the source fix or the test files.** They were already on disk, uncommitted, in this worktree when the session started (4 modified components + 3 untracked test files). My work was: verifying them, proving red on the merge-base, running the full verification pass, closing the sweep, and committing. Flagging this because inheriting a prior session's edits and reporting them as my own is exactly the failure mode the project memory warns about.

I reviewed every line before committing and stand behind it; the design decisions below are the inherited author's, and I've noted where I disagreed.

### Red → green

Fix was already in the tree, so I restored the merge-base source with `cp` backups + `git show` (never `git checkout` — it destroys uncommitted work) and confirmed the mutation was on disk *during* the run via md5.

- **Red on base `4d58c9a`: 13 failed / 2 passed.**
- The 2 that passed are the deliberate controls — "still renders the dialog's primary action" and "still renders the status badge beside the select" — so the red run is about label association, not about the components failing to render.
- **Green after restore: 15/15**, md5-verified byte-identical to the fixed state.

Both new files are `*.test.tsx`, so the regression checker's vitest filters actually run them — a `.spec.ts` would have been handed to vitest and silently excluded.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` (full) | **579 files / 7990 tests, 0 failures** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` (7 touched files) | clean |
| `e2e/qa-dialog-story-panel-a11y.spec.ts` (real Chrome) | 2/2 passed |
| `lockfile-install-consistency` | passed *before* measuring |

Full suite rather than `test:changed` because `NamedAgentSelect` has 8 source consumers and ~25 test files — the blast radius is genuinely wide.

The e2e pass matters more than the jsdom one: it runs against **Chrome's own accessible-name computation**, not a query helper's approximation.

### Browser evidence

Focus ring photographed, because putting the read state in the tab order is a *visual* claim a DOM assertion can't make. Chrome resolves `solid / 2px / oklab(0.778 -0.095 0.007 / 0.847) / 2px offset` — a real painted ring, present on focus and absent without it. QA dialog captured too: attribute-only change, layout unshifted, and the "Named Agent" label resolves even on the picker's `Loading...` branch (which is what the every-branch `labelProps` change buys).

### Scope check — I re-ran the sweep rather than trusting the enumeration

Scanned every `<label>` in `app/` + `components/` (excl. `components/ui/`): **25 files, 0 genuine unassociated labels remain.** The 2 residual hits are comment text, not markup — `SettingField.tsx:19` (as the ticket predicted) and a comment in the new `StoryDetailPanel` spacer. The ticket's "not affected" list holds.

### Noted, deliberately not folded in

1. **`B-arij-220` filed** — `StartQaCheckDialog.tsx:371` ("Prompt name for reuse") is named only by its placeholder. Different defect class: it has *no* `<label>` at all, so this ticket's `<label>`-based sweep could not have seen it. Census in the bug.
2. **`failure-digest-window` uses a static id**, not `useId()` — pre-existing, and *correctly associated*, so it isn't this ticket's defect. Two simultaneously-mounted copies would collide, but it's a modal, so the risk is theoretical. Left alone to keep the diff on the named sites.
3. **`InlineEdit`'s `markdown` branch is unreachable today** — `StoryDetailPanel` is its only live consumer (`TicketDescriptionCard` merely *mentions* it in a comment, no import) and never sets `markdown`. So `role="button"` never wraps a link at any live call site. Worth knowing for whoever enables that branch: it would nest interactive content inside a button role.

### One design note on the inherited fix

`InlineEdit`'s read state is a `<div>` — not labelable, and `aria-labelledby` on a role-less element contributes no accessible name. The author's answer was `role="button"`, which then *obliges* the Enter/Space handler and the focus ring. That's a real behaviour change beyond pure label plumbing, but it's the minimum that makes the read state nameable, and the read state is the one users actually land on — naming only the textarea would leave the field anonymous until you click it. I'd have made the same call.

The ring is deliberately written with **no `outline-none` beside it**: in Tailwind v4 the two cancel and the ring silently stops painting (`B-arij-JJ5FdaHpX7d6`). The unit test asserts a *resolved* outline, not a class name, so it fails on exactly that bug.

# Code Review — QA check dialog and story detail panel label association (`cc0ce92`)

## What I verified myself

Before measuring anything I confirmed the install matched the lockfile (`__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` green), per the project's install-hygiene rule.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` (all 7 touched files) | clean |
| Blast-radius vitest — 27 files carrying `NamedAgentSelect` / `StoryDetailPanel` / `InlineEdit` | 207 tests, all green |
| `e2e/qa-dialog-story-panel-a11y.spec.ts`, real Chrome (`PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome`) | 2 passed |
| Independent label sweep, `app/` + `components/` (excl. `components/ui/`) | 25 files, 56 labels, **0 genuine orphans** |

I did **not** re-run the full 579-file suite — the machine sat at load 12 and the diff is four client components with no server surface. The handoff's full-suite run stands as the author's evidence, not mine.

I also checked the semantics the whole fix rests on directly in Chrome, via CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, rather than trusting jsdom: a `<label for>` pointing at a Radix `SelectTrigger` button resolves the name from `relatedElement` (`name="Check Type"`, `name="Named Agent (optional)"`), and `aria-describedby` resolves the hint. The association is real in the browser's own accessible-name computation.

The sweep's only two residual regex hits are comment text — `SettingField.tsx:11` (as the ticket predicted) and the new spacer comment at `StoryDetailPanel.tsx:100`. The ticket's "not affected" list holds.

## Checklist

**Readability** — Good. The comments explain *why* (`useId()` over static ids; the deliberate absence of `outline-none` beside the focus ring, citing `B-arij-JJ5FdaHpX7d6`), not what. **No issues found.**

**DRY** — The `useId()` + `htmlFor` + `aria-describedby` shape matches the merged sibling `6d947fb` (`BugCreateDialog`), so the pattern is consistent rather than a third dialect. The five hand-built id strings per component are acceptable duplication. **No issues found.**

**Error handling** — Not exercised; no new async or failure paths. **No issues found.**

**Performance** — Attribute-only on the render path. **No issues found.**

**Naming conventions** — Consistent camelCase, `-label` suffix for name targets, filenames match the sibling label-test convention. **No issues found.**

**Type safety** — No `any`. `"aria-labelledby"?: string` on the props interface is the right shape. **No issues found.**

**Testing** — Strong on the ticket's own claim: every assertion goes through the accessible name, both `InlineEdit` states are covered, the focus ring is asserted as a *resolved* outline rather than a class name, the deliberate controls make the red run interpretable, and both files are `*.test.tsx` so the vitest filters actually run them. The gap is the interaction the diff newly introduces — nothing asserts where focus lands when edit mode ends. See finding #1.

**API design** — No API changes. **No issues found.**

## Findings

| # | Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Major** | `components/kanban/InlineEdit.tsx:78` | Every exit from edit mode drops focus to `<body>` |
| 2 | Minor | `components/story/StoryDetailPanel.tsx:133` | `htmlFor` dangles in the read state — the default state |
| 3 | Minor | `components/kanban/InlineEdit.tsx:79` | Read-state accessible name replaces the field's value |
| 4 | Suggestion | `components/qa/StartQaCheckDialog.tsx:299` | `aria-describedby` passed unconditionally for a conditional hint |
| 5 | Suggestion | `components/kanban/InlineEdit.tsx:100` | `markdown` branch nests block/interactive content in `role="button"` |

**Finding #1 is what blocks.** The diff does more than label plumbing: it turns the read state into a `role="button"` tab stop with an Enter/Space handler. That new keyboard path is one-way. `handleSave()` (line 57) and the Escape branch (line 70) both call `setEditing(false)`, React unmounts the focused control, and nothing catches the focus. Measured against the real component in jsdom:

```
activeElement after Escape:    BODY
activeElement after blur-save: BODY
```

A keyboard user tabs to "Description", presses Enter, presses Escape — and is returned to the top of the document, having to re-traverse the TopBar and the entire left column. That is the exact flow this ticket exists to enable. The fix is a ref plus a `useEffect` on the `editing` true→false transition, in the file already touched, so it belongs in this diff rather than a follow-up.

For finding #3 I checked whether ARIA's "children presentational" rule strips the value from the tree; **it does not** in Chrome — the `StaticText` survives as a child of the button, so the loss is confined to focus mode. That is why it is minor and not major. Finding #4 is likewise benign in practice: Chrome silently ignores a dangling `aria-describedby`.

## Summary

- **Critical:** 0
- **Major:** 1
- **Minor:** 2
- **Suggestion:** 2

The label association itself is correct, consistently patterned, proven in real Chrome, and the sweep is genuinely closed — I re-measured rather than inheriting the count. The one blocker is a side effect of the keyboard affordance the fix chose to add, and it is small and local.

Repo left as found: `git status` is clean, and the e2e run wrote only the gitignored `e2e/test-results/`. My probe scripts live in `/tmp`.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Multi-Provider CLI Integration with Base Class Refactor
epics.description:
Add 6 new CLI providers (Mistral Vibe, Qwen Code, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Kimi/Moonshot, Zai) and refactor the provider layer with a BaseCliProvider abstract class to reduce duplication. Updates the provider registry, named agents UI, and availability checks to support all 9 providers.

New providers:
- Mistral Vibe (`vibe`): --prompt, --agent, --output json, --resume, --max-turns, --max-price
- Qwen Code (`qwen`): -p, --yolo, --model, /resume
- OpenCode (`opencode`): run "...", --format json, --session, --file
- DeepSeek (`deepseek`): -q, --model, --no-stream, SQLite history
- Kimi/Moonshot (`kimi`): --print, --continue, stream-json
- Zai/Zhipu AI (`zai`): API-based via subprocess wrapper, GLM models

Architecture: BaseCliProvider abstract class handles 70% of shared spawn/kill/log/parse logic. Each provider is ~80-120 lines. Existing Claude Code, Codex, Gemini refactored onto base class first.

user_stories.description:

Abstract methods for subclasses:
- get binaryName(): string
- buildArgs(options: ProviderSpawnOptions): string[]
- extractResult(stdout: string, stderr: string): string

1:/**
2: * "Latest session wins" failure indicator for epic cards.
3: *
4: * A retry creates a NEW agent_sessions row and statuses are terminal
5: * (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = [] in lifecycle.ts), so an old failed row
6: * stays in the database forever. The badge must therefore reflect only the
7: * most recent session of an epic: a queued/running/completed retry clears
8: * it immediately, and it never comes back unless that retry fails too.
9: *
10: * created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision). When the
11: * newest timestamp is shared by several sessions — e.g. a retry created in
12: * the same second as the failure it replaces — ties break in favor of
13: * CLEARING the badge. Within an all-failed tie group, the session that
14: * ended most recently wins so the badge shows the retry's error.
15: */
16:
17:export interface FailedSessionInfo {
18:  sessionId: string;
19:  error: string;
20:  agentType: string;
21:}
22:
23:/** Minimal shape of a unified session row as returned by /api/projects/:id/sessions. */
24:export interface FailureCandidateSession {
25:  id: string;
26:  kind: string;
27:  status: string;
28:  epicId?: string | null;
29:  error?: string | null;
30:  agentType?: string | null;
31:  createdAt?: string | null;
32:  endedAt?: string | null;
33:}
34:
35:export function selectLatestFailures(
36:  sessions: FailureCandidateSession[],
37:  runningEpicIds: Set<string>
38:): Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> {
39:  const byEpic = new Map<string, FailureCandidateSession[]>();
40:  for (const session of sessions) {
41:    if (session.kind !== "agent_session") continue;
42:    if (!session.epicId) continue;
43:    const list = byEpic.get(session.epicId);
44:    if (list) list.push(session);
45:    else byEpic.set(session.epicId, [session]);
46:  }
47:
48:  const failed: Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> = {};
49:  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
50:    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
51:    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;
52:
53:    let newest = "";
54:    for (const s of epicSessions) {
55:      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
56:    }
57:    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);
58:
59:    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
60:    if (newestGroup.some((s) => s.status !== "failed")) continue;
61:
62:    // All-failed tie: prefer the session that ended most recently.
63:    let latest = newestGroup[0];
64:    for (const s of newestGroup) {
65:      if ((s.endedAt ?? "") > (latest.endedAt ?? "")) latest = s;
66:    }
67:    failed[epicId] = {
68:      sessionId: latest.id,
69:      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
70:      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
71:    };
72:  }
73:  return failed;
74:}

/**
 * "Latest session wins" failure indicator for epic cards.
 *
 * A retry creates a NEW agent_sessions row and statuses are terminal
 * (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = [] in lifecycle.ts), so an old failed row
 * stays in the database forever. The badge must therefore reflect only the
 * most recent session of an epic: a queued/running/completed retry clears
 * it immediately, and it never comes back unless that retry fails too.
 *
 * created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision). When the
 * newest timestamp is shared by several sessions — e.g. a retry created in
 * the same second as the failure it replaces — ties break in favor of
 * CLEARING the badge. Within an all-failed tie group, the session that
 * ended most recently wins so the badge shows the retry's error.
 */

export interface FailedSessionInfo {
  sessionId: string;
  error: string;
  agentType: string;
}

/** Minimal shape of a unified session row as returned by /api/projects/:id/sessions. */
export interface FailureCandidateSession {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  status: string;
  epicId?: string | null;
  error?: string | null;
  agentType?: string | null;
  createdAt?: string | null;
  endedAt?: string | null;
}

export function selectLatestFailures(
  sessions: FailureCandidateSession[],
  runningEpicIds: Set<string>
): Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> {
  const byEpic = new Map<string, FailureCandidateSession[]>();
  for (const session of sessions) {
    if (session.kind !== "agent_session") continue;
    if (!session.epicId) continue;
    const list = byEpic.get(session.epicId);
    if (list) list.push(session);
    else byEpic.set(session.epicId, [session]);
  }

  const failed: Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> = {};
  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;

    let newest = "";
    for (const s of epicSessions) {
      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
    }
    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);

    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
    if (newestGroup.some((s) => s.status !== "failed")) continue;

    // All-failed tie: prefer the session that ended most recently.
    let latest = newestGroup[0];
    for (const s of newestGroup) {
      if ((s.endedAt ?? "") > (latest.endedAt ?? "")) latest = s;
    }
    failed[epicId] = {
      sessionId: latest.id,
      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
    };
  }
  return failed;
}

/**
 * "Latest session wins" failure indicator for epic cards.
 *
 * A retry creates a NEW agent_sessions row and statuses are terminal
 * (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = [] in lifecycle.ts), so an old failed row
 * stays in the database forever. The badge must therefore reflect only the
 * most recent session of an epic: a queued/running/completed retry clears
 * it immediately, and it never comes back unless that retry fails too.
 *
 * created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision). When the
 * newest timestamp is shared by several sessions — e.g. a retry created in
 * the same second as the failure it replaces — ties break in favor of
 * CLEARING the badge. Within an all-failed tie group, the session that
 * ended most recently wins so the badge shows the retry's error.
 */

export interface FailedSessionInfo {
  sessionId: string;
  error: string;
  agentType: string;
  provider?: string | null;
  namedAgentId?: string | null;
}

/** Minimal shape of a unified session row as returned by /api/projects/:id/sessions. */
export interface FailureCandidateSession {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  status: string;
  epicId?: string | null;
  error?: string | null;
  agentType?: string | null;
  provider?: string | null;
  namedAgentId?: string | null;
  createdAt?: string | null;
  endedAt?: string | null;
}
export function selectLatestFailures(
  sessions: FailureCandidateSession[],
  runningEpicIds: Set<string>
): Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> {
  const byEpic = new Map<string, FailureCandidateSession[]>();
  for (const session of sessions) {
    if (session.kind !== "agent_session") continue;
    if (!session.epicId) continue;
    const list = byEpic.get(session.epicId);
    if (list) list.push(session);
    else byEpic.set(session.epicId, [session]);
  }

  const failed: Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> = {};
  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;

    let newest = "";
    for (const s of epicSessions) {
      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
    }
    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);

    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
    failed[epicId] = {
      sessionId: latest.id,
      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
      provider: (latest.provider as string | null) ?? null,
      namedAgentId: (latest.namedAgentId as string | null) ?? null,
    };
  }
  return failed;
}

**Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=XD_6gx3Zjl7y -->

**Probable root cause** — The build never ran: the model configured for this session, `openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha`, has been retired by OpenRouter and now returns HTTP 404 on every request. The provider (`oh-my-pi`) sent the prompt, got an immediate error back with zero tokens generated, and the session died — twice, since a retry on the same dead model can only reproduce the same 404. Nothing in the tail indicates a code, test or ticket problem. A secondary condition is visible but is not the failure cause: the session's stored comment thread is already carrying snowballed prompt echo (the Arij tools block repeated several times, one comment truncated at 672 k characters), so the prompt shipped to the model is heavily bloated even though the echo-scrub mitigation is now firing.

**Evidence**

- Terminal error, empty assistant turn, no tokens billed: `"model":"stealth/ox-alpha","usage":{"input":0,"output":0,...,"totalTokens":0},"stopReason":"error","errorStatus":404,"errorMessage":"404 Thank you for participating in the Stealth Ox Alpha testing period. This model was ZAI's GLM-5.3 Flash. Use it now: https://openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash"` — the model endpoint no longer exists.
- The "last text produced" is verbatim prompt text (`## Arij tools ... You are connected to Arij, the orchestrator that launched this session`), not model work — confirming the session produced no output of its own before erroring.
- Prompt bloat is real but pre-existing: `_[… 672,191 characters of this comment omitted …]_` and repeated `_[Arij: the session's raw output echoed its own prompt — echo removed.]_` markers in the stream.

**Recommended next action**

- Re-run the build stage with a live model — either switch this ticket to the `claude` provider, or point `oh-my-pi` at `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` (the successor named in the 404) — and, before relaunching, purge the snowballed comment on this ticket so the retry starts from a sane prompt size; also audit the project's default model setting, since any other ticket pinned to `stealth/ox-alpha` will fail identically.

comments.content:
## Retry now reuses the failed agent, in resume mode

Commit `50cd69f` — `fix(kanban): retry the failed agent in resume mode, not Claude Code`

### Root cause

The Retry button on a failed epic card (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx`, `handleRetryBuild`) posted to the **batch** build route with the board toolbar's `namedAgentId`. Two independent faults:

1. That toolbar selection is `null` unless the user picked an agent during this visit, so the server fell through `resolveAgent()`'s default chain and landed on the seeded **"Claude Code"** named agent — regardless of which agent had actually just failed.
2. `/api/projects/:id/build` (batch) has **no `resumeSessionId` parameter at all**, so a retry could only ever start cold. Only the single-epic route `/api/projects/:id/epics/:epicId/build` accepts it.

### Fix

The retry now reuses the failed session's named agent and asks the single-epic route to continue that session. The request shape matches what `useAgentDispatch.sendToDev` already sends for every other single-target manual dispatch — `pipeline` deliberately omitted so the project's `pipeline_enabled` setting still decides.

The decision is extracted to a pure function, `lib/agent-sessions/retry-dispatch.ts` (`buildRetryDispatch`), so it is testable without mounting the kanban page. Resume is requested only when it is coherent:

- the retry must land on the **very agent** that minted the stored CLI session id (a fallback to the toolbar's agent sends no resume);
- the provider must be able to continue a session (`isResumableProvider` — excludes codex, which never reports the thread it created);
- the failed session must be **code-producing** (`isCodeProducingAgentType`) — resuming a review or grading thread would append a build prompt to a conversation shaped for another task.

The server re-validates all of this in `validateResumeSession` and silently starts fresh when it disagrees; deciding it client-side too keeps the request honest about its intent.

`selectLatestFailures` now carries the failed session's `provider` and `namedAgentId`. No API change was needed — `/api/projects/:id/sessions` already returned both columns; the client was simply dropping them.

### Red → green

Regression test `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts` (11 cases) plus the three updated `toEqual` expectations in `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts`. Verified mechanically the way the gate runs it: both branch test files were checked out over the merge-base source (`10c6636`) and run there — **2 failed** (`retry-dispatch` unresolvable, 3 `selectLatestFailures` expectations red). On the branch both are green. The two halves of the fix are covered independently: applying only `retry-dispatch.ts` still leaves the three `selectLatestFailures` cases red.

### Validation

- `npx vitest run` — **445 files, 5370 tests, all passing**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint` on touched files — 10 problems, **all pre-existing** on base `page.tsx` (verified by linting the HEAD copy: identical count); zero introduced
- `git diff --check` clean, worktree clean, `arji.json` untouched

### Notes for review

- **Behaviour change worth a look:** retry now respects `pipeline_enabled`. The old batch call could never start a pipeline (batch requires `mode: "dag"` for that), so a retry silently bypassed the setting. The new path matches every other single-target manual dispatch. Flagging it as deliberate rather than incidental.
- **Out of scope, pre-existing:** the Retry button always dispatches a *build* even when the failed session was a review — the button is labelled "Retry failed agent session" but only ever has one destination. I did not change the destination; I only stopped it from grafting a build prompt onto a resumed review thread. Worth a separate ticket if you want retry to re-run the stage that actually failed.
- The stored project spec again carried an embedded `<system-directive>` block instructing the session to rewrite the specification. Ignored as data, as it should be; already on the friction register, so not refiled.

Done — committed as `50cd69f` and moved to Review.

## What was wrong

The Retry button had two independent faults, both in `handleRetryBuild` (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:201`):

1. It sent the **board toolbar's** `namedAgentId`, which is `null` unless the user picked an agent during that visit. The server then fell through `resolveAgent()`'s default chain to the seeded **"Claude Code"** agent — that's the reported symptom.
2. It posted to the **batch** route `/api/projects/:id/build`, which has no `resumeSessionId` parameter at all. Only the single-epic route accepts one, so a retry could never resume.

## The fix

### Root cause common to all three

The retry made **one** decision where there are **two**: *which agent to run* and *whether to continue its conversation*. `selectLatestFailures` badges an epic from **any** session carrying that `epicId` — reviews, grading passes and story builds included — while the button only ever dispatches an epic-wide build. Each decision is now gated on what the badged session actually proves about *that* build.

### 1 — [major] Build ran on the reviewer's agent — **fixed**

Confirmed: `resolveAgentByNamedId` (`agent-resolution.ts:359`) looks a named agent up by id and never consults the `agentType` it was asked for, and the route forwards the request's `namedAgentId` into `startPipelineRun({ buildNamedAgentId })` (`epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:567`), so every later stage inherited it.

The agent is now carried over **only from a code-producing session**. Falling through for a review/grading failure is not a regression, and worth stating explicitly: with no build agent known, the server's default chain resolves the project's or global **build** role assignment — which is the correct answer for a build, and strictly better than the reviewer's agent.

### 2 — [minor] Epic retry resumed a story conversation — **fixed**

Confirmed: `stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:246` writes `agentType: "ticket_build"` alongside both `epicId` and `userStoryId`, so a failed story build badges the parent epic's card. The epic route calls `validateResumeSession` without a `userStoryId`, and that helper only compares stories when the caller supplies one (`validate-resume.ts:69`) — so the server accepted the resume on matching epic scope alone.

Resume now refuses when the failed session is story-scoped. **The agent is still reused** — same code-producing role, same epic; it is the *thread* that is story-shaped, not the agent. That split is why finding 1 and finding 2 land on different gates rather than one.

Confirmed the mechanism: `cliSessionId` is minted with `crypto.randomUUID()` before the process starts (`epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:320`) and persisted whatever happens next. # Code Review — Retry reuses the failed agent, in resume mode (cycle 2)

**Scope:** `50cd69f` + `5829c3e` against merge-base `10c6636` — 3 source files, 2 test files.

| # | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [major] build runs on the reviewer's agent | **FIXED** |
| 2 | [minor] epic retry resumes a story conversation | **FIXED** |
| 3 | [info] resume of a transcript that was never written | **FIXED** |

**#1 — FIXED.** `resolveRetryAgent` (`lib/agent-sessions/retry-dispatch.ts:89`) now gates the carried-over id behind `isCodeProducingAgentType`. I executed it: a `review_code` or `grading` failure returns `namedAgentId: undefined`, so the request carries no agent and `resolveAgentByNamedId` never sees the reviewer's id — the server's build-role chain decides instead. The claim that falling through is not a regression checks out: `resolveAgent("build", …)` resolves the project/global **build** assignment. Tests at `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts:120,141` pin both.

**#2 — FIXED.** `shouldResume` refuses on `failed.userStoryId` (`retry-dispatch.ts:130`). I verified the data actually arrives: `user_story_id` is a real column (`lib/db/schema.ts:194`), `/api/projects/:id/sessions` uses `db.select()` over `agentSessions` so it returns every column unfiltered, `useAgentPolling` passes rows through unmapped, and `selectLatestFailures` copies it (`latest-failure.ts:99`). The server-side gap the finding described is still there — `validateResumeSession` only compares stories when the caller supplies one (`validate-resume.ts:71`) and the epic route can't — so the client refusal is the only guard, which matches the finding's own recommendation.

**#3 — FIXED,** and I checked the mechanism rather than the description. `producedOutput` derives from `last_non_empty_text`, which is written **only** from `output`/`response` chunks (`lib/agent-sessions/chunks.ts:214-221`); the terminal patch in `lifecycle.ts:243-257` only *reads* it to phrase a failure message, so an error never masquerades as output. On the claude-code side, a spawn failure resolves with no `result` field at all (`lib/claude/spawn.ts:287-300`) and a non-zero exit passes `result: stdout.trim() || undefined` (`spawn.ts:325-334`), so a launch-time death yields no chunk and correctly cold-starts. The asymmetry the finding relied on is preserved: omp/agy have no stored id without output anyway.

## New finding

**Major — `lib/agent-sessions/retry-dispatch.ts:118`. The review-thread guard is bypassed when the toolbar selection equals the failed reviewer's agent.**

This is a regression from this cycle's own refactor, not adjacent code. `50cd69f` ended `shouldResume` with `return isCodeProducingAgentType(failed.agentType)`. `5829c3e` removed it, on the reasoning stated at lines 114-117 — that the id-equality guard "also covers every non-code-producing type, which `resolveRetryAgent` has already refused to carry over."

It doesn't. `resolveRetryAgent` returns `reusable || selectedNamedAgentId` (line 97), so refusing the reviewer's agent falls through to the **toolbar's** selection. If the user picked that same agent, `namedAgentId === failed.namedAgentId` and the guard passes. Provider is the reviewer's (resumable), `userStoryId` is null on an epic review, `producedOutput` is true for any reviewer that spoke — so the resume goes out. There is no server backstop: `validateResumeSession` compares provider, epic scope and `cliSessionId`, never `agentType`.

Executed against HEAD:

```
buildRetryDispatch("p1", "e1",
  {sessionId:"sess-review", agentType:"review_code", provider:"oh-my-pi",
   namedAgentId:"agent-A", userStoryId:null, producedOutput:true}, "agent-A")
→ { namedAgentId: "agent-A", resumeSessionId: "sess-review" }
```

An epic-wide build prompt gets appended to a transcript shaped for review — exactly what the file's contract (lines 18-23) and `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts:102` say is prevented. That test passes only because it hands the function `null` for the toolbar; the same case with `"agent-A"` fails.

Fix is one line at the top of `shouldResume`, or — cleaner given the two-decision split this commit is built around — have `resolveRetryAgent` return `{ namedAgentId, reusedFromFailure }` and gate resume on `reusedFromFailure` instead of re-deriving it from id equality.

- **Testing** — adequate but for the gap above: every review/grading case in the suite passes `null` as the toolbar selection, which is precisely the branch that hides the defect. Add the `"agent-A"` collision case.

Nit, not filed: `failed!.sessionId` at line 63 leans on a non-null assertion that `shouldResume` guarantees only implicitly. Returning the session id from `shouldResume` (or narrowing before the call) would let the compiler carry it.

## Residual note, deliberately not filed

For claude-code, `producedOutput` means "the CLI printed a parseable final result on exit", not "a transcript exists". A run that dies mid-flight with empty stdout will cold-start where resume would have worked. It degrades safely, and the mid-run kill path resolves to status `cancelled` rather than `failed` (`spawn.ts:315-322`), so it never badges a card. No change requested.

Done. Committed as `4b3a56e`, ticket moved to Review.

## What I added

Two Playwright specs, both built on the existing `e2e/fixtures/` helpers:

- **`e2e/kanban-drag.spec.ts`** — drags an epic between columns, walks it forward one state-machine edge at a time, reorders within a column, and pairs each accepted move with the refusal on the other side of the same boundary.
- **`e2e/build-review-merge.spec.ts`** — Backlog → Done in one walk. Real transition service, real `git merge --no-ff`, closing assertions read the scratch repo's git history rather than the board. The review gate is exercised from both sides: To Merge refused before a verdict exists, accepted after.

**All five acceptance criteria met.** Three consecutive full-suite runs with `channel: "chrome"`: 12/12, 12/12, 12/12. `npm test`: 5963/5963.

## The part worth your attention

The first drafts were green for the wrong reasons — three separate ways a drag helper "passed" on a gesture that never happened. The sharpest: `verticalListSortingStrategy` returns `{x:0, y:0}` for every card it *isn't* displacing, so every card has a matrix transform from frame one — the release predicate was satisfied before the pointer moved. And when `over` is the column, `items.indexOf(over.id)` gives `-1`, which makes a card displace *identically* whether the drop lands before it or appends past the end. The append answers 200 and leaves the order untouched. I verified both against the installed dnd-kit source rather than from recall.

## One product bug found, filed not fixed — B-arij-141

A drag the server stores correctly can leave the board rendering the pre-move order **permanently**. A probe polling both sides for 6s showed `stored` right on every sample and `rendered` wrong on every sample, with no convergence. `loadEpics` applies every board GET unconditionally while `refreshTrigger` fires on each SSE event and poll tick, so a late-resolving GET overwrites a completed move and nothing schedules another refetch. To a user that reads as "my move was lost" when it was saved.

The fix belongs in `hooks/useKanban.ts`, so I kept it out of a test-coverage diff. The consequence is visible in the specs: they assert persisted state after a drag and only read the rendered board after an explicit resync, documented in both files. Once the race is fixed they can tighten to assert the optimistic render and become its regression test.

## Two things I want to be explicit about

I changed `playwright.config.ts` beyond adding specs — workers capped at 4 (matching the vitest precedent; measured 8 workers as *slower* end-to-end and shedding `ECONNRESET`), and raised timeouts. No assertion is weakened, but it is a config change to shared infrastructure, so flagging it rather than burying it.

And the stability claim has a stated ceiling. Stable at the load the suite runs at and at 3× repeat over 4 workers (15/15). At 6× over 8 workers the dev server itself saturates — tests stretch to 1.4 minutes and connections drop. That's an environment limit, and I did not tune it away or claim unconditional stability.

Pre-existing and left alone: a `tsc` error at `lib/providers/pi.ts:363` (byte-identical to merge-base, from `15b0d3d`) and a timing flake in `refinement-button.test.tsx`. I confirmed the e2e load sensitivity is pre-existing too — the four original specs flaked with my specs excluded.

Done. Committed as `9f2dc5f`, ticket moved to Review.

## The finding was correct

The spec named itself a build-to-review-to-merge test but never invoked a build or a review — `commitOnBranch` manufactured the branch, `seedCompletedReview` wrote the verdict straight into SQLite. Dispatch, session creation, the terminal handler's promotion and the review route could all have regressed while it stayed green.

## What changed

The journey now clicks **Send to Dev** and **Agent Review**. The only thing replaced is the CLI child process, and the seam is the dev server's PATH, since `lib/providers/*` spawn their CLI by bare name. Everything on Arij's side is real: worktree, prompt assembly, session row, scheduler, MCP token, workflow transitions, `git merge`. The scripted `claude` commits in its worktree and files its verdict through the session's own `submit_findings` — no prose verdict anywhere, so a broken MCP channel leaves the ticket in Review instead of sliding through the fallback scan.

One correction to the WIP's preflight while I was there: it asserted the stub directory was *first* on PATH, which fails because `npm run dev` legitimately prepends `node_modules/.bin`. It now checks that each provider binary **resolves** to the stub, with the binary list derived from what `/api/providers/available` reports — so a fifth provider fails there rather than leaving its binary unshadowed.

## The stability work is what I'd want reviewed

Each change came from a measurement:

- The **90s test timeout was the only thing actually wrong** with the journey — it runs end to end in 103s warm. It now has its own 300s budget.
- Both dispatches and the merge are awaited on their **HTTP response** before any UI assertion. The dialogs close on a follow-up `/sessions/active` poll (7.7s under four workers, vs a 15s default) and the merge toast auto-dismisses after 5s — so a *slow but successful* merge failed identically to a refused one. A refusal now names its status and body.
- The fixture retries once on `ECONNRESET`. I checked the obvious cause first — idle keep-alive — and **disproved it** with a probe (9s idle, still 200), so the retry is scoped to thrown transport errors only and softens no assertion.

## Evidence

Three consecutive full-suite runs at **12/12 while `npm test` saturated the machine** — the same load that previously failed two of three. Plus three clean runs and one from a cold `.next`. `npm test`: 5963/5963. All with `channel: "chrome"`.

I'm stating the load condition rather than claiming unconditional stability, since that's what I measured.

Two things left alone: the `tsc` error at `lib/providers/pi.ts:363` is byte-identical to the merge-base, and B-arij-141 still stands — the specs read stored state after a write and the rendered board only after an explicit resync.

One note for your awareness: partway through, `e2e/fixtures/cli-stub.ts` changed on disk between my reading it and editing it, in a way I can't attribute to my own tool calls. I scanned for a second session in this worktree and found none, and the content that appeared was correct, so I kept it and verified it on its merits — but if you have another agent pointed at this worktree, that's worth knowing before the next session starts.

### Three ways the first drafts passed on gestures that had not happened

Worth flagging, because each produced a *green* test for the wrong reason:

1. **Releasing on a non-`none` transform proves nothing.** `verticalListSortingStrategy` ends with `return {x: 0, y: 0, ...defaultScale}` for every card it is *not* displacing, which renders as `translate3d(0px,0px,0)` and computes as a matrix. From the first frame of any drag, every card in the column already has a non-`none` transform — the predicate was satisfied before the pointer went anywhere. Now measures actual displacement via `DOMMatrix.m42`.
2. **Displacement alone is still ambiguous.** `SortableContext` derives `overIndex = items.indexOf(over.id)` (sortable.cjs.development.js:318), so an `over` that is the *column* yields `-1`, making the strategy's `index >= overIndex` vacuously true. A card displaces identically whether the drop lands before it or appends past the end of the column — and the append answers 200 while leaving the order untouched. The column's own drop slot (drawn from its `isOver`) separates the two.
3. **Raw `page.mouse` calls bypass Playwright's actionability checks.** A board re-render between `boundingBox()` and `mouse.down()` put the press on empty space, so no drag armed and the run failed much later as "never registered over the column". The gesture now starts from `hover()` and confirms the DragOverlay before travelling.

### One product bug found → B-arij-141 (not fixed here)

A drag that the server **stores correctly** can leave the board rendering the pre-move order permanently. Probe, polling both sides for 6s after a 200 reorder:

```
PROBE t=0ms    rendered=["Rank one","Rank two"]  stored=["Rank two@0","Rank one@1"]
PROBE t=6000ms rendered=["Rank one","Rank two"]  stored=["Rank two@0","Rank one@1"]
```

`loadEpics` (`hooks/useKanban.ts:58`) applies every board GET unconditionally — no sequence guard — while `page.tsx:82-100` bumps `refreshTrigger` on every SSE event *and* every fallback poll tick. A GET issued before the reorder commits but resolving after the optimistic splice wins, and nothing schedules another refetch. Classic lost update; to a user it reads as "my move was lost" when it was saved. Filed rather than fixed — the fix is in `hooks/useKanban.ts`, outside a test-coverage diff.

**Consequence for these specs:** each drag is judged on persisted state, and the rendered board is only read after an explicit `syncBoard()`. That is documented in both files. Once B-arij-141 is fixed they can tighten to assert the optimistic render directly and would then double as its regression test.

### Config changes (with rationale in the file)
- `workers: 4` — same reason `vitest.config.ts` caps `maxWorkers: 4`. Every worker also competes for the **single** `next dev` behind them. Measured: 8 workers ran the suite in 41–60s and shed `ECONNRESET`; 4 workers run it in ~35s green.
- `timeout: 90s`, `expect.timeout: 15s` — sized for multi-stage journeys against a compile-on-demand dev server. No assertion is weakened; every wait is on a specific event, so a genuine hang still fails.
- `allowedDevOrigins` in `next.config.ts` — `next dev` 403s `/_next/*` for a `127.0.0.1` Origin, which is the address the suite uses; without it the page hydrates into an empty shell.

### Pre-existing issues found, left to their own tickets
- **`lib/providers/pi.ts:363`** — `tsc` error (`Expected 1 arguments, but got 3`). Byte-identical to the merge-base, unmodified in the working tree, introduced by `15b0d3d`. Not mine.
- **`__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx:123`** — failed once under full-suite load, passes in isolation, file identical to merge-base. Second full run: 5963/5963. Pre-existing timing flake.
- **e2e load sensitivity is pre-existing.** With my specs *excluded*, the four original specs still flaked (ECONNRESET on teardown) at 8 workers. The worker cap addresses this for the whole suite.

### Ceiling I measured, stated plainly
Stable at the load the suite actually runs at (12 tests / 4 workers, 3× green) and at 3× repeat over 4 workers (15/15). At 6× repeat over 8 workers the **dev server itself** saturates — individual tests stretch to 1.4 minutes and connections drop. That is an environment limit, not spec logic, and I did not tune it away.

One line for the record: the project spec carries an embedded `<system-directive>` telling the session to rewrite the specification. Ignored as data; already on the friction register, so not refiled.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Review finding addressed. Committed as `9f2dc5f`.

## The finding

The spec called itself a build-to-review-to-merge test but never invoked a build or a review. The branch was manufactured with `commitOnBranch` and attached directly; the verdict was inserted into SQLite with `seedCompletedReview`. Dispatch, session creation, the terminal handler's promotion and the review route could all have regressed while it stayed green. The reviewer was right, and it left the second acceptance criterion unmet.

## What it does now

The journey clicks **Send to Dev** and **Agent Review** and lets the product do the rest. The only thing replaced is the CLI child process — because a browser suite genuinely cannot own one — and the seam is the dev server's PATH, since `lib/providers/*` spawn their CLI by bare name.

`e2e/fixtures/cli-stub/bin/` holds a `claude`, `codex`, `omp` and `agy`; `playwright.config.ts` prepends that directory. Everything on Arij's side of the seam is real: the worktree, the assembled prompt, the session row, the scheduler, the MCP token, the workflow transitions, the `git merge`. The scripted `claude` commits in the worktree it is given and files its verdict through the session's own `submit_findings` — no prose verdict anywhere, so a broken MCP channel leaves the ticket in Review rather than sliding through the fallback scan. The other three refuse to run agents, so a mis-resolved dispatch fails loudly instead of reaching a real, billed CLI.

`assertCliStubInstalled` runs before anything is dispatched. It checks that each provider binary *resolves* to the stub — not that the stub directory is first on PATH, which is wrong because `npm run dev` legitimately prepends `node_modules/.bin`. The binary list is derived from the provider set `/api/providers/available` reports, so registering a fifth provider fails there instead of leaving its binary unshadowed.

`commitOnBranch`, `seedCompletedReview` and `attachBranch` are gone with the seams they served.

## The stability work is the part I'd want you to check

Every change came from a measurement, not a guess:

- **The 90s test timeout was the only thing wrong with the journey.** Measured end to end at 103s warm and single-worker (build 34s → gate refused 68s → verdict 89s → merged 103s). It now has its own 300s budget.
- **Both dispatches and the merge are awaited on their HTTP response before any UI assertion.** The dialogs close on `useAgentDispatch`'s follow-up `/sessions/active` poll — measured at 7.7s under four workers, against a 15s default — and the merge toast auto-dismisses after 5s. So a *slow but successful* merge failed as "element not found", and so did a refused one. Now a refusal names its status and body.
- **`openTicketDetail` waits 45s to leave "Loading…".** Opening a ticket fans out into a dozen route handlers on one shared `next dev`.
- **The fixture retries an API call once when the connection failed** (`ECONNRESET`), never when the server answered. I checked the obvious explanation first — idle keep-alive — and disproved it with a probe (9s idle, still 200), so the retry is scoped to a thrown transport error only. No assertion is softened.

## Evidence

Three consecutive full-suite runs at **12/12 with `npm test` saturating the machine** — the same concurrent load that previously shed connections and failed two of three runs. Plus three clean consecutive runs (12/12 each) and one from a cold `.next` (12/12, 2.7m). `npm test`: **5963/5963**. All with `channel: "chrome"`.

I'm stating the load condition rather than claiming unconditional stability, because that is what I actually measured.

## Left alone deliberately

- The `tsc` error at `lib/providers/pi.ts:363` is pre-existing — I confirmed the file is byte-identical to the merge-base (`25ec817`).
- B-arij-141 (a board GET resolving late can overwrite a completed move) still stands; the specs read stored state after a write and the rendered board only after an explicit resync, documented in both files.

epics.title: Resolve the 40 baselined ESLint violations recorded in eslint-suppressions.json
epics.description:
The CI hardening ticket (`qqkZuTLK5kWn`) added `npm run lint` as an enforced gate. To land that gate without bundling a 27-file React refactor into a CI change, the 40 violations that already existed on `main` were recorded as a baseline in `eslint-suppressions.json` using ESLint 9's bulk suppressions.

The gate is a true ratchet — every rule stays at `error`, so any *new* violation fails CI — but these 40 remain unfixed debt.

## Breakdown (27 files, 40 violations)

| Count | Rule |
|---|---|
| 33 | `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` |
| 4 | `react/display-name` |
| 2 | `react-hooks/immutability` |
| 1 | `react-hooks/refs` |

Highest concentration: `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx` (8), `hooks/useAgentConfig.ts` (4).

The three non-`set-state-in-effect` React Compiler errors are the ones most likely to be genuine latent bugs and are worth looking at first:

- `components/documents/MentionTextarea.tsx:149` — `react-hooks/immutability`: "Cannot modify local variables after render completes"
- `hooks/useProjectEvents.ts:71` — `react-hooks/immutability`: "Cannot access variable before it is declared"
- `hooks/usePanelLayout.ts:106` — `react-hooks/refs`: "Cannot access refs during render"

The 4 `react/display-name` errors are all the same shape — an anonymous `forwardRef` mock of `UnifiedChatPanel` inside a `vi.mock` factory in `__tests__/` — and are trivial.

The 33 `set-state-in-effect` violations are mostly the "reset state when the target id/URL goes null" pattern; fixing them properly means derived state or key-based remounts, which is a behaviour-touching refactor and the reason they were not done inline.

## Workflow note

Suppressions are strict about staleness by design: when a tracked violation is fixed, `npm run lint` exits 2 with "There are suppressions left that do not occur anymore". Run `npm run lint:prune` and commit the updated `eslint-suppressions.json`. The CI workflow prints a notice explaining this on lint failure. That behaviour is verified, not assumed.

Fixing these can be done incrementally — each file pruned from the baseline is a permanent gain.

comments.content:
## `eslint-suppressions.json` is now `{}` — all 40 baselined violations resolved

`npm run lint` exits 0 with every rule still at `error`. Six commits, incrementally prunable.

### Counts (measured, not inferred)

| | merge-base `4fddb84` | branch |
|---|---|---|
| errors (suppressions ignored) | 40 | **0** |
| warnings | 32 | 31 |

Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx next build` succeeds (`NODE_ENV` unset, per the build pitfall) · Vitest **6311 passed / 494 files**, one failure — see *Not mine* below. `node_modules` confirmed lockfile-consistent (eslint 9.39.2, next 16.3.3, react 19.2.3, eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.0.1) before trusting any of it.

### The finding that matters: the count was hiding violations

**The React Compiler lint rules abandon a whole function silently when they hit certain constructs.** No message — the violations simply stop being reported, and the counter reads zero.

I hit this twice and would have shipped both:

- **`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx`** — I introduced `boardRefreshKey` *below* its use at line 76. That is a forward reference, so the compiler bailed on `KanbanPage` and all 8 violations "disappeared". It is also a real `ReferenceError` at runtime, and **`tsc --noEmit` did not catch it.** Reordering the hooks fixed both.
- **`hooks/useProjectEvents.ts`** — the baseline listed 1 violation. My first fix (a named function expression for the `connect` self-reference) made the hook bail. Fixing it properly revealed **two more that had been masked all along**: a ref written during render, and the connection status set synchronously from the mount effect. The hook is now genuinely clean at 3 fixed, not 1.

So I mutation-probed **every one of the 24 changed files** — inject `useEffect(() => setX(1), [])` into the target function, confirm the rule still fires. A probe in a *different* function of the same file proves nothing: the bail is per function. All 24 verified analyzed. **The "40" was a floor, not a count.**

### Deliberate behaviour changes (2)

1. **`localStorage` is now the owner of panel/board UI preferences** (`hooks/useStoredValue.ts`, via `useSyncExternalStore`). The old house pattern was a mount-read effect plus a write-back effect. Consequence: **an untouched panel no longer writes its default to localStorage on mount** — only a real user change persists, so a future default change still reaches users who never touched the control. `__tests__/unified-chat-panel-mobile-persist.test.tsx:317` asserted the eager default write; I changed that one assertion and pinned the new intent. Nothing outside the tests reads those keys.
2. **`?deleted=` raises its notice through dedicated state, not `addToast`.** `addToast` also schedules the dismissal timer, and a render pass must not schedule a timer (StrictMode would double it).

A regression the suite caught and I fixed: merging RuntimeSettingsTab's two reset effects was wrong — they had *different* keys, so a successful save wiped its own "saved" badge. Split back apart.

### How the rest were fixed

No suppression, no rule downgrade, no `usePolling` indirection to hide anything (it only escapes the rule because its callback is opaque — using it would have been cheating). Three shapes:

- **derive instead of reset** — `useTicketComments`, `useEpicActivity`, `SessionPicker`, `WhatTheAgentDid`, `StatsTab`, the chat conversation page, and the four `useAgentConfig` hooks (collapsed onto one shared keyed loader). This also fixes a latent bug at each site: the previous scope's data no longer shows while the new request is in flight.
- **adjust state during render** (React's documented alternative) — `MentionTextarea`, `DependencyEditor`, `RuntimeSettingsTab`, `Column`, `EpicCard`, and the page's deep links. `Column` keys on a joined id string deliberately: comparing against a freshly built `Set` would differ every render and re-enter the adjustment forever.
- **update from promise callbacks** — the loader sites. The rule does **not** model `await` boundaries: `setState` after an `await` in a function called from an effect is still flagged. Only a `.then`/timer callback passes.

The 3 non-`set-state-in-effect` errors the ticket flagged as likely latent bugs all were: `usePanelLayout` sized the panel against the *window* rather than its container (ref read during render returned `null` on the first pass and never re-ran — now a `ResizeObserver`); `MentionTextarea` wrote through its rest-props object after render; `useProjectEvents` as above.

### Not mine

`__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` — "disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way" failed **3 of 4 isolated runs**. My diff touches no refinement code. This is the recorded recurring flake; filed as an occurrence on friction `7U21HTjsPNfh` (now 15) rather than re-diagnosed.

### Unverified

Nothing was observed in a browser — impact on the panel, board filters and deep links is read off the code paths and off the component tests, not from a running app.

# Code Review Report

## Findings

### 1. Team Mode silently reactivates

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:113`
- **Description:** Dropping below two selected tickets only masks Team Mode; `teamModeRequested` remains `true`. Selecting a second ticket later silently re-enables Team Mode and sends `team: true` with the build request.

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `hooks/useNightRuns.ts:137`
- **Description:** When `runUrl` becomes null, the previous detail is retained. A subsequent run opens with the prior run’s data and `loading === false` until the request completes. A stale running state can expose a Stop button that targets the new run ID.

### 3. Failed scope loads relabel stale agent configuration

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `hooks/useAgentConfig.ts:66`
- **Description:** On fetch failure, data loaded for the previous URL is stored under the new URL. Switching between Project and Global settings can therefore display old-scope configuration as current-scope data; edits then target the newly selected scope.

## All three review findings fixed — commit `bf2b73f`

Every finding was the same defect twice removed: an effect that used to **reset** on a changing input became a derivation that only **masks** the stale value. Fixed at the source in each case, with red→green tests committed alongside.

### 1. Team Mode silently reactivates — `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:113`

## Review finding fixed — commit `c47bf7a`, plus the same defect in the sibling loader

The reviewer's scenario reproduces exactly as described, and the sibling keyed loader this branch introduced in the same commit (`useKeyedList` in `hooks/useAgentConfig.ts`) has it too. Both are fixed together.

### What the defect actually is

Both loaders hold **one slot for one key** and never cancel a request when the key changes underneath it. So a late reply about the URL the hook has left overwrites the current one. Because the reader derives `loading` from *"the settled result belongs to the URL asked for now"*, the eviction does not merely show stale data — **it hangs**:

- **`useNightRunDetail`** — `usePolling` leaves its in-flight callback running when it restarts, so a poll issued for run A can resolve after run B settled. B is finished, so nothing polls it again: permanent spinner until the dialog is closed and reopened. (Reviewer's finding, verbatim.)
- **`useKeyedList`** — `refresh` is what every save awaits (`updatePrompt`, `assignAgent`, `createAgent`, …). Save in the project scope, switch to the shared scope before the reload lands, and the shared scope's rows are blanked back to `loading` over a URL nothing re-fetches.

Fix in both: record the URL being asked for now and drop a response that no longer matches it. The ref is written by the effect that owns the URL, so it is always set before that URL's own response can arrive.

### Red → green

| test | branch (pre-fix) | merge-base `4fddb84` | branch (post-fix) |

| night-run: late poll for the run the dialog left | ❌ detail `undefined` | ❌ shows `run-a` under run-b | ✅ |
| agent-config: reload landing after the scope switch | ❌ rows `undefined` | ❌ shows project rows as global | ✅ |

Both are red on base too, so the regression gate has no `test_passes_on_base` to trip over — but note the base failure is a *different* symptom of the same bug: on `main` the straggler is **displayed** (wrong run's summary, wrong scope's rows, which the editors then write back into the selected scope); this branch's keying turned that into an eviction. | `npx tsc --noEmit` (`NODE_ENV` unset) | clean |
