comments.content:
**Merged B-arij-146, B-arij-150, B-arij-161 into B-arij-147** by the refinement re-pass.

> Four filings of one test case, differing only in how many isolated runs each session happened to observe. Merging keeps the strongest evidence — the run counts from all four disagreeing about determinism — in one place, and re-frames the ticket around what is actually left: e81fd4b and 0173d70 are on main, so the open work is a repeat-run verification rather than a fix.

---

**B-arij-146 — __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx fails deterministically on main** (bug, priority 0, was in backlog)

Pre-existing failure on `main`, unrelated to vbxe5miiLKOE — noticed while running the full suite for that ticket, filed rather than fixed there.

```
FAIL __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx > RefinementButton > disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="refinement-button-spinner"]
  at __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx:123
```

**Evidence that it is pre-existing**

- Reproduced with a `npm ci` install matching `package-lock.json` (a hardlinked `node_modules` from the main checkout was stale — `vitest` 3.2.4 vs 3.2.7, `next` 16.1.6 vs 16.3.3 — so the failure was re-confirmed after a clean install).
- The branch head is `5a7d69c`, which is on `main`; `git diff` showed the test file and `components/` byte-identical to the merge-base.
- Fails in isolation as well as under the full suite, so it is not load-related flakiness. The other 10 tests in the file pass.

`npm test` on main is therefore 1 failed / 6192 passed — CI runs the complete Vitest suite on pushes and pull requests, so this is red for every branch.

**Where to look**

The assertion follows a `waitFor` that the button is disabled, which passes; only the spinner testid is missing. Either the spinner element was renamed/removed from the component while the test kept the old testid, or it renders one tick later than the `waitFor` the test settles on.

Depended on: B-arij-159, B-arij-149

**B-arij-150 — refinement-button.test.tsx: spinner test fails on main (unrelated to git-sync epic)** (bug, priority 0, was in backlog)

Tripped over while running the full suite for the git-sync audit ticket. Not caused by that branch — the branch is at merge-base `4fddb84` with only `lib/github/sync-log.ts` and `__tests__/github-sync-log-deleted-project.test.ts` changed, so `refinement-button.test.tsx` and its component are byte-identical to `main`.

**Failure** (`npm test`, and reproduced 3/3 times in isolation — consistent, not flaky):

```
FAIL __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx > RefinementButton
     > disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by:
     [data-testid="refinement-button-spinner"]
  at __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx:123
```

The preceding `waitFor` on `refinement-button` being disabled passes; only the spinner test id is missing from the rendered button. So either the component stopped rendering the spinner element (regression) or it was renamed and the test was not updated.

Full suite otherwise green on that install: 493 files passed / 1 failed, 6313 tests passed / 1 failed, against a lockfile-consistent `npm ci`.

Depended on: B-arij-159, B-arij-149

**B-arij-161 — Flaky test: refinement-button "spinner and badge" case intermittently fails (1-in-N isolated runs)** (bug, priority 0, was in backlog)

Pre-existing flake, NOT caused by epic OhhuWSRBq1sX (the branch does not touch __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx). The build session's handoff claimed this flake was filed as B-arij-159, but no such ticket exists in the project — this ticket is the real filing.

Reproduction: run `npx vitest run __tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` in isolation, repeated. Observed 1 failure in 5 runs (run 2), then 1 failure in the first of 8 more runs — the failing case is always "disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way", failing with `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="refinement-button-spinner"]` while the button renders with `aria-busy="false"` (collapsed back to idle mid-assertion).

Root cause (verified in code): the test's fetch queue is `[idle(), {POST started:true}]` and `mockFetchSequence` repeats the LAST response when the queue is exhausted. After the POST resolves, `RefinementButton`'s effect re-runs (isRunning flips false→true) and immediately re-reads the status; that re-read consumes the repeated POST body, where `data.running` is `undefined`, so the component computes the running→idle edge (firing onFinished spuriously) and collapses to idle — the spinner/badge assertions then find the idle button.

Fix (two words, verified by reading the code path): append a third queue entry `{ data: { running: true, sessionId: "s-42", ticketCount: 5 } }` after the POST body so the post-dispatch status re-read sees `running: true` and the button stays busy for the assertions. The StrictMode test in the same file already uses the "controllable mock rather than a queue" shape for exactly this reason and is not affected.

Per project convention this flake is left unfixed on OhhuWSRBq1sX's branch; it needs its own fix commit. It also explains the single red test (6627/6628) the build session observed on the full suite.

Depended on: B-arij-159, B-arij-149

## Verified green — 31 isolated runs, 0 failures. Closing as verification, no fix needed.

**Install: `npm ci`** (not hardlinked). `node_modules` was absent in this worktree, so this is a clean lockfile install: 1002 packages, `vitest 3.2.7` / `next 16.3.3` / `react 19.2.3`, each matching `package-lock.json`. `__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` green (6/6).

### Run counts — observed in this session, not inherited

| Batch | Tip | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isolated, quiet machine | `434db26` | 10 | 10 pass / 0 fail |
| Isolated, synthetic CPU load (8 busy loops, load avg ~10–14) | `434db26` | 10 | 10 pass / 0 fail |
| Isolated, confirmation | `434db26` | 1 | pass |
| Isolated, after fast-forward | `bb96a66` | 10 | 10 pass / 0 fail |
| **Total isolated runs** | | **31** | **31 pass / 0 fail** |
| Shared worker pool (10 `refinement*` + `mock-fetch-helper` files, 213 tests) | `434db26` | 3 | 3 pass / 0 fail |

Every run: `Tests 13 passed (13)`. The named case *"disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way"* passed in all 31.

`main` moved twice while I worked (`434db26` → `bb96a66` → `456e8c1`). I re-measured against `bb96a66`; the commits after it (`456e8c1`, the focus-ring epic) touch none of `components/kanban/RefinementButton.tsx`, `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx`, `__tests__/helpers/mock-fetch.ts`, or `package-lock.json`, so the result carries — **but it expires as `main` advances**, per the usual rule.

Ancestry confirmed rather than assumed: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says both `e81fd4b` and `0173d70` are ancestors of HEAD.

### The green is not vacuous — mutation probes

31 passes only mean something if the test still detects the defect. Four probes, each confirmed on disk *before and after* the run (checksummed), restored via `cp` backups, never `git checkout`:

1. **Component guard reverted** (`asRefinementStatus` → blind cast) → `ignores a status read whose payload is not a status` reddens, deterministic.
2. **Badge gated on `busy` instead of `running`** → `is inert while the dispatch is in flight, and only then claims a running pass` reddens, deterministic.
3. **Mock helper repeats its tail** (`repeatLast = true` default) → 2 cases of `mock-fetch-helper.test.ts` redden.
4. **All three layers reverted at once** (pre-fix state) → the named case reddens **8/8 isolated runs**, alongside `ignores a status read…`.

So all three layers of the fix are load-bearing and pinned.

**One nuance worth recording:** the historical error string from the four filings — `Unable to find [data-testid="refinement-button-spinner"]` at line 123 — does **not** reproduce verbatim. `0173d70` changed the wait condition to the badge, so on reverted code the same defect now surfaces as `expect(element).toBeDisabled()` at line 131. Same collapse (button falls back to idle mid-pass: not disabled, no spinner, no badge), different assertion trips first. A future session grepping for the old string will not find it.

### On the regression gate

**The diff is empty.** No source file changed; `git status` is clean and the branch carries no commits of its own. The mechanical bug-fix gate will report `no_test_in_diff` — that is correct and expected here, not a fix cycle to run. The ticket was promoted as *"probably a no-op, run it and report the counts"*, and that is what it turned out to be. Adding a test purely to satisfy the gate would be gaming it: the three cases that pin this behaviour already exist and I proved by mutation that each one reddens. Please pass the gate manually or close the ticket directly.

Correspondingly, `tsc --noEmit` / eslint / `next build` / a browser pass had nothing to measure — an empty diff is its own answer, and the probes above are the evidence in their place.

### Memory updated

The `refinement-button-flake` entry still ended with *"`e81fd4b` lives on an unmerged epic branch, a branch off `main` still sees it fail"*. That clause is now false and has been removed; the entry records the 31-run result, the mutation probes, the changed error signature, and keeps `git merge-base --is-ancestor` as the question that decides a future failure.

### Recommendation

Close. And the useful lesson for the fifth session that considers re-filing this: the four filings disagreed on frequency (deterministic / 3-of-3 / 2-of-5 / 1-of-5-then-1-of-8) because they were measuring branches with different ancestry, not a flake with a varying rate. Ancestry is the discriminator, not the observed failure count.

epics.title: QA : le dialogue « Dismiss ce finding » n'a pas de DialogDescription (avertissement Radix à l'exécution)
epics.description:
Rencontré en marge de B-arij-iL4-FmyXgGr (QA mobile — actions hors viewport). Pas causé par ce correctif : l'avertissement est présent avant le diff.

## Observé
`components/qa/DismissDialog.tsx` rend un `DialogContent` sans `DialogDescription` ni `aria-describedby`. Radix émet à chaque ouverture :

```
Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.
```

Reproductible de deux façons :
- `npx vitest run __tests__/qa-findings-actions.test.tsx` — l'avertissement sort sur les trois cas « QaScreen — Dismiss » ;
- dans Chrome, en ouvrant Dismiss sur un finding de `/qa` (vu dans la sortie du serveur pendant `e2e/qa-findings-responsive.spec.ts`).

## Pourquoi c'est un vrai défaut
C'est un trou d'accessibilité au niveau du dialogue, distinct de l'association label/contrôle : un lecteur d'écran annonce le titre sans le contexte du finding qu'on est en train de rejeter. Le dialogue rend déjà le texte du finding — il suffit qu'il devienne la description accessible.

## Périmètre
`DismissDialog` est l'instance rencontrée ici, mais c'est un motif récurrent dans les dialogues construits sur les primitives shadcn/Radix du dépôt : un balayage de `components/**` sur `DialogContent` dira combien d'autres sont dans le même cas. Le correctif est le même partout (ajouter `DialogDescription`, ou `aria-describedby` sur le contenu déjà rendu) et mérite un test qui interroge le rôle `dialog` par son nom et sa description accessibles plutôt qu'un testid.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — `ed7acf38` · QA Dismiss dialog accessible description

**Scope reviewed:** the single commit on this branch (5 files, +269/−2). No unrelated work is present on the branch.

---

## What I verified rather than accepted

The write-up makes several mechanical claims. I re-derived each one independently.

| Claim | How I checked it | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `aria-describedby={undefined}` is Radix's sanctioned opt-out | Read `DescriptionWarning` in the installed `@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` | **Confirmed.** It reads `contentRef.current.getAttribute("aria-describedby")` and only warns when the attribute is present *and* its id resolves to nothing. Removing the attribute silences it. |
| The rendering is unchanged | `twMerge("text-muted-foreground text-sm", "min-w-0 flex-1 font-sans text-[13px] text-foreground")` in node | **Confirmed** — resolves to exactly the old span's class list, byte for byte. |
| The `sr-only` description adds no layout | `sr-only` is `position:absolute`, so it is out of flow and not a flex item; `DialogHeader`'s `gap-2` cannot apply to it | **Confirmed by construction.** |
| 12 `DialogContent` sites, 2 undescribed | Ran the commit's own AST walk per-site from outside the repo, printing *how* each site is satisfied | **Confirmed.** All 12 now pass on a real `DialogDescription`, none on a fallback. |
| `BugCreateDialog` reads as a false OK under grep | `BugCreateDialog.tsx:254` carries `aria-describedby={screenshotsHintId}` on a nested `role="group"` | **Confirmed.** |
| The guard is not vacuous | Mutation probe — reverted the description to a `<span>` on a copy under `/tmp` and re-ran the walk | **Reddens.** |

One subtlety worth calling out as *correct*, because it reads like a quirk: the `describedBy` object at `DismissDialog.tsx:96` cannot be simplified to a literal `aria-describedby={…}` attribute. In JSX, a written-out prop is *present* in the props object even when its value is `undefined`, so it would override Radix's default in the finding-present case too. The spread is the only way to express "leave the default alone". The comment above it explains the why; the construct is right.

**Install and environment.** `lockfile-install-consistency` green (so measurements come from an install matching the lockfile). `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0, with the only `next dev` running in the *main* checkout, not this worktree. Tests run under a load average of ~17 on 16 cores, so I capped threads rather than running the full suite.

**Tests I ran:** the two new files, `qa-findings-actions`, three `bug-create-dialog` files, `qa-components`, `qa-mobile-layout`, `qa-findings-band`, `qa-findings-verdicts`, `qa-check-dialog-labels`, plus the three i18n guards — **98 tests, all green**, no Radix warning left in the output.

**Merge state:** `git merge-tree` against main tip `310b7886` is **clean**, despite both sides touching `BugCreateDialog.tsx` (main's `09c3ff37` edits the same file). I extracted the merged blob and re-probed it — the description survives at line 218. No migrations on either side. The branch is 6 commits behind main; **this reconciliation expires as main advances.**

---

## Checklist

**1. Readability** — No issues found. The comments explain *why* at each non-obvious point (the spread, the twMerge ordering, the `sr-only` choice), which is what these three lines needed.

**2. DRY** — No issues found. The sweep reuses `sourceFiles()` from `helpers/class-list-scan.ts` instead of adding a second tree walker; only the ~30 lines of dialog-specific AST logic are new.

**3. Error handling** — Not applicable. No error paths introduced. The one degenerate input (`finding: null`) is handled explicitly rather than left to crash or warn.

**4. Performance** — No issues found. The sweep reads 503 files once for the filter and parses only the 12 that match: 59 ms.

**5. Naming** — No issues found.

**6. Type safety** — No issues found. No `any`. The `{ "aria-describedby"?: undefined }` annotation is deliberate and narrow.

**7. Testing** — Four findings, all below. The behavioural test does what the ticket asked (queries by role, name and accessible description, not a testid) and spies the right console channel. The class guard is a genuine sweep. The findings are about its *reach*.

**8. API design** — Not applicable. No route or schema change.

---

## Findings

### Minor — the guard credits any `aria-describedby` value
`__tests__/dialog-description-coverage.test.ts:71`

`hasAriaAttribute` accepts the attribute's presence, whatever it points at. I confirmed on a scratch file: `<DialogContent aria-describedby={id}>` with no description reports `described: true`. That is the reported defect in its most common form — an id whose element was renamed or moved — passing the sweep unseen.

The mirror image is also true: the check only sees *literal* JSX attributes, so an `aria-describedby` arriving by spread is invisible. `DismissDialog.tsx:105` is exactly that shape — my probe reports it as `aria=-`; it passes only on its `DialogDescription`. So the one file using the sanctioned opt-out gets no credit for it while a dangling literal gets full credit. The two halves are inverted.

**Recommendation:** credit only the literal opt-out — the attribute whose initializer is a `JsxExpression` wrapping the `undefined` identifier — and require a `DialogDescription` otherwise. `attribute.initializer` is already on the node.

### Suggestion — the sweep's subject is a tag name, not the primitive
`__tests__/dialog-description-coverage.test.ts:64`

`SheetContent` wraps the same `@radix-ui/react-dialog` `Content` and emits the identical warning; `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:394` mounts one with neither title nor description. I confirmed both ends. This is disclosed and filed as B-arij-277, and the ticket's own *Périmètre* says `DialogContent`, so the narrow fix is the right call — but the file gives no hint that its subject is a name rather than the primitive. A comment naming Sheet as out of scope would stop the next reader from over-trusting the sweep.

### Suggestion — loose sentinel
`__tests__/dialog-description-coverage.test.ts:112`

`toBeGreaterThan(5)` against a population of 12 stays green after more than half the sites vanish from the walk — the exact silent-loss mode the imported helper's header was written to end. `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(12)` reddens when discovery breaks.

Related: `hasDescription` requires the tag literally inside the subtree, so a dialog composing its body from a child component would be flagged despite being correct. No such site today, and the false-positive direction is the safe one — worth a line in the header.

### Suggestion — an empty `finding.text` slips both guards
`components/qa/DismissDialog.tsx:126`

`stripSeverityPrefix` returns `""` for a null body and for a body that is only a severity token, so the description can render empty. Radix stays quiet (the element exists), the sweep stays quiet (the tag is present), and the screen reader is back to the reported symptom minus the console warning that made it findable. Degenerate and pre-existing — the old `<span>` was equally empty — so not a regression. Keying the `describedBy` branch on `finding?.text.trim()` would close it cheaply.

Also noted: the behavioural test hardcodes `"Dismiss this finding"` while the component resolves it through `t("dismissDialog.title")`. It fails loudly rather than going mute, so it is safe as written.

---

## Two limits I did not close

- **The "rendering unchanged" claim is class-level, not pixel-level.** I confirmed the resolved class lists are identical and that `sr-only` is out of flow, which is stronger than eyeballing — but like the author, I did not diff before/after screenshots.
- **The merge-clean and 6-behind measurements expire** as `main` moves. Re-check immediately before merging.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 1 |
| Suggestion | 3 |

The fix is small, correct, and better-evidenced than most changes of this size — the sweep the ticket asked for is real, the second instance it found is one grep would have missed, and the mechanical claims hold up when re-derived. The findings are all about the new guard's reach, not the fix, and none of them blocks the merge.

Repository left exactly as found: tree clean at `ed7acf38`, no staged or unstaged changes, no `arji.json` churn. My scratch probes live under `/tmp` only.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: QA dialog's "Prompt name for reuse" input is named only by its placeholder
epics.description:
Found while closing vhFDZvDCY161 (QA check dialog / story detail panel label association). Filed separately because it is a **different defect class** and was therefore never in that epic's sweep.

## The site

`components/qa/StartQaCheckDialog.tsx:371` — the save-prompt name field:

```tsx
<Input
  value={savePromptName}
  onChange={(event) => setSavePromptName(event.target.value)}
  placeholder="Prompt name for reuse"
  className="h-[34px] rounded-[8px] text-[13px]"
/>
```

No `<label>`, no `htmlFor`, no `id`, no `aria-label`. Its only accessible name is the placeholder.

## Why vhFDZvDCY161's sweep did not catch it

That epic's defect class is *"a visual `<label>` with no `htmlFor` that wraps no control"*. The sweep enumerated `<label>` elements. This field has **no `<label>` at all**, so it is invisible to that scan by construction — a placeholder-as-label, not a broken association.

It is a genuine gap because a placeholder is not a reliable accessible name: it disappears once the user types, some screen readers do not announce it, and it fails the "name from author" expectation for a form control.

## Census

Scoped to the two files vhFDZvDCY161 named, after that fix:

- `StartQaCheckDialog.tsx` — 3 `Input`/`Textarea`. Two are correctly associated (`failure-digest-window` via `htmlFor`, Custom Prompt via the new `useId()` id). **This one is the only unnamed control.**
- `StoryDetailPanel.tsx` — 0 raw `Input`/`Textarea` (its fields go through `InlineEdit`, now named).

The wider `app/` + `components/` population of placeholder-only inputs is **unmeasured** — I deliberately did not widen the scan, since that is this ticket's job, not vhFDZvDCY161's. Sizing that population is the first step here.

## Fix shape

Same pattern as the merged siblings: a visible `<label htmlFor={id}>` if the design has room, otherwise an `aria-label` on the `Input`. Ids should be `useId()`-derived — the dialog is a reusable component.

## Verification

Must query by accessible name (`getByLabelText` / `getByRole("textbox", { name })`). A placeholder query (`getByPlaceholderText`) passes today and would keep passing while the control stayed unnamed, so it proves nothing here.

**Scope reviewed:** `app/projects/[projectId]/github-issues/page.tsx` (44 lines changed) and `__tests__/toast-surface-uniformity.test.tsx` (96 lines changed). Nothing else is in the diff.

## What the change does

The page drops its private stack — the `Toast` interface, the `toasts` state, a `showToast` with an unconditional 4000 ms `setTimeout`, and the `fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50` box — and takes `{ toasts, raise: showToast, dismiss: dismissToast }` from `useToastStack()`, rendering `<ToastStack items={toasts} onDismiss={dismissToast} testId="github-issues-toast" />`.

Aliasing `raise` back to the local name `showToast` is the right call: the six raise sites in `syncNow`/`importSelected` are byte-identical, so the diff is entirely the stack and nothing else.

| All 8 `useToastStack(` sites render a `<ToastStack` | yes; `app/projects/[projectId]/layout.tsx` renders none, so no double stack on this route |

1. **Readability** — No issues. The replacement comment at `page.tsx:99-103` states what was removed and which half of the behaviour each new piece owns. The test header explains why the file is an enumeration.
2. **DRY** — No issues. This is a de-duplication: the seventh copy of an id scheme and an expiry timer is gone.

4. **Performance** — No issues. `raise`/`dismiss` are `useCallback`-stable with `onToast` undefined, and no effect in the page depends on them.
5. **Naming** — No issues. `showToast` differs from the `raise`/`addToast` used on sibling surfaces, but preserving it is what keeps the six call sites out of the diff.

epics.title: One-Click Send-to-Dev, Full Agent Resume, and Readable IDs
epics.description:
Implement a QOL continuity and identity upgrade across ticket workflow, session resume, and UI readability. The epic removes friction from re-dispatching work, enforces resume-first execution for all providers (including Codex), and introduces human-readable IDs for tickets and agents with full backfill.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema and constraints: add/extend nullable session continuity fields in `agentSessions` and `chatConversations` for provider session tracking, add immutable `readableId` fields for Epic/Bug records, and add agent display-name fields tied to a predefined name registry; enforce uniqueness with indexes.
2) Provider layer: capture CLI session IDs from provider output and inject resume arguments for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex; extend `resolveAgent()` to return `namedAgentId` for scoped session filtering.
3) Process manager and APIs: persist `cliSessionId` on completion, expose/extend resume endpoints used by work-session actions, and implement resume-first with automatic fallback to fresh prompt when session resume fails or expires.
4) Ticket UX: add `Send to dev` next to `Add comment` at the bottom of ticket detail; clicking it immediately dispatches the assigned/current agent with no dialog and no required comment.
5) Readable ticket IDs: generate IDs using one shared per-project counter across Epic and Bug types (e.g., `E-project-001`, `B-project-002`), keep IDs immutable after assignment, and replace technical IDs with readable IDs on cards/details/activity surfaces.
6) Agent readable identity: seed a predefined Ancient Greek name list, assign deterministic unique names to existing and new agents/sessions, and use these names where agent identity is shown.
7) Backfill and validation: run idempotent backfill for existing tickets and agents, add collision/concurrency tests for counter generation, add resume/fallback tests for all providers, and add UI tests for button placement and readable ID rendering.

epics.title: Un toast levé pendant qu'un dialogue Radix est ouvert n'est pas annoncé (aria-hidden)
epics.description:
Relevé pendant l'épic « Cinq surfaces gardent leur propre pile de toasts » (5X82xUSkxCCQ). Non bloquant pour cet épic : signalé plutôt qu'élargi dans le diff.

## Contexte

`components/notifications/ToastStack.tsx` porte via `createPortal` sur `document.body` et annonce ses toasts avec `role="status"` (succès) / `role="alert"` (erreur, avertissement).

Quand un dialogue Radix modal est ouvert, Radix pose `aria-hidden="true"` sur les autres enfants de `document.body` — dont la `<section aria-label="Notifications">` du portail. Le toast reste **visuellement** au-dessus du dialogue (`z-[100]` contre `z-50`), mais il sort de l'arbre d'accessibilité : ni la région, ni le rôle `alert`, ni le bouton « Fermer la notification » ne sont atteignables au clavier ou par un lecteur d'écran tant que le dialogue est ouvert.

## Reproduction observée

1. `/projects/<id>/stories/<storyId>` → « Delete User Story » → « Confirm Delete » avec une réponse d'erreur du serveur.
2. La suppression échoue, le dialogue **reste ouvert** par conception et le toast d'erreur apparaît en haut à droite, par-dessus lui.
3. Dans le test de composant, `getByRole("region", { name: "Notifications" })` et `getByRole("button", { name: "Fermer la notification" })` ne trouvent rien ; il faut `hidden: true` pour les atteindre (voir le commentaire dans `__tests__/support/toast-contract.tsx`, qui documente précisément ce contournement).

Vérifié aussi dans Chrome : le toast est peint, la boîte est à la même place que sur les autres écrans, mais il est sous l'`aria-hidden` du dialogue.

## Portée

Toute surface qui lève un toast depuis un dialogue ouvert, pas seulement le détail de story : `/projects/:id` lève des toasts depuis ses dialogues (création d'épic, capture rapide, bug), et `QaScreen` en lève un depuis `DismissDialog` quand l'écho du ticket échoue.

## Pistes

Soit monter la pile dans le conteneur que Radix laisse visible (le portail du dialogue actif), soit rendre les dialogues non modaux là où un toast peut survivre à l'échec, soit doubler l'annonce par une région live montée hors du champ de l'`aria-hidden`. C'est une décision de conception sur le comportement modal, pas un correctif au vol.

comments.content:
## Fixed — commit `a23734e8`

**Design decision: keep the dialogs modal and take `aria-hidden`'s own opt-out.**

A modal `DialogContent` calls `hideOthers(content)` from the `aria-hidden` package, which stamps `aria-hidden="true"` on every other child of `document.body`. That package sweeps `[aria-live], script` into the set it *keeps* — its documented escape hatch for exactly this case (its source cites the issue). So the fix is one attribute on the single shared stack: `<section aria-label="Notifications" aria-live="off">`.

Two things pinned that down:

- **It must sit on the `<section>`, not on a toast card.** `hideOthers` snapshots the DOM when the dialog *opens*. The section exists then (it renders even with zero items); the toast the failure is about does not yet. Nodes added later are never stamped — the section is the only node that can be exempted.
- **`off`, not `polite`.** `off` is already the computed default, so writing it claims the opt-out and changes nothing else. `polite` would make the container a second live region and announce the same insertion twice.

### Why the other two options were rejected

- *Mount the stack in the active dialog's portal* — dead end. `DialogContent` carries `translate-x-[-50%]`, which becomes the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants, so the toast would be positioned against the dialog box instead of the viewport. Portalling into the dialog's *portal div* instead gains nothing: `hideOthers` recurses into kept ancestors and would hide the section there too.
- *Make the dialogs non-modal* — loses the scroll lock and the outside-click protection on delete confirmations, which is a worse regression than the bug.

### Measured in real Chrome (CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, exact DOM shape)

| | region "Notifications" | `alert` | "Dismiss notification" |
|---|---|---|---|
| unfixed | absent | absent | absent |
| fixed | exposed, `ignored: false` | exposed | exposed |

Fixed, the section is never stamped at all (no `aria-hidden`, no `data-aria-hidden` marker), the region exposes **no** live property of its own, and the `alert` inside it still computes `live: assertive`, `atomic: true`. That settles the one semantic doubt: an ancestor `aria-live="off"` does **not** suppress a descendant that declares its own liveness.

### Scope covered

The fix is in the one shared `ToastStack`, so it covers every surface in the ticket's Portée at once: story detail, `/projects/:id`'s epic / quick-capture / bug dialogs, and `QaScreen`'s `DismissDialog`.

### Regression proof (red → green)

- **`__tests__/toast-under-open-dialog.test.tsx`** (new, 3 tests) — red on the unfixed code for the reported reason: *"Unable to find an accessible element with the role region and name Notifications"*. All queries deliberately written **without** `hidden: true`. Covers the primitive under a real Radix dialog, the `aria-live="off"` choice, and the named repro (story delete fails → dialog stays open → toast announced).
- **`__tests__/support/toast-contract.tsx`** — the `hidden: true` workaround the ticket points at is **removed**; the helper now uses `getByRole("region", …)` and the plain dismiss-button query, so all five uniformity surfaces carry the guarantee. Proved red by hand (copy-aside, not `git checkout`): with the attribute removed, only the story surface — the one with an open dialog — reddens; the four dialog-free ones stay green.

### Left deliberately, and stated rather than implied

**The keyboard half is not closed, by choice.** With the region back in the accessibility tree, the remaining obstacle to Tab is Radix's `FocusScope trapped` — a `focusin` outside the dialog is bounced straight back, with no escape hatch short of `modal={false}`. That is correct modal behaviour, not an `aria-hidden` defect: while a modal is open it owns the keyboard. A sighted keyboard user reads the toast, cancels or retries, and can Tab to it once the dialog closes — and error toasts never auto-expire, so nothing is lost. Unpicking the modal contract is a separate decision from restoring the announcement.

### Verification state

- Fast-forwarded to `main` first (the branch was born 53 commits behind, pre-i18n-sweep) and ran `npm ci`. All measurements are from that clean install; the strings are now catalogue-resolved ("Dismiss notification", not the old French bytes).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on the touched files.
- Full `npm test`: **8604/8605**. The one failure is `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx`, the documented load-sensitive flake (hard-coded 10 ms budget) — reproduced 2 of 3 runs *in isolation* at load average 26.5, in a component this diff never touches.
- `e2e/desk-toasts.spec.ts` was run separately; result in a follow-up note. Its selectors (`status` / `alert` / the dismiss button) are all confirmed still exposed by the Chrome probe above.

**Review findings (approved with minor issues)**

The fix is correct, minimal and well-evidenced. I independently verified the mechanism it rests on rather than taking the commit message at its word:

- `node_modules/aria-hidden/dist/es5/index.js` — `hideOthers` really does `targets.push(...parentNode.querySelectorAll('[aria-live], script'))`, and `aria-live="off"` matches the attribute-presence selector. The section then lands in both `elementsToKeep` and `elementsToStop`, so `deep()` returns before stamping it *and* before stamping the toast cards inside it. The claim that the attribute must sit on the `<section>` (not on a card) is right: the sweep is a one-shot `querySelectorAll` at dialog-open time, and every `ToastStack` mount renders the section unconditionally once hydrated (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:737`, `stories/[storyId]/page.tsx:202`, `releases`, `git-sync`, `ChatPageView`, and the `onToast ? null :` guards in `NowDesk`/`QaScreen` which never leave a surface stackless).
- `node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` imports `hideOthers` directly (not `suppressOthers`), so the opt-out is live on the pinned version. `react-menu`, `react-select` and `react-popover` route through the same call, so the one attribute also covers Select/Popover/DropdownMenu/Sheet.
- The fix is in the single shared stack, so the ticket's whole Portée (story detail, `/projects/:id`'s epic/quick-capture/bug dialogs, `QaScreen`'s `DismissDialog`) is covered by construction.

## Checklist

**Readability** — No issues found. The comment is long for a one-attribute change, but it matches this file's established density (the dismiss-button comment beside it is the same shape), and it earns its length: an unexplained `aria-live="off"` is exactly the attribute a future cleanup deletes as dead.

**DRY** — No issues found. The fix is in the one shared stack, so the ticket's whole *Portée* closes at once rather than per surface.

**Error handling / Performance / Naming / Type safety / API design** — No issues found. No runtime logic, no new types, no routes, no re-render cost.

**Testing** — Three findings, below. The red→green proof is sound (verified red today for the reported reason), and dropping the `hidden: true` workaround from `toast-contract.tsx` correctly converts five surfaces' queries into real accessibility-tree assertions. The weaknesses are about what the tests *cannot* see.

---

## Findings

### 1. Minor — no positive control in the regression test
`__tests__/toast-under-open-dialog.test.tsx:135`

Every assertion is "the region/alert/button resolves". If `hideOthers` stopped running entirely, nothing reddens — the suite would report the fix healthy while it had become a no-op.

Not hypothetical: `aria-hidden` ships `suppressOthers`, which routes to `inertOthers` when `HTMLElement.prototype.hasOwnProperty('inert')` — and `inertOthers` has **no** `[aria-live]` opt-out. If a Radix upgrade switches to it, Chrome takes the inert path and the bug returns, while jsdom (I checked: `inert` unsupported) keeps taking the `hideOthers` path and stays green. Testing Library's `isInaccessible` ignores `inert` too, so even a jsdom that gained it wouldn't help.

**Fix:** after the dialog opens, also assert RTL's own container — a non-live direct child of `document.body`, so `hideOthers` stamps it — *did* get hidden: `expect(container).toHaveAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")`. That pair fails when the mechanism changes shape; the current pair cannot.

### 2. Minor — the contract helper's new comment overclaims
`__tests__/support/toast-contract.tsx:61`

"Dismissible by hand … including from under an open dialog" is more than line 63 proves. `fireEvent.click` dispatches only `click`; `DismissableLayer` listens for **`pointerdown`** on the document (`react-dismissable-layer/dist/index.mjs:141,166`).

In a browser: `DialogContentModal` passes `disableOutsidePointerEvents: true` and prevents dismissal only for right/ctrl-clicks (`react-dialog/dist/index.mjs:145,150-155`). A left press on the toast — portalled outside `DialogContent`, clickable via its own `pointer-events-auto` — fires `onPointerDownOutside` undefeated, so `onDismiss()` closes the dialog. On the ticket's own repro, dismissing the error toast also closes the delete confirmation the user was still in.

This is **pre-existing and not introduced** by the diff, and it is source-derived — I did not confirm it in a browser. But the diff now documents the opposite in the one helper five surfaces read. Scope the comment to what jsdom proves, and file the interaction beside the focus-trap boundary already declared in `ToastStack.tsx`.

### 3. Info — only the `alert` tone is exercised under a dialog
`__tests__/toast-under-open-dialog.test.tsx:145`

Both `StackUnderDialog` tests use an error toast, and the commit's Chrome CDP table reports only the `alert` row. The semantic question the fix had to settle — does an ancestor `aria-live="off"` suppress a descendant declaring its own liveness — is measured only for implicit-assertive. `role="status"`/implicit-polite is the commoner tone and the weaker signal. `it.each` over both tones closes it cheaply.

---

## On the deliberately-unclosed half

The commit is explicit that the focus trap still owns Tab, so the keyboard half of the ticket's symptom ("ni … atteignables au clavier") remains. I agree that is the right call — unpicking `modal` on a delete confirmation is a worse regression than the bug, and the announcement is the half that made the failure *silent*. It is disclosed in the commit, the source comment and the test file, which is the standard this codebase asks for.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 2 |
| Suggestion / Info | 1 |

The design decision is the right one and is argued from the dependency's actual source rather than from intuition; the rejected alternatives are rejected for correct reasons (`DialogContent`'s `translate-x-[-50%]` really would become the containing block for a `position: fixed` descendant). Nothing here blocks the merge.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: THe chat bar is too small in chat
Six primitives Piscine interactives avalent encore data-testid (CheckMark, IdentityChip, SegmentedControl, SelectPill, UnderlineTabNav, DeskHeader)
epics.description:
Recensement complet du barrel `components/piscine/` (29 composants), demandé par la portée de LsDPFzTpvhwA « QuietDangerAction avale data-testid ». Ce ticket-ci ne corrigeait que `QuietDangerAction` ; voici le reste, mesuré.

## Le trou

Ces six primitives rendent un élément **cliquable** (`<button>` ou `<Link>`), ne spreadent aucun `...rest`, et n'exposent aucune prop `testId` :

| Primitive | Élément cliquable | Prop manquante |
|---|---|---|
| `CheckMark` | `<button onClick={onToggle}>` | `testId` |
| `IdentityChip` | `<button onClick>` (branche cliquable) | `testId` |
| `SegmentedControl` | un `<button>` par option | `testId` par option, comme `CappedBarChart` le fait pour ses barres |
| `SelectPill` | `<button>` déclencheur | `testId` |
| `UnderlineTabNav` | un `<Link>` par item | `testId` par item |
| `DeskHeader` | `<Link href={titleHref}>` sur le titre | `testId` (composant en voie de retrait au profit de `TopBar` — à confirmer avant de le corriger) |

Comme pour `QuietDangerAction`, TypeScript **attrape** l'appel (la prop n'est pas dans l'interface), donc le coût est du frottement, pas un faux vert : on retombe sur `getByRole("button", { name: … })`, fragile dès que le libellé bouge ou se répète dans la page.

Le correctif est celui déjà arrêté deux fois dans le dossier (`QuietLink`, puis `QuietDangerAction` dans LsDPFzTpvhwA) : une prop `testId` explicite posée **sur l'élément interactif lui-même**, jamais sur un wrapper — un test doit pouvoir cliquer ce qu'il a trouvé. Pour `SegmentedControl` et `UnderlineTabNav`, l'id est par option/item, sur le modèle de `CappedBarChart` (`bar.testId`).

## Recensement complet (29 composants)

- **Spreadent `...rest`/`...props` sur la racine DOM — rien à faire (3)** : `GhostInputPill`, `PillButton`, `SurfaceCard`.
- **Prop `testId` explicite déjà en place (4)** : `QuietLink`, `CappedBarChart` (racine + par barre + cap), `ProgressTrack` (`fillTestId` sur le remplissage), `QuietDangerAction` (ajouté par LsDPFzTpvhwA).
- **Écrivent leurs propres `data-testid` en dur, non paramétrables mais autosuffisants (2)** : `TopBar`, `TopBarMenu`.
- **Aucun chemin pour un testid appelant (20)** : les 6 du tableau ci-dessus, plus 14 non interactifs — `AvatarSquare`, `BandHeader`, `BreathingDot`, `Chrono`, `DiffDelta`, `FieldKicker`, `KbdHint`, `Mono`, `PipelineChain`, `RatioBar`, `Stamp`, `StatNumeral`, `StrataBand`, `TimelineLine`.

`Mono` et `StrataBand` sont les cas déjà connus et consignés dans la mémoire projet : eux avalent la prop **en silence** (pas d'erreur TS quand le testid arrive via un objet plus large), ce qui est la variante dangereuse. Les 12 autres non interactifs sont un simple frottement de requête et peuvent rester tels quels si personne n'en a besoin.

## Reproduction

```tsx
<SelectPill label="Claude Code" testId="agent-picker"><div /></SelectPill>
// TS2322: Property 'testId' does not exist on type SelectPillProps
```

## Test attendu

`__tests__/piscine-testid-forwarding.test.tsx` (créé par LsDPFzTpvhwA) est le fichier d'accueil : il vérifie déjà, pour `QuietDangerAction` et `QuietLink`, que l'id atterrit sur l'élément interactif (`tagName`, `data-slot`, clic → handler appelé) et qu'aucun attribut n'est écrit sans `testId`. Étendre le même triptyque à chaque primitive corrigée.

Added explicit `testId` prop forwarding across all 6 interactive Piscine primitives:
- `CheckMark`: `testId` forwarded to interactive `<button>` when `onToggle` is given, or `<span data-testid>` when read-only.
- `IdentityChip`: `testId` forwarded to clickable `<button>` when `onClick` is given, or `<span data-testid>` when static.

All components omit `data-testid` when `testId` is undefined.

Demonstrated red-to-green regression in `__tests__/piscine-testid-forwarding.test.tsx` (9 failing tests before the fix, 21 passing after). Type checking (`tsc --noEmit`) and full test suite pass cleanly.

comments.content:
**Review findings (approved with minor issues)**

The fix is correct and complete for the six primitives the ticket names. All six now place `data-testid` on the interactive element itself (`<button>` / `<Link>`), with a documented static fallback where the primitive has a non-interactive branch, and per-item ids on `SegmentedControl` / `UnderlineTabNav` modelled on `CappedBarChart.bar.testId` — exactly the shape settled by `QuietLink` and `QuietDangerAction`.

Verified independently (not taken from the handoff):
- Red proof reproduced outside the repo: `git archive 25a836d6^` into /tmp with only the new test file overlaid → **9 failed / 12 passed**, matching the claim exactly. Green in the worktree → **21/21**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors; `npx eslint` on all 7 changed files → clean.
- 12 test files (237 tests) that mount any of the six primitives → all pass. No call site passes the new props yet, so blast radius is nil.
- Census re-checked mechanically: the 14 "non-interactive" primitives really do render no `<button>`/`<Link>`/`onClick`/`href` — the scope selection is right.
- Radix `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` does preserve the child's `data-testid` (confirmed by the passing SelectPill test, not assumed).
- Measurements come from the existing install; `__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` passes (6/6).

One census correction the implementation handled correctly but did not record: **`SelectPill` already spread `...rest` before this commit** and already forwarded `data-testid` — its own docblock said so, and `components/shared/AgentSelectPill.tsx:221` relies on it. The ticket filed it under "aucun chemin pour un testid", which was only true for the camelCase `testId` spelling. The commit correctly destructures `"data-testid"` out of `rest` and re-applies it as `testId ?? dataTestId`, which is *necessary*: the explicit `data-testid={…}` sits after `{...rest}`, so without the fallback an `undefined` would have deleted the caller's attribute. That is a real regression avoided, but the surrounding prose and the test that guards it both misdescribe it.

No correctness, performance, type-safety or API-design defects. Findings below are documentation/naming accuracy plus one unrecorded scope confirmation. Nothing blocking.

Note beyond this ticket's scope: `Mono` and `StrataBand` — the *silent* swallow variant the ticket names as the dangerous one — remain unfixed (correctly out of scope), and no scanner or lint rule sees this mechanism, so this closes six instances, not the class. That guard is worth its own item.

Repository left exactly as found: no files edited, `git status` clean, scratch tree under /tmp removed.

**Code Review**

# Code Review — mLnxTsdqKUiP

**Commit reviewed:** `25a836d6` — *fix(piscine): forward testId on CheckMark, IdentityChip, SegmentedControl, SelectPill, UnderlineTabNav, and DeskHeader*
**Scope:** 7 files, +256/−6 (6 primitives + 1 test file)

---

## Verification performed

I did not take the handoff's claims on trust. Measurements, all from the existing install (`__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` → 6/6 green, so no stale-install triage risk):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Red proof, reproduced independently** | `git archive 25a836d6^` into `/tmp`, new test file overlaid, components left at pre-fix state → **9 failed / 12 passed**, matching the claimed count exactly |
| Green in the worktree | **21/21** |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `npx eslint` on all 7 changed files | clean |
| Tests mounting any of the six primitives | 12 files, **237 tests**, all pass |
| Census re-check | The 14 "non-interactive" primitives really render no `<button>`/`<Link>`/`onClick`/`href` — scope selection is correct |
| Radix `asChild` merge | Confirmed (not assumed) that `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` preserves the child's `data-testid` |

The scratch tree is removed and `git status` is clean — **no repository files were modified.**

---

## Checklist

**1. Readability** — Clear and idiomatic. Each new prop carries a JSDoc line naming the exact element it lands on. Two accuracy defects (findings 2, 4).

**2. DRY** — No issues found. The branch/static split is duplicated across `CheckMark`, `IdentityChip` and `DeskHeader`, but that is the pre-existing shape of each primitive, not new duplication; abstracting it would be a larger refactor than this ticket warrants.

**3. Error handling** — Not applicable (pure presentational props). Correctly, all six omit the attribute entirely when `testId` is undefined rather than emitting `data-testid="undefined"`, and each has a test pinning it.

**4. Performance** — No issues found. No new renders, allocations or state.

**5. Naming conventions** — No issues found. `testId` matches the four existing precedents (`QuietLink`, `QuietDangerAction`, `CappedBarChart`, `ProgressTrack`'s `fillTestId`); per-item ids follow `CappedBarChart`'s `bar.testId` as the ticket specified.

**6. Type safety** — No issues found. No `any`, all props optional and correctly typed; `SegmentedControlOption<T>` keeps its generic.

**7. Testing** — Strong. The triptych the ticket asked for (placement on the interactive node, click/select reaches the handler, no attribute when omitted) is applied to every primitive, and the red proof is real. One test is misnamed (finding 1).

**8. API design** — Consistent, with one wrinkle: `SelectPill` now carries two spellings with silent precedence (finding 3).

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Minor** | `__tests__/piscine-testid-forwarding.test.tsx:224` | Test named *"supports passing data-testid directly via rest props"* passes on the pre-fix tree, and after the fix `data-testid` no longer travels through `rest` at all. What it actually guards — that the explicit attribute after `{...rest}` must not erase a caller's `data-testid` — is valuable; the name hides it. |
| 2 | **Minor** | `components/piscine/SelectPill.tsx:38` | Docblock says the interface spread is what makes `data-testid` reach the DOM. No longer true: line 77 destructures it out, line 89 re-applies it. A reader "simplifying" line 89 to `data-testid={testId}` breaks `components/shared/AgentSelectPill.tsx:221`. |
| 3 | **Minor** | `components/piscine/SelectPill.tsx:64` | `"data-testid"?: string` is undocumented, and `testId` silently wins when both are passed. Dual API is justified (live consumer predates the commit) — precedence should be stated. |
| 4 | Info | `__tests__/piscine-testid-forwarding.test.tsx:11` | Docblock still says "pin that placement for **both**"; the file now covers eight primitives. |
| 5 | Info | `components/piscine/DeskHeader.tsx:25` | The ticket asked to confirm `DeskHeader` isn't being retired before fixing it; that confirmation isn't on the ticket. For the record: mounted only in `app/piscine-preview/page.tsx:857` (specimen gallery), no product screen renders it. Harmless to keep. |

**Note on the census (handled correctly, not recorded):** `SelectPill` already spread `...rest` and already forwarded `data-testid` before this commit — the ticket's "aucun chemin pour un testid" was true only for the camelCase spelling. The implementation got the tricky part right: because the explicit `data-testid={…}` sits *after* `{...rest}`, an unguarded `undefined` would have **deleted** the caller's attribute, so the `?? dataTestId` fallback is load-bearing, not decorative. Findings 1–3 are about making that legible.

**Beyond scope:** `Mono` and `StrataBand` — the *silent*-swallow variant the ticket names as the dangerous one — are correctly left alone, and no scanner or lint rule sees this mechanism. This closes six instances, not the class; the mechanical guard is worth its own item.

---

## Summary

- Critical: 0 · Major: 0 · **Minor: 3** · Info: 2

The fix does what the ticket asked, on the six primitives it named, in the shape the two prior tickets settled, with a regression proof I reproduced myself. All remaining findings are documentation and naming accuracy — none change behaviour.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: THe chat bar is still to small in Chat and comment
Composeur du chat : le placeholder passe à deux lignes et « doc » est rogné dès que le champ est sous ~380 px
epics.description:
Défaut cosmétique **préexistant**, observé pendant B-arij-180 et volontairement laissé de côté : il est visible sur `main` et sur l'état revu du ticket, à 1280 × 800 — c'est-à-dire à l'un des deux viewports que B-arij-180 interdit de régresser. Le corriger dans ce diff-là aurait cassé la preuve de non-régression (captures identiques octet pour octet).

## Ce qui est observé

`CHAT_COMPOSER_PLACEHOLDER` (`components/chat-page/ChatComposer.tsx:27`) vaut « Écris — ⏎ envoie, ⇧⏎ saute une ligne, @ cite un doc », soit 51 caractères. Dès que le champ descend sous ~380 px, le placeholder passe à deux lignes, et la seconde (« doc ») est coupée en bas de la bande.

Mesuré en Chrome, capture d'élément de `chat-composer` :

- **1280 × 800**, colonne de fil 628 px, champ **297 px** → deux lignes, « doc » rogné. Reproduit à l'identique sur l'arbre d'avant et d'après B-arij-180 (mêmes octets).
- **768 × 1024**, champ 409 px → une seule ligne, rendu correct.

La bascule est donc entre ~300 et ~409 px de champ. Le seuil exact n'a pas été mesuré.

## Mécanisme (non confirmé)

La bande porte `min-h-[58px]` et devrait donc grandir ; le `<textarea>` de `MentionTextarea` a `rows={1}` et `min-h-[24px] max-h-[120px] py-[17px]`, ce qui fixe sa hauteur à une ligne. Le placeholder déborde de cette hauteur au lieu de la faire croître. À vérifier avant de choisir le correctif : le rendu du placeholder n'agrandit pas un textarea, contrairement à une valeur saisie.

## Pistes

Trois directions, aucune évidente — c'est une décision produit autant que technique :

1. `text-ellipsis`/`whitespace-nowrap` sur le placeholder, pour couper proprement à droite plutôt qu'en bas ;
2. un placeholder plus court sous un certain seuil (le raccourci `@ cite un doc` est le moins nécessaire) ;
3. laisser la bande grandir à deux lignes quand le placeholder ne tient pas.

## Preuve

Capture `kwRiiCPK8bVN.png`, attachée à la session de B-arij-180 (référence 1280 × 800 avant correctif). Aucun agent lancé pour ce constat.

epics.description:
Found while fixing `DrsYAB9iY9kE`. That ticket named `hooks/useTicketOverlayData.ts` as a sibling to check; it is **clean on the guard the ticket named**, but it has a different, real problem. Filing rather than widening.

## Verdict on the stale-write guard: clean

`hooks/useTicketOverlayData.ts:322-350` already carries a `cancelled` flag, checked before both of its writes (`setSessionId` and `setSessionActions`). A stale response cannot land. No fix needed there.

This matters more than it looks: the overlay is the one place in this family that genuinely takes the re-render path. The cross-project desk at `/` opens tickets from different projects **without remounting**, so its `projectId` prop changes under a component that stays put. (The Sessions page and the project desk both remount on a `[projectId]` segment change — verified in Chrome.)

## The actual problem

```js
const rows = await fetchUnifiedSessions<UnifiedSessionRow>(projectId);
const latest = rows.find((row) => row.kind === "agent_session" && row.epicId === currentEpicId);
```

Two costs:

1. **No `signal` is passed.** `fetchUnifiedSessions` follows the route's keyset cursor to the end, so closing the overlay — or opening a different ticket — leaves the loop paging a list nobody will read. Measured on the Sessions page under the same shape: four extra requests after a switch on a 733-session project. The overlay opens and closes far more often than a page navigates.

2. **It fetches the entire list to find one row.** The route already sorts newest-first across pages, and the code takes the *first* match, so every page after the one containing that match is pure waste. On a project with a few thousand sessions this is several sequential round trips to answer "what was the newest session for this epic?".

## Suggested fix

Pass an `AbortController` signal from the effect (the cleanup already exists — it only flips `cancelled` today). Better still, stop early: either short-circuit inside the page loop once a matching row is found, or give the list route an `epicId` filter so the answer is one page.

## Not measured

I did not measure the overlay's request count in a browser — the read of the code plus the Sessions-page measurement is the evidence. The early-exit option is a route/contract change and is a product call, not a drive-by.

epics.title: Clearing a conversation's named agent falls back to claude-code, not the resolved chat default
epics.description:
Found while addressing the cg0Q review. Filed rather than folded in: the review's findings name `lib/chat/default-chat-mode.ts` and the three selector surfaces, and this is a fourth route with its own contract question.

## What happens

`PATCH /api/projects/{projectId}/conversations/{conversationId}` has three branches. The last one — clear the named agent without naming a provider — still uses the pre-epic resolution:

```ts
} else {
  // Clearing a conversation-specific named agent falls back to configured chat default.
  const resolved = resolveAgent("chat", projectId);
  updates.namedAgentId = null;
  updates.provider = resolved.provider;
```
(`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:155-162`)

Creation now goes through `resolveDefaultChatMode()`, which can return `openai-compatible` or a `*-persistent` mode. This route cannot: `resolveAgent`'s return type is `AgentProvider`, the exact ceiling the epic lifted everywhere else.

So a conversation created on `claude-code-persistent` — the default on any machine with `claude` installed — silently becomes one-shot `claude-code` the moment its agent link is cleared. The warm process the epic exists to give people is dropped, with no signal.

## Reachability

**Not reachable from the UI today.** `agentSelectionPatch()` emits either `{ namedAgentId }` or `{ provider, namedAgentId: null }`; the second carries a valid chat provider, so it lands in the `else if` above. The `else` needs a body with `namedAgentId` present-and-empty and no valid provider — an API client, not the pill.

That makes it a defensive contract rather than a live defect, which is why this is low. It is still worth closing: it is the only remaining `resolveAgent("chat", …)` call site that means "what should this conversation run on?" and answers with the narrow union.

## The other call site, deliberately left

`conversations/route.ts:155` also calls `resolveAgent("chat", …)` and should stay: it fires only when a conversation carries a `namedAgentId`, and the stream route ignores the stored provider whenever it does (`overridesProvider = provider && !namedAgentId`), so a chat-only value there would be dead state. That one is documented in place.

## Suggested shape

Await `resolveDefaultChatMode(projectId)` in the `else` branch and write both `provider` and `namedAgentId` from it — note it can return a named agent (the assignment rung), so the branch should stop hard-coding `namedAgentId = null`. The handler is already async.

A regression test wants the persistent case specifically: assert that clearing the agent on a `claude-code-persistent` conversation does not leave it on one-shot `claude-code`.

No other writer touches `chat_conversations.provider` / `named_agent_id`; the four stream-route updates write only `status`, `label`, `cliSessionId`.
- *Reachability.* `agentSelectionPatch()` returns `null` rather than a bare `{ namedAgentId: null }`, and `ChatPageView` / `UnifiedChatPanel` are its only callers. Defensive contract, as filed.

The focus-ring unit sweep can never see the ring's colour — a transparent ring would pass all 50 sites
epics.description:
Found while closing B-arij-206 / B-arij-205 / B-arij-203 (the focus-ring epic). Filed separately rather than widened into that diff.

## The gap

`__tests__/helpers/tailwind-outline.ts` compiles the class list under test with the real Tailwind engine, but only from a bare `@import "tailwindcss"` — it never loads `app/globals.css`:

```ts
compilerPromise ??= compile(`@import "tailwindcss";`, { base: process.cwd(), … });
```

`focus-visible:outline-ring` resolves its colour through `--color-ring`, and `--color-ring` is defined in `app/globals.css` (`:root` for day, `.dark` for night), not in the framework theme. So the utility emits nothing the resolver can read and `resolved.color` is **`undefined` for every control in the app**, correct ones included.

## Observed

Measured on this branch, adding `expect(resolved.color).toBeDefined()` to the two inputs pinned by `__tests__/focus-ring-undeclared.test.tsx`:

```
× the ⌘K command palette input > paints a keyboard focus ring
  → the ⌘K search input outline-color: expected undefined to be defined
× the sessions ticket filter input > paints a keyboard focus ring
  → the sessions ticket filter outline-color: expected undefined to be defined
```

The assertion was removed with a comment explaining why, because it fails on correct code.

## Why it matters

The sweep in `__tests__/focus-ring-paints.test.tsx` now covers 50 sites in 40 files and asserts `outline-style` and `outline-width`. It cannot assert the third thing a ring needs to be seen. A control given `focus-visible:outline-transparent`, or a `--color-ring` that resolves to the surface it sits on, would keep `outline-style: solid` and `outline-width: 2px` and pass all 50 assertions while painting nothing visible.

This is the same class of defect the epic was about — a ring that is declared, type-checks, asserts green, and is not on screen — one property over.

## Coverage today

`e2e/focus-ring-inputs.spec.ts` (added by this epic) does read the resolved colour in real Chrome and rejects a fully transparent one, in day and night — but only for the two inputs it names. `e2e/focus-ring.spec.ts` covers the six TopBar controls and does not assert colour at all. The other ~42 sites have no colour evidence at any layer.

## Leads

- Load `app/globals.css` into the helper's `compile()` so `--color-ring` resolves, then assert a non-transparent colour across the sweep. The helper already has a `loadStylesheet` hook that resolves project-relative paths, so the plumbing exists; the day/night split would need the resolver to pick a `:root` vs `.dark` variable set, which it does not model today.
- Or accept the unit layer's limit and widen `e2e/focus-ring.spec.ts` to assert colour on the controls it already tabs through, and say plainly in both files that colour is an e2e-only claim.

The fix does what the ticket asked, and I verified the red→green claim mechanically rather than taking it on trust.

VERIFIED
- The premise: compiling `@import "tailwindcss";` alone emits no `outline-ring` rule and no `outline-color` at all (probed directly against the pinned tailwind build). So `resolved.color` really was `undefined` for every control.
- The fix: `resolveFocusVisibleOutline(RING)` now returns `color: "var(--ring)"`, `colorIn: { day: "#24907a", night: "#6fcbb4" }`, both painting.
- The sweep is complete: all 5 consumers of the helper (`focus-ring-paints`, `focus-ring-undeclared`, `chat-thread-pane-focus-ring`, `story-detail-panel-labels`, plus the new `focus-ring-color`) assert the colour per theme; none was left behind. All 52 scanned sites resolve a declared `var(--ring)` — no site leans on the base-layer fallback, so the sweep's colour assertion is non-vacuous everywhere it runs.
- The mutation direction: `focus-visible:outline-transparent` → `transparent` in both themes; `outline-ring/0` → a 0% `color-mix`; `outline-ring/50` → still paints. `colorPaints` correctly rejects `#abc0`, `#12345600`, `oklab(… / 0)`, `color(srgb … / 0)`, `hsl(… / 0%)`, and an unresolved `var()`.
- The two-set modelling guard (`colorIn.night !== colorIn.day`) is load-bearing, not brittle padding: it is what stops the night set silently collapsing onto day if the `.dark` block ever moves somewhere `themeVariables` does not look.
- The `@layer base` fallback and the `@supports` handling match what Chrome does; competing colour utilities resolve by the utility layer's own emission order, as in a real browser.

MEASUREMENTS: `npm ci` not needed — `__tests__/lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` is green, so installed == locked. `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on all 8 changed files; the 5 focus-ring files 125/125 green; `focus-ring-scan` + `top-bar` 106/106 green (tip c96da73). The diff is test-only — no route, component or lib file — so there is no build or browser pass to skip; the browser claim that does apply is the e2e layer, which I did not run (shared machine, and the diff there is one assertion on an already-captured field). Working tree left exactly as found.

Findings below are all minor and none blocks the merge. Two are about the e2e half of the change, which is the weaker layer here; one is a latent hole in the rewritten resolver; one is duplication.

Also noted, not filed: `colorPaints` fails open for functional notations it does not know — measured, `light-dark(transparent, transparent)` and `color-mix(in srgb, #fff calc(0 * 1%), transparent)` both read as painting. Neither is emitted by Tailwind today and the doc-comment states the default explicitly, so this is a note rather than a defect. Likewise `themeVariables(css)` re-parses the whole compiled sheet on every call; measured cost is negligible (52 sites in ~200ms) and it is trivially memoizable if that ever changes.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — B-arij-pJ7Gf8eAh7QO

**The focus-ring unit sweep can never see the ring's colour**

Diff: 8 files, +818/−90, all under `__tests__/` and `e2e/`. No source file changed. Measured at tip `c96da73`.

---

## Verification before review

I did not take the ticket's premise or the fix's claim on trust.

**The gap was real.** Compiling `@import "tailwindcss";` alone against the pinned Tailwind build and asking for the ring class list:

```
emits outline-ring rule? false
emits any outline-color?  false
```

**The fix closes it.** `resolveFocusVisibleOutline(RING)` on this branch:

```
{ style: 'solid', width: '2px', offset: '2px',
  color: 'var(--ring)',
  colorIn: { day: '#24907a', night: '#6fcbb4' },
  paints: true }
```

**The mutation direction works.** `focus-visible:outline-transparent` → `transparent` in both themes; `outline-ring/0` → a 0% `color-mix`, rejected; `outline-ring/50` → still paints. `colorPaints` correctly rejects `#abc0`, `#12345600`, `oklab(… / 0)`, `color(srgb … / 0)`, `hsl(… / 0%)`, and an unresolved `var()`.

**The sweep is complete.** All five consumers of the helper assert the colour per theme — none was left behind. I resolved all 52 scanned sites: every one declares `var(--ring)`, so the assertion leans on the base-layer fallback nowhere and is vacuous nowhere.

Install: `lockfile-install-consistency` green, so installed == locked; no `npm ci` needed. `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on all 8 changed files, 125/125 on the five focus-ring files, 106/106 on `focus-ring-scan` + `top-bar`. Test-only diff, so no build or browser pass applies to it; I did not run the e2e suite (shared machine, and its diff is one assertion on an already-captured field). Working tree left exactly as found.

---

## Checklist

**1. Readability** — No issues found. The header comments carry real information (why the bare theme emitted nothing, what the model does and does not cover). One comment is inaccurate — Finding 3.

**2. DRY** — Finding 4: the per-theme assertion is copy-pasted six times across five files.

**3. Error handling** — No issues found. `resolveStylesheet` throws by name rather than compiling a sheet with a hole in it; `substituteVars` bounds itself at 16 passes and a cycle degrades to an unresolved `var()`, which `colorPaints` treats as not painting — failing loud, in the right direction.

**4. Performance** — No blocking issues. `themeVariables(css)` re-parses the whole compiled sheet on every call and is trivially memoizable, but the sheet is ~15 KB (`source(none)` means no scanning) and 52 sites resolve in ~200 ms.

**5. Naming conventions** — No issues found.

**6. Type safety** — No issues found. No `any`. Two `as` casts (`Object.fromEntries` → `Record<Theme, …>`, the `exports` entry shape); both are narrow and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

**7. Testing** — Findings 1–3. The unit layer is the strong net and it is sound. The e2e half is the weaker one: its transparency guard misses two of the notations Chrome emits, and its prose claims a ground-contrast check that no spec implements.

**8. API design** — N/A, no routes touched.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Minor | `e2e/focus-ring.spec.ts:157` | Transparency regex blind to slash-alpha notations |
| 2 | Minor | `e2e/focus-ring-inputs.spec.ts:32` | Header claims a ground-contrast check neither spec makes |
| 3 | Minor | `__tests__/helpers/tailwind-outline.ts:260` | `&:focus` blocks dropped and mis-documented as "a state the element is not in" |
| 4 | Info | `__tests__/focus-ring-paints.test.tsx:338` | Assertion duplicated 6× across 5 files |

**Finding 1** is the one with teeth. Measured in Chrome 152: `color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 0%, transparent)` computes to `oklab(0 0 0 / 0)` and `oklch(0.7 0.1 180 / 0)` stays as written — neither matches `/rgba\([^)]*,\s*0\)$/`. Switch a TopBar control to `focus-visible:outline-ring/0` and the spec passes on an invisible ring. The unit sweep catches that shape, so the class is covered; the browser-side claim is just weaker than its comment reads. Note the trap in the fix: a bare `/[,/]\s*0\)$/` would reject opaque `rgb(0, 0, 0)`.

**Finding 2** matters because it is this ticket's own defect one layer up: `focus-visible:outline-card` resolves to `#fffef8` on a `#fffef8` card in day and passes every assertion in both layers. Contrast is covered nowhere, and should be named as uncovered rather than attributed to a spec that does not check it.

**Finding 3** is latent, not live — I censused every `outline-*` utility in `components/`, `app/`, `hooks/`, `lib/`: the only `focus:outline-hidden`/`focus:outline-none` sites are shadcn primitives using `focus:ring-*`, none in the scanned set, and there are no `dark:` outline variants at all.

Two things I chose not to file, noted for the record: `colorPaints` fails open on functional notations it doesn't know (`light-dark(transparent, transparent)` reads as painting — measured), which is documented behaviour and unreachable from Tailwind's output today; and the `colorIn.night !== colorIn.day` assertion, which looks like a brittle palette pin but is load-bearing — it is what stops the night variable set silently collapsing onto day if `.dark` ever moves somewhere `themeVariables` doesn't look.

---

**Total: 0 critical, 0 major, 3 minor, 1 info.** The fix delivers what the ticket asked for, in the stronger of the two forms its "Leads" offered, and the sweep it repairs is genuinely complete.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: English-only interface on a localization substrate
epics.description:
## Problem

Arij's interface is a French/English mix, unevenly spread. The recently rebuilt Piscine screens (`components/desk/`, `spec/`, `qa/`, `chat-page/`, `settings-piscine/`, `piscine/`, `session-live/`, `agents-workshop/`) are largely French, while older screens are English. `lib/piscine/nav.ts` mixes both *inside one nav table*: `Work`, `Tickets`, `Spec & Memory`, `QA`, `Releases`, `Agents`, `Sessions`, `Chat`, `Usage` — then `Réglages` and `Intégrations`.

The goal is twofold and must not be conflated: (1) normalize the interface to English as the single source language, and (2) extract copy behind a translation layer so a further language is a catalogue file, not another code sweep. Doing (1) without (2) means paying the sweep twice. Doing (2) without (1) means translating from a source language that does not exist yet.

## Measured state (main, 2026-08-31)

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| i18n library in `package.json` | none |
| `<html lang>` | hardcoded `"en"` in `app/layout.tsx:66` |
| Files containing French | 99 (`components/` 67, `app/` 14, `lib/` 8) |
| Copy in JSX text + copy-bearing props | ~1,022 |
| Copy in module-scope constant tables (excl. dev harness) | 174 |
| Locale-sensitive format calls (`toLocale*`, `Intl.*`) | 19 |
| Pages/layouts that are server components | 12 of 47 |
| Test files asserting French copy | 43 |

Realistic translatable inventory is 1,500–2,500 strings — the scans miss template literals, ternary copy and toast messages.

## Two findings that shape the work

1. Copy lives in module-scope constant tables, not only in JSX. 174 strings sit in `Record<string, string>` maps and object literals evaluated at *import* time, so they cannot call a `t()` hook: `lib/piscine/nav.ts` (14), `lib/providers/options-registry.ts` (40 — its header states "The UI renders its CLI options section from this file"), `components/session-live/labels.ts`, `SETTINGS_TABS` in `app/settings/layout.tsx:28`. They must become key references resolved at render, or factories taking `t`. This is the one genuinely non-mechanical extraction pattern and it must be settled in story 1, before the sweeps.

2. Server components do render copy. `app/settings/layout.tsx` is a server component whose tab labels — including `Intégrations` — live in a constant table. The translation layer therefore has to work server-side, not only inside a client provider.

## The drift this epic stops

Language divergence has already produced duplicated *logic*, not just duplicated words:

- Three relative-time formatters, one per language, each documented as deliberately not sharing: `lib/utils/format-date.ts:timeAgo()` (English, used by 20+ screens); `components/spec/spec-format.ts:formatFrenchRelative()` (French, whose comment calls it "a local French sibling, not a change to it"); `components/chat-page/relative-age.ts:relativeAge()` (French, whose comment states "There is no shared helper").
- French grammar hardcoded in a component: `components/piscine/TopBarMenu.tsx:39` ships a bespoke `plural(count, one, many)` (`"1 prêt"` / `"2 prêts"`).
- A hand-rolled number formatter avoiding `Intl`: `components/spec/spec-format.ts` reimplements thousands grouping because `Intl.NumberFormat("fr-FR")` emits U+202F while the design frame wanted U+0020.

Each collapses into one locale-aware call once a runtime exists.

## Decisions taken

Locale mechanism — a stored setting, not URL routing. Next 16's bundled guide (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/internationalization.md`) recommends `[lang]` sub-path routing with `Accept-Language` negotiation. That is right for a public multilingual site and wrong here: Arij is a single-user localhost app with no SEO and no shareable URLs (spec §3.1). Adopting `[lang]` means moving all 47 route files under a dynamic segment and rewriting every internal `href`, for no benefit. Instead a `ui_locale` row in the existing `settings` table (free-form settings keys need no migration, spec §3.2), read through `app/api/settings/route.ts`, plus a provider mounted next to `ThemeProvider` in `app/layout.tsx`. `middleware.ts` keeps doing only its localhost-origin job.

Library — `next-intl`, mounted without its routing layer. ICU message format (plurals and dates handled properly rather than by bespoke helpers) and it works in server *and* client components, which finding 2 makes non-negotiable. Alternatives considered: `react-i18next` (routing-agnostic, weaker server-component story) and a ~150-line in-house `t()` (zero deps, but rebuilds plural rules and loses extraction tooling at 2,000 strings).

## Scope

In scope: the interface only. Client and server rendered copy, including copy held in `lib/` constant tables that the UI renders.

Out of scope, settled with the user:
- Code comments. French comments stay as they are.
- Server-generated and persisted text — notification rows, activity entries, API error strings. No key+params persistence scheme, no schema change. This epic touches no migration and no table.
- `app/piscine-preview/page.tsx` + `app/_piscine-preview/` — a dev harness whose own header reads "DEV HARNESS — NOT A PRODUCT SCREEN … Delete both files when the redesign lands". It is the single largest string file (153) and excluding it is a real reduction.
- Agent-facing text. `lib/chat/board-tools.ts` (MCP tool descriptions sent to models) and the prompt builders in `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts` stay English: the spec and project memory are English, and localizing them would degrade model behaviour for zero user benefit.
- User data. French epic titles, ticket bodies and comments belong to the user and are never touched.

## Follow-up epic (not this one)

"French locale + language switcher": complete the `fr` catalogue seeded by story 3, add the switcher to the Settings appearance band, verify plural/date/number behaviour under `fr-FR`. Small, and it is the real proof that the substrate works.

## Implementation order

1. Runtime, `ui_locale` setting, and the constant-table pattern — demonstrated on `lib/piscine/nav.ts` and `app/settings/layout.tsx` (which also proves the server-component path).
2. Locale-aware formatting primitives, merging the three `timeAgo` variants, the French `plural()` and the manual thousands grouping.
3. Sweep the 99 French-bearing files to English + keys, capturing the existing French copy into `fr.json` in the same edit.
4. Extract the already-English screens to keys.
5. Guardrails: key-coverage check in CI, an ESLint rule against bare JSX literals, and migration of the 43 French-asserting test files.

## Verification

`npm run test:changed` per story, full `npm test` before merge, `tsc --noEmit` and eslint on touched files, `npm run test:e2e` on swept screens (system Chrome, `channel: "chrome"`). A manual browser pass on every swept screen is mandatory: the Piscine rebuild is design-sensitive (Space Mono advance widths, em dashes, U+00B7 separators), so string length changes reflow bands. Reading the diff is not sufficient evidence.

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want the already-English screens extracted to catalogue keys, so that no part of the interface is left outside the translation layer
user_stories.description:
The mechanical half of the extraction: roughly 1,000 remaining strings across the screens that were already in English — the older surfaces under `app/projects/[projectId]/`, `components/night/`, `components/routines/`, `components/usage/`, `components/monitor/`, `components/review/`, `components/import/`, `components/ticket/`, `components/story/`, `components/github/` and the shared components.

Larger in file count than story 3, smaller in judgment: the copy does not change, only its location. Apply the same two patterns — JSX strings to `t()` calls, module-scope tables to the story-1 pattern. Since the source text is already the English catalogue value, `fr.json` gains untranslated keys here; that is expected and is the follow-up epic's work, so leave them absent from `fr.json` rather than filling them with English placeholders that would later read as "already translated".

This story completes the inventory, which is what makes the story-5 guardrails enforceable: an ESLint rule against bare JSX literals is only adoptable once there is nothing left to flag.

- [ ] A representative sample of the touched screens is opened in a browser and renders unchanged; the screens checked are listed in the ticket comment
