user_stories.title: As a developer, I want CI to fail on missing or orphan translation keys and on new hardcoded strings, so that the interface cannot drift back into a language mix
user_stories.description:
Close the loop so the sweep is not repaid later. Three deliverables:

1. A key-coverage check run in CI: every key referenced in code exists in `en.json`, and `en.json` carries no orphan keys. It must fail the build, not warn — spec §3.6 notes that type checking, linting and builds are expected verification steps but are not all enforced by the current workflow, and this check should not join that list.
2. An ESLint rule against bare string literals in JSX for the `components/` tree, so a new hardcoded string is caught at review time. Story 4 must be complete first or the rule is unadoptable. If a genuine exception exists (icon-only labels, punctuation, mono glyphs), encode it in the rule's options rather than sprinkling disable comments.
3. Migration of the 43 test files that assert French copy. Rewrite the assertions against keys or English text. Migrate them — do not delete them: several pin real behaviour, and deleting a test to make a sweep green removes the only evidence that the screen still works.

Run the full suite, not `test:changed`, since the assertion rewrites touch tests across the whole tree. Note that `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` is a known flake already filed as its own ticket; if it trips here, record the occurrence and do not diagnose it as a regression from this epic.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A key-coverage script fails on a referenced-but-missing key and on an orphan key; both directions are proven by a deliberate temporary break
- [ ] The script is wired into the CI workflow as a failing gate, not an advisory step
- [ ] An ESLint rule forbids bare user-facing string literals in JSX under `components/`, with any exceptions expressed as rule options rather than inline disables
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes on the whole repo with the new rule enabled
- [ ] All 43 French-asserting test files are migrated to assert on keys or English; none is deleted
- [ ] `npm test` (full suite) passes; the observed pass/fail counts are reported in the ticket comment
- [ ] `npm run test:e2e` passes against system Chrome (`channel: "chrome"`) on the swept screens
- [ ] If `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` trips, the occurrence is recorded against its existing ticket and explicitly named as not caused by this epic

comments.content:
**Code Review**

Findings submitted. Here is the full report.

---

# Code Review — E-arij-155: English-only interface on a localization substrate

**Scope:** 423 files, +13,644 / −4,014, commits `970382d…fca06c03` against merge-base `main` 77b0039.
**Measured on:** the installed dependency tree (`next-intl` 4.14.2 installed and locked; `lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` green in the full run).

## Mechanical verification (run here, not quoted from the handoff)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` (full) | **619 files / 8507 tests, all passing** — the known `refinement-button` flake did not trip |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` | 0 errors, 28 warnings |
| `npm run i18n:check` | 2141 defined, 2141 referenced, **0 missing, 0 orphan** |
| `next build` (`NODE_ENV=production`) | exit 0 |
| Independent AST scan for French literals in `app/`+`components/`+`lib/`+`hooks/` | **0** outside the catalogue and excluded paths |
| Independent ICU parse of 2141 `en` + 344 `fr` messages | 0 syntax errors, 0 arg drift, 0 fr keys absent from en |
| Independent AST check of every `t("key", {…})` against required ICU args | **0** call sites missing an argument |
| Live locale round-trip (production server, port 3391) | `ui_locale=fr` → 200, `<html lang="fr">`, French rendered, English fallback; `ui_locale=de` → 400 typed error |
| `proxy.ts` / `middleware.ts` | byte-identical to `main` |
| `eslint --print-config` on `components/desk/NowDesk.tsx` | `i18n/no-bare-jsx-copy` at severity **2**; absent from `eslint-suppressions.json` |

## Checklist findings

**1. Readability** — No issues found. `lib/i18n/catalogue.ts` is the strongest artefact in the diff: it *argues* the pattern-3 choice and states why factories-taking-`t` were rejected, so stories 3–4 could apply it mechanically. `check-keys.mjs`'s header records why rule 4 exists (it was wrong first, and says so). The sweeps genuinely followed the header.

**2. DRY** — Story 2 delivered. Five relative-age formatters, the French `plural()` and the hand-rolled thousands grouper are gone, replaced by one locale-parameterised family. Two residues:
- **[Minor]** `lib/i18n/format.ts:39` — `catalogueValue` for two values drags the whole message tree into the client graph (see Performance).
- **[Minor]** The unification dropped the month/year bands that `EditorFooterBar`'s formatter had (`components/agents-workshop/EditorFooterBar.tsx:65`) — `created 1y ago` is now `created 425d ago`, with no migrated test recording the loss.

**3. Error handling** — No issues found. `readStoredUiLocale` swallows a failed read to `null` with a stated reason (the chrome's locale is not worth a 500 per route); `formatDateTime` falls back on an unknown IANA zone rather than blanking the row; `PATCH /api/settings` rejects an unknown locale with a typed 400 — verified live.

**4. Performance** — **[Minor]** Measured on the production build: `.next/static/chunks/29xf26xxjfe18.js` is **115,448 bytes** carrying **both** the `en` and `fr` catalogues, and sits in the client-reference manifest of essentially every route. Separately, `NextIntlClientProvider` (`app/layout.tsx:84`) resolves to next-intl's server variant, which awaits `getMessages()` when given no `messages` prop — **118,164 of `/`'s 144,357 bytes** are that flight payload. ~230 KB of message data per page load, and the `fr` seed ships to every user although `NEGOTIABLE_UI_LOCALES` never selects it. Loopback makes this parse/eval cost rather than transfer, but it is a property of the substrate and grows by a full catalogue per added locale.

**5. Naming conventions** — No issues found. PascalCase namespaces, camelCase keys, `<field>Key` consistently typed `TranslationKey`.

**6. Type safety** — No issues found; no `any` in the new code. The `next-intl.d.ts` augmentation makes `t("Nav.entries.tikcets")` a compile error, and `PlacementKey = Extract<TranslationKey, …>` in `placement.ts` documents a real TS2590 it avoids. (One redundant `useLocale() as UiLocale` at `EditorFooterBar.tsx:66` against 34 uncast siblings — not worth a finding.)

**7. Testing** — Strong. `__tests__/i18n-key-coverage.test.ts` proves both gate directions by writing into the *real* source tree and restoring it, with a final case asserting the restore. The `next-intl` stand-in resolves against the real catalogue with `createTranslator` and **throws on a missing key**, so migrated tests still assert real English copy rather than key paths — and its header is honest about what it does not prove. No test files deleted.

**8. API design** — No issues found. `GET /api/settings` keeps `ui_locale` out of `data` so a round-trip cannot write a computed default back as stored; the routes that compose server-side copy use `resolveUiLocaleForRequest(request)` rather than `next/headers`, with the reason recorded.

## Blocking

**[Major] `components/releases/derive.ts:172`** — `upperAge` matches English literals (`=== "just now"`, `endsWith(" ago")`) on `formatRelative` output whose locale `ReleaseStatTiles.tsx:40` has already threaded through. Verified inert under `fr`: every French shape falls through unchanged, so the caption renders lowercase where the frame draws it uppercase. Worse, `"just now"` is a hard copy of the *value* of `Format.justNow` — re-wording it in English alone breaks this silently.

**[Major] `lib/types/kanban.ts:17` (and siblings)** — `COLUMN_LABELS` and `PRIORITY_LABELS` are module-scope copy tables rendered across seven surfaces, left as bare English *in the same file* where `USER_STORY_STATUS_LABELS:214` was converted. `RegistryFilters.tsx:197` puts both halves in one expression: `status === "all" ? t("Registry.filters.statusAll") : COLUMN_LABELS[status]`. Same class in `lib/kanban/status-transitions.ts:54-58,107`, `lib/epics/manual-epic-form.ts:63-70`, `lib/pipeline/constants.ts:325`+`hooks/usePipelineRuns.ts:56`. This misses story 4's second AC, and **neither guardrail sees the class** — the ESLint rule is scoped to JSX literals in `components|app/**/*.tsx` (confirmed `undefined` for `lib/types/kanban.ts`) and `check-keys.mjs` only compares keys, never hunts un-extracted words. So it will not be caught later.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 2 |
| Suggestion | 0 |

The English-only interface is delivered and the substrate works end to end — I confirmed the locale round-trip in a real browser-facing server, not just in the diff. The two blocking items are small and mechanical (the pattern for the second is already proven twice inside the file that misses it), but both are substrate defects the follow-up French epic hits on its first day, and the second sits in the one class the epic's own guardrails cannot detect.

**Repository state:** working tree clean at `fca06c03`; scratch server stopped and worktree `data/arij.db` removed; `.next/` holds an uncommitted production build from this review. The port-3000 orchestrator was not touched. This reconciliation is against `main` 77b0039 and expires as `main` advances.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

# Code Review — E-arij-155: English-only interface on a localization substrate

**Cycle 2.** Scope: fix commit `bdffec91` against the previously reviewed `fca06c03`; merge-base `main` 77b0039.
**Measured on:** the installed dependency tree — `lockfile-install-consistency.test.ts` 6/6 green, no reinstall needed.

## Prior findings

`[RC:g7gIbc_o7AaV] FIXED` — `components/releases/derive.ts:167`. `upperAge` now takes `locale: UiLocale` and returns `relative.toLocaleUpperCase(locale)`; both English literal comparisons (`=== "just now"`, `.endsWith(" ago")`) are gone, and `ReleaseStatTiles.tsx:40` threads the locale in. Non-English and reworded-copy regression cases added at `__tests__/releases-derive.test.ts:189-195`.

The side effect is real and was disclosed: the DOM text changed from `4d AGO` to `4D AGO`. I checked the claim that the pixels are unchanged rather than accepting it — `StatNumeral.tsx:55` renders the caption through `FieldKicker`, whose class string at `FieldKicker.tsx:66` carries an unconditional `uppercase`. Captured the tile in Chrome: it renders **`CURRENT · 4D AGO`**, glyph-identical to before. Story 4's byte-identity AC holds at the rendered layer.

`[RC:7IDtybhD9qHE] FIXED` — `lib/types/kanban.ts:17,84`. `COLUMN_LABELS`/`PRIORITY_LABELS` became `COLUMN_LABEL_KEYS`/`PRIORITY_LABEL_KEYS` typed `TranslationKey`, matching the `USER_STORY_STATUS_LABELS` pattern already proven in the same file. I grepped every consumer: all eleven sites the finding named resolve at the render boundary (inbox, `RegistryFilters` — *both* branches of the expression the finding called out, `RegistryRow`, `NewTicketView`, `BugCreateDialog`, `PriorityBadge`, `StatusControl`, `csv.ts`, `ticket/derive.ts`).

The three sibling tables the finding also named are converted: `status-transitions.ts` (option labels plus a `{status}`-parameterised `noDirect` reason), `manual-epic-form.ts:65-71` (keys with `{max}` interpolated at render, so validation limits stay out of the catalogue), `pipeline/constants.ts:326` with `usePipelineRuns.ts:53` (caller-resolved phrases). `prompt-builder.ts:2312` resolves agent-facing priority words via `catalogueValue(DEFAULT_UI_LOCALE, …)` — exactly the fix proposed. All 39 new English values are byte-identical to the constants they replaced.

`[RC:f0ZbmjjngmaA] FIXED` — `lib/i18n/format.ts:151`, via a `maxUnit: "year"` option used at `EditorFooterBar.tsx:65`. I probed `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat("en", {style:"narrow"})` directly rather than trusting the shape: it emits `1y ago` and `5mo ago`, matching the deleted `relativeFromNow` byte for byte. The `>30d` pin the finding asked for exists at `__tests__/i18n-format.test.ts:45` (29/30/359/360/425 days). Chrome screenshot confirms a 425-day-old agent's footer reads `created 1y ago`.

`[RC:_0CSG2dr1HU9] FIXED` — `lib/i18n/format.ts:39`, taking the finding's second suggested option (a small locale-data map local to the module). `format.ts` now imports only `en/fr Format.json` (2 keys); `options-registry.ts` only `en/ProviderOptions.json`. **Measured on a production build I ran:** the 115,448-byte both-catalogues chunk is gone. The only catalogue-bearing chunks are 30,655 and 15,429 bytes, and neither carries the `fr` nav words. `__tests__/i18n-client-catalogue-graph.test.ts` walks the transitive static import graph with the TS compiler API and pins both entry points — a real guard, not a comment.

The provider-serialisation half, which that finding framed as separate context ("on top of what the provider already serializes"), is untouched and was disclosed as such in the commit. I measured it: 97,852 bytes of `en` JSON, and `/`'s 145,752-byte HTML contains the `/agents`-only string `Bypass permissions` at offset 86,225. Filed as **B-arij-274** rather than blocking — it is loopback parse cost on a single-user local app, and it was visible to cycle 1.

## New findings

Bounded to what `bdffec91` changed. **One, info severity, cosmetic:** the commit inserted imports above the module docblock in `lib/pipeline/constants.ts:1`, `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1-3` and `components/ticket/TicketOverlay.tsx:3`. The first is the awkward one — that header exists to document what the module may import, and the new import now sits above the rule it is subject to. One-line fix each, no behaviour change.

I checked the rest of the diff for substance and found nothing to file. `PriorityBadge` moves its new hook above the early return (hook order intact); `csv.ts` adds `tKey` to its memo deps; `descriptionMeta`'s `toLocaleLowerCase(locale)` reproduces the old `toLowerCase()` output for all four English values; `optionLabel`'s hand-rolled reduce is less defensive than `catalogueValue` but its input is registry-owned and type-constrained to `ProviderOptions.*`, so no path reaches an undefined node.

## Mechanical verification (run here)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` (full) | **621 files / 8,524 tests, all passing** — the known `refinement-button` flake did not trip |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` | 0 errors, 28 warnings |
| `npm run i18n:check` | 2,180 defined, 2,180 referenced, **0 missing, 0 orphan** |
| `next build` (`NODE_ENV=production`) | exit 0 |
| Playwright, system Chrome, port 3418 | **8/8 passed** — `i18n-interface`, `i18n-review-regressions`, `tickets-registry-filters` |
| Independent `en`/`fr` catalogue diff | 344 `fr` seed entries, **0** identical to their `en` value, 0 absent from `en` |
| `proxy.ts` / `middleware.ts` vs `main` | byte-identical; no `[lang]` segment |
| CI gate | `i18n:check` is a `run:` step in the workflow, not advisory |
| `eslint --print-config` | `i18n/no-bare-jsx-copy` at severity **2**, exceptions as rule options |

`__tests__/i18n-review-regressions.test.tsx` is the right shape for this defect class: it `vi.unmock`s next-intl, mutates catalogue values, and asserts the changed words reach rendered components — proving the `lib/` tables genuinely resolve at the boundary rather than merely holding key-shaped strings. The QA report is also honest about what the guardrails still cannot see (arbitrary untranslated `lib/` words), with friction `ypq9m3Ou7Quz` recording the limit.

epics.description:
Rework Kanban ticket detail behavior from a blocking right-side modal to a non-modal experience in the shared left panel area. Clicking a ticket must both select it and open its details, while the board remains fully interactive for additional selections and quick actions.

Implementation plan:
1. Refactor board UI state to keep ordered selection (`selectedTicketIds`) and derive `activeDetailTicketId` from the first selected ticket.
2. Update card interaction so primary ticket click selects the ticket and opens details in the shared left panel container (same area used by chat/epic panels).
3. Keep multi-select active while details are open using existing additive selection controls; additional selections must not block board interaction.
4. Enforce first-selected anchoring: detail content follows the first selected ticket; adding more tickets does not switch detail; if the first selected ticket is removed, promote the next oldest selected ticket; if none remain, close details.
5. Remove all modal mechanics across desktop/tablet/mobile: no dim layer, no pointer-event lock, no focus trap, no modal fallback.
6. Increase detail panel width for readability using responsive sizing target `clamp(420px, 34vw, 560px)` and preserve usable board space.
7. Add/adjust tests for selection-order logic, non-modal interactivity, quick-action continuity, and responsive rendering. No DB/schema/API/provider changes are expected.

Dependency-Aware Batch Ticket Orchestration
epics.description:
Build an orchestration epic for Arij that adds ticket dependencies and batch actions while reusing existing PR/Git/review flows. Scope is limited to dependencies inside one project (including tickets across different epics in that project), with schema designed for future cross-project expansion.

Implementation plan:
1. Dependency domain model
- Add dependency edges (`ticket_id`, `depends_on_ticket_id`, `project_id`) plus extensibility fields (`scope_type`, `scope_id`) for future scope expansion.
- Enforce current business rule: dependencies are valid only within the same project.
- Persist dependency metadata generated by the ticket-creation agent.
2. Ticket detail dependency management
- Add dependency editor in ticket detail to add/remove predecessors.
- Validate DAG integrity on every update (cycle detection with explicit error path).
3. Batch selection UX
- On ticket selection, auto-include all transitive prerequisites.
- Mark auto-included tickets as required and non-deselectable while dependents remain selected.
- Show batch actions `Review all` and `Merge all` when multiple tickets are selected.
4. DAG scheduler and execution engine
- Implement topological planning for batch `build`, `review`, and `merge` actions.
- Run dependent chains sequentially and independent branches in parallel, while respecting existing agent concurrency guardrails.
- Track per-ticket states: `ready`, `running`, `blocked`, `failed`, `success`.
5. Failure policy and remediation
- If a ticket fails, block descendants and continue all independent branches.
- For `Merge all`, add a batch toggle to auto-launch a merge agent on first failure for every failed ticket (including auto-included tickets), with no retry limit; rely on existing manual agent stop controls.
6. Integration and quality
- Reuse existing single-ticket PR/Git/review/build pathways; do not duplicate core Git/PR logic.
- Add tests for transitive auto-inclusion, DAG validation, topological execution, failure propagation, and auto-merge triggering.

Named Agents with Model Selection & Gemini CLI Provider
epics.description:
Extend the agent system from simple CLI provider selection to named agents that combine a CLI provider with a specific model. Users can create named agents like 'CC Opus 4.6' (Claude Code + claude-opus-4-6), 'Codex GPT-5.3' (Codex + gpt-5.3), or 'Gemini Flash' (Gemini CLI + gemini-2.0-flash), then assign one named agent per task type (build, review, chat, etc.). This also adds full Gemini CLI support as a third provider alongside Claude Code and Codex.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Schema & Types
- Add `namedAgents` table to Drizzle schema with columns: id, name, provider (claude-code | codex | gemini-cli), model (text), createdAt
- Add `namedAgentId` foreign key column to `agentProviderDefaults` table
- Extend all provider type unions to include `gemini-cli`

### Phase 2: Gemini CLI Provider
- Create `lib/gemini/spawn.ts` implementing the spawn interface using `gemini --prompt` with `--model`, `--yolo`, and `--output-format stream-json` flags
- Create `lib/providers/gemini-cli.ts` provider adapter returning `SpawnedClaude`-compatible interface
- Register Gemini CLI in the provider factory alongside claude-code and codex
- Generalize process manager dispatch to handle all three providers

### Phase 3: Named Agent CRUD & Resolution
- Create `lib/agent-config/named-agents.ts` with list, create, update, delete operations
- Implement `resolveAgent(taskType, projectId)` function that looks up the named agent for a task type and returns { provider, model }
- Backward compatibility: when `namedAgentId` is null, fall back to existing `provider` column behavior

### Phase 4: API Routes
- Add CRUD API routes for named agents at `/api/agent-config/named-agents`
- Update provider defaults API to accept `namedAgentId`
- Update build, review, and chat dispatch routes to use `resolveAgent()` instead of direct provider lookup

### Phase 5: UI
- Add new 'Agents' tab in agent settings for creating/editing/deleting named agents (name + provider dropdown + model text input)
- Update 'Providers' tab to show a named agent dropdown per task type instead of raw provider select
- Show agent name in session monitoring and activity indicators

epics.title: Permanent Delete Actions for Epic and User Story Detail
epics.description:
Add destructive delete actions directly in Epic Detail and User Story (US) Detail views, with explicit confirmation and immediate permanent deletion (no recovery, undo, or trash).

Implementation plan:
1. Add a `Delete` action in the danger zone of Epic Detail and US Detail, visible only to users who already have edit/delete permissions.
2. Implement a shared confirmation dialog used by both pages with irreversible copy (`This action cannot be undone`), Cancel, and Confirm actions.
3. Wire/extend backend `DELETE` handlers for epics and user stories to perform transactional hard deletes only.
4. Ensure relationship handling is deterministic: deleting an epic removes its child user stories and dependent planning artifacts in the same transaction; deleting a US removes its dependent links/comments/tasks per FK rules with no partial writes.
5. On successful deletion, redirect to the correct parent list view (epics/backlog), invalidate cached queries, and refresh UI state so removed items disappear from detail, kanban, and lists immediately.
6. Add regression coverage for confirmation, successful deletion, authorization, and failure paths for both entity types.

Unified Chat Final Cutover: Left Panel Only
epics.description:
Finalize chat convergence by making the left workspace (opened from New Epic and the left Chat button) the only chat interface, with full feature parity and complete migration from the legacy right panel. This epic is a final cutover/decommission effort (not a redesign), aligned with prior work in Unified Chat & Epic Creation Workspace, Fuse New Epic into Chat Panel, Session Management & Monitoring, and Codex Session Tracking Hardening.

Implementation plan:
1. Define a strict parity contract from the legacy right panel: tab taxonomy, labels, filters, sorting, status semantics, history behaviors, and chat capabilities.
2. Implement parity in the left panel using the same canonical chat/session data sources, ensuring all existing chat capabilities remain available.
3. Build and run a migration that preserves conversation/session/message IDs and metadata (timestamps, project linkage, statuses), with validation reports and backup before cutover.
4. Execute a big-bang cutover: left panel becomes the single entry point; right panel UI and triggers are removed.
5. Decommission legacy technical surface: routes, stores, hooks, components, feature flags, and obsolete services tied to the right panel.
6. Validate with automated and manual regression checks, including session continuity, history completeness, tab behavior parity, and no data loss.

Out of scope: historical deep-link/bookmark redirection from the old right chat panel.

epics.description: Implement a project-scoped document registry that standardizes storage and powers @filename mentions across the app. Phase 1: add a documents persistence model (projectId, originalFilename, kind=text|image, markdownContent, imagePath, mimeType, size, timestamps) with a case-insensitive unique constraint per project on filename. Phase 2: build ingestion rules—text files are converted to markdown at upload and only markdown is stored in DB; images are stored on disk and only their path/metadata is stored in DB. Phase 3: deliver a unified Docs tab listing all uploaded docs (text + image) by original filename with delete actions. Phase 4: add @mention autocomplete/parser in all editors and validate mentions at submit time. Phase 5: integrate mention resolution into dispatch so each send resolves docs and enriches the final prompt before CLI execution: full markdown for text, filesystem path sentence for images; keep this provider-agnostic and route through resolveAgent() to pass provider/model correctly for Claude Code and Gemini CLI headless flows. Phase 6: add migration, API, and integration coverage for upload/list/delete/mention/dispatch behavior, including deletion and cross-project isolation.

epics.title: Kanban Ticket Cards: Agent Activity, Hover Link, and Unread AI Indicator
epics.description:
Implement a focused Kanban ticket-card UX epic that adds visual agent signals and card-to-agent interaction without changing agent orchestration/dispatch logic.

Implementation plan:
1. Scope and boundaries
- Limit changes to Kanban ticket cards, shared frontend state wiring, and bottom agent panel highlighting.
- Reuse existing runtime ticket/agent state; do not change backend workflows for build/review/merge.

2. Agent activity icon on ticket cards
- Add a single activity icon slot on each ticket card for active agent work.
- Map action type to icon: `build`, `review`, `merge`.
- Render only when the ticket has an active agent action; hide otherwise.
- Add tooltip and aria-label with action type and agent name.

3. Hover link between ticket card and bottom agent panel
- On ticket-card hover/focus, emit selected agent context to bottom panel.
- Bottom panel highlights only the linked agent card/row; remove highlight on unhover/blur.
- Safely no-op if ticket has no linked active agent.

4. Unread AI last-message indicator (session-scoped)
- Show an unread indicator on ticket card when the latest ticket comment is AI-originated (including system/status messages) and has not been seen in the current browser session.
- Persist seen state in `sessionStorage` (project+ticket scoped), not user-global persistence.
- Clear unread indicator immediately when ticket is opened.

5. UI cohabitation and accessibility
- Define deterministic placement when both activity and unread indicators are present.
- Ensure contrast, tooltip text, keyboard focus behavior, and aria labels are compliant.

6. Validation and regression safety
- Add component tests for icon mapping/visibility and unread logic.
- Add integration/E2E tests for hover highlight lifecycle and unread-clearing-on-open.
- Verify no regressions in Kanban drag-and-drop, ticket open flow, or bottom panel rendering.

The icon must reflect the action type (`build`, `review`, `merge`) and be sourced from existing frontend runtime state. This is a visual layer only and must not alter orchestration rules.

- [ ] A ticket with active `build` work shows the build icon; active `review` shows review icon; active `merge` shows merge icon.
- [ ] Tickets without active agent work show no activity icon.

Bug Tickets with Direct Creation and Agent Dispatch
epics.description:
Add a new 'bug' ticket type to the existing kanban system. Bugs are standalone kanban cards that reuse the epics table (with a new `type` column: 'feature' | 'bug') and the full dispatch/worktree/PR pipeline. Bugs have a simplified creation flow — a direct form (title, description, images) with no mandatory chat step. They can optionally link to an existing epic. A 'Create and Resolve' action creates the bug and immediately dispatches a selected agent (via the existing provider/agent selector) in an isolated worktree+branch. Bug cards have a distinct background color on the kanban board.

## Implementation Plan

1. Schema migration: Add `type` column ('feature'|'bug') to `epics` table (default 'feature'), add optional `linkedEpicId` self-referencing FK, add `images` JSON column for bug attachments.
2. API routes: New POST `/api/projects/[id]/bugs` for direct creation (no chat), POST `/api/projects/[id]/bugs/create-and-resolve` that creates + dispatches agent. Existing epic routes continue working unchanged.
3. Bug creation form: Modal/panel with title, description, image upload (reuse existing image infra from chat), optional epic linker dropdown, and agent selector for 'Create and Resolve'.
4. Kanban integration: Filter/display bugs alongside epics, distinct BG color for bug cards, badge or icon to distinguish type. Drag-and-drop, status transitions, and column behavior remain identical.
5. Agent dispatch: Reuse existing worktree+branch creation and agent dispatch logic. When linked to an epic, inject epic context (title, description, user stories) into the agent prompt.
6. Bug detail view: Lighter version of epic detail — shows title, description, images, linked epic, status, and agent session if dispatched.

Generate and push the Drizzle migration. Ensure all existing epics default to type 'feature' and all existing queries/API routes continue to work without changes.

- [ ] `type` column added to `epics` schema with 'feature' | 'bug' enum, defaulting to 'feature'

epics.title: Unified Chat & Epic Creation Side Panel
epics.description:
Rework the separate chat panel and epic creation flow into a single unified side panel component. The panel lives on the right side of the screen, collapsed by default (showing ~5% as a grayed-out edge). Clicking 'Chat' or 'New Epic' expands the panel, splitting the screen into a resizable two-pane layout (board + chat). The panel supports tabbed conversations with agent activity indicators and mandatory agent type selection on each new chat.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Unified Panel Shell
- Create a `UnifiedChatPanel` component that replaces the current separate chat panel and epic creation chat
- Panel has three visual states: collapsed (5% visible, grayed overlay on the right edge), expanded (resizable split with the board), and hidden (0%)
- Default state is collapsed — a thin vertical strip visible on the right side
- Clicking the collapsed strip or toolbar buttons ('Chat', 'New Epic') transitions to expanded state
- Use a resizable split layout (e.g. `react-resizable-panels` or custom CSS resize) so the user can drag the divider between the board and the chat panel
- Persist the panel width in local state (or localStorage) so it remembers the user's preferred split

### Phase 2 — Tabbed Conversations
- The panel supports multiple open conversations as tabs (similar to browser tabs)
- Each tab represents a chat conversation (brainstorm, epic creation, or general)
- Tabs show the conversation title (truncated) and a close button
- A '+' button creates a new tab
- Active tab is visually highlighted
- Tab state persisted in the existing `chatMessages` / `chatConversations` DB tables

### Phase 3 — Agent Activity Indicator in Tabs
- When an agent is actively working on a conversation (streaming response, building, etc.), display a small animated icon (spinner or pulsing dot) on the corresponding tab
- The indicator is visible even when the panel is collapsed, appearing on the thin right-edge strip as a subtle glow or badge
- Poll agent session status to determine which conversations have active agents

### Phase 4 — Agent Type Selector on New Chat
- When creating a new conversation ('+' tab or 'New Epic' / 'Chat' trigger), show a mandatory agent type selector before the first message
- Agent types: 'Brainstorm' (plan mode), 'Epic Creation' (spec generation mode), or custom types from agent config
- The selected type determines the prompt builder and Claude Code mode used
- Selector displayed as a prominent dropdown or button group at the top of the empty chat
- Once the first message is sent, the agent type is locked for that conversation

### Phase 5 — Board Integration
- Remove the old chat panel toggle from the project header
- The kanban board occupies 100% width when the panel is collapsed
- When expanded, the board flexes to fill the remaining space
- 'New Epic' button in the board toolbar opens the panel with a new 'Epic Creation' tab pre-selected
- 'Chat' button opens the panel with a new 'Brainstorm' tab or focuses the last active tab
- Ensure the kanban board remains fully functional (drag-and-drop, selection, build toolbar) in the reduced width

The strip should have a subtle visual cue (e.g. a chat icon or vertical text) indicating it can be expanded. Clicking anywhere on the strip expands the panel.

epics.title: Agent Busy Guards & Visual Feedback
epics.description:
Prevent overlapping agent actions on epics and stories by enforcing busy guards across all action types, and provide clear visual feedback on kanban cards and story views when an agent is actively working.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Unified Agent Busy State Detection
- Create a shared utility/hook `useAgentBusyState(entityId, entityType)` that checks whether any agent session (build, review, chat) is currently running for a given epic or story
- Query the `agentSessions` table for running sessions linked to the entity
- Return `{ isBusy, sessionType, sessionId }` so the UI knows what kind of work is happening
- This replaces the scattered `isRunning` checks with a single source of truth

### Phase 2 — Backend Concurrency Guards
- Add a generic `checkActiveSession(entityId, entityType)` helper in the API layer
- Apply it to ALL agent dispatch endpoints: build, review, send-to-dev, team build, chat
- Return HTTP 409 Conflict with a descriptive message when an agent is already working on the entity
- Ensure the guard checks both epic-level and story-level sessions (e.g., a story build blocks epic-level actions on the same epic's worktree)

### Phase 3 — Kanban Card Busy Indicators
- Add a visual indicator (spinner, pulsing dot, or animated border) on kanban epic cards when an agent is actively working
- Show the type of work in progress (e.g., 'Building...', 'Reviewing...') as a small badge on the card
- The indicator should be visible without opening the epic detail panel
- Poll or use existing session polling to keep the indicator in sync

### Phase 4 — Greyed-Out Actions in Epic & Story Views
- In `EpicActions`, disable ALL agent action buttons (Build, Review, Send to Dev) when any agent session is active for the epic — not just the same action type
- In `StoryActions` and `UserStoryQuickActions`, disable agent action buttons when a session is running for that story or its parent epic's worktree
- Show a tooltip on disabled buttons explaining why (e.g., 'Agent is currently building this epic')
- Replace loading-only disabled state with session-aware disabled state

### Phase 5 — Review Endpoint Concurrency Check
- The review endpoint currently lacks the same concurrency guard as the build endpoint
- Add `checkActiveSession` to the review dispatch route
- Prevent launching multiple overlapping review agents for the same story
- Allow multiple different review types to run in parallel (security + code review) but prevent duplicate types

epics.title: Fuse New Epic into Chat Panel
epics.description:
Remove the standalone 'New Epic' modal/flow and instead open epic creation as a new tab in the existing UnifiedChatPanel. When the user clicks 'New Epic', the chat panel opens with a new tab of type `epic_creation`. The chat stream API route checks the conversation type and uses the epic refinement prompt for `epic_creation` conversations. After the brainstorming chat converges, a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button triggers epic + user story creation from the conversation context.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Server-side routing in /api/chat/stream
- Modify the chat stream endpoint to check the conversation's `type` field
- When type is `epic_creation`, use the epic refinement prompt builder (existing `buildSpecPrompt` or a new `buildEpicCreationPrompt`) instead of the default brainstorm prompt
- Ensure the prompt includes project context (spec, documents) and instructs Claude to help the user define an epic with user stories

### Step 2 — New useEpicCreate hook
- Create a small React hook (`useEpicCreate`) that takes the conversation context and calls the API to create an epic with generated user stories
- The hook calls `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/epics` with the epic data extracted from the conversation
- Returns loading/error/success states

### Step 3 — UnifiedChatPanel UI updates
- Add a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button that appears in `epic_creation` conversations once enough context has been discussed
- Differentiate tab icons: sparkles icon for `epic_creation` tabs vs message icon for regular chat tabs
- Add an empty-state hint in new `epic_creation` tabs explaining what the user can do
- Wire `onEpicCreated` callback to refresh the kanban board and optionally close the tab

### Step 4 — MessageInput placeholder
- Add a `placeholder` prop to the MessageInput component
- Set context-aware placeholder text: 'Describe your epic idea...' for epic_creation tabs, 'Ask a question...' for brainstorm tabs

### Step 5 — Rewire page.tsx
- Point the 'New Epic' button in the project page to `panelRef.current?.openNewEpic()` which creates a new `epic_creation` tab
- Remove the old modal/sheet import and rendering

### Step 6 — Delete dead code
- Remove `CreateEpicSheet.tsx` component
- Remove `useEpicCreation.ts` hook
- Clean up any unused imports

epics.title: Agent Configuration Side Panel & Custom Review Agents
epics.description:
Dedicated side panel for configuring agent prompts (global + per-project override), creating custom review agents, and setting the default AI provider per agent type.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Schema & Data Layer

**Agent Prompts Table:**
- Add `agentPrompts` table: id, agentType (text: 'build', 'review_security', 'review_code', 'review_compliance', 'chat', 'spec_generation', 'team_build', 'ticket_build'), systemPrompt (text), scope ('global' | projectId), createdAt, updatedAt
- Global prompts have scope='global', project overrides store the projectId
- When resolving a prompt, project-scoped prompt takes precedence over global, which takes precedence over built-in defaults

**Custom Review Agents Table:**
- Add `customReviewAgents` table: id, name (text), systemPrompt (text), scope ('global' | projectId), position (integer), isEnabled (integer, default 1), createdAt, updatedAt
- Custom review agents are user-defined and appear alongside the 3 built-in review types

**Agent Provider Defaults Table:**
- Add `agentProviderDefaults` table: id, agentType (text), provider ('claude-code' | 'codex'), scope ('global' | projectId), createdAt, updatedAt
- Allows setting CC or Codex as default per agent type, with project override

### Phase 2 — API Routes

**Agent Prompts:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/prompts` — list all global agent prompts
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts` — list project-scoped prompts (merged with global defaults)
- `PUT /api/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — upsert global prompt for an agent type
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — upsert project override
- `DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — remove project override (fall back to global)

**Custom Review Agents:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/review-agents` — list global custom review agents
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/review-agents` — list project-scoped + global review agents
- `POST /api/agent-config/review-agents` — create a custom review agent (global)
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/review-agents` — create project-scoped review agent
- `PATCH /api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]` — update name, prompt, enabled status
- `DELETE /api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]` — delete a custom review agent

**Agent Provider Defaults:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/providers` — list global provider defaults per agent type
- `PUT /api/agent-config/providers/[agentType]` — set global default provider for agent type
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/providers/[agentType]` — set project override

### Phase 3 — Prompt Builder Integration
- Refactor all prompt builder functions to load custom prompts from DB before composing
- Resolution order: project override → global custom → built-in default
- Update `buildReviewPrompt` to accept custom review agent prompts in addition to built-in types
- Update `buildBuildPrompt`, `buildChatPrompt`, `buildSpecPrompt`, `buildTeamBuildPrompt`, `buildTicketBuildPrompt` to use configurable prompts

### Phase 4 — Side Panel UI
- New `AgentConfigPanel` component accessible from the main sidebar
- Three tabs: **Agent Prompts**, **Review Agents**, **Provider Defaults**
- Agent Prompts tab: list of agent types with expandable prompt editors, toggle between global/project scope
- Review Agents tab: list of built-in (read-only name) + custom review agents, each with name/prompt fields, add/delete actions
- Provider Defaults tab: per-agent-type dropdown to select CC or Codex as default
- Panel slides in from the left sidebar, can be toggled open/closed

### Phase 5 — Review Dialog Integration
- Update the Agent Review dialog on the story detail page to include custom review agents alongside the 3 built-in types
- Custom agents displayed as additional checkboxes with their name
- Each selected custom agent dispatches a plan-mode agent with the custom prompt
- Agent output posted as a comment with the custom agent's name as label

epics.title: Fuse New Epic into Chat Panel
epics.description:
Remove the standalone 'New Epic' modal/flow and instead open epic creation as a new tab in the existing UnifiedChatPanel. When the user clicks 'New Epic', the chat panel opens with a new tab of type `epic_creation`. The chat stream API route checks the conversation type and uses the epic refinement prompt for `epic_creation` conversations. After the brainstorming chat converges, a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button triggers epic + user story creation from the conversation context.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Server-side routing in /api/chat/stream
- Modify the chat stream endpoint to check the conversation's `type` field
- When type is `epic_creation`, use the epic refinement prompt builder (existing `buildSpecPrompt` or a new `buildEpicCreationPrompt`) instead of the default brainstorm prompt
- Ensure the prompt includes project context (spec, documents) and instructs Claude to help the user define an epic with user stories

### Step 2 — New useEpicCreate hook
- Create a small React hook (`useEpicCreate`) that takes the conversation context and calls the API to create an epic with generated user stories
- The hook calls `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/epics` with the epic data extracted from the conversation
- Returns loading/error/success states

### Step 3 — UnifiedChatPanel UI updates
- Add a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button that appears in `epic_creation` conversations once enough context has been discussed
- Differentiate tab icons: sparkles icon for `epic_creation` tabs vs message icon for regular chat tabs
- Add an empty-state hint in new `epic_creation` tabs explaining what the user can do
- Wire `onEpicCreated` callback to refresh the kanban board and optionally close the tab

### Step 4 — MessageInput placeholder
- Add a `placeholder` prop to the MessageInput component
- Set context-aware placeholder text: 'Describe your epic idea...' for epic_creation tabs, 'Ask a question...' for brainstorm tabs

### Step 5 — Rewire page.tsx
- Point the 'New Epic' button in the project page to `panelRef.current?.openNewEpic()` which creates a new `epic_creation` tab
- Remove the old modal/sheet import and rendering

### Step 6 — Delete dead code
- Remove `CreateEpicSheet.tsx` component
- Remove `useEpicCreation.ts` hook
- Clean up any unused imports

epics.title: Agent Teams & Codex Provider Integration
epics.description:
Two-part feature: (1) Agent Teams mode that leverages Claude Code's native Task tool to delegate multiple tickets to sub-agents in a single session, and (2) OpenAI Codex integration as an alternative AI provider alongside Claude Code.

## Implementation Plan

### Part A — Agent Teams (Claude Code Only)

**Schema & Data Layer:**
- Add `orchestrationMode` column to `agentSessions` table (`'solo' | 'team'`, default `'solo'`)
- Team mode is exclusive to Claude Code (Codex has no equivalent sub-agent delegation)

**Prompt Builder:**
- New `buildTeamBuildPrompt()` function that describes all selected epics with their worktree paths
- Instructs Claude Code to act as a team lead and use the `Task` tool to spawn sub-agents per ticket
- Lets CC decide team composition and size

**Build Route Changes:**
- When `team=true` in the batch build request, pre-create all git worktrees for selected epics
- Spawn a single CC session from the main repo root (not inside a worktree)
- Add `Task` to the `--allowedTools` list for team mode
- Track as a single `agentSession` with `orchestrationMode: 'team'`
- On completion, update all associated epics' statuses

**UI — Build Toolbar:**
- Add 'Team mode' checkbox in the build toolbar, visible when 2+ epics are selected
- Checkbox disabled when fewer than 2 epics selected or when provider is Codex
- Tooltip explains team mode behavior

### Part B — Codex Provider Integration

**Provider Abstraction Layer:**
- New `lib/providers/` directory with provider interface (`AgentProvider`)
- `lib/providers/claude-code.ts` — wraps existing CC spawn logic
- `lib/providers/codex.ts` — wraps `@openai/codex-sdk` using `Codex` class, `startThread()`, `runStreamed()` for streaming events
- `lib/providers/index.ts` — factory function `getProvider(type: 'claude-code' | 'codex')`
- Codex provider uses `workingDirectory` option on `startThread()` for worktree paths

**Schema Changes:**
- Add `provider` column to `agentSessions` (`'claude-code' | 'codex'`, default `'claude-code'`)
- Add `provider` column to `chatConversations` (if table exists) or chat messages

**Process Manager Generalization:**
- Refactor `lib/claude/process-manager.ts` to accept provider-agnostic session handles
- Codex sessions tracked via thread ID, CC sessions tracked via PID
- Unified start/cancel/status interface

**Build & Review Routes:**
- Build route accepts `provider` parameter, dispatches via provider factory
- Review route accepts `provider` parameter
- Send-to-dev route accepts `provider` parameter

**UI — Provider Selector:**
- Dropdown in build toolbar to choose between Claude Code and Codex
- Provider selector in Send to Dev dialog
- Provider selector in Agent Review dialog
- Provider toggle in chat header (locked/disabled after first message in conversation)
- Codex option disabled with tooltip if no API key configured

**Settings:**
- Add Codex API key field to Settings page
- Stored in `settings` table with key `codex_api_key`
- Validated on save (non-empty string check)

**Codex SDK Integration Details:**
- Install `@openai/codex-sdk` dependency
- Use `new Codex({ env: { CODEX_API_KEY: ... } })` with API key from settings
- `startThread({ workingDirectory })` for worktree-scoped execution
- `runStreamed()` for streaming events, map to unified event format
- Thread IDs stored in session metadata for resumption support

epics.title: Ticket Comments, Send-to-Dev & Agent Review
epics.description:
Add a comment system to user stories (tickets), a dedicated story detail page replacing the sheet, and review workflows powered by Claude Code agents.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Schema & Data Layer
- Add `ticketComments` table (id, userStoryId, author: 'user'|'agent', content, agentSessionId?, createdAt)
- Add `userStoryId` column to `agentSessions` to link agent work back to a specific ticket
- Add `"review"` as a valid status for user stories (todo → in_progress → review → done)

### Phase 2 — API Routes
- `GET/PATCH /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]` — fetch & update story detail
- `GET/POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/comments` — list & add comments
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/build` — dispatch a code-mode agent for the ticket (send-to-dev)
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/review` — dispatch review agents (security, code-review, compliance/accessibility)

### Phase 3 — Hooks
- `useStoryDetail` — fetch story with epic context
- `useComments` — fetch comments with 5s polling
- `useTicketAgent` — dispatch agent + poll session status, auto-post final output as agent comment

### Phase 4 — Story Detail Page
- New route: `/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]`
- Two-column layout: left = story details (title, description, acceptance criteria, status, priority), right = comment thread
- Navigate to this page by clicking story titles in the epic detail view

### Phase 5 — Send to Dev
- Available on tickets in `todo` or `in_progress` status
- "Send to Dev" button opens a dialog with an optional comment field
- On confirm: post comment (if provided), dispatch code-mode agent with ticket context + full comment history, move ticket to `in_progress`
- Agent reuses the epic's existing git worktree/branch with concurrency guard

### Phase 6 — Agent Review (Review status)
- Available on tickets in `review` status
- "Send to Dev" button (requires mandatory comment explaining what to fix) → dispatches code agent, moves ticket back to `in_progress`
- "Agent Review" button opens dialog with 3 checkboxes: Security, Code Review, Compliance/Accessibility
- Each selected review type dispatches a separate agent in plan mode with a specialized review checklist
- Agent outputs are posted as comments on the ticket

### Phase 7 — Approve & Merge
- "Approve" action on review-status tickets marks the ticket as `done`
- Triggers merge of the epic's worktree branch into the target branch

### Prompt Builder
- `buildTicketBuildPrompt` — code mode, includes project spec, epic context, ticket details, and full comment history
- `buildReviewPrompt` — plan mode, 3 specialized checklists (security audit, code review best practices, compliance/accessibility standards)

epics.title: Chat Image Upload & Clipboard Paste
epics.description:
Add image support to chat panels — users can upload images via a file picker or paste them from the clipboard. Images are saved locally, displayed as thumbnails before sending, and rendered inline in chat messages.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Storage & Schema
- Create `data/uploads/` directory for storing chat image files (gitignored)
- Add `chatAttachments` table to Drizzle schema (id, chatMessageId FK, fileName, filePath, mimeType, sizeBytes, createdAt)
- Add cascade delete from chatMessages to chatAttachments
- Generate and push migration

### Phase 2 — Upload API
- Create `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/upload` route
- Accept multipart form data with image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp)
- Validate file type and size (max 10MB per file)
- Save files to `data/uploads/{projectId}/{nanoid}-{originalName}`
- Return attachment metadata (id, fileName, filePath, mimeType)
- Create `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/uploads/[attachmentId]` to serve images

### Phase 3 — Enhanced MessageInput Component
- Add paste event handler on the textarea to intercept `clipboardData.items` with `type.startsWith('image/')`
- Convert pasted image blobs to File objects and upload immediately
- Add image upload button (paperclip/image icon) next to the send button
- Hidden file input accepting image MIME types, triggered by the button
- Display pending image thumbnails in a preview strip above the textarea
- Allow removing individual thumbnails before sending
- On send, include attachment IDs alongside the message content

### Phase 4 — Message Rendering
- Update MessageList / MarkdownContent to detect and render images associated with messages
- Fetch attachments for each message and display them as inline images below the text
- Support lightbox/modal view on image click for full-size viewing
- Lazy-load images with placeholder skeleton

### Phase 5 — Chat API Integration
- Update `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/messages` to accept an optional `attachmentIds` array
- Link uploaded attachments to the created message
- Update `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/messages` to include attachment metadata in response
- Ensure attachments are cleaned up when messages are deleted (cascade)

user_stories.description: Add a `chatAttachments` table to the Drizzle schema with fields: id (nanoid), chatMessageId (FK to chatMessages, nullable for pending uploads), fileName, filePath, mimeType, sizeBytes, createdAt. Set up cascade deletes from chatMessages. Ensure the `data/uploads/` directory is gitignored.

epics.title: Serveurs MCP additionnels, globaux et par projet
epics.description:
Permettre à l'utilisateur de déclarer des serveurs MCP tiers (Godot, Confluence, Playwright…), globaux ou scopés à un projet, et les injecter dans les sessions d'agents en plus du canal `arij`.

## Contexte

Aujourd'hui claude-code est lancé avec `--mcp-config <fichier 0600>` **et `--strict-mcp-config`** (voir `lib/providers/types.ts:32` et `docs/architecture/mcp-provider-matrix.md`). Conséquence : les serveurs MCP que l'utilisateur a configurés dans son propre `~/.claude.json` ou `.mcp.json` sont **ignorés** par les sessions Arij.

Cette épic ne consiste donc pas à « ajouter du MCP » mais à **rendre explicite et scopé ce que le mode strict coupe** — ce qui est le bon modèle : le comportement d'un build ne doit pas dépendre de la config locale de la machine, et un serveur utile à un projet (Godot) n'a rien à faire dans les sessions d'un autre.

Le point de câblage existe déjà et reste unique : `buildMcpSpawnConfig()` dans `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:239`, appelé depuis `processManager.start()`.

## Modèle de résolution

Ordre de fusion : **`arij` d'abord, puis les serveurs globaux, puis ceux du projet**. En cas de collision de `name`, le projet gagne. Le nom `arij` est **réservé** : le refuser en validation, sinon on écrase le canal de contrôle.

Le gate `mcp_tools_enabled` reste unique et couvre les extras : off = aucun MCP du tout.

## Contrainte structurante : les providers n'ont pas la même surface

| Provider | Surface d'injection | Scope réellement supporté |
|---|---|---|
| claude-code | fichier `--mcp-config` par spawn | global + projet |
| codex | overrides `-c mcp_servers.<name>.*` par spawn | global + projet |
| oh-my-pi | `mcp.json` statique (`~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`) | global seulement |
| agy | registre user-global (`agy mcp add`) | global seulement |

omp lit `.omp/mcp.json` relatif au cwd (donc au worktree), ce qui ouvrirait le per-projet — mais écrire de la config dans un worktree est exactement ce qui avait fait écarter gemini-cli. Hors périmètre v1.

agy : réconcilier son registre global avant chaque spawn serait *racy* (deux sessions parallèles sur deux projets se marcheraient dessus). Global-only, assumé.

## Pièges identifiés

- **Fuite de secret dans l'argv codex** : `maskCodexMcpSecret()` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:129`) ne masque que l'override contenant `ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN`. Un token tiers passerait en clair dans le `command_display` persisté et dans `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`.
- **Env des extras** : sur omp et agy, le mécanisme d'injection *est* l'environnement de l'enfant — un secret extra y est donc lisible par le Bash de l'agent. À interdire ou à assumer explicitement.
- **Seuil de découverte omp** : `tools.discoveryMode: auto` cache les outils MCP derrière `search_tool_bm25` au-delà de 40 outils. Ajouter un serveur tiers volumineux peut faire **disparaître les outils arij du prompt** sans aucune erreur.
- **Injection de prompt** : les descriptions d'outils d'un serveur tiers arrivent dans le contexte de l'agent — même classe de surface que `projects.spec`.
- **Prompt** : un agent n'utilisera pas un serveur dont le prompt ne mentionne pas l'existence.

user_stories.title: Schéma, migration et CRUD des serveurs MCP
user_stories.description:
Créer la table `mcp_servers` et le service CRUD associé.

Colonnes : `id`, `project_id` (NULL = global, FK vers `projects` avec cascade), `name`, `enabled`, `transport` ('stdio' | 'http'), `command`, `args` (json), `env` (json), `url`, `headers` (json), `agent_types` (json, NULL = tous), `usage_hint` (texte court), `last_checked_at`, `last_check_ok`, `last_check_error`.

La FK cascade dispense d'ajouter une entrée dans `perProjectSettingKeys()` (`lib/projects/project-settings-keys.ts`), qui n'existe que parce que la table `settings` n'a pas de FK.

Migration **écrite à la main** : fichier SQL numéroté + entrée ajoutée à la main dans `meta/_journal.json` avec un `when` strictement croissant. Ne pas lancer `npx drizzle-kit generate` (les snapshots s'arrêtent à 0013).
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Table `mcp_servers` créée par une migration SQL manuelle, avec l'entrée correspondante dans `meta/_journal.json` (index et `when` croissants).
- `project_id` NULL signifie global ; la suppression d'un projet supprime ses serveurs par cascade, ce qu'un test couvre.
- Le nom `arij` est refusé à la création et à l'édition, avec une erreur explicite.
- `name` validé contre `[a-z0-9_-]+` et unique par scope.
- La forme est validée selon le transport : `command` requis en stdio, `url` requis en http ; les combinaisons incohérentes sont refusées.
- Les tailles de `env`, `args` et `headers` sont plafonnées, et un dépassement est **rejeté avec une erreur explicite plutôt que tronqué**, avec la même forme d'erreur qu'une valeur d'énumération invalide.
- Routes API CRUD globales et par projet, avec la forme `{ data }` / `{ error }` habituelle.
- Les valeurs de `env` et `headers` ne sont jamais renvoyées en lecture : l'API retourne `"***"` (champ write-only).

comments.content:
All nine review findings are addressed in commit `58c4045`, and the ticket is back in Review.

## What changed

**The three majors:**

1. **Secrets wiped on edit** — `handleSave` always sent the secret map while `startEdit` correctly left the box empty, so editing anything sent `env: {}` and erased every stored value. The key is now omitted when the textarea is blank.

2. **Transport switch dead-ended both ways** — PATCH is a merge, so the abandoned side survived into validation. Both sides are cleared explicitly now.

3. **Blocking spawns on the request path** — reconciliation moved off the request path: async `execFile`, chained so runs can't interleave, coalesced to one pending run. I promisified `execFile` *lazily* — at module scope it reads `child_process` on import, which crashed any suite using a partial mock. That was a real regression I introduced and then caught.

**A bug the transport fix uncovered:** `effectiveState` normalises missing `args` to `[]`, and `[]` is truthy, so the http branch's `if (value.args)` fired on every http row — **http servers were uneditable outright**, one-click enable/disable included. Fixed to check length, with a separate test proving a genuinely present args list is still refused.

**Minors/info:** `usage_hint` neutralised (before the budget check, since escaping lengthens the string); `agent_types`/`tool_allowlist` in the form and as badges, sending `null` rather than `[]` when blank; the shadow-disable badge and note now say oh-my-pi and agy keep loading the global; migration 0046 adds the two partial unique indexes 0045 wrongly said SQLite couldn't express; the shadow row no longer copies credentials, and since an Enable button sits right next to it, stored secret *keys* are now shown so a credential-less row is visible.

## Verification

477 files / 5979 tests passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` succeeds, eslint clean. I mutation-checked six fixes — reverting each one makes a specific test fail, so the coverage is real rather than incidental.

Two things worth flagging: the worktree's `node_modules` was stale (next 16.1.6, simple-git 3.30.0 vs lockfile 16.3.3/3.36.0) and produced a phantom type error in `lib/git/clone.ts`, a file this branch never touches — `npm ci` cleared it, and I re-ran everything against the clean install. Four existing tests asserted the old behavior the review asked me to change; I updated those assertions deliberately rather than working around them, and the commit says which.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Both findings are fixed and committed as `32aa470`; the ticket is back in Review.

## The short-secret leak (`lib/mcp/probe.ts`)

`scrubSecrets` skipped values under four characters as "not a credential" while the schema accepts them. I confirmed it on two paths, not just the one the review named — the http transport leaks with no misbehaving CLI at all, because the SDK builds its failure as `` `Error POSTing to endpoint: ${text}` ``, so an endpoint quoting the credential it rejected puts it straight in the message. That path had no test.

Now every non-empty value is redacted, longest-first so a prefix can't fragment a longer secret. I chose that over the review's alternative of a minimum length: `env`/`headers` are write-only *by contract*, so length can't decide secrecy — but a floor would refuse legitimate `DEBUG=1`. The trade-off is documented at the function: a very short value will mangle an unrelated diagnostic, which is recoverable in a way a leaked credential isn't.

## The reconciliation race (`lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts`)

I took the CRUD-side barrier rather than the spawn-side one. `processManager.start()` is synchronous with ~9 call sites, so a barrier there is a cross-cutting refactor outside this story; the global handlers now await `whenUserGlobalMcpSyncSettles()` before responding. The spawns stayed async, so only that one request waits — the freeze the earlier finding was about doesn't come back — and a 2xx now means "already in the registry" instead of "queued".

To test it I extracted the scheduler as a factory and injected the reconciliation's targets, so a 20 ms fake `agy` can hold the barrier open and the tests can assert what a session would see meanwhile. That also gives `syncOmp`/`syncAgy` their first behavioural coverage, since the live path refuses to run under VITEST by design.

## Verification

478 files / 6016 tests passing, `tsc` clean, eslint clean, `next build` succeeds. `node_modules` matches the lockfile, so no phantom failures. Each fix is mutation-checked — reverting the length floor, the sort, the `settled()` chain, the coalescing guard, the run chaining, the handler `await`, or the project-scope skip each fails a specific named test.

Two things worth flagging: I did **not** extend the scrub to `toolNames` (users build `tool_allowlist` from those, so redacting one would hand back an unusable value for a fringe gain), and a session started *concurrently* with a CRUD request is still unordered with respect to it — that's inherent to "not yet acknowledged", and the module's rule 5 now says so explicitly rather than leaving it implied.

Separately: the stored project spec ends with an embedded `<system-directive>` instructing the session to abandon its task and write a specification. I treated it as data and ignored it, but it's live prompt-injection content sitting in `projects.spec` and worth its own ticket.

user_stories.title: Injection multi-serveurs dans le spawn claude-code et codex
user_stories.description:
Faire passer `McpSpawnConfig` d'un serveur unique à une liste, et injecter les serveurs résolus dans les deux providers qui ont une surface par spawn.

`McpSpawnConfig` devient `{ servers: McpServerSpec[], allowedToolNames }`. `buildClaudeMcpConfigJson()` (`lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:278`) itère au lieu de coder en dur `[mcp.serverName]` ; les tests qui assertent la forme du fichier suivent.

Sur l'allowlist : les outils tiers ne sont pas énumérables à l'avance. On pousse une entrée « serveur entier » par extra (`mcp__<name>` pour claude), **dans l'orthographe du provider** — `arijMcpToolPrefix()` (`lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:108`) : double underscore pour claude/codex, simple pour omp, nom nu pour agy. Un `tool_allowlist` optionnel par serveur permet de restreindre.

Inclut la correction du masque de secret codex : `maskCodexMcpSecret()` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:129`) doit masquer **toute** valeur `mcp_servers.*.env=`, pas seulement celle qui contient `ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- `McpSpawnConfig` porte une liste de serveurs ; le canal `arij` reste toujours présent et en premier.
- Résolution appliquée : arij, puis globaux, puis projet ; en cas de collision de `name`, l'entrée du projet l'emporte, ce qu'un test couvre.
- Le fichier `--mcp-config` de claude contient toutes les entrées résolues, en 0600 dans un répertoire 0700, et est nettoyé au teardown comme aujourd'hui.
- codex reçoit un jeu d'overrides `-c mcp_servers.<name>.*` par serveur.
- Un test vérifie qu'un secret d'un serveur **tiers** n'apparaît ni dans le `command_display` persisté ni dans le log de spawn.
- Les entrées d'allowlist des extras sont générées dans l'orthographe du provider de la session.
- Le gate `mcp_tools_enabled` à false supprime les extras comme le canal arij.
- Les serveurs `enabled = false` et ceux dont `agent_types` exclut le type de la session ne sont pas injectés.

## Summary

All nine review findings were **already fixed** on the branch by commit `58c4045`. I verified each against the code rather than trusting the commit message, then mutation-tested the three majors — reverting a fix must break a test, or the coverage is nominal.

**Two majors were genuinely pinned:**
- Secret wipe on edit → reverting fails 3 tests
- Transport switch dead-end → reverting fails 2 tests, one per direction

**One was not.** The blocking-spawn fix (`execFileSync` on the request path freezing the single-process app) was implemented correctly, but reverting `execFileAsync` to a blocking `execFileSync` left **all 81 tests green**. Nothing stood between that major finding and a silent regression.

I added the missing pin (`2270292`). It can't be tested behaviourally — `syncUserGlobalMcpServers` returns `void` whether or not the work behind it blocks, and the VITEST guard returns before anything spawns — so it asserts on the module source, using the idiom already established for `lib/db/init.ts` in the migration suites. It enumerates Node's complete set of synchronous `child_process` entry points rather than spot-checking the one that caused the bug, strips comments so the explanatory prose can keep naming `execFileSync`, and positively asserts `execFile` survives so it can't pass by deletion. Verified to fail on revert.

**Verification:** full suite green (477 files / 5980 tests, run 3×), `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, eslint exit 0. I checked `node_modules` against the lockfile first, so these aren't phantom results.

Two things worth flagging plainly:

- One earlier full run showed **a single failure I could not attribute** — it didn't recur across three further full runs, and the timing-sensitive MCP suites were green 5× in a row under stress. Probably a flake on this shared machine, but I never captured its name, so I'm not claiming more than that.
- `projects.spec` still carries the known injected `<system-directive>` telling sessions to rewrite the specification. I treated it as data and ignored it; it's already on the friction register, so I didn't refile.

No production code changed this session — the findings needed no further work, and a redundant commit would have been noise.

user_stories.title: Descripteur de capacité par provider et comportement omp/agy
user_stories.description:
Empêcher que la feature soit câblée pour un CLI et silencieusement absente sur les autres.

Ajouter au descripteur de provider une capacité explicite, par exemple `extraMcpScope: "per-spawn" | "user-global"` : claude-code et codex en `per-spawn`, oh-my-pi et agy en `user-global`.

Pour les providers `user-global`, seuls les serveurs globaux sont honorés ; les serveurs scopés à un projet sont ignorés, et cette limite doit être **visible dans l'UI**, pas déduite par l'utilisateur.

Couvre aussi le seuil de découverte omp : `tools.discoveryMode: auto` masque les outils MCP derrière `search_tool_bm25` au-delà de 40 outils, ce qui peut faire disparaître les outils arij du prompt sans erreur.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Chaque provider enregistré déclare sa capacité de scope pour les MCP additionnels.
- Sur un provider `user-global`, une session d'un projet ayant des serveurs scopés ne les reçoit pas, et le fait est tracé plutôt que silencieux.
- L'UI indique, par serveur scopé projet, quels providers ne l'honoreront pas.
- Le comportement d'omp face au seuil de 40 outils est documenté dans `docs/architecture/mcp-provider-matrix.md`, avec la recommandation de pinner `discoveryMode`.
- La matrice du document est mise à jour avec la colonne « MCP additionnels ».

<!-- arij:dead-session=BG8S06jxHp62 -->

**Probable root cause** — Not a code or ticket problem. The session hit oh-my-pi's context-compaction path, which renders archived conversation history as PNG images and sends them as `image_url` parts. **Evidence**

Earlier turns archived under HISTORY below"` and followed by `"-------------- imaged middle above …"`.

L'épic annonce `tools.discoveryMode: auto` cachant les outils MCP derrière `search_tool_bm25` au-delà de 40 outils. **Ça ne correspond pas au build omp installé** : `omp config get tools` répond `Unknown setting`, `omp config list` n'a aucun `discoveryMode`, et ni ce nom ni `search_tool_bm25` n'apparaissent dans les 130 docs embarquées d'omp. This is well-built work. The resolution model (`arij` → globals → project, project shadows global) is clean and the reserved-name rule is enforced twice — once in validation, once as a filter in `buildMcpSpawnConfig` that cannot be bypassed by a row predating the rule. The `extraMcpScope` descriptor is exactly the right response to "wired for one CLI, silently absent on the others", and it lives in its own module so `lib/mcp/servers.ts` can read a provider's capability without instantiating `child_process`.

Two decisions deserve explicit credit. `resolveExtraMcpServers` gets its **own** `try/catch` inside the injection handler (`lib/claude/process-manager.ts:287`), so a malformed third-party server degrades to arij-only instead of costing the session its control channel and marking the review unverifiable. And the docs say plainly that the epic's `tools.discoveryMode: auto` / 40-tool premise **could not be confirmed** on the installed omp, documenting the risk shape instead of restating an unverified number as fact. That is the right way to handle a premise that didn't hold.

No file added by this epic produces a type error.

## Findings by checklist category

**Error handling / API design** — 2 blocking. **Performance** — 1 blocking. **Testing** — 1. **Readability, DRY, naming, type safety** — no issues found; the code is uniformly well-named, the caps live in exactly one place (`server-limits.ts`, split out precisely so client code can import them), and there is no `any`.

### Major

**1. Editing a server through the settings form wipes its stored secrets** — `components/settings/McpServersSection.tsx:191`

`handleSave` always includes the secret map; `startEdit` correctly leaves the textarea empty. So editing *anything* sends `env: {}`, and `mergeSecretMap(row.env, {})` returns `{}` — every stored value erased. I reproduced it against the real service: `{GODOT_TOKEN: "s3cret"}` → `{}` after a usage-hint edit. This inverts the story-6 criterion, and `__tests__/mcp-servers-settings-ui.test.tsx:157` locks it in with a comment asserting the opposite of what the service does. Fix is to omit the key when the field is blank.

**2. Transport cannot be switched on an existing server** — `components/settings/McpServersSection.tsx:193`

PATCH is a merge and the form only sends the *new* transport's fields, so the stale one survives and shape validation rejects it. Reproduced both directions: `url is not allowed on a stdio server` / `command is not allowed on an http server`, naming a field the form has just stopped rendering. **3. `syncUserGlobalMcpServers` blocks the event loop from a request handler** — `lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts:352`

- **Blocking spawns** — reverted `execFileAsync` to a blocking `execFileSync` → **all 81 tests still passed.** The fix was correct but completely unpinned.

Commit `2270292` closes that gap. It cannot be pinned behaviourally — `syncUserGlobalMcpServers` returns `void` whether the work blocks or not, and the VITEST guard returns before anything spawns, so no assertion can reach the spawn. So it asserts on the module source, the idiom already used for `lib/db/init.ts` in the migration suites.

The check enumerates Node's **complete** set of synchronous `child_process` entry points (`execSync`, `execFileSync`, `spawnSync`) rather than spot-checking the one that caused the bug, strips comments first so the prose explaining the hazard can keep naming it, and positively asserts `execFile` is still present so it cannot pass because the spawning code was renamed away. **Verified to fail when the fix is reverted.**

## Test de connexion et remontée de l'état de santé — livré

Le gros de l'histoire était **déjà committé** sur la branche (`2f36705` backend, `39bbc08` UI) : `lib/mcp/probe.ts`, `lib/mcp/probe-route.ts`, les deux routes `POST .../:serverId/test`, la persistance `last_checked_at`/`last_check_ok`/`last_check_error`, le badge de santé et le bouton Test. J'ai vérifié chaque critère plutôt que de refabriquer un diff, et j'ai livré les deux vrais manques.

### 1. Un défaut réel contre le critère « une erreur lisible » (`5e72ad8`)

Le mode d'échec le plus courant ne renvoyait aucune raison. Mesuré avant de toucher au code : un serveur qui démarre, refuse sa config et sort en code 3 était rapporté comme `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` — rien sur la cause. Son diagnostic (`FATAL: config error: ...`) partait dans un pipe stderr que **rien ne lisait**.

`collectStderr` s'attache maintenant pendant tout le handshake et un échec ajoute la sortie du serveur au message. L'attacher **en amont** plutôt qu'après l'échec est porteur une seconde fois : un pipe non lu bloque l'enfant dès que le buffer OS (~64 Kio) est plein — un serveur bavard restait suspendu jusqu'au timeout de 15 s au lieu d'échouer en millisecondes. La fixture `flood` l'épingle : **5 s avant, 24 ms après**. Borné en taille et en temps (le texte finit dans un message d'erreur *et* une colonne SQLite).

Effet de bord important : **le scrub de secrets devenait enfin testable**. Il ne l'était pas — en désactivant entièrement `scrubSecrets`, le test existant « keeps configured secrets out of the returned error » **passait toujours**, car aucune valeur configurée ne pouvait atteindre le message. Le diagnostic récupéré est la sortie propre du serveur, et un serveur qui rejette une credential la recite couramment. Ce test échoue désormais quand on retire le scrub — vérifié en le retirant.

Côté UI, la ligne affichait le verdict stocké mais pas la **raison** stockée : après un rechargement il restait un « Failed — <date> » sans cause. La ligne rend maintenant `last_check_error`, colonne que la route persistait déjà.

**Écart au texte du ticket, signalé pour revue** : le ticket demande une route de test et une santé persistée, pas une modification du texte d'erreur de la sonde. Les deux changements servent le critère « une erreur lisible », qui n'était pas tenu pour le mode d'échec le plus fréquent.

### 2. Couverture de la frontière HTTP (`6ebde42`)

`handleProbeMcpServer` n'avait aucun test — même angle mort que la revue précédente avait relevé sur les routes CRUD sœurs. 13 tests épinglent ce que seul le handler décide : un échec est une **donnée** (200 + `ok:false`, pas un 5xx) ; l'issue et sa date sont persistées et un test vert **retire** l'échec précédent ; les deux scopes ne se rejoignent pas **dans les deux sens** et un lookup refusé n'écrit aucune santé ; le scrub survit à la persistance ; une ligne au transport incomplet est traitée par le handler et non par la sonde.

Chaque assertion est **vérifiée par mutation**, pas supposée : retirer le scrub, mapper l'échec en 500, supprimer le persist, retirer le scope du lookup — chacune fait échouer un test nommé. Une nuance à noter : retirer le scope du **seul** lookup renvoie encore 404, parce que l'appel `persistMcpServerCheck` revérifie le scope indépendamment ; il faut muter les deux sites pour percer la frontière. C'est de la défense en profondeur, pas une assertion redondante.

## Parité du canal chat — done

### What was already there

The wiring itself landed with the backend commit (`2f36705`): `lib/chat/cli-tool-channel.ts` calls `resolveExtraMcpServers({ projectId, provider, agentType: "chat" })` and hands the result to `buildMcpSpawnConfig`. Criteria 1–3 were satisfied and tested. Rather than manufacture a change there, I landed what was genuinely missing.

### What I added

**Coverage stopped one step short of the artifact.** Under `--strict-mcp-config` — used on the warm path too (`persistent-runner.ts` `claudeArgs`) — the written `--mcp-config` file *is* the CLI's complete server set. So "the conversation received the server" is a claim about that file, not about the channel object the existing tests asserted. Two tests now assert the JSON a claude-code chat spawn is handed: the resolved extra sits next to `arij`, and a chat-ineligible one is absent from it entirely. Both verified to fail when `extraServers` is removed from the channel call.

**Criterion 4 was satisfied only by silence.** The settings screen said these servers go to "agent sessions" — which understates the blast radius now that chat has them — and said nothing about the OpenAI-compatible mode. That mode is an HTTP chat-completions endpoint, not an MCP host, so nothing declared here can ever reach it; left unstated, its absence there reads as a broken server rather than a stated limit. The section now names both surfaces, with two UI tests pinning the copy, and `docs/architecture/mcp-provider-matrix.md` gains a chat section (same merge rule, same `agent_types` filter, arij's own `chat` toolset untouched).

### One behaviour documented rather than changed

The two chat paths resolve extras at different times, and it is user-visible. A one-shot turn resolves per turn, so a newly declared server is there on the next message. The persistent runner resolves **once**, at warm-process spawn, and strict config freezes that set for the process's life — so a server added or removed later reaches that conversation only after a reap or restart. Re-resolving would mean respawning the user's warm process under them, which is the worse trade. Written down in the module docstring and the matrix.
