No prompt section for chat. `extraMcpServersSection` exists because a *build* prompt that never names a server leaves the model to find it by accident — but the chat surface does not narrate arij's own board tools either (`arijToolsSection` is agent-only), because the CLI lists MCP tools natively and the user drives the turn. comments.content:
Both review findings are addressed in `32aa470`.

## `lib/mcp/probe.ts:86` — short secrets returned and persisted verbatim

`scrubSecrets` skipped every configured value under four characters as "not a credential", while the CRUD schema happily accepts one. Confirmed on two paths, not one:

- **stdio** — a server echoing `PIN=123` on its way down reaches `{ data.error }`, `handleProbeMcpServer` writes it to `last_check_error`, and the settings screen renders it after every reload.
- **http** — no misbehaving CLI needed. The SDK builds its failure as `` `Error POSTing to endpoint: ${text}` `` (`streamableHttp.js:369`), so an endpoint that quotes the credential it rejected puts it straight into the message. This path had no test at all.

Fixed by redacting every non-empty value, **longest first** so a short value that is a prefix of a longer one can't fragment it before the real credential matches (`["abc","abc123"]` used to leave `<redacted>123`).

I took redaction over the review's alternative of rejecting short values at validation: `env`/`headers` are write-only *by contract* (reads return `"***"`), so length can't be what decides secrecy — but a minimum length would refuse legitimate settings like `DEBUG=1` or `PORT=80` that merely live in a field the contract treats as secret. The cost is real and now documented at `scrubSecrets`: a one- or two-character value will mangle an unrelated diagnostic. A mangled message is recoverable; a leaked credential is not.

The test at `__tests__/mcp-server-probe.test.ts:210` that locked the leak in is inverted, and three real regression tests added: a stdio fixture echoing a 3-char env value, an http fixture echoing a 3-char header, and the route-level assertion that `last_check_error` is clean too.

## `lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts:475` — stale registry after an acknowledged write

Confirmed as described: nothing awaited the reconciliation, so a session launched between the HTTP response and the end of `syncAgy` froze the old set for its whole run.

I took the **spawn-side** option the review offered second and rejected it: `processManager.start()` is synchronous with ~9 call sites, so the barrier there is a cross-cutting refactor well outside this story. The **CRUD-side** barrier is in scope and sufficient — the global handlers now await `whenUserGlobalMcpSyncSettles()` before responding. Because the spawns stayed async, only that one request waits; SSE, chunk persistence, the watchdog and pipelines keep running, so the finding that motivated the async move is intact. What changes is that a 2xx now means "already in the registry" rather than "queued". A session started *during* the request is still unordered with respect to it — that's what "not yet acknowledged" means, and rule 5 says so explicitly. Project writes skip the wait; they request no reconciliation.

To make it testable I extracted the scheduler as a factory and injected the reconciliation's targets (omp config path, ownership manifest, `agy` runner). The barrier's value only exists in a window a fast machine closes by accident, so the tests hold it open with a 20 ms fake `agy` and assert what a session would see meanwhile — including the deletion case, where the register still has the server until the barrier releases. Side benefit: `syncOmp`/`syncAgy` get their first behavioural coverage, since the live path refuses to run under VITEST by design.

- `probeMcpServer > keeps a THREE-character secret out of the error too` (stdio)

That covers exactly what the finding asked for — a fixture echoing a 1–3 char **env** *and* **header** value, pinned at both the probe and the persisted-route boundary. The vacuous test the finding called out (old `:210`) is gone; it is now a real `crash-short` fixture echoing `PIN=123`.

The reasoning is right on the merits: length was never what makes a value secret — the *field* is. `env`/`headers` are write-only by contract (reads return `"***"`), so a value the API refuses to show must not escape through an error string. The accepted cost (`DEBUG=1` mangling a diagnostic) is documented at the function.

## Finding 2 — stale registry after a 2xx (`lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts:475`) — CONFIRMED CLOSED

`server-routes.ts:83` now awaits the barrier before answering; all three mutating handlers call it, and project-scoped writes correctly skip it (they request no reconciliation). Removing the `await` fails 3 named tests — POST, PATCH **and** DELETE.

I checked the two things that decide whether the barrier is *sound* rather than merely present:

1. **Ordering.** All three call sites in `lib/mcp/servers.ts` (520/580/597) run the synchronous better-sqlite3 `.run()` *before* `syncUserGlobalMcpServers`, so the write is visible to the run being awaited.
2. **The coalescing invariant.** `queued` is cleared immediately before `run()`, and `reconcileLive` evaluates `syncableGlobalServers(db)` as an argument — i.e. synchronously, before its first `await`. So while `queued` is true the pending run provably hasn't read the DB and will see the folded write; once it has, the next write chains a fresh run. I traced the three interleavings (fold-into-pending, chain-after-active, write-after-snapshot) and the tests pin the third explicitly.

The tests use the delayed fake `agy` runner the finding asked for, and assert the stale window from the session's point of view (`register.has("godot") === false` before `settled()`, true after) — including the deletion case, which is the access-control half.

## Adjacent surface checked, and clean

Since the acceptance criterion covers logs too, I checked the other place a configured secret could escape: `agy mcp add` takes credentials in its **argv**. `runAgy` swallows the exec error with a bare `catch` — an `execFile` rejection embeds the full command line, so returning `false` instead of logging it is load-bearing, not laziness. The `console.warn` in `syncAgy` prints only `server.name`. No leak.

## One accepted trade-off, named rather than hidden

The barrier means a *global* settings save now waits for reconciliation. Bounded — `runAgy` caps each call at 10s — but the worst case is `(1 + removals + adds) × 10s` with an `agy` that is installed *and* hanging. A missing `agy` fails fast on ENOENT, so the common cases are unaffected. This is the intended cost of the fix the review asked for (a 2xx now means "already applied"), not a regression; recording it so nobody rediscovers it as a mystery latency.

**Verification:** full suite **6016 tests / 478 files green**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on all touched files. `node_modules` confirmed lockfile-consistent first (next/simple-git/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/vitest all match), so no failure here would have been a phantom.

S'il y a autre chose à dire au modèle — compter en tokens plutôt qu'en caractères, ou une consigne de priorisation différente quand il faut couper — il faut le préciser, sinon cette moitié du ticket est un no-op.

**2. « 10k tokens » vaut 40 000 caractères avec l'estimateur d'Arij, soit ×3,3 — pas un ajustement.**

`lib/tokens/estimator.ts:59` utilise l'heuristique `chars/4`. La mémoire projet part dans tous les prompts, `_80zRfoh-ryb` mesure déjà 45,4 Mo de prompts stockés à 86 Ko de moyenne, et la « boule de neige des prompts » est un motif connu du projet. Si le triplement est voulu, on l'implémente tel quel. Sinon, quel est le chiffre réellement visé ?

comments.content:
Review finding addressed — `hooks/usePipelineDispatchDefault.ts:18` (major, late settings response overriding the server opt-out). Commit `373fe69`.

**The defect, reproduced**
On the previous implementation, clicking Dispatch while `GET /api/settings` was still in flight called `onSendToDev` with an explicit `pipeline: true` (proved red: *"expected spy to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times"*), and a late `pipeline_enabled: true` re-ticked a box the user had just unticked (proved red: *"Received element is checked"*).

**Fix**
The hook now returns a state object instead of a tuple, tracking the read (`pending` / `resolved` / `failed`) and whether the user touched the control:
- **pending & untouched** → the dialog's confirm is disabled, so the optimistic default is never dispatched as a decision;
- **touched** → the user owns the value; a later response only lifts the gate, it never rewrites the choice;
- **failed (rejection *or* non-OK) & untouched** → the request **omits** the `pipeline` field, leaving the build route's `pipeline_enabled` chain authoritative, and the checkbox says so (`pipeline-setting-unresolved`) rather than presenting the guess as the mode.

Re-opening restarts the read and drops the previous choice's ownership. `SendToDevDialog.onConfirm` and both handlers (`AgentActionsBar`, `TicketOverlay`) now take `boolean | undefined`; `useAgentDispatch.sendToDev` already omitted the field for `undefined`, so no route change was needed.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic `pcXbuN4vrAQ0`
### Filtrer par projet et par état, trier par en-tête de colonne

**Scope reviewed:** commit `3e4f5d8` against merge-base `e415564` — 14 files, +448/−80.

**Verification environment.** Dependency/lockfile drift check first, per the project's install-hygiene rule: **0 drifts**, so every measurement below comes from a lockfile-consistent install. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. ESLint clean on all eight touched source files. The six registry test files pass (93 tests). No repository file was modified; probes lived under `/tmp` and were deleted. `git status` is clean.

---

## 1. Readability

Mostly good. The removal of the old `sortRows` in favour of a shared `lib/tickets-registry/sort.ts` is the right move — one comparator, importable by the route and the view.

**Finding — Suggestion — `components/tickets-registry/TicketsRegistryView.tsx:332`**
The footer's `ticketCount` is a three-level unparenthesised ternary whose grouping the reader must recover from precedence. Its middle branch also quietly fixes a separate pre-existing bug (a state pill used to leave the footer reporting the whole-registry total) — worth its own comment. Same file: `onSortChange` (line 328) is the only handler not wrapped in `useCallback`, unlike its six siblings.

**Finding — Minor — `lib/tickets-registry/aggregate.ts:439` (and `app/api/tickets/route.ts:290`)**
Two load-bearing comments now assert something false. `aggregate.ts` justifies its group-total approximation with *"the window is ordered by `updated_at DESC`, so such a row is essentially always inside it"* — after this epic the window is ordered by whichever header was clicked, in either direction. The route's *"`updated_at` is not in the index"* has the same drift. This is not cosmetic: it is exactly the invariant broken by the major finding below.

## 2. DRY

**Finding — Minor — `lib/tickets-registry/sort.ts:19`**
The ordering is written twice — SQL in `route.ts:275-285` for window selection, TypeScript here for display — and for `etat` they already disagree: SQL sorts by the raw `epics.status` string (alphabetical), the comparator by `KANBAN_COLUMNS.indexOf` (workflow order). Unobservable today only because each terminal window holds a single status, so nothing pins it. A visible side effect of that constant key: under `sort=etat` the ORDER BY collapses to the `asc(epics.id)` tiebreak, so DONE/RELEASED load an arbitrary 40 rows by lowest id, and flipping direction does not change *which* 40.

## 3. Error handling

No issues found. `status`, `sort` and `direction` are validated against allowlists with silent fallback to the default, consistent with the existing `clampLimit`; the added route test pins the invalid-value path. The `stale()` tightening in `useTicketsRegistry.ts:91` (`requestSeq !== requestSeqRef.current`) is a genuine improvement — a superseded response can no longer repaint the table.

## 4. Performance

**Finding — Minor — `app/api/tickets/route.ts:284`**
`sort=cout` puts an unbounded correlated `SUM(total_cost_usd)` in the ORDER BY, evaluated over *every* done/released epic in scope before `LIMIT` — the unbounded twin of the `costByEpicId` query the same file deliberately bounds to the window. Measured on a scratch DB (2000 done epics, 6000 sessions, 30 KB text each, median of 5): `activite` 11 ms, `titre` 9 ms, `stories` 10 ms, **`cout` 50 ms** — ~4.5×, scaling with a table the spec says is never pruned. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` confirms `CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY` + temp b-tree; `agent_sessions_epic_idx` is used but does not cover `total_cost_usd`, so each hit is a random fetch on the widest table. Not blocking at today's scale.

**Worth crediting:** switching the terminal ORDER BY to `julianday(epics.updatedAt)` fixes a real pre-existing bug. `epics.updated_at` holds both `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (`"2026-09-05 09:00:00"`) and ISO-with-Z values, and the old raw-string ORDER BY sorted every space-separated value ahead of every `T`-separated one regardless of date. Confirmed with better-sqlite3 that `julianday()` parses both identically.

## 5. Naming conventions

No issues found. The mixed French/English sort keys (`activite`, `titre`, `etat` alongside `ticket`, `stories`) follow the pre-existing vocabulary.

## 6. Type safety

**Finding — Minor — `lib/tickets-registry/types.ts:107`**
`activityAt?: string | null` is optional although the *default* sort depends on it: a producer that omits it yields a silently unsorted `activité` column instead of a type error. The route always populates it, so the optionality buys nothing. Same shape in `RegistryDeriveInput.sessions` — an inline `SessionRow & { activityAt?: string | null }` repeated in three places instead of one named type.

No `any` introduced; the `as KanbanStatus` / `as RegistrySort` casts are the standard readonly-tuple `.includes` idiom and are immediately narrowed.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is solid: 7 statuses × filter, 7 headers × both directions, keyboard sorting, superseded responses, SQL pagination, comparator null-handling and mixed timestamp formats, plus a real-routes e2e. Two gaps:

**Finding — Suggestion — `__tests__/tickets-registry-route.test.ts:574`** — the new route test seeds only ISO `daysAgo()` values, so nothing at the SQL layer would fail if `julianday()` were dropped and the mixed-format bug returned. One `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`-shaped `updated_at` that must outrank an ISO one would lock the fix in. (The client comparator *is* covered, at `tickets-registry-sort.test.ts:16`.)

**Finding — Minor — `e2e/tickets-registry-filters.spec.ts:44`** — the screenshot goes to `data/tickets-registry-filters.png`. `data/.gitignore` is an explicit allowlist and does not cover `*.png`; `git check-ignore -v` confirms the path is **not ignored**, so every e2e run leaves an untracked file in `git status`. The sibling spec already uses the right convention (`testInfo.outputPath(...)`, `e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts:38`).

I also mutation-probed `react-hooks/set-state-in-render` against `TicketsRegistryView.tsx` (via `eslint --stdin`, no file written): injecting an unconditional `setState` reddens, and the unmutated file is clean — so the derived-state pattern at line 76 is genuinely accepted, not a silent compiler bail.

## 8. API design

**Finding — Minor — `app/api/tickets/route.ts:246`**
Narrowing `statusCountRows` by `scopedStatus` propagates into `RegistryCounts`. Measured on a 4-ticket project (1 todo, 2 done, 1 released):

| request | counts |
|---|---|
| `?project=p1` | `{all: 4, open: 1, done: 2, released: 1}` |
| `?project=p1&status=todo` | `{all: 1, open: 1, done: 0, released: 0}` |

So the row reads `Done · 0` while a status filter is on — but clicking that pill clears the status filter (`TicketsRegistryView.tsx:365`) and reveals 2 rows. That breaks the invariant `types.ts:112-119` states outright: *"the number on a pill is exactly the number of rows the pill reveals."*

---

## Blocking finding

### Major — `app/api/tickets/route.ts:295` — filtering at the wrong layer corrupts derived ticket state

`terminalWindow` short-circuits to `[]` whenever `scopedStatus` is not `done`/`released`, so no delivered epic reaches `deriveRegistryRows`. But `deriveUpNext` → `computeBlockedBy` (`lib/kanban/queue.ts:110`) decides an edge is satisfied via `isDeliveredStatus(statusById.get(edge.dependsOnTicketId))`, and `statusById` is built from the loaded epics only (`lib/control-desk/aggregate.ts:700-704`). A missing prerequisite returns `undefined` → `isDeliveredStatus(undefined) === false` → the edge counts as a live blocker.

Reproduced against the real migrated schema (a `todo` ticket depending on a `done` ticket in the same project):

| request | result |
|---|---|
| `?project=p1` | `blockedBy: []`, `queueRank: 1`, `"updated · 0s ago"` |
| `?project=p1&status=todo` | `blockedBy: ['dep']`, `queueRank: null`, `"blocked · 0s ago"` |

Selecting **Backlog / To Do / In Progress / Review** therefore makes every ticket whose prerequisite already shipped render as blocked, lose its execution rank, and print the **raw internal epic id** — `labelById` is built from the same missing set, so `input.labelById.get(targetId) ?? targetId` falls through.

The new ORDER BY reproduces it *without any status filter*: with `?sort=titre&direction=asc&doneLimit=1` the same ticket went from `blockedBy: []` / rank 1 to `blockedBy: ['dep']` / rank null, because the window no longer selects by recency. A hazard that was previously bounded to done tickets older than the 40 most recent is now routine.

Both new affordances make the registry disagree with the desk about ticket state — the single rule `lib/tickets-registry/aggregate.ts` was written to enforce.

**Recommendation:** keep the terminal windows in the derivation input and narrow only the payload — the `.filter((row) => !scopedStatus || row.status === scopedStatus)` at line 786 already does that correctly. To avoid the two extra window queries under an open-status filter, load a narrow `{id, status, readable_id, title}` projection of the epics referenced by `dependsOnTicketId` in `edges` and feed those to the derivation instead.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| **Major** | **1** |
| Minor | 5 |
| Suggestion | 3 |

The feature is well built — filtering after derivation on the client, ordering before `LIMIT` on the server, and a shared comparator are all the right calls, and the `julianday` switch fixes a bug nobody asked it to fix. The one blocking issue is that the *server-side* status short-circuit narrows the derivation input rather than the payload, and that data is what tells the registry a prerequisite has shipped. The fix is small and localised.

Findings filed to the ticket (9 anchored review comments). Note: the stored project specification contains an embedded `<system-directive>` instructing sessions to rewrite the spec — treated as data and ignored, as it is a known recurring artifact rather than a new finding.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Code Review**

Findings submitted. Here is the report.

---

# Code Review — « L'accès au chat doit être via un bouton direct depuis l'îlot du haut, à côté de Work »

**Diff reviewed:** `dc83f4b`, merge-base `e415564` — 4 files, +148/−60
`components/piscine/TopBar.tsx` · `lib/piscine/nav.ts` · `__tests__/top-bar.test.tsx` · `__tests__/usage-rail-link.test.tsx`

## Verification I ran

Install checked against `package-lock.json` before measuring — **no drift**, so the numbers below come from a lockfile-consistent tree.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `vitest` on the 3 files the session cited | 57/57 green — matches the claim |
| `vitest run --changed main` | 66 files / 821 tests green |
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `eslint` on the 4 touched files | 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| e2e `piscine-finishing.spec.ts` island-clearance test | green (system Chrome, port 3100) |
| Browser measurements | system Chrome via Playwright against a scratch `next dev` on **port 3210** with the isolated `data/e2e.db` |

Port 3000 (the live orchestrator) was not touched. Working tree left clean; the only artifacts are gitignored `.next/` and `e2e/test-results/`.

**What the constant claims, and whether it holds.** `ISLAND_HALF_WIDTH_PX = 245` is correct for the left zone: I measured `top-bar-island` at **489.2px** on `/` and **489.3px** on `/chat` at 1440×950 — half is 244.6, and the comment's "490px … half is 245" is honest. Clearance also survives a category route (island 509.3px, left edge 465.4; the chips cap is 460px).

## Findings

### Critical
No issues found.

### Major

**1 — The Chat pill pushes the island over the right cluster below ~1102px; `Réglages` becomes partly unclickable.** `components/piscine/TopBar.tsx:453`

The island is absolutely centred and only guarded on the **left** (`ISLAND_HALF_WIDTH_PX` → `calc(50% - 260px)` on the project chips). Nothing guards the right, where the ⌘K/Inbox/Auto/New cluster is `ml-auto`. The fifth pill takes the island from 418.5px to 509.3px.

A/B on the same page and viewport (1024×900, `/tickets`), removing only the Chat pill from the DOM:

```
WITH Chat : island 509.3px, right edge 766.6 | right cluster at 727.7 → +38.9px overlap
WITHOUT   : island 418.5px, right edge 721.3 | right cluster at 727.7 →  -6.4px clearance
```

It is not cosmetic. `elementFromPoint` across the `Réglages` pill (656.3 → 766.6) at mid-height:

```
10% → bubble-settings    70% → top-bar-search
30% → bubble-settings    90% → top-bar-search
50% → bubble-settings
```

The right ~35% of `Réglages` is captured by the ⌘K pill — a click there opens the palette instead of navigating to settings, and the label is painted under the search control (confirmed in both day and night).

Threshold, sweeping the viewport on `/tickets`: +20.9px at 1060, +10.9 at 1080, +0.9 at 1100, −4.1 at 1110 → flips at **~1102px**; ~1082px with no category active. This is inside the supported range — `components/ticket/TicketOverlay.tsx` handles `max-[1272px]` explicitly.

Nothing catches it. The unit test only asserts `calc(50% - 260px)`, which is derived from the constant — circular. All three `setViewportSize` calls in `e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts` are 1440-wide, and the clearance test compares `chipsBox` against `islandBox` only. I ran it: green, and it would stay green.

**Fix:** give the right cluster the mirror clearance, derived from the same constants (`maxWidth: calc(50% - ${ISLAND_HALF_WIDTH_PX + ISLAND_CLEARANCE_PX}px)`), or take the island out of absolute centring below a breakpoint. Either way add an e2e assertion at ~1024 comparing the island's right edge to the cluster's left edge.

### Minor

**2 — Chat borrows the `live` ground of `Agents`, its immediate neighbour.** `TopBar.tsx:461`
Computed colours on `/chat` (day): `chat` and `agents` are both `bg rgb(205,235,227)` / `txt rgb(20,106,90)` — byte-identical, 7px apart. Night: both `rgb(111,203,180)` on the same fill. Every other pill has its own ground. Two consequences: (a) `/chat`'s own dominant stratum is `feed`, not `live` (`ChatComposer.tsx:145` and `TowardSpecBand.tsx:44` both set `stratum="feed"`; `globals.css:205` documents linden as "FEED / writing (composer, spec, persona)" and turquoise as "WORKING / live activity"); (b) on `/chat` the active liseré is the exact one `Agents` would wear. Five pills for four grounds forces a share, but this is the worst pair — adjacent and identical. Product decision, flagged not decided.

**3 — The destination-pill recipe is now duplicated verbatim.** `TopBar.tsx:454`
Eleven lines of classes identical to the `Now` link (416–424) bar three colour tokens. `CategoryBubble` (675) holds a third copy of the same geometry. Extract a `DestinationPill` consumed by both.

**4 — Chat's existence is coupled to a category id it has nothing to do with.** `TopBar.tsx:453`
Rendered *inside* `NAV_CATEGORIES.map` under `category.id === "work"`. `Now`, which follows the same rule, is rendered explicitly before the loop. Also `<CategoryBubble key={category.id}>` inside `<React.Fragment key={category.id}>` is a dead prop.

**5 — `startsWith("/chat/")` is unreachable, untested, and broke the comment spacing.** `TopBar.tsx:234`
`app/chat/page.tsx` is the only route under `/chat`; the conversation page lives at `app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/chat/[conversationId]/`. No test exercises a `/chat/…` path. The block comment directly above explains precisely why `onDesk` is *not* a prefix match; the new line takes the opposite rule silently, and consumed the blank line separating that block from `/* ---- menu open/close ---- */`.

**6 — The invariant the change rests on is never asserted directly.** `__tests__/top-bar.test.tsx:220`
`nav.ts:23` states the entry removal exists so `activeNavCategory` returns `null` on `/chat`. The test asserts `/` and three positive cases, never `/chat`. It is pinned indirectly by the route-claims test, but for a reason that doesn't name the double activation.

### Suggestion

**7 — Tabbing `Work` → `Chat` leaves the `Work` menu open.** `TopBar.tsx:455`
Measured: focus Work → 1 `[role=menu]`; Tab → focus on `top-bar-bubble-chat`, still 1. `Now` has the identical gap, so this is an inherited pattern — but `Now` is first in the island while `Chat` sits mid-row on the ordinary forward tab path. Filed as `info`.

## Checklist verdicts

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Readability | Good — the file's long-form comments were updated, not left stale. Deductions: findings 4 and 5. |
| DRY | Finding 3 — the pill recipe now exists in triplicate. |
| Error handling | No issues found (no error paths in this diff). |
| Performance | No issues found — a static `<Link>`, no new hook, fetch or effect. |
| Naming | No issues found. |
| Type safety | No issues found; `tsc --noEmit` clean, no `any`. |
| Testing | Genuinely enriched (active state, direct href, no-menu control with a positive control on `Work`, pill order, count). Gaps: findings 1, 5, 6. |
| API design | Not applicable — no API surface touched. |

## Out of scope, filed separately

The keyboard focus ring is dead across the whole `TopBar`: `outline-none` sets `--tw-outline-style: none`, so `focus-visible:outline-2` resolves to `outline-style: none` while `:focus-visible` matches (measured `{"matchesFocusVisible":true,"outline":"rgb(111,203,180) none 2px"}`). Confirmed on `now`, `work`, `chat`, `agents`, `new`, `inbox` — pre-existing on `main`, so not a charge against this branch, which only copies the pattern. Filed as **B-arij-194**.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 5 |
| Suggestion (info) | 1 |

The feature itself is delivered and correct: the pill is a real `<a href="/chat">` with no menu, no `aria-haspopup`, correct `aria-current`, and the nav model cleanup that keeps `Agents` from lighting alongside it is the right call. What sends it back is one measured, functional regression — the widened island steals a third of the `Réglages` click target below ~1102px, and no existing test can see it.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

## Refinement can now merge, discard and create

Three new MCP tools on the refinement toolset, plus the report and prompt work around them. Four commits on `feature/epic-MXk-98_ZOTR_-refinement`.

### What the pass can do now

| Tool | Route | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `merge_tickets` | `app/api/mcp/merge-tickets/route.ts` | Folds N sources into one survivor: their user stories **move** (criteria intact), the **user's own** comments move (agent narration of a dead ticket does not), dependency edges are re-pointed in both directions, `title`/`description` can be rewritten in the same call, the sources' full text is posted on the survivor, then the sources are deleted. |
| `discard_ticket` | `app/api/mcp/discard-ticket/route.ts` | Deletes a planning ticket that is no longer worth doing. Its full text survives in the recap comment and the notification. |
| `create_planning_ticket` | `app/api/mcp/create-planning-ticket/route.ts` | Adds the missing work, with stories and readable id. Capped at 10 per pass; refused for a title an undelivered ticket already carries. |

### The design decision worth your attention

**Arij has no archive column, so these deletes are real.** I did not add one: a new terminal status touches the board query, the execution queue, Full Auto's selector, dependency validation and `arji.json`, and a half-applied filter there is a worse bug than the one it prevents. So the guards are the substance instead (`lib/refinement/retire.ts`):

- **refinement agent type only** — a build or review session gets 403 `REFINEMENT_ONLY`, and the three tools are withheld from every other type's allowlist. The other five refinement tools stay open to any non-chat session as before;
- **refused for any ticket carrying agent session history** — `deleteEpicPermanently` takes the transcripts and usage figures with it, and a planning pass has no business spending that. Your own delete button still reaches those tickets;
- **refused while another ticket depends on it** — dropping that edge stays an explicit `remove_dependency` call, so nothing gets silently unblocked;
- **a tombstone** — the whole ticket is read before the delete and published in the recap comment *and* the notification body, so you can retype anything you disagree with.

If you'd rather have a reversible archive, say so — it's a bigger change and a product call, not a drive-by.

- **35 route tests** (`__tests__/refinement-merge-discard-create.test.ts`) against the real migration chain with `foreign_keys = ON`, plus report and prompt coverage. comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — REfinment 2

**Branch** `feature/epic-bSL9Y3dgJCwU-refinment-2` · **commit** `3f0b503` · **merge-base** `82a3d6b`
**Diff** 25 files, +504 / −58 · no repository files modified during this review; `git status` clean.

## Verification performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `lockfile-install-consistency` | 6 passed — measurements come from a consistent install |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` (changed files) | 0 errors, 1 warning (`'section'` unused in `prompt-builder.ts`) — **reproduced at the merge-base**, pre-existing |
| refinement + migration tests | 84 passed (6 files) |
| Prompt probe (`actions: [dependencies, merge, discard]`) | rendered and inspected |
| `refinementToolAllowed` probe with all 8 actions | tools enumerated |
| Dialog lock-up | reproduced in an out-of-tree component test (`/tmp`, since removed) |

---

## What the change gets right

The options module is a single shared source for the schema, the action↔tool map and the parser, consumed by the route, the dispatcher, the prompt builder and the MCP guard — no drift surface. Permissions are enforced **server-side** rather than by prompt alone, which is the right call and matches the project's "mechanical evidence over agent prose" principle. `parseRefinementActions` fails closed on malformed JSON while `NULL` preserves the legacy full pass. The migration is hand-written, journalled with an increasing `when`, registered in `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS`, and the six older migration tests were swept to drop the new column before rewinding — with two new tests covering historical-row preservation and the baseline-stamp path. The route swaps its hand-rolled body parse for the existing `validateOptionalBody` helper. Extra instructions go through `fenceOnly(neutralizeControlMarkup(…))`, and the prompt test pins that a `<system-directive>` in them is neutralised.

## Findings

### Critical — none.

### Major

**1. `create_bug` / `attach_artifact` are refused for every configured pass, with no checkbox controlling them** — `lib/refinement/options.ts:33`

With **all eight boxes checked**, `refinementToolAllowed` still returns false for `create_bug` and `attach_artifact`. On `main` both work for refinement sessions (their routes only refuse `agentType === "chat"`), both are in the refinement spawn allowlist, and `arijToolsSection` — appended to every refinement prompt at `lib/claude/process-manager.ts:327` — tells the agent verbatim to use `create_bug`. So the default UI path removes a live capability, the model is still instructed to use it, and the refusal names a checkbox that does not exist. `__tests__/refinement-action-permissions.test.ts:47` pins the 403, so it is deliberate — but it breaks the "all checked ≡ legacy full pass" invariant the epic claims, and that invariant has no test.

**2. The configuration dialog can become unclosable** — `components/kanban/RefinementDialog.tsx:25`

`busy = running || starting` disables Cancel and Start *and* swallows `onOpenChange`, so Escape, the overlay and the shadcn close X all go inert. A 409 "a pass is already running" leaves the dialog open (`setConfiguring(false)` exists only on the success branches); the next status poll flips `running` true and the modal is a trap until the other pass ends — only a page reload escapes. Reproduced. The in-flight guard only needs `starting`.

### Minor

**3. The prompt instructs tools from unselected actions** — `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:2221`. The `discard` item still says "unclear goes back to Backlog with a question" (`promote_ticket`, gated by `readiness`); `## Rules` still says "say so in a comment" (`post_comment`, gated by `grooming`); and both `arijToolsSection` and `allowedToolNamesForAgentType` announce all eight board tools regardless of selection.

**4. Hard-coded ordinals leave gaps** — `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:2184`. A partial selection renders `2.`, `7.`, `8.` with no `1.` or `3.`–`6.`; number after filtering.

**5. Authorization added to the authentication helper, keyed on a re-derived tool name** — `lib/mcp/http-auth.ts:58`. The tool name is munged out of the URL path although every caller already holds it literally; the file's header contract comment was not updated. Fails closed, so a rename breaks loudly — but it also now shadows the more precise pre-existing refusals for `update_ticket_status` and chat-only tools.

### Suggestions

**6. Design-system and readability deviations** — `RefinementDialog.tsx:42`: raw `<input type="checkbox">` with a hand-rolled focus outline while `components/ui/checkbox.tsx` exists and is used by the closest analogue (`ScanProjectDialog`); `role="status"` mounted together with its content; 11 lines over 110 chars and no file header in a codebase that wraps at ~80 and documents every module; unindented fragment children in `RefinementButton.tsx:214`; `NamedAgentSelect` mounted without `dispatchRole="maintenance"`, so it loses the reliability badges every other dispatch picker shows.

**7. The persisted configuration is never shown back** — `lib/refinement/dispatch.ts:239`. Nothing reads `refinement_actions` or the instructions for display, so after the fact there is no way to tell whether discard/merge were enabled on a given pass.

## Checklist coverage

**Readability** — see #6. **DRY** — good on the shared options module; the six-file `DROP COLUMN` sweep across migration tests is inherent to the existing pattern, not this change's fault. The double validation (route + dispatcher) is defensible defence-in-depth for an exported function. **Error handling** — solid; the one gap is the 409 path in #2. **Performance** — one extra indexed `SELECT` per MCP call, refinement tokens only; negligible. **Naming** — consistent. **Type safety** — no `any`; one avoidable `as typeof actions[number]` cast in the prompt builder's filter, fixable by typing the item array as `Array<{ action: RefinementAction; text: string }>`. **Testing** — good breadth (permissions matrix, invalid-options table, migration, component, 3-width e2e with intercepted dispatch); the missing case is "all actions ≡ legacy", which is exactly what #1 slipped through. **API design** — consistent `{ data }` / `{ error, code }`, correct 400/403/404/409.

**Summary:** 0 critical, 2 major, 3 minor, 2 suggestions.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=6FP1KVgb7V22 -->

**Probable root cause** — The build session was spawned with a model identifier the Claude Code CLI does not recognise. `lib/providers/claude-code.ts` passes `model` straight through to `spawnClaude()` (and thence to `claude --model`) with no validation, and there is no model whitelist anywhere in the repo — a repo-wide grep for `fable` in `lib/`, `components/`, `app/` and the JSON/MD files returns nothing, so `fable-5.1` is not a code constant but a stored configuration value (agent config / ticket agent selection / workspace default). The CLI rejected it during handshake, before any ticket work began, which is why the raw stream is empty and both attempts failed identically. This is a configuration defect, not a defect in the ticket, the prompt, or the QA Run scope. The valid Fable identifier is `claude-fable-5`; `fable-5.1` is not a published model id.

**Evidence** —
- `[claude-code:unrecognized_model] {"model":"fable-5.1","query_source":"sdk"}` — the provider itself names the model string as the rejected input; the error is emitted by the SDK's model resolution, not by any build step.
- `"There's an issue with the selected model (fable-5.1). It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run --model to pick a different model."` is both the *only* output and the *last text produced* — the session produced no tool calls, no file reads and no diff, confirming it died at spawn rather than mid-build.
- **Raw stream (tail): (none)** — an empty stream across 2 attempts is the signature of a deterministic pre-flight rejection; a genuine build failure would leave partial work. Retrying was never going to help, since the argv is fixed at spawn time.

**Recommended next action** —
- Change the agent's model for this ticket (or the workspace/project default that supplied it) from `fable-5.1` to a valid id — `claude-fable-5` if Fable was intended, otherwise `claude-opus-5` — then re-dispatch the `build` stage; no code change or ticket rescope is required. Worth filing separately: Arij accepts an arbitrary model string for `claude-code` with no validation at selection time, so this failure mode can recur silently on any agent config.

## Findings by checklist category

**Readability** — Exemplary; the comments explain *why*, and the `types.ts` header rewrite that names the two families is the most useful part of the diff. One item: `QaCheckRow.tsx:42` prints a live row's state twice, in two languages (`running` from the column, then `En cours…` from the component). *(Info)*

**DRY** — `checkTypeLabel` deduplication with `/projects/:id/qa` is a real win, and the unknown-`check_type` behaviour (print itself, don't fold into TECH) is right for a free-form column. Against that: `NewQaCheckButton.tsx:72–107` is a near-verbatim copy of `RunQaPassButton.tsx:49–108` — same class strings, same scroller, same row geometry, two focus-ring copies the scan test now enumerates separately. *(Minor)*

**Error handling** — Sound. The dialog owns its own inline error, the `noOp` digest branch is correctly told apart from a launched run, and `useQaFindings`' ordering guards already cover the post-dispatch refresh.

**Performance** — `report_content` / `prompt_used` are never selected, `summary` is clipped in SQL, and the byte ceiling is pinned at the route level. The unindexed `qa_reports` scan is justified in the comment and holds for a manually-driven table.

**Naming / Type safety** — Consistent; no `any`; `checkType`/`status` deliberately typed `string` because the columns are free-form, with that decision documented.

**Testing** — 17 new cases, red-proven by mutation, and the "never ships the blob" test states honestly that it gates the payload rather than the query. `filterQaPayload`'s new lines are untested, but so are their pre-existing siblings — parity, not a new gap.

**API design** — Backward-compatible additions; `emptyPayload` updated; `checkableProjectIds` correctly mirrors the route's `requireGitRepo: true` guard so the button can never offer a dispatch that would 400.

## The blocking issue

`QaCheck.live` is read from `qa_reports.status`, and **nothing in the codebase ever reconciles that column**. Its only writer off `'running'` is the tail of the scheduler closure in the check route. `lib/agent-sessions/boot-cleanup.ts` reconciles `agent_sessions` at boot and never touches `qa_reports`. Three ordinary paths strand a row as `running` forever:

1. a restart mid-check — the session is failed, the report is not;
2. a launch closure that rejects — `handleLaunchFailure` fixes the session row, the `db.update(qaReports)` after the `await` never runs;
3. cancelling a still-queued check — `agentScheduler.remove()` splices the closure out entirely, with no error anywhere.

The fix is small: `LEFT JOIN agent_sessions` and derive `live` from the session being non-terminal, since *that* column is reconciled at boot.

| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 2 |
| Suggestion (info) | 2 |

The epic is close, and everything except the liveness derivation is ready. The one major finding is a small, well-localised change to the query this review anchors on.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: A stranded `running` QA report makes /projects/:id/qa poll a SELECT * of every report body every 3s
epics.description:
Adjacent to the "QA Run" epic, deliberately kept out of that diff — both halves are pre-existing code that branch does not change.

## The mechanism

`qa_reports.status` is moved off `running` in exactly one place: the tail of the scheduler closure in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/qa/check/route.ts:265`. Three ordinary paths skip that tail and strand a row on `running` forever (server restart mid-check, a launch closure that rejects, cancelling a still-queued check). The QA Run epic established this and derives `interrupted` for `/qa` (`lib/qa/aggregate.ts:isCheckLive`).

The per-project QA page does neither:

1. **It prints the raw word.** `app/projects/[projectId]/qa/page.tsx:211` renders `report.status` straight from the column, so the same row that reads `interrupted` on `/qa` reads `running` here — indefinitely.

2. **It polls forever, on a fat route.** `hooks/useQaReports.ts:56` gates polling on `reports.some(r => r.status === "running")`. A stranded row makes that predicate permanently true, so the page re-fetches every 3s for as long as it is open. The route it re-fetches is `app/api/projects/[projectId]/qa/reports/route.ts:15` — a bare `db.select().from(qaReports).where(projectId)` with **no limit and no column narrowing**, so every response carries every `report_content` and `prompt_used` for the project.

## Measured cost

Synthetic table, 300 reports at a realistic 120 KB `report_content` + 60 KB `prompt_used` (better-sqlite3, same schema and column order):

- `SELECT *` on that table: **91 ms** per call, ~53 MB of payload.
- Repeated every 3s, forever, on the single shared synchronous better-sqlite3 connection that also serves SSE.

## Fix sketch

Three independent halves, any of which helps:

- Derive the displayed word the way `/qa` now does — reuse `checkStatusLabel`/`isCheckLive` from `lib/qa/aggregate.ts` (already client-safe, and this page already imports `checkTypeLabel` from it).
- Gate the poll on that derived liveness rather than on the raw column, so a stranded row stops the poll.
- Narrow `app/api/projects/[projectId]/qa/reports/route.ts` to the columns the list renders (the report body is already served per-report by `reports/[reportId]/route.ts`), and give it a limit.

Note the write-path half is separate and not covered here: nothing reconciles `qa_reports` at boot the way `failOrphanedRunningSessions()` reconciles `agent_sessions`, so the stranded rows already in a user's database stay stranded whatever the readers do.

epics.title: Kanban Workflow Stability & Real-Time Synchronization
epics.description:
Comprehensive refactor of the ticket workflow system to eliminate erratic behaviors, ensure consistent state transitions, and provide real-time updates without page refresh. This epic addresses critical bugs where tickets move to 'Done' prematurely or don't respect review workflows, while adding WebSocket-based live synchronization and enhanced visual feedback through animations.

Implementation Plan:
1. Workflow Rule Engine: Implement strict state machine for ticket transitions with explicit guards (e.g., no 'Done' without completed review, no premature closure when agent asks questions)
2. WebSocket Infrastructure: Set up Socket.io or native WebSocket server for bidirectional communication, broadcasting ticket updates, agent session status, and column movements to all connected clients
3. Event-Driven Architecture: Unify agent hooks (build complete, review complete) and manual user actions under consistent event bus that enforces workflow rules
4. Animation System: Enhance dnd-kit with custom transitions for programmatic moves (agent-triggered) and add visual indicators (sounds optional, glow effects) for state changes
5. Optimistic UI Updates: Implement optimistic updates with rollback capability for instant feedback, confirmed by WebSocket events
6. Agent Session Integration: Ensure agent session lifecycle (start, resume, completion) properly gates ticket transitions and broadcasts status in real-time

epics.title: e2e : « centres Now and keeps eight project chips clear » échoue en parallèle (compte de projets global)
epics.description:
Découvert pendant la revue de l'épic « L'accès au chat doit être via un bouton direct ». **Préexistant** : reproduit à l'identique sur la merge-base `e415564`, même ligne. Ce n'est pas une régression de cette branche.

## Symptôme

```
npx playwright test e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts
  1 failed
    [chromium] › e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts:77:5 › centres Now and keeps eight project chips clear of the navigation island
  1 passed
```

Échec à `e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts:94` :
```
> 94 |     await expect(chips.getByRole("link")).toHaveCount(9);
```

## Cause

Le test crée 7 projets, plus celui de sa fixture `project` = 8, plus le lien « New project » = 9 liens attendus dans `top-bar-project-chips`.

Mais `playwright.config.ts` a `fullyParallel: true`, et les puces projet de la `TopBar` listent **tous** les projets de la base, pas ceux du test. Le test voisin du même fichier (`keeps the Piscine desk balanced and re-arms dismissed signals on a new failure`) crée son propre projet en parallèle, qui apparaît donc dans la liste. Le snapshot d'erreur le montre :

```yaml
- link "E2E centres Now and keeps eight project chips clear of the navigation island #1"
- link "E2E keeps the Piscine desk balanced and re-arms dismissed signals on a new failure #0"
- link "Navigation 0 ilBb3AaSUcRb"
```

Le compte observé est 10, pas 9.

## Preuve que c'est bien l'isolation

Le même test seul passe :
```
npx playwright test e2e/piscine-finishing.spec.ts -g "centres Now" --workers=1
  1 passed (5.6s)
```

Et la même exécution complète sur la merge-base `e415564` (arbre extrait par `git archive`, `node_modules` en hardlink, DB isolée) échoue à la même ligne 94.

## Pistes

L'assertion de compte absolu est le point fragile — le reste du test (dégagement gauche de l'îlot, absence de menu sur `Now`, débordement scrollable des puces) ne dépend pas du nombre exact. Soit filtrer les puces sur le préfixe de nom propre au test, soit `expect(...).toHaveCount` remplacé par une borne inférieure, soit marquer le test `test.describe.serial` / `test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" })` s'il faut vraiment le compte exact.

Vérifié avec `PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome` (le chromium fourni ne s'installe pas sur cette machine), install cohérent avec le lockfile, sur un port et une DB de brouillon.

Même mécanisme exact. Après « Tous les projets » le registre couvre **tous** les projets (`app/tickets/page.tsx` : « When `?project=` is absent the registry spans every project »), donc `toHaveCount(1)` puis `toHaveCount(4)` comptaient le workspace.

**Reproduit de façon déterministe**, pas déduit du code : un spec sonde jetable maintenant un ticket `review` vivant 45 s en parallèle →

```

Expected: 1 / Received: 2

la signature exacte du ticket. Sans la sonde, le fichier passe seul : les deux tests du fichier finissent trop tôt l'un pour l'autre — c'est bien une course, pas un échec stable.

Le premier correctif (tout passer en `.filter({ hasText })`) **a échoué** :

```
> 62 | await expect(rows.filter({ hasText: title })).toHaveCount(1);
Expected: 1 / Received: 0
```

`GROUP_PREVIEW` (`lib/tickets-registry/aggregate.ts:88`) tronque chaque groupe à 3–4 lignes. Sur un `/tickets` non filtré, les lignes du test sont poussées derrière « + n autres » et **disparaissent**. Sur cette surface la *présence* est aussi peu fiable que le compte — nommer ses identités ne suffit pas.

Donc : l'assertion « Tous les projets » garde ce qu'elle démontre vraiment (le ticket `review` de ce projet revient, les autres restent masqués), et la remise à zéro du filtre d'état est repassée **sous le filtre projet du test**, seul endroit où un compte exact veut dire quelque chose. Les titres portent le `project.id`.

## Preuve rouge → verte

`__tests__/e2e-workspace-scope-counts.test.ts` parse les specs avec l'API TypeScript (pas de regex — cf. la leçon du scan focus-ring) et échoue quand un `toHaveCount(n>0)` sur une collection `getByTestId` se trouve en portée workspace sans `.filter(…)`.

Rejoué avec **la procédure de la porte elle-même** (`git archive` de la merge-base, seul le fichier de test copié dessus) :

| arbre | résultat |
|---|---|
| merge-base `0203b7e` | **1 failed** — `tickets-registry-filters.spec.ts:38` et `:42`, nommées |
| branche | 27 passed |

Des contrôles synthétiques (forme cassée / corrigée / scopée / champ de formulaire) épinglent ce que le scan voit, et deux assertions non vides interdisent un balayage vide. Le scan lit de la **syntaxe, pas du comportement** : un compte passé par une fonction auxiliaire, ou une assertion workspace écrite autrement que `toHaveCount`, lui échappe — c'est écrit dans le fichier.

`e2e/README.md` perd au passage l'affirmation qui a laissé le bug atterrir deux fois (« Tests never share a board, so they stay safe under `fullyParallel` ») : vrai jusqu'à la frontière projet, faux sur `/`, `/tickets` sans `?project=`, `/qa` et les puces du bandeau.

`main` a avancé de `434db26` à `0203b7e` pendant la session et a touché **le fichier que je modifie** (`ee75b6b`, filtres du registre dans l'URL). J'ai fusionné `main` (ajout en fin de fichier, aucun conflit), réinstallé, et **tout re-mesuré** contre `0203b7e` : la preuve rouge, la reproduction avec la sonde, tsc, eslint, vitest et la suite e2e. Les chiffres ci-dessus sont ceux de l'arbre fusionné.

## Non absorbé, filé

Trois échecs rouges sur `main`, reproduits sur `0203b7e`, hors de la classe ou du mécanisme de cet épic :

- **B-arij-228** — `desk-toasts` : troisième instance de la classe, mécanisme différent. Le composer global retombe sur `projects[0]` (`DeskComposer.tsx:64`) et crée dans le projet d'un spec voisin. Non corrigé ici parce que la réparation propre exige d'accrocher un `SelectPill` qui ne forwarde pas de `testId` — la lacune Piscine connue, dont le rayon d'action dépasse cet épic. Mon garde-fou ne le voit pas (ce n'est pas un compte) : c'est dit dans le fichier.

epics.title: React Compiler bails on 48 of 113 probeable components — every rule silent, no diagnostic
epics.description:
Found while fixing `-rZwgotHQkD2` (the `React.`-namespaced hooks blind spot). This is a **second, larger blind spot with the same symptom and a different cause**, deliberately left out of that diff. B-arij-212 — the Sessions page instance, found independently with a positive control — is folded in below.

## The defect

Even with hooks called by their bare name, the React Compiler declines to analyse many components outright. When it bails, every compiler-backed rule goes silent on that component — and there is no diagnostic. `react-hooks/unsupported-syntax` (enabled at warning) reports nothing.

So a bailed component is indistinguishable from a clean one, exactly like the namespace bug. Fixing the namespace issue does **not** fix this: measured identical before and after conversion.

## Measured

Probe: inject a self-contained `const [__p, __setProbe] = useState(0); useEffect(() => __setProbe(1), []);` at the top of the component body and lint with the repo's own ESLint config. A component that is analysed reports `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`; a bailed one is silent.

Across `components/`, `app/`, `hooks/`, `lib/`:

- **113 probeable components, 65 open, 48 BAILED.**

`NowDesk` is the clearest demonstration that this is a bail and not a probe artefact:
- `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` (a syntactic rule, not compiler-backed) **does** fire inside it;
- every compiler-backed rule is silent, including a violation injected at the very first line of the component body;
- it is the only component in its 816-line file.

## The 48

`components/`: `agents-workshop/AddAgentCard`, `agents-workshop/AgentsWorkshopView`, `agents-workshop/AssignmentsView`, `agents-workshop/WhereHeWorksBand`, `auto-mode/AutoModeDialog`, `chat-page/DraftedEpicCard`, `desk/DeskComposer`, `desk/NowDesk`, `documents/ScanProjectDialog`, `epic/UserStoryQuickActions`, `github/GitHubConnectBanner`, `kanban/BugCreateDialog`, `kanban/EpicCreateDialog`, `kanban/InlineEdit`, `kanban/QuickCapture`, `kanban/RefinementButton`, `night/NightRunDialog`, `qa/QaScreen`, `qa/ReportDetail`, `qa/StartQaCheckDialog`, `review/InlineCommentForm`, `review/ReviewActions`, `routines/RoutinesSettings`, `sessions/SessionOutputStream`, `settings/McpServersSection`, `settings-piscine/GitHubCard`, `settings-piscine/OpenAiCard`, `settings-piscine/WebhooksBand`, `shared/AgentActionsBar`, `spec/DocsCard`, `spec/MemoryPanel`, `spec/SpecUpdateDialog`, `story/CommentThread`, `tickets-registry/NewTicketView`, `usage/MonthlyCapTile`.

`app/`: `inbox/page`, `projects/[projectId]/{documents,frictions,git-sync,github-issues,layout,settings,spec}/page`, `projects/[projectId]/sessions/page`, `projects/[projectId]/sessions/[sessionId]/page`, `projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/page`, `projects/import/page`, `projects/new/page`.

## The Sessions page instance, with a positive control (from B-arij-212)

Found while fixing `DrsYAB9iY9kE`. The same textbook `set-state-in-effect` violation — `useEffect(() => { setSummaryRunId(null); }, [projectId]);`, a real setter already declared in the component — was injected into three files and each linted with `npx eslint <file>`:

| file | diagnostic |
|---|---|
| `app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/page.tsx` | **none** |
| `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts` | reported |
| `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx` | reported |

The two positives prove the harness, the rule and the `app/**` + `hooks/**` scope all work, so this is a per-component bail, not a config-scope problem. The file imports bare (`import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react"`) and calls hooks by bare name throughout, so the namespace fix cannot apply and `__tests__/react-compiler-namespaced-hooks.test.ts`, which scans for `React.use*` call sites, cannot catch it by construction. Consequence: the Sessions page's own lint result cannot be cited as evidence in review.

## Already pinned (verified on `0484bdf`)

`__tests__/react-compiler-namespaced-hooks.test.ts:118-123` pins four as `KNOWN_BAILED` — `components/chat-page/DraftedEpicCard.tsx`, `components/desk/DeskComposer.tsx`, `components/desk/NowDesk.tsx`, `components/qa/QaScreen.tsx` — with the probe helper (`withBailProbe`) reusable as-is for the rest. Shrinking that list fails the test on purpose. But both probe loops iterate only the fixed 26-file `CONVERTED` list (`:70`, `:380`, `:415`); no test enumerates client components, and the coverage guard is `expect(checked.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4)` (`:410`). So the test asserts a *cause* (`React.use*`) on 26 files, not *coverage* of the app.

Note the original epic's spot-check called `NowDesk` and `QaScreen` "clean once analysed" — they are not clean, they are never analysed. Any "no diagnostics here" conclusion about a bailed component is worthless.

`next.config.ts` does not enable `reactCompiler` (its `experimental` block holds only `proxyClientMaxBodySize`), so today the cost is lost lint coverage rather than lost optimisation. That changes the day the compiler is switched on.

## Not attempted

The root cause per component. `NowDesk` was bisected far enough to confirm the bail is real and to rule out the namespace issue, but a statement-level bisect needs a proper AST walk — a line/brace-based splitter drifts on template literals and comments and gave a misleading answer. Finding what makes each component un-compilable is real per-component work, not a mechanical rewrite.

## Work

1. For each of the 48, isolate the construct that makes the compiler bail (AST-driven bisect against the injected probe), and either rewrite it so the component is analysed or record it in `KNOWN_BAILED` with a one-line reason naming the construct.
2. Turn the guard test from a cause check into a coverage check: enumerate every client component under `app/`, `components/`, `hooks/`, inject the probe, and require a diagnostic unless the file is in `KNOWN_BAILED` with a reason. That is the only check that distinguishes "clean" from "unread", and it would have caught both the Sessions page and the original 26.
3. Report the population counts (probeable / analysed / bailed) after the sweep, not the delta.

## Acceptance

- Every component in the list above either reports the probe diagnostic or appears in `KNOWN_BAILED` with a reason naming the construct; `app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/page.tsx` specifically reports the probe.
- The guard test enumerates client components rather than a fixed file list, and fails when a component outside `KNOWN_BAILED` goes silent.
- `KNOWN_BAILED` shrinking still fails the test on purpose; growing it requires a reason string.
- Counts (probeable / analysed / bailed) are reported in the ticket comment against the tip they were measured on.

## Both review findings addressed — commit `6375f3e4`

### Major — anonymous default exports escaped the coverage guard

Reproduced exactly as reported. `probeTargets` mirrored the compiler's inference all the way down to `getFunctionName`, which returns `null` for `export default function () {}` and `export default () => {}` — so those functions were not *declined*, they were never **listed**. Measured in memory on `app/projects/new/page.tsx`: the named form draws `set-state-in-effect` on the injected probe, the anonymous form draws nothing, and `probeTargets` returned `[]`.

Mirroring the inference is the point; agreeing with it about what *exists* is what let a rename delete a component from the population and take every compiler-backed rule inside it along with it.

**Fix:** `export default` is now the population's own floor, *below* the compiler's inference (`__tests__/helpers/react-compiler-probe.ts`, `isDefaultExport`). A default export that calls hooks or renders is listed whatever the compiler manages to call it, with the naming as its bail reason. Two forms of the same hole are covered:

| form | key | reason |
|---|---|---|
| `export default function () {}` / `export default () => {}` | `#(anonymous-default)` | no name for the compiler to take |
| `export default function page()` | `#page` | neither PascalCase nor `use`-prefixed |

The second is the same loss with a name attached — `isComponentName`/`isHook` decline it just as silently — so it is closed in the same pass. Every default export in the tree is PascalCase today, so **the population is unchanged**: the hole is closed, not paid for.

**Regression:** the reviewer's actual mutation, applied in memory to a real page. Each mutant must come back **listed** *and* **bailed** *and* absent from `KNOWN_BAILED` — i.e. it must fail the sweep — plus the arrow form on a synthetic page. Red on base at `expected +0 to be 1` (`probeTargets` returned nothing).

Confirmed. `Promise<unknown>` does not prohibit a callback throwing *before* it returns a promise; the throw unwinds through the call expression before `.finally` is attached, and the spinner then runs for the life of the component. The three `ReviewActions` handlers and `InlineCommentForm` now settle the callback through an async wrapper first, as `DeskComposer` already did. The rejection still reaches the caller — the tests assert that too, so a later "fix" that swallows it fails rather than passes.

Aujourd'hui trois mécanismes distincts choisissent ou re-choisissent un agent, et ils ne se parlent pas :

1. `named_agents.escalates_to` (`lib/db/schema.ts:517`, migration `0039_named_agent_escalation`) est une chaîne de repli d'agent nommé, mais elle refuse tout changement de provider (`readEffortEscalationTarget()`, `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:530-562`) et ne se déclenche qu'à la tentative 3 — or `DEFAULT_PIPELINE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:60`). Sans relever `pipeline_max_attempts`, cette escalade n'est jamais atteinte : le mécanisme est de fait mort par défaut.
2. `pickAlternativeReviewProvider()` (`lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts:129-149`) parcourt la liste ordonnée en dur `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (`lib/agent-config/constants.ts:232-241`) pour l'escalade des tentatives 3/4+ (`stages.ts:781-796`) — mais au grain *provider*, et elle jette l'agent nommé (`namedAgentId: null`, modèle par défaut du CLI).
3. Le smart dispatch (`lib/agent-config/smart-dispatch.ts`) choisit par fiabilité mesurée, mais uniquement en Full Auto et opt-in.

Décision produit : modèle binaire. Soit on choisit un agent spécifique et on s'y tient, soit on utilise un agent composite — une liste ordonnée d'agents nommés, dont on peut créer autant qu'on veut. L'existant (1) et (2, en tant qu'escaladeur) est retiré.

## Plan d'implémentation

### Schéma

Un composite est une ligne de `named_agents` portant `kind = 'composite'`, pas une table séparée. C'est la décision structurante : `agent_provider_defaults.named_agent_id` (les 21 `AGENT_TYPES`, scope global et projet), `chat_conversations.named_agent_id`, `qa_reports.named_agent_id`, `agent_sessions.named_agent_id` et les deux sélecteurs (`AgentSelectPill`, `NamedAgentSelect`) pointent déjà vers `named_agents.id` — un composite devient donc assignable partout sans toucher une seule FK. Une table `composite_agents` séparée obligerait à unir deux types dans chaque FK et chaque picker.

- `named_agents.kind` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT `'simple'` (`'simple' | 'composite'`).
- Nouvelle table `composite_agent_members` : `composite_id` (FK → `named_agents.id` ON DELETE CASCADE), `member_id` (FK → `named_agents.id` ON DELETE CASCADE), `position` INTEGER, index unique `(composite_id, position)` et `(composite_id, member_id)`.
- Pas d'imbrication : un membre doit être `kind = 'simple'`. Refusé à l'écriture, ce qui évite de réintroduire une détection de cycle.
- Un composite n'a ni `provider` ni `model` propres : les colonnes existantes sont neutralisées pour lui (valeur sentinelle documentée), la validation d'écriture les ignore.
- `agent_sessions.composite_agent_id` (nullable) : le composite qui a dispatché. `agent_sessions.named_agent_id` continue d'enregistrer le membre qui a réellement tourné, sinon `getNamedAgentDispatchReliability()` (`lib/agent-config/stats.ts:208`) regroupe tout sur le composite et les statistiques de fiabilité perdent leur sens.
- Migrations écrites à la main : fichier numéroté sous `lib/db/migrations/` + entrée dans `meta/_journal.json` avec un `when` strictement supérieur au dernier appliqué. `npx drizzle-kit generate` est interdit (snapshots figés à 0013). Vérifier le numéro le plus haut contre le tip de `main` juste avant le merge — plusieurs branches ajoutent « le prochain » numéro en parallèle.

### Démolition

- Retrait de la colonne `named_agents.escalates_to` (migration de suppression), de `validateEscalationTarget()` (`lib/agent-config/named-agents.ts:105-140`), du contrôle `escalatesTo` dans `components/agents-workshop/AgentIdentityCard.tsx`, de `readEffortEscalationTarget()` et du compteur d'escalades dans `getNamedAgentStats()` (`lib/agent-config/agent-stats.ts`).
- Retrait des deux branches de bascule d'agent de `resolveStageAgent()` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:760-796`) et de la trace `PIPELINE_REASONS.effortEscalation` (`lib/pipeline/constants.ts:203-206`).
- Piège à ne pas rater : la branche « autre provider » appelle `pickAlternativeReviewProvider()`, mais cette fonction sert *aussi* à la ségrégation de review (reviewer ≠ builder, `lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts:129-149`), qui reste voulue. On retire l'appel comme escaladeur, pas la fonction.

### Résolution et échelle

- `resolveAgentByNamedId()` / `resolveAgentForDispatch()` (`lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:397-515`) déplient un composite en un membre pour un rang donné.
- Échelle du runner : agent simple → on retente le *même* agent (reprise de session en tentative 2 via `previousAttemptSessionId`, puis à neuf), jamais de bascule. Composite → chaque tentative descend d'un rang ; la longueur de la liste devient le budget de tentatives, ce qui retire `pipeline_max_attempts` comme verrou d'escalade. `PIPELINE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN = 12` reste le garde-fou global.
- Ce qui fait descendre d'un rang : `status: failed`, `transition_refused`, et `silent`. Ce qui ne fait pas descendre : un verdict de review négatif et un échec de la porte de régression ou de la vérification déterministe — ce sont des cycles de fix, avec leur propre budget (`maxFixCycles`) ; les confondre consommerait la liste d'agents pour un désaccord de review. `asked_question` et `cancelled` restent terminaux : si l'agent pose une question, on attend l'utilisateur.

### Hors périmètre (tickets de suivi à filer)

- Le sort du smart dispatch : c'est un troisième chemin de choix automatique qui contredit le modèle binaire ; le convertir en « stratégie d'ordre » d'un composite (ordre manuel vs par fiabilité) est une idée à part entière.
- Le plafond de concurrence par agent nommé : la limite est globale (une colonne sur `named_agents`, valable partout, y compris hors composite), donc elle n'a plus rien à voir avec les composites. C'est un changement d'ordonnanceur (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts`, qui ne compte aujourd'hui qu'un `Set` de sessions par projet sans savoir quel agent tient chaque slot), avec sa propre question de blocage de tête de file (position retenue : admission dans le désordre) et un paramètre à propager sur la vingtaine d'appelants de `agentScheduler.submit()`. Epic distincte.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Composite agents — epic complete, suite green

Continued from `5f51904` (stories 1–6 + the resolution/ladder halves) and finished the epic. Four commits added:

| commit | what |
|---|---|
| `402e9de` | greened the branch under `tsc`/lint |
| `de1e1bd` | stub-binary argv dispatch test (story 3's last criterion) |
| `1eb49ff` | real-browser e2e: focus ring in both themes + 390px (story 7's last two) |
| `69ca4c0` | typed the argv probe's dispatch options |

Plus the **stored specification rewritten** (story 8), written through `PATCH /api/projects/u1HcvrXnpuvm` — 52 593 → 56 450 bytes.

### Measurements — all against `main` at **77b0039** (main has not moved; it is still the merge-base)

- **Full suite: 611 files / 8441 tests, 0 failures.**
- `tsc --noEmit`: **clean**. It was *not* clean when I picked this up — 9 errors in two test files (eight `resolveAgent*` mock literals predating `compositeAgentId`, one fixture missing `kind`/`members`/`isDefault`).
- `eslint`: **0 errors, 26 warnings**, all 26 in files this branch never touched. Six warnings *were* mine — dead bindings left by the demolition (`namedAgents`/`AgentProvider` in `stages.ts`, `pipelineMaxAttemptsSettingKey`, `settings`, `verifyCommandsSettingKey`, `emitTicketUpdated`, `fsMock`) — and are gone.
- **Migration numbering re-checked at merge time**: `main` tops out at `0052_refinement_actions`; the branch adds `0053`/`0054`/`0055` with `idx` and `when` both strictly increasing. This reconciliation expires as `main` advances.
- **Migration validated on a copy of the real dev DB** (`VACUUM INTO` off the live 1.16 GB file — read-only on the source), not just a fresh one: **6 pre-existing `named_agents`, 1391 `agent_sessions`**. After the chain: all 6 rows `kind='simple'` (zero exceptions), `escalates_to` dropped, `composite_agent_members` present with both unique indexes and CASCADE FKs, `agent_sessions.composite_agent_id` present with `ON DELETE SET NULL` and NULL on all 1391 rows. A second `initDb()` on the same file is a no-op — the chain is re-runnable.

### Evidence quality — every new test proven non-vacuous by mutation

Each mutation was **re-read on disk when the suite reported**, per the false-negative trap:

- `resolveCompositeMemberAtRank` pinned to `members[0]` → rank-1 argv test red.
- codex's non-resume `args.push("-m", model)` removed → rank-0 and the `cli_command` test red.
- `focus-visible:outline-solid` dropped from `IconControl` → **both** themes red with the exact historical signature: `outline-style "none"` (`--tw-outline-style: "none"`) while width 2px and colour `rgb(36, 144, 122)` applied.

One probe failed honestly and is worth recording: my first codex mutation hit the **resume** branch's identical `-m` push, which this path never takes, and the suite stayed green. That was a bad probe, not a coverage hole.

### Boundaries — what the evidence does and does not cover

- **The dispatch binaries are stubs.** `codex` and `agy` are node scripts on a temporary PATH that record their argv and exit 0. Honest evidence about Arij's selection and argv assembly; **no evidence at all** about the agents' behaviour. Nothing ran Codex or Antigravity.
- The e2e spec needs `E2E_PORT=3187 PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome` — the default 3100 collides between worktrees, and Playwright's own chromium will not install on this host.
- **Prose copies corrected: the stored spec only** (§1.1, §1.2, §5.4, §5.5.1, §6.7, §7, §8). **Left untouched: `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/`** — I grepped both for `escalat` and they never described the mechanism, so there was nothing to correct rather than nothing checked.
- §1.2 now names this epic as the branch the composite description lands from, and says plainly that `main` at 77b0039 still carries the escalation column. The spec is stored live while the branch is unmerged; that note is what keeps it truthful until the merge.
- The spec write re-exported **`arji.json` in the main checkout** (`/home/orosius/workspace/arij`), which is now modified there. That is a legitimate export of the new stored spec, not churn to revert — but it is not mine to commit, and it is in a different checkout.

### One test failure investigated, and it is not this branch

The first full-suite run failed on `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx > "is inert while the dispatch is in flight…"`. I did not dismiss it — my own notes say a failure there is a real regression, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms both historical fixes are ancestors of HEAD. Measured under 14 synthetic load workers:

| variant | failures |
|---|---|
| `HEAD` (this diff) | **5 / 12** |
| `HEAD` with `main`'s `NamedAgentSelect.tsx` swapped in | **5 / 12** |

**Identical rates ⇒ the diff is not implicated.** The test carries a hard-coded **10 ms real-time budget** (`delayMs: 10`, then a `waitFor` before the in-flight assertions); under contention the `waitFor` polling alone exceeds it. The prior closure rested on 31 runs of the *isolated file*, which is exactly the condition under which a 10 ms budget holds. Filed as friction (register shows **24 occurrences**, deduplicated) and not fixed here — absorbing it would mix an unrelated change into this diff. **Code Review**

Findings filed (6 review comments, verdict `changes_requested`).

# Code Review — Composite agents (E-BwEtdU8xBcbs)

**Scope:** `77b0039..69ca4c0`, 5 commits, 78 files, +3966/−1497. Measured against `main` at `77b0039`, still the merge-base. No repository file was modified; `git status` is clean.

## What holds up

The demolition (story 2) is complete and honest. `escalates_to`, `validateEscalationTarget`, `validateIncomingEscalations`, `readEffortEscalationTarget`, both agent-switch branches of `resolveStageAgent`, the `escalatesTo` UI control, the escalation stat query and the two `PIPELINE_REASONS` strings are all gone; `pickAlternativeReviewProvider` survives and reviewer segregation still routes through it. Grep on the three tokens is clean outside historical migrations.

Migrations `0053`–`0055` are hand-written, journalled with strictly increasing `idx` and `when` above `main`'s `0052_refinement_actions`, and `lib/db/init.ts`'s post-baseline probe list is correctly extended — including the deliberate omission of an entry for the DROP migration, whose reasoning I checked and agree with.

The "a composite is a row of `named_agents`" decision pays off as claimed: `compositeAgentId` was swept onto all 15 `agent_sessions` insert sites, and the non-session `namedAgentId` sites (`review-resolution`, `conversations`, `default-chat-mode`) are legitimately exempt. `getNamedAgentDispatchReliability` groups by `named_agent_id`, so a composite genuinely never becomes a reliability row.

`tsc --noEmit` clean. The seven composite-touching test files pass: 156 tests.

## Blocking

**1. Critical — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:362`.** The build stage's attempt budget is never sized from the composite. `stageMaxAttempts` is reassigned only inside `dispatch()` under `request.attempt === 1`, and the initial build never goes through `dispatch()`. I ran `runPipeline` directly: with `maxAttempts: 2` and `attemptBudget: () => 4`, a failing build gives requests `[{build,2}]` and `"stage build failed after 2 attempts"`; the same options with the failure on review give `[1,2,3,4]`. Members 3 and 4 of a build composite are unreachable, while `CompositeIdentityCard` tells the user the member count *is* the attempt budget. The mirror case (a 2-member composite with `pipeline_max_attempts: 5`) makes attempts 3–5 throw `"Composite agent has no member at rank N"` inside `launchStage`, burning attempts on an internal error and skipping the forensic stage.

`pipeline-e2e.test.ts` misses this because its composite has exactly 2 members — the same number as `DEFAULT_PIPELINE_MAX_ATTEMPTS`.

**2. Major — `lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:491`.** The default-composite branch of `resolveAgent()` is unguarded, so an emptied designated default composite throws `CompositeAgentUnusableError` for every agent type with no explicit assignment. Confirmed on a scratch DB: designate a composite as default, delete the simple agent that is its only member (an ordinary roster action, no guard, `composite_agent_members` cascades), and both `resolveAgent('build')` and `resolveAgent('chat')` throw. Throwing is correct when the caller *named* the composite; here the user asked the server to decide, and `readDefaultCompositeAgentId()` already degrades a *deleted* composite to "no designation" — an emptied one should match.

## Non-blocking

- **Minor** — `WhereHeWorksBand.tsx:174` and `AssignmentsView.tsx:160` render a composite as an empty provider label plus a false `· CLI default model`. These are the pickers where a composite gets assigned to a role, and they are the only agent pickers not swept.
- **Minor** — five exported helpers in `composite-agents.ts` have zero callers, including `listMembersByComposite`, whose absence leaves `listNamedAgents` doing one membership query per composite.
- **Minor** — `updateCompositeAgent` commits the rename before validating members, so a rejected reorder still renames the agent.
- **Minor** — the review resolution (with its `isAvailable()` subprocess probes) now runs twice per stage entry.

## Coverage gaps against acceptance criteria

Not filed as anchored findings, but worth naming: story 3's "composite assigned to a role in `agent_provider_defaults` at global **and** project scope is unfolded at dispatch" and "a composite selected on a chat conversation is unfolded" have no test — the `legacy-fallback-named-agents.test.ts` changes are queue adjustments for the new settings read, not new coverage. Both paths look correct by inspection. `CompositeAgentUnusableError` is thrown but never asserted, caught, or mapped to a status code anywhere.

## Category summary

| Category | Result |
|---|---|
| Readability | No issues found — comment density is unusually high and the rationale is accurate. |
| DRY | 2 findings (dead helpers + N+1; duplicate review resolution). |
| Error handling | No issues found in the new code paths; finding 2 is a missing guard, not a broken handler. |
| Performance | 2 minor findings (N+1 on the picker route, doubled CLI probes). |
| Naming | No issues found. |
| Type safety | No issues found. No `any`; the one `as unknown as AgentProvider` is the documented sentinel cast. |
| Testing | 2 blocking defects the suite does not reach, plus 3 untested acceptance criteria. |
| API design | No issues found. |

**Total:** 1 critical, 1 major, 4 minor.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: /projects/:id/qa dessine son propre en-tête de page, contre la règle Piscine « aucun header d'écran »
epics.description:
## Ce que je vois `app/projects/[projectId]/qa/page.tsx` rend son propre en-tête : ```tsx

QA

Run tech checks, E2E tests, and recurring-failure digests; …

``` plus une rangée de boutons shadcn `Button` (« Refresh », « New Check ») et des pastilles de filtre faites main (`rounded-full … bg-foreground text-background`), là où le reste de l'app utilise `PillButton` / `SegmentedControl` du barrel Piscine. C'est contraire à deux règles explicites de `CLAUDE.md` : - « `components/piscine/TopBar.tsx` … est le seul chrome de l'app. Un écran ne rend **aucun en-tête de page** — pas de logo, pas de nav, pas de ⌘K. » - « Composer depuis `@/components/piscine`. Ne pas re-styler une primitive shadcn en sosie. » Une pastille remplie `bg-foreground text-background` est en plus un bouton **noir**, alors que la règle est : rempli = `--action` (vert d'eau profond), jamais noir. ## Pourquoi maintenant L'écran est resté hors de la refonte : il n'était atteignable que depuis le menu déroulant icône-seule « Project pages » du desk. L'epic QA Run vient de le remettre dans le bar (entrée Work → « QA checks »), donc c'est désormais une destination de premier plan et l'écart de style est visible à chaque visite. Capture au 1440×900 : le `

QA

` et sa description occupent la bande sous le TopBar, à l'endroit exact où les autres écrans commencent directement par leur première `StrataBand`. ## Ce que ça n'est pas Ce n'est pas une régression de l'epic QA Run : le header existait déjà avant, à l'identique. Il est déposé séparément parce que le porter dans ce diff aurait mélangé un portage visuel complet de l'écran (bandes, primitives, pastilles) avec la restauration de la capacité de lancer un QA run — deux périmètres, deux preuves. ## Périmètre attendu Porter l'écran sur les primitives Piscine : retirer le header, passer l'historique et le détail du rapport en `StrataBand` + `BandHeader`, remplacer les `Button` par `PillButton` et les pastilles de filtre par `SegmentedControl` (ou `FindingFilterPills`, qui répond déjà à cette forme sur `/qa`). Les contrôles par écran vont dans une seconde rangée du contenu, comme `QaScreen` le fait pour « Run QA pass » et « New check ». `components/qa/ReportDetail.tsx` (535 lignes) fait partie du périmètre et n'a pas été mesuré ici.
